# Native Docs reader, wave 5 part 1 — the Docs screen Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** this wave is dispatched by the programme's coordinator as one run (see "How this wave runs" below). The worker executes it with REQUIRED SUB-SKILL superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans, task by task, under the `ccrc-worker` skill. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Give the operator the Docs screen: `/docs` and every page under it renders the fleet's project docs from W3's routes, in the PWA, with no server change. The L0 `GithubTarget` widening and the permalink builder land FIRST (§3.11); then `api.docs.*` with the marker header and its answer unions; every sentence map and the failure view; W4's r10, r11 and 2-2 bounded in the shared Markdown components for docs and chat alike, each value measured; the docs profile's real `<br>`; `useDocsVisit` (tree and file slots, the expected pin, auto-refresh once per open, retries, re-list on return and after sign-in); the docs link and image policy (`detachUrls`, `DocLink`, `DocImage`, `imagePinFor`, the fetch queue, raster object URLs, SVG `data:` images, the page highlight budget); `DocMarkdown` (gate, parse on `docsRunner`, notes, `DocPlain`, the doc-body boundary); `DocsScreen` with the index, project, section, directory and leaf views and the `docs` arm of the app; the header (truth line, freshness chip, banners, View on GitHub, Open committed version, copy commit); the Docs door and the session links; `docs.css` with its contrast and tap-target registrations; and the `browser (pwa)` leg with M5.B5 and M5.B6 (required by `full-suite`, never a branch-protection check: operator ruling 2026-10-13). Share and Export are W5 part 2 (refinement (a)).

**Architecture:** Every new unit lives under `pwa/src/docs/` plus `pwa/src/screens/DocsScreen.tsx`, over W1's L0 (`shared/docs.ts`), W3's four routes and W4's pipeline. L0 gains only the widened `GithubTarget`/`GithubLink`, `GithubPermalink`, `githubPermalink` and the private `githubUrlAt` (Task 1). The data path is one funnel: `api.docs.*` inside `createApi` (so a 401 still raises the overlay) answers a discriminated union, never an exception for a docs word (`docs/failures.ts` holds the client slots, the classifier and the retry plan); `docs/useDocsVisit.ts` owns the visit's slots and timers; the views are pure renderers of those slots plus `docs/docsText.ts`'s sentence maps. Markdown goes `useParsedMarkdown(text, docsRunner.parse, {profile: 'docs'})` → `detachUrls` (a copy, URLs moved into a `WeakMap`) → `renderHast(tree, {components: DOC_COMPONENTS})` inside a `RenderBoundary` keyed by the pin; `DOC_COMPONENTS = {...SHARED_COMPONENTS, a: DocLink, img: DocImage}`, and the page highlight budget reaches `CodeBlock` through one context `lib/markdown.tsx` declares (chat provides none, so chat is byte-identical). The three bounds live where the cost is: r10 (one long word in a highlighted fence) and r11 (a whitespace-flooded code span) in `lib/markdown.tsx`, and 2-2 (chips drawn from many spans) in the parse's own element count in `lib/markdownParse.ts`, so `too-wide` fires before anything renders; both constants are declared once in `lib/markdownLimits.ts`. The browser leg is a second vitest config over `pwa/browser/`, driving a real Chrome through `playwright-core`, with its own CI job, a leg `full-suite` requires (not a branch-protection check). One run: one worker, one reviewer.

**Tech Stack:** TypeScript 6 (pwa's own `tsc`: lib ES2023 + DOM, `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noUnusedLocals`/`Parameters`, `erasableSyntaxOnly`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`) and the server's TypeScript 7 for `shared/docs.ts` and the server tests; React 19.2.7; Vite 8.1; vite-plugin-pwa 1.3; vitest 4.1 on jsdom 28 (no `Worker` global, `css: false`); react-markdown 10.1.0, remark-gfm 4.0.1, highlight.js 11.11.1 (15 grammars registered at the base, `php` from #111); `playwright-core` (new exact-version devDependency; downloads no browser) driving Chrome from `CCRC_CHROME` or `/usr/bin/google-chrome`; Node `>=22.13.0` (the box runs v24.14.1).

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-01-native-docs-reader-design.md` as amended 2026-10-13 (Share and Export, #385) — §0 (goals 3 and 4, the `session-links`, `Q1`, `Q4`, `freshness`, `http`, `U1`, `U4`, `sharing` and `share-export` rows); §1's PWA units; §3.1, §3.2, §3.9, §3.11 (whole); §4.1's W5 rows; §4.2's docs arm; §4.3-§4.8; §4.9's limits table; §4.10 (DocMarkdown, `DOC_COMPONENTS`, highlighting, the bounds on the shared components); §4.11; §4.12's doc-body mount and chat clause on the bounds; §4.14 (the docs chrome); §4.15's M4.R1 (W5 half), M4.R2, M4.R4, M4.L1, M4.L2, M4.P1, M4.P6, M4.P7, M4.P12 (W5 halves), M4.P9, M4.H2, M4.U1-U7, M4.T1-T7 (T7's base form), M4.F1-F6, M4.A1-A3, M4.B1 (W5 half), M4.B2, M4.S1 (its docs-chrome form); §2's rows 54, 60, 61 (PWA half), 66, 67; §3.14's M3.11 (its `repo`, `root`, `bad-slug` and `bad-target` rows), M3.16-M3.18; §5.1, §5.4 (`api.docs`, `rasterObjectUrl`, `downloadDocFile`, `saveBytes`), §5.5, §5.7; §5.8's M5.3 (leaf-routing half), M5.17 (its `rasterObjectUrl`, `downloadDocFile` and `saveBytes` clauses), M5.18, M5.20, M5.B5, M5.B6; §6.1; §7.1's PWA rows; §7.7's W5 row; §7.8's R1 and R2; §7.9's every-wave and W5 suites; §7.10's M7.1. And `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-rich-docs-reader-and-shared-renderer-design.md`: W5 stays plain plus a real `<br>` in the docs profile (its A16, M9.1), W5b after W5 (RD23), A22.

**Format:** Markdown, by the operator's ruling of 2026-10-07. `server/test/deviation-refs.test.ts` and the ledger's floor scan read `*.md` plans, and Task 14's scratch tools parse this file's `### Task` headings and its JSON row fences.

## Global Constraints

- SAFETY: never run `ccd` against the live HOME, never run a destructive ccd verb, never touch tmux, `~/.cc-sessions`, `~/.cc-limits` or `claude-session@*` units, never call the live ccrc server, never print a secret file's contents. Every Docs test injects its loaders or a `createApi(fetchImpl)`; no test reaches a real server. Mutations and build gates run in a scratch COPY of the tree (`git archive HEAD | tar -x -C <copy>`, `git -C <copy> init -q`, `pwa/node_modules` and `server/node_modules` linked in) under `$HOME/.cc-tmp/docs-w5p1-<task>`, never `/tmp` (the fleet box's reaper deletes `/tmp` entries older than 12 h) and never in the worktree.
- Scope. - Rings and seams. `shared/docs.ts` stays L0: it imports nothing, its whole text is pure ASCII, and no comment in it contains `import (`, `require (`, `Buffer`, `process.` or `node:` (`docs-shared.test.ts`'s L0 refusals read comments too). The worker closure (`markdownLimits.ts`, `markdownGuard.ts`, `remarkAlerts.ts`, `markdownParse.ts`, `markdownWorker.ts`) gains no import and no file (`markdown-purity.test.ts`'s ROOTS and ALLOWED_PACKAGES do not change). `renderHast` stays pure and never mutates its tree; `detachUrls` returns a copy. No overloaded `null` at a seam: every `null` or optional in a W5 signature has exactly one stated meaning (each Interfaces block says which). The PWA imports every docs constant, type and function from `shared/docs.ts` and redeclares none (`single-definition.test.ts` holds the caps, the page prefix, the header literal, the CSP text, the PNG magic, the redactor fragments, the section literals and every L0 name to `shared/docs.ts`).
- Exact values, copied from the spec (tests import them; nothing restates them):
  - Caps and limits: `DOCS_MAX_IMAGES_PER_PAGE` = 30 and `DOCS_STALE_MS` = 600 000 (imported from `shared/docs.ts`, never restated); `DOCS_CLASS_CAP` (2 097 152 for every class at the base); `DOCS_PWA_FETCH_CONCURRENCY` = 2, in `docs/fetchQueue.ts`; `DOCS_RENDER_GATE_BYTES` = 524 288; `DOCS_PARSE_BUDGET_MS` = `min(10 000, 2 000 + 1 000 x floor(bytes / 65 536))` over UTF-8 bytes; `DOCS_PARSE_BUDGET_LARGE_MS` = 30 000 (Format anyway); `DOCS_HIGHLIGHT_PAGE_MAX_CHARS` = 524 288; `MD_HIGHLIGHT_BLOCK_MAX_CHARS` = 65 536; `CHAT_SYNC_MAX_BYTES` = 4 096; `DOCS_MAX_RENDER_ELEMENTS` = 20 000; `MD_MAX_CONTAINER_DEPTH` = 32; `MD_MAX_TREE_DEPTH` = 64. The two new bound constants (refinements (e), (f)) are declared once in `lib/markdownLimits.ts`.
  - L0 widening (§3.11), verbatim: `GithubTarget` = `{ kind: 'leaf'; section: DocSectionSlug; path: string; uncommitted: boolean } | { kind: 'section'; section: DocSectionSlug } | { kind: 'dir'; section: DocSectionSlug; path: string } | { kind: 'repo'; repoPath: string } | { kind: 'root' }`; `GithubLink` = `{ ok: true; url: string; note: 'may-differ' | null } | { ok: false; why: 'no-github-origin' | 'not-on-origin' | 'uncommitted' | 'bad-slug' | 'bad-target' }`; `GithubPermalink` = `{ ok: true; url: string; commit: string } | { ok: false; why: 'no-github-origin' | 'not-on-origin' | 'unmeasured' | 'uncommitted' | 'bad-slug' | 'bad-target' }`; `githubPermalink(github: DocsGithub, ref: DocsTreeOk['ref'], commit: string, target: GithubTarget): GithubPermalink`. `githubBlobUrl`'s rows, first match wins: `github.state === 'none'` gives `no-github-origin`; a slug segment `.` or `..`, or an owner starting with `.`, gives `bad-slug`; an `at` or path segment empty, `.` or `..` gives `bad-target`; `relation === 'local-only'` or `via` `default:local-main`/`default:local-master` gives `not-on-origin`; a leaf with `uncommitted` gives `uncommitted`; `side === 'origin'` or `relation === 'equal'` links; `side === 'local'` with `local-ahead`, `local-behind`, `diverged` or `unmeasured` links with the note `may-differ`. `githubPermalink`'s rows, first match wins: `no-github-origin`; `bad-slug`; `commit` not 40 or 64 lowercase hex, or an `at` or path segment empty, `.` or `..`, gives `bad-target`; `local-only` or `default:local-*` gives `not-on-origin`; a leaf with `uncommitted` gives `uncommitted`; `side === 'origin'` (covering `origin-only`), or `relation` `equal` or `local-behind`, links; `side === 'local'` with `local-ahead` or `diverged` gives `not-on-origin`; `relation === 'unmeasured'` gives `unmeasured`. URLs: `/blob/<at>/<repoPath>` for a leaf or `repo`, `/tree/<at>/<path>` for a section or directory, `/tree/<at>` for `root`; each segment through `encodeURIComponent`; View on GitHub's `at` is `ref.name`, the permalink's is the full commit, a `#fragment` is never written. ONE private `githubUrlAt(slug, at, target)` holds the file's one `'https://github.com/'` literal.
  - The visit (§4.3), verbatim: `TreeSlot` = `{ s: 'loading' } | { s: 'ok'; answer: DocsTreeResponse; receivedAt: number } | { s: 'failed'; body: DocsFailureBody } | { s: 'auth' } | { s: 'unreachable' } | { s: 'no-docs-route' } | { s: 'unexpected-response'; status: number; contentType: string }`, keyed `project + NUL + (docsRefText(ref) or '')`; `DocsLoaders` = `{ projects(): Promise<DocsIndexAnswer>; tree(project: string, ref: DocsRefSpec | null): Promise<DocsTreeAnswer>; file(project: string, pin: DocPin, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<DocsFileAnswer>; raster(project: string, pin: DocPin, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<DocsRasterAnswer>; refresh(project: string, body: { ref: string | null; reason: 'auto' | 'manual' }): Promise<DocsRefreshAnswer> }`; `DocsScreen(p: { path: string; search: string; loaders?: DocsLoaders; parser?: MarkdownParser }): ReactNode`, defaults module-scope constants (`DEFAULT_DOCS_LOADERS = api.docs`, `parser = docsRunner.parse`). Re-fetch triggers: mount; a refresh answer; `draft-changed`, `worktree-moved`, `worktree-gone` or `unknown-commit` from a file read (once automatically, then an inline "changing, Retry"); `visibilitychange` to visible with the slot older than `DOCS_STALE_MS` (a GET, never a refresh); `onAuthRegained` for slots in `auth`. Auto-refresh: when a tree slot becomes `ok` with `refreshDue` true and its key is not in `autoRefreshed` (a `Set` in a `useRef`, checked and added synchronously before the POST), add it, then `POST refresh {ref: docsRefText(page.ref) or null, reason: 'auto'}`; an `unresolved-ref` page offers a manual **Fetch from origin** (`reason: 'manual'`). On the answer: an ok `tree` replaces the slot; a `fetch` failure changes only the chip; a `tree` failure keeps the old listing and shows "re-list failed: <sentence>" in the chip; a changed leaf pin re-reads, keeping scroll, with "Updated to <short commit>".
  - Truth line (§4.5): served ref `origin/<b>` or `<b> (local)` with the full refname in `title`; commit = first 8 hex, mono, full id in `title` and in "copy commit"; `VIA_SENTENCE`: `default:origin-head` "default branch (origin/HEAD)"; `default:origin-main` "default branch (origin/main; origin/HEAD unset)"; `default:origin-master` "default branch (origin/master; origin/HEAD unset)"; `default:local-main` "default branch (local main; no origin branch)"; `default:local-master` "default branch (local master; no origin branch)"; `local` "you asked for <requested>, showing local"; `origin` "you asked for <requested>, showing origin's"; `qualified` "exactly the ref you asked for". `RELATION_SENTENCE`: `equal` "local and origin agree"; `local-only` "not on origin"; `origin-only` "only on origin"; `local-ahead` "local is {ahead} ahead of origin"; `local-behind` "origin is {behind} ahead of local"; `diverged` "local and origin have diverged ({ahead} vs {behind}), showing local" (warn tone); `unmeasured` "local vs origin not measured". A dangling `origin/HEAD` in `tried[0]` adds "origin/HEAD points at a missing branch". Source: `committed`, `committed (view=committed)` or `draft · <state> in <worktree label>`; worktree label "main checkout", "workspace <last segment>" or the last two segments, full path in `title`.
  - Freshness chip (`.docs-fresh`, a `<button>`; age = `attemptAgeMs + (now - receivedAt)`, `now` from `useNow(30_000)`, formatted by `formatAge` in seconds): `remote === null` → `none` "no origin" (static); `stamp === null` → `never` "never fetched ↻"; `lastOutcome === 'ok'` → `ok` "fetched {age} ↻"; `remote-branch-absent` → `local` "local only ↻"; any other outcome → `failed` "fetch failed {age}: {sentence} · last good {okAge or never} ↻"; in flight → `fetching` "fetching…"; answered `fetch-too-soon` → `soon` "fetched moments ago; again in {n}s", one auto-retry at `retryAfterMs`; answered `ref-locked` with `lockAgeMs >= 60 000` → `failed` "stale lock on {ref}", no auto-retry; answered `skipped: local-ref` → `local` "local ref; fetch does not change it".
  - Banners (§4.5's table, verbatim): the default-view hint "{n} uncommitted doc{s} in {worktree label} on {drafts.branch}" · **Open the draft view** linking `ref = refs/heads/<drafts.branch>`; the ref-view base hint "{n} uncommitted doc{s} in {worktree label} are based on local {branch} at {short head}; this page shows {served}" · **Open the local view**; `ambiguous` "Two or more worktrees hold {branch}, so drafts are not shown:" + candidates; `untrusted` "The worktree holding {branch} failed the ownership check ({why}); drafts are not shown."; `unreadable` "Drafts could not be read ({step}); showing committed only."; `unsettled` "The worktree changed while Docs read it; showing committed only." · Retry; `too-many` "{count} uncommitted files is over the limit; showing committed only."; `none` with `skipped` "{k} worktree records for {branch} were skipped ({why list})."; caveats "Some drafts were found by content hash." / "Clean/smudge filters were bypassed; drafts show raw working-tree bytes."; withheld `WITHHELD_SENTENCE[reason]` + "Showing the committed version."; "Deleted in {label} (uncommitted)." / "Its type changed in {label}; the draft is not read." + "Showing the committed version."; "Contains unresolved merge-conflict markers."; `onRef === 'not-contained'` "Commit {short} is no longer on {served} (the branch was rewritten)." · Re-list; "This draft page embeds {k} uncommitted asset{s}."; `view=committed` "Showing the committed version at {short}." · **Back to the draft**.
  - Failures (§4.7): `DOCS_FAILURE_SENTENCE: Record<DocsFailure, string>` with every value at least 20 characters, the spec's seven examples verbatim (`unknown-project` "There is no project by that name under the fleet box's projects folder ({root})."; `too-large` "This file is {size}; Docs shows files of this kind up to {cap}."; `helper-unavailable` "The fleet box has no usable python3, which Docs needs; run ccrc doctor there."; `unsupported` "The fleet box's ccd predates Docs; roll out a newer release."; `not-granted` "The fleet agent has not loaded the Docs grants yet. If a rollout is running this clears when it finishes; otherwise update the fleet box."; `foreign-request` "The server refused a request that did not come from the Docs screen."; `raster-mismatch` "These bytes are not a {declared} image."); an unknown word "The server answered '{word}', which this app version does not know; reload to update."; the slots `auth` "Sign in to read Docs.", `unreachable` "The server could not be reached; Docs needs a connection." with Retry, `no-docs-route` "This server predates Docs; update the server box.", `unexpected-response` "The server answered {status} ({contentType})."; retry from L0 `DOCS_FAILURE_RETRY` (`auto` once after `retryAfterMs`, 3 s for a young `ref-locked`, or 5 s for `caps-unknown`, then Retry; `manual` Retry; `none` nothing). Placement: a tree failure replaces the listing and keeps the crumbs; a file failure replaces the body and keeps the header and truth line; a fetch failure appears only in the chip; an image failure is a per-image chip.
  - DocMarkdown (§4.10), verbatim: the gate "This document is {MiB}. Formatting it may take a while." with **Format anyway** (30 s budget) and **Show as text**, the parser not called until a choice; `worker-unavailable` with size at most `CHAT_SYNC_MAX_BYTES` parses on the main thread, above it plain text with its own note; notes: refused "Line {line} nests {value} levels deep (limit 32); shown as plain text." (and the delimiter-run equivalent), `too-wide` "This document would draw {elements} elements (limit 20 000); shown as plain text.", `threw` "could not be formatted ({error})", `timeout` "Formatting took longer than {s} s" with **Format anyway** (only after the normal budget), `worker-failed` with **Retry**; the doc-body boundary's fallback `DocPlain` "This document could not be displayed; shown as plain text."; a `.md` that arrived as base64 is formatted when its bytes are strict UTF-8, and only bytes that are not valid UTF-8 decode through a non-fatal `TextDecoder('utf-8')` and show as plain text: "Not valid UTF-8." (refinement (x), a deviation from §4.10 step 6's text)
  - Links and images (§4.11): no URL-bearing attribute reaches the DOM except through `DocLink` and `DocImage`; `DocLink`'s `doc` arm builds `href` with `docsPageUrl` (same project, the page's `ref`, `view` dropped), a plain left click navigates in-app, modifier and middle clicks are the browser's; `fragment` scrolls the matching element inside the article, found by comparing ids as strings so no selector is built from document text (Task 6 Decision 5; coordinator ruling R3, a refinement of §4.11's `CSS.escape`), no history entry; `external` gets `target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"` and opens with `openExternal` on tap only; `repo` is a GitHub link through `githubBlobUrl` with a trailing "↗ GitHub" mark, else inert; everything else `<span className="doc-link-inert" title="<sentence>: <raw>">` with no `href`. `DocImage` follows the pin rule through `imagePinFor`, defers the image at or past index 30 behind **Load image**, loads through the per-screen queue, turns a raster into an object URL through `rasterObjectUrl` (revoked on unmount or replacement) and an SVG into `data:image/svg+xml;base64,...` (never `blob:`), renders `<button className="doc-img-link"><img src alt className="msg-img" /></button>` whose tap opens the image's own leaf in-app, and refuses with `<span className="doc-img-refused" role="img" aria-label={alt}>` "Image not loaded: {reason}".

The coordinator asks whether #346 lands before part 1 and re-measures part 1's anchors on it at dispatch.

Routing: Opus main loop, `sonnet` implementers, an `opus` per-task reviewer, the whole-branch panel on `opus` (Task 13), every subagent's `model` passed explicitly (never inherited, never Fable), workflows off. Subagent prompts forbid mail, `pkill`/`killall` and any pattern kill (kill only recorded PIDs), and approval-prompting shell forms.
- The worker acks, runs the tasks with native subagents, puts questions to the operator as structured asks, and lists mail before its wave-done. Task 13 is the held-out whole-branch review and its fix wave: it runs after the last implementation task (Task 12) and BEFORE the close. Task 14 closes: the suites, the invariants, the build gate and the whole mutation table; it appends `## Wave 5 part 1 results` (that commit is the `handoffCommit` and the tip), pushes the workspace branch, opens the wave's ONE pull request, measures the fingerprint with that PR's number and `prPhase: 'open'`, and sends the wave-done. Part 1 edits `pwa/package.json`, the lock, `pwa/tsconfig.json`, a vitest config and `.github/`, so its PR runs the FULL server suite by design.

Copy the wave-done and the review report into `.superpowers/` on receipt. The coordinator rules; a fix round is a scoped re-review.
- Merge gate (§7.7's W5 row, §7.8): part 1 does NOT merge until **R1 and R2 are recorded as passing**: the operator runs W3's dark rollout (fleet first), then R2 (every remote class answers `fetch.state === 'ran'`) and R1 (p95 under docs load minus p95 idle at most 250 ms), and the coordinator appends their results to this plan's `## Wave 5 part 1 results` under `### Merge gate` in a docs-only commit on the branch before merging. An R1 failure fires `docs-chunked-reads` (a W3b run becomes a precondition of the merge). Also gating: the r10, r11 and 2-2 bounds in place with each value measured and stated here, and each case and row green (Task 14's table). The work proceeds while the gate waits; only the merge waits.
- After the merge, NOT in this wave: the merge becomes a prerelease (the `dev` channel). It is rolled out normally, fleet first (`ccrc rollout --to <tag>`, the coordinator's or the operator's act): part 1's L0 change is additive (no wire field, route or argv), so fleet first holds, and the Docs screen goes live with no Share or Export. Part 2 follows; W5b follows part 2 (RD23), rolled `--server-first` (A23). Retiring the standalone docs server follows W7.

## Review Focus

The five inputs a person using this will meet first, each pinned in the task that owns it:

1. **A repository document built to freeze or break the renderer.** A 32 KiB `ts` fence of one identifier, a code span of `a`, 80 000 spaces and `b`, four hundred 32-part chords, 10 000 nested `>`, 90 000 `hr`s, a 600 KiB doc, `<br>`, `<br/>`, `<br />`, `<br class=x>`, `<script>x</script>`, a `.md` that is not UTF-8, a renderer that throws. Each gives an unhighlighted block with its label, plain code, `too-wide` before any render, the gate, a real `br` only in the docs profile, literal text or `DocPlain` with the truth line intact; chat stays byte-identical. Pinned by T3 (r10, r11, 2-2), T4 (M9.1), T8 (M4.P1, P6, P7, P9, P12, B2).
2. **A link or image in a doc that points somewhere it must not.** `/api/example/x`, `//evil.example/x.png`, `https://evil.example/x.png`, `data:`, `blob:`, `javascript:`, a leading control character, a backslash form, `../../../../x.png`, an SVG carrying script, thirty-one images, a `.png` answered as `text/html` or holding GIF bytes, a docs raster `<img>`'d from another origin. Each gives an inert span, a refused image, an object URL or `data:` image of verified bytes, a deferred **Load image**, never a request to `/api/` from markup and never a running script. Pinned by T2 (M5.18), T6 (M4.U3, U4, U7), T7 (M4.U1, U2, U5, U6, M5.17, row 66), T9 (M5.20), T12 (M5.B5, M5.B6).
3. **A URL a person types, follows or shares into Docs.** `/docsearch`, `/docs/`, `?ref=a` then `?ref=b`, a pin key or a repeated key in the query, `%2F` in a segment, a directory without its slash, a linked worktree's project with a named, a null or no owner, a deep link while signed out, a session whose workspace was renamed. Each canonicalises by replace, renders its parse sentence, redirects without a history entry, re-fetches after sign-in, or links the branch the worktree holds now. Pinned by T5 (M4.F5), T9 (M4.R1, R2, R4, B1), T11 (M4.L1, L2).
4. **A server or fleet that answers something other than a page.** A pre-Docs 404, a proxy's HTML, `docs-busy`, `caps-unknown`, `ref-locked` at 5 s, at 120 s and with no measured age, `fetch-too-soon`, `unresolved-ref` with a tag hint, a word from a newer server, offline. Each gets its own sentence, its own retry class, and its own placement (listing, body, chip or image), never a folded word. Pinned by T2 (M4.F1, F2, F3, F6), T5 (M4.A1, A2, A3, rows 60, 61), T10 (M4.F4).
5. **Drafts and a branch that moves during the visit.** A dirty main checkout behind the default view, a ref view with `baseEqual` false and true, withheld, deleted, typechange and conflicted drafts, a drafted image on a committed page, a commit no longer on its branch, an auto-refresh that moves the leaf's pin. Each page says exactly what it served: the hint links `refs/heads/<b>`, the overlay appears only when the base is equal, the badge text is one function's, the commit never enters the URL, and the leaf re-reads with "Updated to <short>". Pinned by T5 (`pinFor`), T7 (row 66), T10 (M4.T1-T7, rows 54, 67).

## Spec refinements (decided while planning)

These refine the spec where it is silent, stale, or could be built two ways. Each is applied in the task named; W7's prose pass carries the spec text into line with them. Five of them, (a), (b), (c), (d) and (x), contradict the spec's TEXT rather than fill a silence: they are deviations, which Task 12's last step defines with issued numbers (Global Constraints, "Deviations"), and the text here is the rationale those entries carry.

- **(a) W5 is two sequential runs** (all tasks). §7.7 makes each wave "one run row, with one worker and one reviewer run". W5's row ships about twenty right-sized tasks (the L0 widening, the screen, the pipeline bounds, the link and image policy, the header, the doors and CSS, the browser leg, then Share, the export builder, its sheet, its scans, M5.B9 and its built-artefact tests), which does not fit one context with a held-out review and a close. Part 1 (this plan, run 413) ships the L0 widening, the Docs screen, `DocMarkdown` with the bounds, the docs `<br>`, the doors, `docs.css` and the browser leg with M5.B5 and M5.B6; part 2 (its own plan, run, PR and review, dispatched after part 1 merges) ships Share, Markdown/text/image Export, `ExportAssets`, the settled-outcome context, the Markdown CSS move and M5.B9. Three rows the spec amended in place split along the same line: M4.T7's base form (row and leaf badge equal, the scan over `pwa/src/docs`) is part 1's and its amended clause (share, provenance, export) part 2's; M4.S1's docs-chrome registrations are part 1's and its re-keying and Share/Export chrome part 2's; M5.17's `rasterObjectUrl`, `downloadDocFile` and `saveBytes` clauses are part 1's and its `downloadExport` clause part 2's. The gate splits by what each part ships: R1 and R2 gate part 1's merge (part 1 issues all of W5's docs traffic); §4.17's measurements, M5.B9 and the Export-time finding gate part 2's. **A deviation** from §7.7's wave preamble and W5 row: Task 12's last step defines it, and part 2 cites it.
- **(b) The `html` leaf is a stand-in until W6** (T9). §4.4 says class `html` "gives §5's `MockupView`", which is W6's. Part 1 renders the leaf's header and truth line, the sentence "HTML mockups open in a later release; Source shows the file and Download saves it.", the size, **Source** (the text renderer over `docs.file`) and **Download** (`downloadDocFile`); no iframe, no `srcDoc`, no frame. `?frame=full` renders the same stand-in. W6 replaces the stand-in with `MockupView` in `DocsLeaf.tsx`'s `html` arm, and part 2's Share notes it as source (`html-source`), with Export not offered for `html` in W5 (M4.SH8). **A deviation** from §4.4's leaf row: Task 12's last step defines it.
- **(c) A linked worktree with `branch: null` is not called detached** (T9). §4.7's sentence "that checkout is detached; showing <owner>'s default branch" asserts more than `null` means: the carried constraint (ledger, W2 adapter) is that `branch: null` covers both a detached HEAD and an unmeasured read. The page says "That checkout is not on a named branch, or its branch could not be read; showing <owner>'s default branch." and redirects to the owner's default view (`ref: null`) as §4.7 says. Goal 4 ("a page says exactly what it served") outranks the quoted sentence. **A deviation** from §4.7's redirect sentence: Task 12's last step defines it.
- **(d) The 2-2 bound is the parse's own element count** (T3). §4.10 and the coordinator's ruling put all three bounds "in the shared Markdown components". 2-2 is a count problem: `measure` counts an inline `code` as one element while the chip component draws up to `2 x parts` more, so `DOCS_MAX_RENDER_ELEMENTS` does not bound the DOM. A budget kept inside the components would be render-time mutable state (StrictMode's double render and React's render order would make it nondeterministic) and would cut a document mid-render. Part 1 instead makes `markdownParse.ts`'s `measure` add, for every inline `code` element (not under `pre`), `inlineCodeExtraElements` of its text: exactly what the component draws (2N-1 for a chord of N parts, beyond the one `code` the walk already counts; 0 for a span that is not a chord), through the one `keystrokeParts`, now in `markdownGuard.ts`, which both `markdownParse.ts` and `markdown.tsx` already import, so the count and the component answer through one predicate and no import or file joins the worker closure. It is not an upper bound: the upper bound first planned (`2 x (its '+' count) + 1` for every short span) pushed four real documents under `docs/superpowers` over `DOCS_MAX_RENDER_ELEMENTS` (Task 3 Step 0), and the exact count moves none. So `too-wide` fires before anything renders, in the worker, for docs, chat's worker path and Export alike; chat's synchronous path (at most 4 096 bytes) is bounded by its size. The components keep r11's length bound (refinement (f)), which also caps one span at 32 parts. **A deviation** from §4.10's "in the shared Markdown components" (the bound is in the parse's count, which the components' output is measured by): Task 12's last step defines it.
- **(e) r10's bound: no highlighting for a block holding a word longer than 256 characters** (T3). `MD_HIGHLIGHT_MAX_WORD_CHARS = 256` in `lib/markdownLimits.ts`; `CodeBlock` scans `raw` once, linearly, for its longest run of `[A-Za-z0-9_$]` and does not call `hljs.highlight` when it exceeds the limit, labelling the block `{label} · not highlighted (a {n}-character word)`. Measured at planning (Node v24.14.1, highlight.js 11.11.1, load average about 50, `hljs.highlight(..., {ignoreIllegals: true})`): one identifier run in `typescript` costs 21, 11, 146 and 2 291 ms at 256, 1 024, 4 096 and 16 384 characters (quadratic: the spec's 32 KiB ≈ 12 s); `javascript` 1 385 ms, `rust` 497 ms and `bash` 516 ms at 16 384, every other registered grammar under 30 ms; in `bash` a 16 384 run of digits, of `_` or of hex is just as slow (all inside the class), while runs of `.`, `-`, spaces and strings stay under 160 ms. 64 KiB filled with runs of 128, 256, 512 and 1 024 characters costs 60, 131, 268 and 749 ms in `typescript`, against 139 ms for 64 KiB of ordinary code. **Basis:** at 256 a block's worst case equals ordinary code of the same size, so `DOCS_HIGHLIGHT_PAGE_MAX_CHARS` keeps bounding the page as §4.9 states. Task 3 Step 0 re-measures on the base's versions and measures the real corpus' longest word in a registered-language fence (every `.md` under `docs/superpowers/**` and W4's chat corpus), which must be under 256, or Task 3 stops and asks.
- **(f) r11's bound: a code span longer than 64 characters is never a chord** (T3). `MD_KEYSTROKE_MAX_CHARS = 64` in `lib/markdownLimits.ts`; `keystrokeParts` returns `null` for a longer `raw` BEFORE it trims or splits, and the module-private `KEYSTROKE_MAX_PARTS` (2 048) goes (a 64-character span has at most 32 parts). Measured at planning: `'a' + ' '.repeat(L) + 'b'` through `trim().split(/\s*\+\s*/)` costs 0.09, 0.84, 16, 396 and 3 854 ms at L = 64, 1 024, 4 096, 16 384 and 40 000. **Basis:** the longest chord the grammar admits from named keys is about 40 characters (`Ctrl + Shift + Alt + Option + PageDown`), and at 64 the split costs under 0.1 ms. Task 3 Step 0 measures the longest code span `keystrokeParts` accepts in the golden corpus and the docs corpus (must be at most 64).
- **(g) The 2-2 count is measured on real documents** (T3). Task 3 Step 0 runs `parseMarkdown(src, 'docs')` over every `.md` under `docs/superpowers/**` and the golden corpus before and after the count, and records the largest element count; no real document may cross `DOCS_MAX_RENDER_ELEMENTS`, or Task 3 stops and asks. The 2-2 case: 400 spans of a 31-`+` chord give `too-wide` with 25 601 elements (a tree of 401 before the count), and 300 such spans give a tree whose rendered DOM holds exactly the 19 201 counted elements (Task 3 Decision 2).
- **(h) The page highlight budget reaches `CodeBlock` through one context** (T6). `lib/markdown.tsx` declares `PreHighlightContext: React.Context<((pre: HastElement) => boolean) | null>` (null = no page budget, the chat case) and `SHARED_COMPONENTS.pre` reads it with the `node` it is passed, giving `CodeBlock` `highlight={false}` for a block the budget refused. `DocMarkdown` provides `(pre) => urls.get(pre)?.highlight !== false` from `detachUrls`' decisions. So `DOC_COMPONENTS` stays exactly `{...SHARED_COMPONENTS, a: DocLink, img: DocImage}` (§4.10), chat provides nothing and stays byte-identical, and part 2's static `pre` reads the same decisions.
- **(i) The docs `<br>` is exactly three spellings, in the docs profile only** (T4). `settleHast(tree, profile = 'chat')` gains its parameter (one-argument callers keep chat); in the docs profile a `raw` node whose whole value is `<br>`, `<br/>` or `<br />` (the regular expression `^<br(?: ?\/)?>$`, lower case only) becomes `{type: 'element', tagName: 'br', properties: {}, children: []}`; every other raw node, `<BR>`, `<br class=x>`, `<br onclick=x>` and a block-level raw node that holds more than the tag, stays text. No package and no import is added to the worker closure (no `rehype-raw`). W4's profile-equality case becomes "equal, except on inputs that hold `<br>`, which differ only by `br` elements in the docs profile" (A16).
- **(j) The hook's commit-to-effect window is closed** (T4). `useParsedMarkdown` sets `jobs.latest` in a layout effect, so a reply for an earlier text that settles after a commit can no longer show under the newer text; `pending` keeps its meaning. Residue R5's measured example (the reply for text A, resolved between text B's commit and its passive effect) is the red case.
- **(k) The docs answer is a union; `ApiError` carries the content type** (T2). `ApiError` gains `readonly contentType: string | null` (null = the response had no `content-type` header), set by `request`'s non-2xx branch; nothing else in `api.ts` changes. `api.docs.*` resolves `{s: 'ok', value}` or a failure arm: an `ApiError` whose body has a string `failure` is `{s: 'failed', body}` (unknown words kept whole); a 401 is `{s: 'auth'}` after `request` has raised the overlay; a 404 whose body is `{error: 'not-found'}` with no `failure` is `{s: 'no-docs-route'}` (the status AND the code); a `TypeError` from `fetch` is `{s: 'unreachable'}`; anything else, and a 200 that is not the expected envelope, is `{s: 'unexpected-response', status, contentType}` (`''` = no header). An abort rejects with the signal's `AbortError` (the caller aborted; no slot). `docs.raster` checks the content type against `DOCS_RASTER_TYPES` and then `sniffRaster`, answering `unexpected-response` or a client-built `{ok: false, failure: 'raster-mismatch', declared, size}`; `docs.file` throws `wrong-representation` for a raster path (a programming error, §5.4).
- **(l) Retry timing and the three lock ages** (T2, T5). `docs/failures.ts` declares the PWA's own waits from §4.7: `DOCS_REF_LOCKED_RETRY_MS = 3000`, `DOCS_LOCK_STALE_MS = 60000`, `DOCS_CAPS_UNKNOWN_RETRY_MS = 5000` (the server's `Retry-After` header never reaches the PWA: `ApiError` keeps no headers, and `caps-unknown` carries no wait in its body). `docsRetryPlan(body)` answers `{kind: 'auto', afterMs} | {kind: 'manual'} | {kind: 'none'}`: `auto` words wait `retryAfterMs` when present, else 5 000 for `caps-unknown`; `ref-locked` waits 3 000 when `lockAgeMs` is a number under 60 000 or `null` (the lock already gone), is `none` with "stale lock on {ref}" at 60 000 or more, and is `manual` when `lockAgeMs` is ABSENT (unmeasured; never folded into `null`).
- **(m) Auto-refresh never fires on a `refs/heads/` page** (T5). Besides `refreshDue`, `useDocsVisit` refuses an automatic POST when `page.ref` is a qualified `refs/heads/<b>` ref (§2 row 60's PWA half), so the property holds whatever the server says.
- **(n) `detachUrls` returns a copy** (T6). It copies the root and every element (text nodes shared), moves every `html-url-attributes` property of the copy into a `WeakMap<HastElement, DetachedUrls>`, numbers `img` elements in document order and records each `pre`'s highlight decision by summing `pre > code` text against `DOCS_HIGHLIGHT_PAGE_MAX_CHARS`; it never writes its input, so a kept outcome can be detached again (`useMemo` per outcome in `DocMarkdown`) and part 2's Export reuses the copy and its map.
- **(o) Fragments** (T6, T9). A same-doc `#id` scrolls inside the article. A cross-doc link's `href` carries `#fragment` after `docsPageUrl(...)` (so a new tab keeps it); its plain click navigates to the URL without it (`navigate`'s contract has no `#`) and hands the fragment to the visit, which scrolls to it once after the new body renders; a direct load's `location.hash` is honoured the same way once.
- **(p) Where unnamed units live** (T6-T9). `DocLink` and `DocLinkContext` in `docs/DocLink.tsx` (a file §4.1's table does not list); `DOC_COMPONENTS` in `docs/DocMarkdown.tsx`; `detachUrls`, `docLinkTarget`, `docsLocation`, `imagePinFor` and `sessionDocsHref` in `docs/docsLinks.ts`; `DocsAssetContext` (`{loaders, queue}`) in `docs/DocImage.tsx`, provided by `DocsScreen`; `DocsLoaders` and the answer unions in `docs/failures.ts`, imported by `api.ts`. `DocLinkContext` holds §4.11's fields `{project, pageRef, view, section, path, tree, pageSource}` plus the `urls` map and the fragment hand-off.
- **(q) One location builder** (T6, T9). Every page URL a view writes is `docsPageUrl(docsLocation(page, to))`, where `docsLocation` spreads the parsed page (keeping `project` and `ref`) and applies the target; no view builds a `DocsPageLocation` literal (W5b adds `at` in one place). Section labels are a `Record<DocSectionSlug, string>` and `SECTION_ORDER` a `Record<DocSectionSlug, 'newest-first' | 'alphabetical'>`, so a new slug is a compile error; the count string is built over `DOC_SECTION_SLUGS`.
- **(r) The index's extra fields** (T9). `unwalked` renders the footer "{n} projects not checked (Docs ran out of time listing them)."; rows sharing a `repoKey` (`duplicates`) say "same repository as {other}"; `cacheAgeMs` is not shown. Withheld counts: a project's section rows show "{n} drafts · {m} withheld" in a ref view; a directory row shows its entry's badge; a withheld leaf shows its banner (§2 row 54).
- **(s) Short commit is the first 8 hex characters everywhere** (`shortCommit` in `docsText.ts`).
- **(t) `saveBytes` and `copyText` arrive in part 1** (T7, T10). `saveBytes(name, bytes)` is `downloadDocFile`'s primitive (§5.4: "`downloadDocFile` uses it"), and `copyText(text)` in `docs/share.ts` is the truth line's "copy commit" writer, the one clipboard writer under `pwa/src/docs` (M4.SH7's allowance names that file); part 2 adds `downloadExport` beside `saveBytes` in `docs/objectUrls.ts` and `shareTargetFor` beside `copyText` in `docs/share.ts`.
- **(u) `docs.css`'s overflow pin sits in `shell-css.test.ts`** (T11), as §4.14 says: an appended describe reads `docs/docs.css` and the file's scope sentence is widened in place to name that one rule. `contrast.test.ts`'s sheet list grows from six to seven (`src/docs/docs.css`); part 2 makes it nine.
- **(v) The browser leg runs where the `test` legs run** (T12): every pull request, merge-queue run, daily run and `workflow_dispatch` full run, skipped by `CCRC_LEG` steps exactly as `test` and `build-pwa` are; it joins `full-suite.needs` and `RESULTS` and `ci-pipeline.test.ts`'s required-name and step-skip pins; it is not added to `ci-merge-queue.test.ts`'s roots. The harness exists without W6's artefacts: M5.B5 and M5.B6 need only `DOCS_RESPONSE_HEADERS` and fixture bytes. On the fleet box no `/usr/bin/google-chrome` exists (measured at planning), so local runs set `CCRC_CHROME` to a Chromium binary already on the box (Task 12 Step 0 finds one; it never installs a browser or a system package); if none exists, Task 12 asks the coordinator and CI is the leg's arbiter.
- **(w) Not in part 1** (pre-empting part 2, W5b, W6, W7 or W8): Share's sheet and `shareTargetFor`, every Export unit, `ExportAssets`, the settled-outcome context, `lib/markdown.css`, `?inline`, `react-dom/server`, the `docs-scans.test.ts` clauses M4.SH7, M4.EX2, M4.EX11 and M4.EX16, M5.B9; `vision`, `promise`, `docs-log`, `at=`; `MockupView`; README and CLAUDE.md; the shared Markdown library and the reader frame.
- **(x) A base64 `.md` is formatted when its bytes are strict UTF-8** (T8, T9). §4.10 step 6 says a `.md` that arrived as base64 "decodes through a non-fatal `TextDecoder('utf-8')` and shows as plain text: 'Not valid UTF-8.'". But ccd's encoding rule (§2 (f)'s "Encoding", as §6.1 restates it) also sends VALID UTF-8 as base64, when the text holds a NUL or when base64 frames shorter (a quote-heavy file), so the literal reading would label a valid file "Not valid UTF-8." and decline to format it. Part 1's `docMarkdownSource` decodes with `{fatal: true}` first: strict UTF-8 is Markdown, formatted like any other; only bytes that are not valid UTF-8 get the non-fatal decode (each bad sequence a U+FFFD) and show as `DocPlain` with "Not valid UTF-8.", which is the spec's behaviour for them. Goal 4 ("a page says exactly what it served") decides (coordinator ruling, 2026-10-13). The letter is the next free one, after (w); it is not refinement (e), which is r10's bound. **A deviation** from §4.10 step 6's text, the fifth: Task 12's last step defines it after (a)-(d).

### Task 1: L0 first: widen GithubTarget (repo, root) and GithubLink (bad-slug, bad-target); add GithubPermalink, githubPermalink and the private githubUrlAt; M3.11 amended, M3.16-M3.18, appended single-definition pin

One L0 file, pure functions, every row of two first-match-wins tables pinned by an oracle over the type's own unions, plus named cases for the rows off the oracle's axes; no React, no build, no package. The judgment is in the row ORDER (a refusal that must win over a later one), which the oracle and the named "ahead of" cases pin.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes, from `shared/docs.ts` at `BASE` (W1): `type DocsGithub = { state: 'named'; slug: string } | { state: 'none' }`; `DocsTreeOk['ref']` (`name`, `side: 'local' | 'origin'`, `commit`, `via`, `relation`); `type DocSectionSlug`; `DOC_SECTIONS`; `docRepoPath(section: DocSectionSlug, path: string): string` (validates nothing); `isDocsCommit(s: string): boolean` (40 or 64 lowercase hex; reused, never redeclared).
- Produces, exported from `shared/docs.ts`:
  - `export type GithubTarget = { kind: 'leaf'; section: DocSectionSlug; path: string; uncommitted: boolean } | { kind: 'section'; section: DocSectionSlug } | { kind: 'dir'; section: DocSectionSlug; path: string } | { kind: 'repo'; repoPath: string } | { kind: 'root' };` — `repoPath` is relative to the repository root (`resolveDocRef`'s `repo` kind); `root` is the repository itself (the project page). Only `leaf` carries `uncommitted`.
  - `export type GithubLink = { ok: true; url: string; note: 'may-differ' | null } | { ok: false; why: 'no-github-origin' | 'not-on-origin' | 'uncommitted' | 'bad-slug' | 'bad-target' };` — `note: null` has ONE meaning: GitHub's copy of the branch is this view's (the origin side is served, or the local side equals origin). `bad-slug` judges the slug; `bad-target` judges `ref.name` and the path.
  - `export type GithubPermalink = { ok: true; url: string; commit: string } | { ok: false; why: 'no-github-origin' | 'not-on-origin' | 'unmeasured' | 'uncommitted' | 'bad-slug' | 'bad-target' };` — no null. `commit` on the ok arm is the argument, verbatim (the full id). `bad-target` also covers a commit that is not 40 or 64 lowercase hex.
  - `export function githubBlobUrl(github: DocsGithub, ref: DocsTreeOk['ref'], target: GithubTarget): GithubLink` — signature unchanged; `at` = `ref.name` (branch URLs). Rows, first match wins: `no-github-origin`; `bad-slug`; `bad-target`; `not-on-origin` (`local-only`, `default:local-main`, `default:local-master`); `uncommitted` (a leaf); link with `note: null` (`side === 'origin'` or `relation === 'equal'`); link with `may-differ` (every other local side).
  - `export function githubPermalink(github: DocsGithub, ref: DocsTreeOk['ref'], commit: string, target: GithubTarget): GithubPermalink` — `at` = `commit`, always the full id, never `ref.name`. Rows, first match wins: `no-github-origin`; `bad-slug`; `bad-target` (commit grammar, or an empty, `.` or `..` segment); `not-on-origin` (`local-only` or a local default); `uncommitted` (a leaf); link (`side === 'origin'`, or `relation` `equal` or `local-behind`); `unmeasured` (`relation === 'unmeasured'`); `not-on-origin` for everything left (`local-ahead`, `diverged`, and the off-contract local side reading `origin-only`).
- Module-private in `shared/docs.ts` (not exported; Task 6's `DocLink` and part 2's Share reach them only through the two builders):
  - `function githubUrlAt(slug: string, at: string, target: GithubTarget): { ok: true; url: string } | { ok: false; why: 'bad-slug' | 'bad-target' }` — the file's ONE `'https://github.com/'` literal; `bad-slug` for a slug segment `.` or `..` or a slug starting with `.` (the owner); `bad-target` for an empty, `.` or `..` segment of `at` or of the repo path; `/blob/<at>/<repoPath>` for `leaf` and `repo`, `/tree/<at>/<repoPath>` for `section` and `dir`, `/tree/<at>` for `root`; every segment through `encodeURIComponent`; no fragment.
  - `function servedRefIsLocalOnly(ref: DocsTreeOk['ref']): boolean` — true for `relation === 'local-only'` or `via` `default:local-main`/`default:local-master`; both builders' `not-on-origin` row.

**Decisions this task makes (none departs from the spec's text):**
1. **M3.11's oracle grows by one origin and one target, not only by the two kinds.** The architecture's outline names the target factor going from 4 to 6 (`repo`, `root`); but the describe's first case checks that EVERY oracle row is reached by the product, and the new `bad-slug` and `bad-target` rows sit on axes the product did not have (its slug and `ref.name` were fixed and well formed). So the origin axis gains `dot-slug` (`example-org/..`) and the target axis gains `dotRepo` (`{kind: 'repo', repoPath: 'docs/../README.md'}`) as well: 3 origins x 2 sides x 7 relations x 8 vias x 7 targets = 2 352 cases (was 896). The two new rows are labelled `1a` and `1b`, so every existing row label, and every named case below them, is unchanged.
2. **The permalink oracle keeps the spec table's row numbers.** Its rows are `1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8` plus `9` (the off-contract local side reading `origin-only`, which no row of the table links, so the builder refuses it as `not-on-origin`, the cautious answer, as View on GitHub's builder lands it on `may-differ`). Rows 2 and 3 (`bad-slug`, `bad-target`) are reached by named cases, each also pinning that it wins over every later row.
3. **`githubUrlAt` runs before the ref rows, in both builders.** Its two refusals are table rows 2 and 3, ahead of `not-on-origin` and `uncommitted`, so each builder calls it right after the `no-github-origin` row and returns its refusal as is (its union is a subset of both answer types). The permalink's commit-grammar check comes after it; both are `bad-target`, so their mutual order changes no answer.
4. **A dot or empty segment anywhere in the URL is `bad-target`, including `ref.name` and a directory with an empty path.** `docRepoPath('conventions', '')` is `docs/conventions/`, whose last segment is empty, so a `dir` target with `path: ''` (which nothing builds: the section page uses the `section` kind) answers `bad-target` where it used to link a trailing slash. `GithubLink` has no consumer outside `shared/docs.ts` and its tests at `BASE` (measured: `grep -rn 'githubBlobUrl\|GithubLink' pwa/src server/src agent/src` prints nothing), so the widened union and this refusal move no caller.
5. **M3.17's literal pin is a text scan, and says it is not exhaustive** (lesson 8). It counts quoted `https://github.com/` (single, double or back quote) and every bare `github.com` in `shared/docs.ts`, comments included, and finds the one quoted literal inside `githubUrlAt`'s body. Its header lists what it cannot see: an address assembled from held-apart pieces, from character codes, or read from another module. The same describe's behavioural case (where both builders link, their URLs agree but for the `at` segment, over 240 pairs) is what catches a second assembler that the scan misses. The docstrings this task writes therefore never spell the host: they say "GitHub's address".
6. **The single-definition append's CONTROL plants a third file in memory** (a `[path, text]` pair passed to the holder function), never on disk, so no fixture file joins the roots and no cleanup is needed. The docs section H block's `TYPES`/`FUNCTIONS` lists above it are not edited.
7. **`servedRefIsLocalOnly` is a private helper both builders call**, so the `not-on-origin` row has one spelling; it is not pinned by the appended describe (it is private, and its body is the spec's row), and its two call sites each carry a mutation row (W5P1-T1-M12 for the permalink, W5P1-T1-M13 for View on GitHub's row order).

- [ ] **Step 2: Write M3.16, M3.17 and M3.18.** Append exactly this block to the end of `server/test/docs-shared.test.ts` (the file ends with `});` and a newline; the block starts with an empty line). It uses the file's top-level `DOCS` (the path of `shared/docs.ts`) and `readFileSync`; every fixture is a placeholder (`example-org/example-repo`, `ws/a b`, `main`, `e` x 40), and no line holds a non-ASCII character or a `\u` escape.

```ts

// ---- Section H, W5 part 1 Task 1: githubPermalink, the one assembler, and the repo and root targets ------------
// Spec 2026-10-01 3.11 as amended 2026-10-13 (Share and Export): M3.16, M3.17 and M3.18. M3.11's widened oracle is
// in the githubBlobUrl describe above. APPENDED after the file's last line. One namespace import, so no binding
// here can collide with a name an earlier block imported.
import * as docsP from '../../shared/docs.js';

describe('docs section H, W5: githubPermalink, the one assembler, and the repo and root targets', () => {
  type Ref = docsP.DocsTreeOk['ref'];
  type Target = docsP.GithubTarget;
  const SIDE_KEYS: Record<Ref['side'], true> = { local: true, origin: true };
  const RELATION_KEYS: Record<Ref['relation'], true> = {
    equal: true, 'local-only': true, 'origin-only': true, 'local-ahead': true, 'local-behind': true,
    diverged: true, unmeasured: true,
  };
  const VIA_KEYS: Record<Ref['via'], true> = {
    'default:origin-head': true, 'default:origin-main': true, 'default:origin-master': true,
    'default:local-main': true, 'default:local-master': true, local: true, origin: true, qualified: true,
  };
  // The target kinds as a Record over the type's own union: a kind added to GithubTarget without a row here is a
  // compile error (typecheck-tests), and the first case below checks that TARGETS reaches every kind.
  const KIND_KEYS: Record<Target['kind'], true> = { leaf: true, section: true, dir: true, repo: true, root: true };
  const SIDES = Object.keys(SIDE_KEYS) as Ref['side'][];
  const RELATIONS = Object.keys(RELATION_KEYS) as Ref['relation'][];
  const VIAS = Object.keys(VIA_KEYS) as Ref['via'][];
  const NAMED: docsP.DocsGithub = { state: 'named', slug: 'example-org/example-repo' };
  const NONE: docsP.DocsGithub = { state: 'none' };
  const named = (slug: string): docsP.DocsGithub => ({ state: 'named', slug });
  // The commit the page opened. It is neither ref.commit ('c' x 40) nor ref.name, so a builder that wrote either
  // instead of its argument is seen.
  const COMMIT = 'e'.repeat(40);
  const refOf = (side: Ref['side'], relation: Ref['relation'], via: Ref['via'], name = 'ws/a b'): Ref => ({
    requested: null, served: (side === 'local' ? 'refs/heads/' : 'refs/remotes/origin/') + name, name, side,
    commit: 'c'.repeat(40), via, tried: [], relation, counterpart: null,
  });
  const ORIGIN_EQUAL = refOf('origin', 'equal', 'origin');
  const TARGETS = {
    leaf: { kind: 'leaf', section: 'plans', path: 'sub dir/x y.md', uncommitted: false },
    newLeaf: { kind: 'leaf', section: 'plans', path: 'sub dir/x y.md', uncommitted: true },
    section: { kind: 'section', section: 'plans' },
    dir: { kind: 'dir', section: 'plans', path: 'sub dir' },
    repo: { kind: 'repo', repoPath: 'README.md' },
    root: { kind: 'root' },
  } as const satisfies Record<string, Target>;
  type TargetName = keyof typeof TARGETS;
  const TARGET_NAMES = Object.keys(TARGETS) as TargetName[];
  const GH = 'https://github.com/example-org/example-repo';
  // Hand-written; never built by the code under test. `newLeaf` never reaches a link (row 5 refuses it first).
  const PERMALINK_OF: Record<Exclude<TargetName, 'newLeaf'>, string> = {
    leaf: `${GH}/blob/${COMMIT}/docs/superpowers/plans/sub%20dir/x%20y.md`,
    section: `${GH}/tree/${COMMIT}/docs/superpowers/plans`,
    dir: `${GH}/tree/${COMMIT}/docs/superpowers/plans/sub%20dir`,
    repo: `${GH}/blob/${COMMIT}/README.md`,
    root: `${GH}/tree/${COMMIT}`,
  };
  const canon = (o: object): string => JSON.stringify(Object.entries(o).sort(([a], [b]) => (a < b ? -1 : 1)));

  describe('githubPermalink (M3.16)', () => {
    interface PermaCase {
      github: 'named' | 'none'; side: Ref['side']; relation: Ref['relation']; via: Ref['via']; target: TargetName;
    }
    const permalinkFor = (c: PermaCase): string => (c.target === 'newLeaf' ? 'unreachable' : PERMALINK_OF[c.target]);
    // THE ORACLE: spec 3.11's permalink table, in its order, the first match winning, numbered as the table's
    // rows. Rows 2 (bad-slug) and 3 (bad-target) are off this product's axes (its slug and commit are well
    // formed); the named cases below reach them. One row the table leaves out: a local side reading `origin-only`
    // cannot arrive, and no row of the table links it, so the builder refuses it as not-on-origin.
    type PermaRow = { row: string; when: (c: PermaCase) => boolean; want: (c: PermaCase) => docsP.GithubPermalink };
    const PERMA_ROWS: readonly PermaRow[] = [
      { row: '1 no github origin', when: (c) => c.github === 'none', want: () => ({ ok: false, why: 'no-github-origin' }) },
      {
        row: '4 local-only, or a local default',
        when: (c) => c.relation === 'local-only' || c.via === 'default:local-main' || c.via === 'default:local-master',
        want: () => ({ ok: false, why: 'not-on-origin' }),
      },
      { row: '5 a new draft leaf', when: (c) => c.target === 'newLeaf', want: () => ({ ok: false, why: 'uncommitted' }) },
      {
        row: '6 origin side, or equal, or local-behind',
        when: (c) => c.side === 'origin' || c.relation === 'equal' || c.relation === 'local-behind',
        want: (c) => ({ ok: true, url: permalinkFor(c), commit: COMMIT }),
      },
      {
        row: '7 local side, ahead or diverged',
        when: (c) => c.side === 'local' && (c.relation === 'local-ahead' || c.relation === 'diverged'),
        want: () => ({ ok: false, why: 'not-on-origin' }),
      },
      { row: '8 unmeasured', when: (c) => c.relation === 'unmeasured', want: () => ({ ok: false, why: 'unmeasured' }) },
      {
        row: '9 local side reading origin-only (off-contract)',
        when: (c) => c.side === 'local' && c.relation === 'origin-only',
        want: () => ({ ok: false, why: 'not-on-origin' }),
      },
    ];
    const PERMA_CASES: PermaCase[] = [];
    for (const github of ['named', 'none'] as const) for (const side of SIDES) for (const relation of RELATIONS) {
      for (const via of VIAS) for (const target of TARGET_NAMES) PERMA_CASES.push({ github, side, relation, via, target });
    }
    const permaOf = (c: PermaCase): docsP.GithubPermalink =>
      docsP.githubPermalink(c.github === 'named' ? NAMED : NONE, refOf(c.side, c.relation, c.via), COMMIT, TARGETS[c.target]);

    it('the table covers 2 origins x 2 sides x 7 relations x 8 vias x 6 targets (every kind), and every oracle row is reached', () => {
      expect(PERMA_CASES.length).toBe(2 * 2 * 7 * 8 * 6);
      expect([...new Set(Object.values(TARGETS).map((t) => t.kind))].sort()).toEqual(Object.keys(KIND_KEYS).sort());
      const reached = new Set(PERMA_CASES.map((c) => PERMA_ROWS.find((r) => r.when(c))?.row ?? 'no row'));
      expect([...reached].sort()).toEqual(PERMA_ROWS.map((r) => r.row).sort());
    });

    it('githubPermalink equals the oracle on every case', () => {
      const wrong: string[] = [];
      for (const c of PERMA_CASES) {
        const row = PERMA_ROWS.find((r) => r.when(c));
        const want = row === undefined ? null : row.want(c);
        const got = permaOf(c);
        if (want === null || canon(got) !== canon(want)) {
          wrong.push(`${JSON.stringify(c)} [${row?.row ?? 'no row'}]: got ${JSON.stringify(got)}, want ${JSON.stringify(want)}`);
        }
      }
      expect(wrong.slice(0, 10)).toEqual([]);
      expect(wrong.length).toBe(0);
    });

    it('every link names the full commit it was given, never ref.name and never the served commit', () => {
      let links = 0;
      for (const c of PERMA_CASES) {
        const got = permaOf(c);
        if (!got.ok) continue;
        links += 1;
        expect(got.commit, JSON.stringify(c)).toBe(COMMIT);
        expect(got.url.includes(`/${COMMIT}`), JSON.stringify(c)).toBe(true);
        expect(got.url.includes('ws/a%20b') || got.url.includes('c'.repeat(40)), JSON.stringify(c)).toBe(false);
      }
      expect(links).toBe(6 * (6 + 2) * 5);
      const sha256 = 'e'.repeat(64);
      expect(docsP.githubPermalink(NAMED, ORIGIN_EQUAL, sha256, TARGETS.repo))
        .toEqual({ ok: true, url: `${GH}/blob/${sha256}/README.md`, commit: sha256 });
    });

    it('local-ahead and diverged give not-on-origin and unmeasured gives unmeasured, where View on GitHub links all three (decision 10)', () => {
      for (const relation of ['local-ahead', 'diverged'] as const) {
        const ref = refOf('local', relation, 'local');
        expect(docsP.githubPermalink(NAMED, ref, COMMIT, TARGETS.leaf), relation).toEqual({ ok: false, why: 'not-on-origin' });
        expect(docsP.githubBlobUrl(NAMED, ref, TARGETS.leaf), relation).toMatchObject({ ok: true, note: 'may-differ' });
      }
      const unmeasured = refOf('local', 'unmeasured', 'qualified');
      expect(docsP.githubPermalink(NAMED, unmeasured, COMMIT, TARGETS.leaf)).toEqual({ ok: false, why: 'unmeasured' });
      expect(docsP.githubBlobUrl(NAMED, unmeasured, TARGETS.leaf)).toMatchObject({ ok: true, note: 'may-differ' });
    });

    it('an origin side links whatever the relation, origin-only included; a local side links when equal or behind', () => {
      for (const relation of ['origin-only', 'local-ahead', 'local-behind', 'diverged', 'unmeasured', 'equal'] as const) {
        expect(docsP.githubPermalink(NAMED, refOf('origin', relation, 'default:origin-head'), COMMIT, TARGETS.dir), relation)
          .toEqual({ ok: true, url: PERMALINK_OF.dir, commit: COMMIT });
      }
      for (const relation of ['equal', 'local-behind'] as const) {
        expect(docsP.githubPermalink(NAMED, refOf('local', relation, 'local'), COMMIT, TARGETS.section), relation)
          .toEqual({ ok: true, url: PERMALINK_OF.section, commit: COMMIT });
      }
    });

    it('the slugs ../x, .x/y, a/.., ./x, a/. and .. give bad-slug in both builders, ahead of every later row; org/.github links', () => {
      for (const slug of ['../x', '.x/y', 'a/..', './x', 'a/.', '..']) {
        expect(docsP.githubPermalink(named(slug), ORIGIN_EQUAL, COMMIT, TARGETS.leaf), slug).toEqual({ ok: false, why: 'bad-slug' });
```

```ts
/** What a "View on GitHub" action points at. A leaf's `uncommitted` is true when the entry has no committed side
 *  (`e.committed === null`): GitHub holds no copy of it, whether or not the draft opens (a withheld new file has
 *  `opens: 'none'` and is still uncommitted). A directory's `path` is relative to its section, like a leaf's. */
export type GithubTarget =
  | { kind: 'leaf'; section: DocSectionSlug; path: string; uncommitted: boolean }
  | { kind: 'section'; section: DocSectionSlug }
  | { kind: 'dir'; section: DocSectionSlug; path: string };

/** A link, with the caution `may-differ` ("GitHub's copy may differ from this view") or none; or the reason
 *  there is no link. `not-on-origin` is the PWA's "not pushed". */
export type GithubLink =
  | { ok: true; url: string; note: 'may-differ' | null }
  | { ok: false; why: 'no-github-origin' | 'not-on-origin' | 'uncommitted' };

/** The View on GitHub builder (spec 3.11). The rows are checked in the spec table's order, the first match
 *  winning:
 *   1. no GitHub-shaped origin was read: `no-github-origin`;
 *   2. a `local-only` relation, or a default resolved to a local branch (`default:local-main`,
 *      `default:local-master`): `not-on-origin`;
 *   3. a leaf whose entry has no committed side (`uncommitted`, i.e. `e.committed === null`, whether or not the
 *      draft opens): `uncommitted`;
 *   4. the origin side is served, or the local side equals origin: a link with no note;
 *   5. otherwise (the local side ahead, behind, diverged or unmeasured): a link with `may-differ`. A local side
 *      reading `origin-only` cannot arrive, because a local side means the local branch exists; if it did, it
 *      would land here, on the cautious answer.
 *  The URL names the branch, never a commit (the durable-link convention):
 *  `https://github.com/<slug>/blob/<ref.name>/<repo path>` for a leaf, and `/tree/` for a section or directory.
 *  Each `/`-separated segment of the slug, the branch name and the repo path is `encodeURIComponent`-encoded on
 *  its own, so the branch `ws/a b` keeps its `/` and is written `ws/a%20b`. */
export function githubBlobUrl(github: DocsGithub, ref: DocsTreeOk['ref'], target: GithubTarget): GithubLink {
  if (github.state === 'none') return { ok: false, why: 'no-github-origin' };
  if (ref.relation === 'local-only' || ref.via === 'default:local-main' || ref.via === 'default:local-master') {
    return { ok: false, why: 'not-on-origin' };
  }
  if (target.kind === 'leaf' && target.uncommitted) return { ok: false, why: 'uncommitted' };
  const segments = (p: string): string => p.split('/').map((s) => encodeURIComponent(s)).join('/');
  const repoPath = target.kind === 'section' ? DOC_SECTIONS[target.section] : docRepoPath(target.section, target.path);
  const url = 'https://github.com/' + segments(github.slug) + (target.kind === 'leaf' ? '/blob/' : '/tree/')
    + segments(ref.name) + '/' + segments(repoPath);
  return { ok: true, url, note: ref.side === 'origin' || ref.relation === 'equal' ? null : 'may-differ' };
}
```

Replace with:
```ts
/** What a "View on GitHub" action or a permalink points at. A leaf's `uncommitted` is true when the entry has no
 *  committed side (`e.committed === null`): GitHub holds no copy of it, whether or not the draft opens (a withheld
 *  new file has `opens: 'none'` and is still uncommitted). A directory's `path` is relative to its section, like a
 *  leaf's. `repo` is resolveDocRef's in-repo, out-of-section kind (spec 4.11), its `repoPath` relative to the
 *  repository root; `root` is the repository itself, for the project page. Neither has an uncommitted form. */
export type GithubTarget =
  | { kind: 'leaf'; section: DocSectionSlug; path: string; uncommitted: boolean }
  | { kind: 'section'; section: DocSectionSlug }
  | { kind: 'dir'; section: DocSectionSlug; path: string }
  | { kind: 'repo'; repoPath: string }
  | { kind: 'root' };

/** A View on GitHub link, or the reason there is none. `note` is `'may-differ'` ("GitHub's copy may differ from
 *  this view") or `null`, which means one thing: GitHub's copy of the branch is this view's (the origin side is
 *  served, or the local side equals origin). `not-on-origin` is the PWA's "not pushed". `bad-slug` judges the
 *  slug; `bad-target` judges the branch name and the path, which come from the page, so a caller can tell the
 *  two apart. */
export type GithubLink =
  | { ok: true; url: string; note: 'may-differ' | null }
  | { ok: false; why: 'no-github-origin' | 'not-on-origin' | 'uncommitted' | 'bad-slug' | 'bad-target' };

/** A commit permalink (spec 3.11; Share's link), naming the full commit it was given, or the reason there is none.
 *  `not-on-origin` covers a ref never pushed and a local side ahead of origin or diverged from it (decision 10: the
 *  commit may not be on GitHub, so the link would open a 404); `unmeasured` is a local side whose relation to
 *  origin was not measured; `bad-target` also covers a commit that is not 40 or 64 lowercase hex. */
export type GithubPermalink =
  | { ok: true; url: string; commit: string }
  | { ok: false; why: 'no-github-origin' | 'not-on-origin' | 'unmeasured' | 'uncommitted' | 'bad-slug' | 'bad-target' };

/** True when the served ref is not on origin: a `local-only` relation, or a default resolved to a local branch
 *  (`default:local-main`, `default:local-master`). Both builders answer it `not-on-origin`. */
function servedRefIsLocalOnly(ref: DocsTreeOk['ref']): boolean {
  return ref.relation === 'local-only' || ref.via === 'default:local-main' || ref.via === 'default:local-master';
}

/** THE one assembler of a GitHub URL (spec 3.11, "One assembler"): private, called by both builders, and the only
 *  place this file spells GitHub's address. It refuses, in this order:
 *   1. a slug segment that is `.` or `..`, or an owner (the first segment) that starts with `.`: `bad-slug`. A
 *      repository name may start with a dot, so `org/.github` passes;
 *   2. a segment of `at` or of the repo path that is empty, `.` or `..`: `bad-target`. encodeURIComponent leaves
 *      `.` and `..` as they are, and a browser would resolve such a URL to another page.
 *  Otherwise the URL is `/blob/<at>/<repo path>` for a leaf or a `repo` target, `/tree/<at>/<repo path>` for a
 *  section or a directory, and `/tree/<at>` for `root`, after the slug. Each `/`-separated segment of the slug, of
 *  `at` and of the repo path is encodeURIComponent-encoded on its own, so the branch `ws/a b` keeps its `/` and is
 *  written `ws/a%20b`. No fragment is ever written. */
function githubUrlAt(slug: string, at: string, target: GithubTarget):
  { ok: true; url: string } | { ok: false; why: 'bad-slug' | 'bad-target' } {
  const slugParts = slug.split('/');
  if (slug.startsWith('.') || slugParts.some((s) => s === '.' || s === '..')) return { ok: false, why: 'bad-slug' };
  const repoPath = target.kind === 'root' ? null
    : target.kind === 'repo' ? target.repoPath
      : target.kind === 'section' ? DOC_SECTIONS[target.section]
        : docRepoPath(target.section, target.path);
  const atParts = at.split('/');
  const pathParts = repoPath === null ? [] : repoPath.split('/');
  if ([...atParts, ...pathParts].some((s) => s === '' || s === '.' || s === '..')) {
    return { ok: false, why: 'bad-target' };
  }
  const encoded = (parts: readonly string[]): string => parts.map((s) => encodeURIComponent(s)).join('/');
  const blob = target.kind === 'leaf' || target.kind === 'repo';
  const url = 'https://github.com/' + encoded(slugParts) + (blob ? '/blob/' : '/tree/') + encoded(atParts)
    + (pathParts.length === 0 ? '' : '/' + encoded(pathParts));
  return { ok: true, url };
}

/** The View on GitHub builder (spec 3.11). The rows are checked in the spec table's order, the first match
 *  winning:
 *   1. no GitHub-shaped origin was read: `no-github-origin`;
 *   2. a dot-segment slug: `bad-slug`; 3. an empty, `.` or `..` segment in the branch name or the path:
 *      `bad-target` (both judged by githubUrlAt);
 *   4. a `local-only` relation, or a default resolved to a local branch: `not-on-origin`;
 *   5. a leaf whose entry has no committed side (`uncommitted`, i.e. `e.committed === null`, whether or not the
 *      draft opens): `uncommitted`;
 *   6. the origin side is served, or the local side equals origin: a link with no note;
 *   7. otherwise (the local side ahead, behind, diverged or unmeasured): a link with `may-differ`. A local side
 *      reading `origin-only` cannot arrive, because a local side means the local branch exists; if it did, it
 *      would land here, on the cautious answer.
 *  The URL names the branch (`at` is `ref.name`), never a commit: the durable-link convention. */
export function githubBlobUrl(github: DocsGithub, ref: DocsTreeOk['ref'], target: GithubTarget): GithubLink {
  if (github.state === 'none') return { ok: false, why: 'no-github-origin' };
  const built = githubUrlAt(github.slug, ref.name, target);
  if (!built.ok) return built;
  if (servedRefIsLocalOnly(ref)) return { ok: false, why: 'not-on-origin' };
  if (target.kind === 'leaf' && target.uncommitted) return { ok: false, why: 'uncommitted' };
  return { ok: true, url: built.url, note: ref.side === 'origin' || ref.relation === 'equal' ? null : 'may-differ' };
}

/** The permalink builder (spec 3.11, amended 2026-10-13; decisions 10 and 11). `commit` is the commit the page
 *  opened, and the URL's `at` is always that full id, never `ref.name`. The rows are checked in the spec table's
 *  order, the first match winning:
 *   1. no GitHub-shaped origin was read: `no-github-origin`;
 *   2. a dot-segment slug: `bad-slug` (githubUrlAt);
 *   3. `commit` not 40 or 64 lowercase hex (isDocsCommit), or an empty, `.` or `..` segment in it or in the path:
 *      `bad-target`;
 *   4. a `local-only` relation, or a default resolved to a local branch: `not-on-origin`;
 *   5. a leaf whose entry has no committed side: `uncommitted`;
 *   6. the origin side is served (which covers `origin-only`), or the relation is `equal` or `local-behind`: a
 *      link, because the commit is on origin;
 *   7. the local side ahead of origin or diverged from it: `not-on-origin`;
 *   8. the relation was not measured: `unmeasured`.
 *  Rows 7 and 8 are disjoint, so their order is the table's and changes nothing. A local side reading
 *  `origin-only` cannot arrive (a local side means the local branch exists); no row links it, and it lands on
 *  the refusal `not-on-origin`. */
export function githubPermalink(
  github: DocsGithub, ref: DocsTreeOk['ref'], commit: string, target: GithubTarget,
): GithubPermalink {
  if (github.state === 'none') return { ok: false, why: 'no-github-origin' };
  const built = githubUrlAt(github.slug, commit, target);
  if (!built.ok) return built;
  if (!isDocsCommit(commit)) return { ok: false, why: 'bad-target' };
  if (servedRefIsLocalOnly(ref)) return { ok: false, why: 'not-on-origin' };
  if (target.kind === 'leaf' && target.uncommitted) return { ok: false, why: 'uncommitted' };
  if (ref.side === 'origin' || ref.relation === 'equal' || ref.relation === 'local-behind') {
    return { ok: true, url: built.url, commit };
  }
  if (ref.relation === 'unmeasured') return { ok: false, why: 'unmeasured' };
  return { ok: false, why: 'not-on-origin' };
}
```

**Decisions this task makes (none departs from the spec's text):**
1. **`DocsRefreshAnswer` is named `DocsRefreshLoaderAnswer` in the PWA.** `server/src/docs/policy.ts` already exports `DocsRefreshAnswer` (the refresh route's own verdict, `{kind: 'refuse' | 'send'}`), and `single-definition.test.ts`'s "every export under server/src/docs is declared exactly once across the four roots" reds on a second declaration (measured: `DocsRefreshAnswer: expected [ 'server/src/docs/policy.ts', 'pwa/src/docs/failures.ts' ]`). The other four aliases and every other name this task exports are absent from `server/src/docs`'s exports (measured by listing them). Later tasks read the loader's refresh answer as `DocsRefreshLoaderAnswer`.
2. **`docsText.ts` joins the files excused for the docs reader's `worktree-gone`, by an in-place edit.** `DOCS_FAILURE_SENTENCE: Record<DocsFailure, string>` must spell `'worktree-gone'` as a quoted key on a code line, and the archive-door describe ("`'worktree-gone'` is a code-line literal in shared/api.ts alone") excuses the docs reader's word by FILE (`server/src/docs/policy.ts`, `shared/docs.ts`), so a third file is red (measured: `1 failed | 541 passed (542)`). The describe's own header says its excusals are named, never widened by pattern, so the fix names `pwa/src/docs/docsText.ts` in the `want` line and in the header's comment line, each edited in place. This departs from the architecture's file-shape invariant ("`single-definition.test.ts` changes only by one end-of-file append"), whose reason is `session-hook.test.ts`'s line citations: no line moves, the file stays 5 730 lines, and `session-hook -t citation` stays `13 passed`. An appended describe cannot do it (the `it.each` above would still be red). Mutation row M48 proves the excusal is by file: the same literal in `failures.ts` is still red. A later task that spells the word in another file (Task 5's re-list triggers, if written as literals) must add that file the same way, or compare through a set declared in `docsText.ts`.
3. **`failures.ts` imports `ApiError` as a type only** and recognises it by its `name` (`'ApiError'`, set by its constructor): `lib/api.ts` imports `failures.ts`, and the codebase keeps its modules acyclic (`lib/auth.ts` says why it never imports `lib/api.ts`). A type-only import is erased under `verbatimModuleSyntax`.
4. **The classifier's order is refinement (k)'s, first match wins:** a string `failure` (any status, unknown words kept whole), then `401` `auth`, then `404` with `error: 'not-found'` `no-docs-route`, then any other `ApiError` `unexpected-response` (`contentType ?? ''`), then a `TypeError` `unreachable`; anything else is rethrown. An abort is a `DOMException` named `AbortError`, neither an `ApiError` nor a `TypeError`, so it is rethrown by that last rule: the caller aborted, and there is no slot for it. A separate abort check would change no answer, so it is not written (it would be a guard no mutation can red).
5. **"Not the expected envelope" is measured per route:** a 2xx body that is not JSON, not an object, has `ok` other than `true`, or lacks a field the route always sends (`index`; `tree` and `refreshDue`; `contentClass` and `show`; `fetch` and `tree`) is `unexpected-response` with the response's own status and content type. Deeper shape checks are the views' business (Task 9 renders what the tree answer holds).
6. **`raster` is `GET docsApi.file(...)` on a raster path**, checked twice in order (spec 5.4): the `content-type` must EQUAL `DOCS_RASTER_TYPES[t].mime` (so `image/jpg` for a `.JPG` is refused), then `sniffRaster(t, bytes)` must match, else the client builds `{ok: false, failure: 'raster-mismatch', declared: t, size}` exactly as the server's own refusal reads. `t` comes from `declaredRaster(path)`, the PWA's reading of the extension (the server's `docsRasterType` is in `server/src`, which the PWA cannot import). `bytes` is typed `Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>` so Task 7's `new Blob([bytes])` type-checks under TypeScript 6's DOM lib.
7. **`refresh` sends exactly `{ref, reason}`**, copied field by field, so a caller's wider object (TypeScript allows one) never reaches the route, which refuses any other key with `bad-query`.
8. **An unknown word's retry plan is `none`.** Its sentence says to reload; the same server would answer the same word to a Retry.
9. **`fillSentence` renders an absent field as `?`**, never the braces, in one pass (a value holding braces is not filled again). Sentences that depend on a field that may be `null` (`linked-worktree`'s and `shared-repo`'s `owner`) do not name it: Task 9 redirects or renders the sentence alone, as §4.7 says.
10. **The sentences §4.7 does not give are written here**, in its register (B6 of the ground). None of them says "trying again": the view's actions say what will happen, so no sentence goes false once an automatic retry is spent. `kib` rounds up, so a non-empty file never reads as `0 KiB`.
11. **Retry is offered when the caller passes `onRetry` AND the answer allows it:** a word by `docsRetryPlan(body).kind !== 'none'`; `unreachable` and `unexpected-response` always (a proxy's 502 during a restart is worth a second ask; §4.7 is silent on the second); `auth` never (sign-in re-fetches, Task 5) and `no-docs-route` never. When to pass the handler (after the one automatic retry an `auto` word gets) is Task 5's.
12. **Fixtures never spell magic bytes or a quoted marker header:** the PNG, GIF and JPEG fixtures are built from `DOCS_RASTER_TYPES` (single-definition holds the PNG signature to `shared/docs.ts`), and the header is read through `DOCS_REQUEST_HEADER`. Every fixture is a placeholder (`demo`, `ws/a`, `ws/b`, `main`, `demo-root`).
