- [ ] **Step 1: Write the client's test.** Create `pwa/test/docs-api.test.ts` with exactly this content (no line holds a raw control byte; the PNG, GIF and JPEG bytes come from `DOCS_RASTER_TYPES`):

```ts
// Docs W5 part 1, Task 2: `api.docs.*` (spec 2026-10-01 4.3, 5.4; refinement (k)). Every call goes through
// `createApi`'s one `request` funnel with the marker header, answers a union and never throws for a docs word, and
// a raster is checked twice on the client (M5.18). Every fetch is injected: no case reaches a server.
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import {
  DOCS_RASTER_TYPES, DOCS_REQUEST_HEADER, DOCS_REQUEST_HEADER_VALUE, docsApi, type DocPin,
} from '../../shared/docs';
import { ApiError, createApi } from '../src/lib/api';
import { authLost, clearAuthLost } from '../src/lib/auth';

const jsonResponse = (status: number, body: unknown, contentType: string | null = 'application/json; charset=utf-8'): Response =>
  new Response(JSON.stringify(body), { status, headers: contentType === null ? {} : { 'content-type': contentType } });

const bytesResponse = (status: number, bytes: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>, contentType: string): Response =>
  new Response(bytes, { status, headers: { 'content-type': contentType } });

// Magic bytes come from L0's own table (single-definition holds the PNG signature to shared/docs.ts), padded so a
// fixture is longer than its magic.
const magicOf = (t: keyof typeof DOCS_RASTER_TYPES): Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer> => {
  const out = new Uint8Array(16);
  for (const run of DOCS_RASTER_TYPES[t].magic[0] ?? []) out.set(run.bytes, run.at);
  return out;
};
const PNG = magicOf('png');
const GIF = magicOf('gif');
const JPEG = magicOf('jpeg');

const C = 'c'.repeat(40);
const committed = (path: string): DocPin =>
  ({ kind: 'committed', commit: C, servedRef: 'refs/remotes/origin/main', section: 'specs', path });
const DRAFT: DocPin =
  { kind: 'draft', branch: 'ws/a', head: 'd'.repeat(40), section: 'plans', path: 'a b+c.md', fp: 'f'.repeat(64) };

const TREE_OK = { ok: true, tree: { project: 'demo' }, refreshDue: false };
const FILE_OK = { ok: true, contentClass: 'markdown', show: { text: '# a' }, from: 'ccd' };

const apiOver = (impl: (url: string, init: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>) => {
  const spy = vi.fn(impl);
  return { api: createApi(spy as unknown as typeof fetch), spy };
};
const callOf = (spy: { mock: { calls: unknown[][] } }, i = 0): [string, RequestInit] =>
  spy.mock.calls[i] as [string, RequestInit];

afterEach(() => { clearAuthLost(); vi.restoreAllMocks(); });

describe('api.docs: the marker header and the URL on every call', () => {
  it('projects, tree (default and ref view), file (committed and draft pins), raster and refresh each send the marker through the constants, to docsApi\'s URL', async () => {
    const { api, spy } = apiOver(async (url) =>
      url.includes('/file') ? (url.includes('.png') ? bytesResponse(200, PNG, 'image/png') : jsonResponse(200, FILE_OK))
        : url.endsWith('/refresh') ? jsonResponse(200, { ok: true, fetch: { state: 'skipped', why: 'local-ref' }, tree: TREE_OK })
          : url.endsWith('/projects') ? jsonResponse(200, { ok: true, index: { projects: [] }, cacheAgeMs: null })
            : jsonResponse(200, TREE_OK));
    await api.docs.projects();
    await api.docs.tree('demo', null);
    await api.docs.tree('demo', { kind: 'bare', name: 'ws/a' });
    await api.docs.file('demo', committed('a.md'));
    await api.docs.file('demo', DRAFT);
    await api.docs.raster('demo', committed('img/a.png'));
    await api.docs.refresh('demo', { ref: null, reason: 'auto' });
    const expected = [
      docsApi.projects(), docsApi.tree('demo', null), docsApi.tree('demo', { kind: 'bare', name: 'ws/a' }),
      docsApi.file('demo', committed('a.md')), docsApi.file('demo', DRAFT), docsApi.file('demo', committed('img/a.png')),
      docsApi.refresh('demo'),
    ];
    expect(spy.mock.calls.map((c) => c[0])).toEqual(expected);
    for (let i = 0; i < expected.length; i += 1) {
      const [, init] = callOf(spy, i);
      expect(new Headers(init.headers).get(DOCS_REQUEST_HEADER), `call ${i} carries the marker`).toBe(DOCS_REQUEST_HEADER_VALUE);
    }
  });

  it('refresh POSTs exactly {ref, reason} as JSON, with the marker', async () => {
    const { api, spy } = apiOver(async () =>
      jsonResponse(200, { ok: true, fetch: { state: 'skipped', why: 'local-ref' }, tree: TREE_OK }));
    const answer = await api.docs.refresh('demo', { ref: 'refs/heads/main', reason: 'manual' });
    expect(answer.s).toBe('ok');
    const [url, init] = callOf(spy);
    expect(url).toBe(docsApi.refresh('demo'));
    expect(init.method).toBe('POST');
    const headers = new Headers(init.headers);
    expect(headers.get('content-type')).toBe('application/json');
    expect(headers.get(DOCS_REQUEST_HEADER)).toBe(DOCS_REQUEST_HEADER_VALUE);
    expect(JSON.parse(init.body as string)).toEqual({ ref: 'refs/heads/main', reason: 'manual' });
  });

  it('refresh sends only ref and reason, whatever else the caller\'s object holds (the route refuses any other key)', async () => {
    const { api, spy } = apiOver(async () =>
      jsonResponse(200, { ok: true, fetch: { state: 'skipped', why: 'local-ref' }, tree: TREE_OK }));
    const wide = { ref: null, reason: 'auto' as const, page: 'demo' };
    await api.docs.refresh('demo', wide);
    expect(JSON.parse(callOf(spy)[1].body as string)).toEqual({ ref: null, reason: 'auto' });
  });

  it('an ok answer is {s: ok, value} with the server\'s envelope as is', async () => {
    const { api } = apiOver(async () => jsonResponse(200, TREE_OK));
    expect(await api.docs.tree('demo', null)).toEqual({ s: 'ok', value: TREE_OK });
  });
});

describe('api.docs: every answer that is not a page is a union arm, never an exception', () => {
  it('a 401 with a verdict raises the login overlay through request, and answers auth', async () => {
    const { api } = apiOver(async () => jsonResponse(401, { ok: false, error: 'unauthenticated', verdict: 'no-session' }));
    expect(await api.docs.tree('demo', null)).toEqual({ s: 'auth' });
    expect(authLost()).toEqual({ lost: true, verdict: 'no-session' });
  });

  it('a 401 with no verdict answers auth and raises nothing (request\'s positive-evidence rule)', async () => {
    const { api } = apiOver(async () => jsonResponse(401, { ok: false, error: 'unauthenticated' }));
    expect(await api.docs.projects()).toEqual({ s: 'auth' });
    expect(authLost().lost).toBe(false);
  });

  it('a 403 foreign-request body answers failed with the body whole, and raises nothing', async () => {
    const body = { ok: false, failure: 'foreign-request', site: 'cross-site' };
    const { api } = apiOver(async () => jsonResponse(403, body));
    expect(await api.docs.tree('demo', null)).toEqual({ s: 'failed', body });
    expect(authLost().lost).toBe(false);
  });

  it('a 404 {error: not-found} with no failure is a pre-Docs server: no-docs-route (M7.1)', async () => {
    const { api } = apiOver(async () => jsonResponse(404, { ok: false, error: 'not-found' }));
    expect(await api.docs.tree('demo', null)).toEqual({ s: 'no-docs-route' });
  });

  it('a 404 carrying a failure word is that word, never no-docs-route', async () => {
    const body = { ok: false, failure: 'unknown-project', root: 'demo-root', error: 'not-found' };
    const { api } = apiOver(async () => jsonResponse(404, body));
    expect(await api.docs.tree('demo', null)).toEqual({ s: 'failed', body });
  });

  it('no-docs-route needs the status AND the code: a 404 with another code, and a 500 not-found, are unexpected-response', async () => {
    const a = apiOver(async () => jsonResponse(404, { error: 'gone' }));
    expect(await a.api.docs.projects()).toEqual({ s: 'unexpected-response', status: 404, contentType: 'application/json; charset=utf-8' });
    const b = apiOver(async () => jsonResponse(500, { error: 'not-found' }));
    expect(await b.api.docs.projects()).toEqual({ s: 'unexpected-response', status: 500, contentType: 'application/json; charset=utf-8' });
  });

  it('an unknown word from a newer server is kept whole, never folded', async () => {
    const body = { ok: false, failure: 'brand-new-word', detail: 'x' };
    const { api } = apiOver(async () => jsonResponse(409, body));
    expect(await api.docs.tree('demo', null)).toEqual({ s: 'failed', body });
  });

  it('a fetch that rejects with a TypeError (offline) answers unreachable', async () => {
    const { api } = apiOver(async () => { throw new TypeError('Failed to fetch'); });
    expect(await api.docs.projects()).toEqual({ s: 'unreachable' });
  });

  it('a 502 proxy page answers unexpected-response with its status and content type', async () => {
    const { api } = apiOver(async () => new Response('<html>bad gateway</html>', { status: 502, headers: { 'content-type': 'text/html' } }));
    expect(await api.docs.tree('demo', null)).toEqual({ s: 'unexpected-response', status: 502, contentType: 'text/html' });
  });

  it('a failure answer with no content-type header reads contentType as the empty string', async () => {
    // A null body: the Response constructor adds a content type for a string body, never for none.
    const { api } = apiOver(async () => new Response(null, { status: 500 }));
    const answer = await api.docs.projects();
    expect(answer).toEqual({ s: 'unexpected-response', status: 500, contentType: '' });
  });

  it('a 200 that is not the envelope is unexpected-response: not JSON, ok not true, or a route field missing', async () => {
    const html = apiOver(async () => new Response('<html>portal</html>', { status: 200, headers: { 'content-type': 'text/html' } }));
    expect(await html.api.docs.tree('demo', null)).toEqual({ s: 'unexpected-response', status: 200, contentType: 'text/html' });
    const notOk = apiOver(async () => jsonResponse(200, { ok: false, tree: {}, refreshDue: false }));
    expect((await notOk.api.docs.tree('demo', null)).s).toBe('unexpected-response');
    const noTree = apiOver(async () => jsonResponse(200, { ok: true, refreshDue: false }));
    expect((await noTree.api.docs.tree('demo', null)).s).toBe('unexpected-response');
    const noShow = apiOver(async () => jsonResponse(200, { ok: true, contentClass: 'markdown' }));
    expect((await noShow.api.docs.file('demo', committed('a.md'))).s).toBe('unexpected-response');
    const noIndex = apiOver(async () => jsonResponse(200, { ok: true, cacheAgeMs: null }));
    expect((await noIndex.api.docs.projects()).s).toBe('unexpected-response');
    const noFetch = apiOver(async () => jsonResponse(200, { ok: true, tree: TREE_OK }));
    expect((await noFetch.api.docs.refresh('demo', { ref: null, reason: 'auto' })).s).toBe('unexpected-response');
    const array = apiOver(async () => jsonResponse(200, [TREE_OK]));
    expect((await array.api.docs.tree('demo', null)).s).toBe('unexpected-response');
    const nul = apiOver(async () => jsonResponse(200, null));
    expect(await nul.api.docs.tree('demo', null))
      .toEqual({ s: 'unexpected-response', status: 200, contentType: 'application/json; charset=utf-8' });
  });

  it('an aborted signal rejects with the AbortError: the caller aborted, so there is no slot', async () => {
    const { api } = apiOver((_url, init) => new Promise<Response>((_resolve, reject) => {
      init.signal?.addEventListener('abort', () => reject(new DOMException('The operation was aborted.', 'AbortError')));
    }));
    const controller = new AbortController();
    const pending = api.docs.file('demo', committed('a.md'), controller.signal);
    controller.abort();
    await expect(pending).rejects.toMatchObject({ name: 'AbortError' });
  });

  it('raster: an aborted signal rejects with the AbortError: the caller aborted, so there is no slot', async () => {
    const { api } = apiOver((_url, init) => new Promise<Response>((_resolve, reject) => {
      init.signal?.addEventListener('abort', () => reject(new DOMException('The operation was aborted.', 'AbortError')));
    }));
    const controller = new AbortController();
    const pending = api.docs.raster('demo', committed('i.png'), controller.signal);
    controller.abort();
    await expect(pending).rejects.toMatchObject({ name: 'AbortError' });
  });

  it('a non-2xx records its content type on ApiError (null when the header is absent); nothing else about ApiError changes', async () => {
    const typed = createApi((async () => new Response('x', { status: 500, headers: { 'content-type': 'text/plain' } })) as typeof fetch);
    const err = await typed.updates().then(() => null, (e: unknown) => e);
    expect(err).toBeInstanceOf(ApiError);
    expect((err as ApiError).contentType).toBe('text/plain');
    expect((err as ApiError).status).toBe(500);
    const bare = createApi((async () => new Response(null, { status: 500 })) as typeof fetch);
    expect(((await bare.updates().then(() => null, (e: unknown) => e)) as ApiError).contentType).toBeNull();
    expect(new ApiError(409, { error: 'x' }).contentType).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe('api.docs.raster: the two client checks (M5.18) and the representation split', () => {
  it('a 200 text/html holding PNG bytes is unexpected-response: the content type must be the declared raster MIME', async () => {
    const { api } = apiOver(async () => bytesResponse(200, PNG, 'text/html'));
    expect(await api.docs.raster('demo', committed('img/a.png')))
      .toEqual({ s: 'unexpected-response', status: 200, contentType: 'text/html' });
  });

  it('a 200 image/png holding GIF bytes is a client-built raster-mismatch with the declared type and the size', async () => {
    const { api } = apiOver(async () => bytesResponse(200, GIF, 'image/png'));
    expect(await api.docs.raster('demo', committed('img/a.png'))).toEqual({
      s: 'failed', body: { ok: false, failure: 'raster-mismatch', declared: 'png', size: GIF.byteLength },
    });
  });

  it('a 200 image/png holding PNG bytes answers the bytes and the MIME from the table', async () => {
    const { api } = apiOver(async () => bytesResponse(200, PNG, 'image/png'));
    const answer = await api.docs.raster('demo', committed('img/a.png'));
    expect(answer.s).toBe('ok');
    if (answer.s !== 'ok') return;
    expect(Array.from(answer.value.bytes)).toEqual(Array.from(PNG));
    expect(answer.value.mime).toBe('image/png');
  });

  it('a .JPG path is the jpeg type: image/jpeg with JPEG bytes loads, the non-standard image/jpg is refused', async () => {
    const ok = apiOver(async () => bytesResponse(200, JPEG, 'image/jpeg'));
    const answer = await ok.api.docs.raster('demo', committed('a.JPG'));
    expect(answer.s === 'ok' ? answer.value.mime : answer.s).toBe('image/jpeg');
    const odd = apiOver(async () => bytesResponse(200, JPEG, 'image/jpg'));
    expect(await odd.api.docs.raster('demo', committed('a.JPG')))
      .toEqual({ s: 'unexpected-response', status: 200, contentType: 'image/jpg' });
  });

  it('a raster failure body (422 raster-mismatch from the server) is that word', async () => {
    const body = { ok: false, failure: 'raster-mismatch', declared: 'png', size: 9 };
    const { api } = apiOver(async () => jsonResponse(422, body));
    expect(await api.docs.raster('demo', committed('a.png'))).toEqual({ s: 'failed', body });
  });

  it('file() on a raster path and raster() on a non-raster path are programming errors: wrong-representation, before any fetch', () => {
    const { api, spy } = apiOver(async () => jsonResponse(200, FILE_OK));
    expect(() => api.docs.file('demo', committed('img/a.png'))).toThrow('wrong-representation');
    expect(() => api.docs.raster('demo', committed('a.md'))).toThrow('wrong-representation');
    expect(() => api.docs.raster('demo', committed('a.svg'))).toThrow('wrong-representation');
    expect(spy).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });
});

// Docs W5 part 1, Task 2: the docs words (spec 2026-10-01 4.7). Every sentence map is exhaustive over its word's
// type (the `Record<..., true>` sets below make a word missing from a set a compile error in this file, under pwa's
// tsc and server/test/typecheck-tests), the spec's own sentences are verbatim, an unknown word is never folded
// (M4.F2), the retry plan follows L0's classes and the three lock ages (M4.F3), and a pre-Docs server's 404 renders
// "predates Docs" and no docs sentence (M4.F6 = M7.1).
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { cleanup, fireEvent, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import {
  DOCS_FAILURE_RETRY, DOCS_FAILURES, type DocsFailure, type DocsFailureBody, type DocsNotAFileKind,
  type DocsPageParseFailure, type DocsTreeOk, type EntryBadge, type WithheldReason,
} from '../../shared/docs';
import { createApi } from '../src/lib/api';
import {
  DOCS_CAPS_UNKNOWN_RETRY_MS, DOCS_LOCK_STALE_MS, DOCS_REF_LOCKED_RETRY_MS, docsAnswerFromError, docsRetryPlan,
  type DocsClientSlot, type DocsNotOk,
} from '../src/docs/failures';
import {
  DOCS_FAILURE_SENTENCE, DOCS_PAGE_INVALID_SENTENCE, DOCS_SLOT_SENTENCE, ENTRY_BADGE_TEXT, NOT_A_FILE_KIND_TEXT,
  RELATION_SENTENCE, UNRESOLVED_TAG_HINT, VIA_SENTENCE, WITHHELD_SENTENCE, failureSentence, fillSentence, kib,
  shortCommit, unknownWordSentence,
} from '../src/docs/docsText';
import { DocsFailureView } from '../src/docs/DocsFailureView';

afterEach(() => { cleanup(); vi.restoreAllMocks(); });

// Each set is exhaustive by type: a key missing or extra is a compile error here.
const PAGE_FAILURES: Record<DocsPageParseFailure, true> = {
  'not-docs': true, 'bad-project': true, 'bad-section': true, 'bad-path': true, 'bad-ref': true, 'bad-view': true,
  'bad-frame': true, 'bad-escape': true, 'encoded-slash': true, 'commit-in-page': true, 'unknown-param': true,
  'repeated-param': true, 'reserved-node': true,
};
const KINDS: Record<DocsNotAFileKind, true> = {
  'directory': true, 'section-not-a-directory': true, 'symlink': true, 'submodule': true, 'file-in-path': true,
  'special': true, 'hardlink': true, 'foreign-owner': true, 'other-device': true,
};
const VIAS: Record<DocsTreeOk['ref']['via'], true> = {
  'default:origin-head': true, 'default:origin-main': true, 'default:origin-master': true, 'default:local-main': true,
  'default:local-master': true, 'local': true, 'origin': true, 'qualified': true,
};
const RELATIONS: Record<DocsTreeOk['ref']['relation'], true> = {
  'equal': true, 'local-only': true, 'origin-only': true, 'local-ahead': true, 'local-behind': true, 'diverged': true,
  'unmeasured': true,
};
const BADGES: Record<EntryBadge, true> = {
  'modified': true, 'new': true, 'deleted': true, 'typechange': true, 'conflicted': true, 'withheld': true,
};
const WITHHELD: Record<WithheldReason, true> = { 'too-large': true, 'unreadable': true, 'not-a-file': true };
const SLOTS: Record<DocsClientSlot['s'], true> = {
  'auth': true, 'unreachable': true, 'no-docs-route': true, 'unexpected-response': true,
};
const keysOf = (o: object): string[] => Object.keys(o).sort();

/** A failure body for `word`, known or not, with any context. */
const bodyOf = (word: string, ctx: Record<string, unknown> = {}): DocsFailureBody =>
  ({ ok: false, failure: word, ...ctx }) as unknown as DocsFailureBody;
const failed = (word: string, ctx: Record<string, unknown> = {}): DocsNotOk => ({ s: 'failed', body: bodyOf(word, ctx) });
/** A template's longest run of fixed text between placeholders: what any filling of it must contain. */
const stem = (template: string): string =>
  template.split(/\{[A-Za-z]+\}/).reduce((a, b) => (b.length > a.length ? b : a), '');

describe('the sentence maps (M4.F1)', () => {
  it('every DOCS_FAILURES word has a sentence of 20+ characters, and the map holds no other key', () => {
    expect(keysOf(DOCS_FAILURE_SENTENCE)).toEqual(keysOf(DOCS_FAILURES));
    for (const [word, sentence] of Object.entries(DOCS_FAILURE_SENTENCE)) {

    }
  });

  it('every DocsPageParseFailure has a sentence of 20+ characters, and the map holds no other key', () => {
    expect(keysOf(DOCS_PAGE_INVALID_SENTENCE)).toEqual(keysOf(PAGE_FAILURES));
    for (const [why, sentence] of Object.entries(DOCS_PAGE_INVALID_SENTENCE)) {

  it('the seven sentences spec 4.7 gives are verbatim', () => {

      'unsupported': "The fleet box's ccd predates Docs; roll out a newer release.",
      'not-granted': 'The fleet agent has not loaded the Docs grants yet. If a rollout is running this clears when it finishes; otherwise update the fleet box.',
      'foreign-request': 'The server refused a request that did not come from the Docs screen.',

    }

  it('the not-a-file kinds, the vias, the relations, the badges, the withheld reasons and the slots each have exactly their type\'s keys, every text non-empty', () => {
    const pairs: [object, object][] = [

      [WITHHELD_SENTENCE, WITHHELD], [DOCS_SLOT_SENTENCE, SLOTS],

    for (const [map, set] of pairs) {

  it('the truth line\'s sentences and the slots are spec 4.5\'s and 4.7\'s, verbatim once filled', () => {
    expect(fillSentence(VIA_SENTENCE.local, { requested: 'ws/a' })).toBe('you asked for ws/a, showing local');
    expect(fillSentence(VIA_SENTENCE.origin, { requested: 'main' })).toBe("you asked for main, showing origin's");
    expect(VIA_SENTENCE['default:origin-head']).toBe('default branch (origin/HEAD)');
    expect(VIA_SENTENCE['default:origin-main']).toBe('default branch (origin/main; origin/HEAD unset)');
    expect(VIA_SENTENCE['default:origin-master']).toBe('default branch (origin/master; origin/HEAD unset)');
    expect(VIA_SENTENCE['default:local-main']).toBe('default branch (local main; no origin branch)');
    expect(VIA_SENTENCE['default:local-master']).toBe('default branch (local master; no origin branch)');
    expect(VIA_SENTENCE.qualified).toBe('exactly the ref you asked for');
    expect(fillSentence(RELATION_SENTENCE.diverged, { ahead: 2, behind: 3 }))
      .toBe('local and origin have diverged (2 vs 3), showing local');
    expect(fillSentence(RELATION_SENTENCE['local-ahead'], { ahead: 4 })).toBe('local is 4 ahead of origin');
    expect(fillSentence(RELATION_SENTENCE['local-behind'], { behind: 1 })).toBe('origin is 1 ahead of local');
    expect(RELATION_SENTENCE.unmeasured).toBe('local vs origin not measured');
    expect(ENTRY_BADGE_TEXT.modified).toBe('draft · modified');
    expect(ENTRY_BADGE_TEXT.new).toBe('draft · new');
    expect(DOCS_SLOT_SENTENCE.auth).toBe('Sign in to read Docs.');
    expect(DOCS_SLOT_SENTENCE.unreachable).toBe('The server could not be reached; Docs needs a connection.');
    expect(DOCS_SLOT_SENTENCE['no-docs-route']).toBe('This server predates Docs; update the server box.');
  });
});

describe('fillSentence, failureSentence, kib and shortCommit', () => {
  it('fills each placeholder in one pass: an absent field renders ?, never the braces, and a value holding braces is not filled again', () => {
    expect(fillSentence('a {x} b {y}.', { x: 1, y: 'two' })).toBe('a 1 b two.');
    expect(fillSentence('the {root} folder', {})).toBe('the ? folder');
    expect(fillSentence('{word}!', { word: '{word}' })).toBe('{word}!');
  });

  it('a known word is filled from its own context, sizes in KiB', () => {
    expect(failureSentence(bodyOf('too-large', { size: 3145728, cap: 2097152 })))
      .toBe('This file is 3072 KiB; Docs shows files of this kind up to 2048 KiB.');
    expect(failureSentence(bodyOf('raster-mismatch', { declared: 'png', size: 9 })))
      .toBe('These bytes are not a png image.');
    expect(failureSentence(bodyOf('unknown-project', { root: 'demo-root' })))
      .toBe("There is no project by that name under the fleet box's projects folder (demo-root).");
  });

  it('kib rounds up so a non-empty file never reads as 0; shortCommit is the first 8 hex characters', () => {
    expect([kib(0), kib(1), kib(1024), kib(1025), kib(2097152)]).toEqual(['0 KiB', '1 KiB', '1 KiB', '2 KiB', '2048 KiB']);
    expect(shortCommit('0123456789abcdef'.repeat(4).slice(0, 40))).toBe('01234567');
  });
});

describe('an unknown word is never folded (M4.F2)', () => {
  it("{failure: 'brand-new-word'} renders a sentence naming it, and no known word's sentence", () => {
    render(<DocsFailureView answer={failed('brand-new-word')} onRetry={() => undefined} />);
    const text = screen.getByRole('alert').textContent ?? '';
    expect(text).toContain('brand-new-word');
    expect(text).toContain(unknownWordSentence('brand-new-word'));
    expect(unknownWordSentence('brand-new-word'))
      .toBe("The server answered 'brand-new-word', which this app version does not know; reload to update.");
    for (const sentence of Object.values(DOCS_FAILURE_SENTENCE)) expect(text).not.toContain(stem(sentence));
    expect(screen.queryByRole('button', { name: 'Retry' }), 'the same server would answer the same word').toBeNull();
  });

  it('the retry plan of an unknown word is none', () => {
    expect(docsRetryPlan(bodyOf('brand-new-word', { retryAfterMs: 10 }))).toEqual({ kind: 'none' });
  });
});

describe('docsRetryPlan (M4.F3)', () => {
  it('the three PWA waits are the spec\'s', () => {
    expect([DOCS_REF_LOCKED_RETRY_MS, DOCS_LOCK_STALE_MS, DOCS_CAPS_UNKNOWN_RETRY_MS]).toEqual([3000, 60000, 5000]);
  });

  it.each(Object.entries(DOCS_FAILURE_RETRY))('%s (class %s) with no context follows its class', (word, cls) => {
    const plan = docsRetryPlan(bodyOf(word));
    if (cls === 'none') expect(plan).toEqual({ kind: 'none' });
    else if (cls === 'manual') expect(plan).toEqual({ kind: 'manual' });
    else if (cls === 'auto-while-young') expect(plan, 'lockAgeMs absent: unmeasured').toEqual({ kind: 'manual' });
    else expect(plan).toEqual({ kind: 'auto', afterMs: word === 'caps-unknown' ? DOCS_CAPS_UNKNOWN_RETRY_MS : 0 });
  });

  it.each(Object.entries(DOCS_FAILURE_RETRY))('%s (class %s) with retryAfterMs 1234 waits it only when auto', (word, cls) => {
    const plan = docsRetryPlan(bodyOf(word, { retryAfterMs: 1234 }));
    if (cls === 'auto') expect(plan).toEqual({ kind: 'auto', afterMs: 1234 });
    else expect(plan.kind).not.toBe('auto');
  });

  it('a negative retryAfterMs is not a wait: the word\'s own fallback applies', () => {
    expect(docsRetryPlan(bodyOf('docs-busy', { retryAfterMs: -5 }))).toEqual({ kind: 'auto', afterMs: 0 });
    expect(docsRetryPlan(bodyOf('caps-unknown', { retryAfterMs: -5 }))).toEqual({ kind: 'auto', afterMs: 5000 });
  });

  it('ref-locked: a young lock and a lock already gone wait 3 s; at or past 60 s it is stale (none); an unmeasured age is manual', () => {
    const plan = (lockAgeMs?: number | null) =>
      docsRetryPlan(bodyOf('ref-locked', lockAgeMs === undefined ? {} : { lockAgeMs }));
    expect(plan(5000)).toEqual({ kind: 'auto', afterMs: 3000 });
    expect(plan(0)).toEqual({ kind: 'auto', afterMs: 3000 });
    expect(plan(59999)).toEqual({ kind: 'auto', afterMs: 3000 });
    expect(plan(null)).toEqual({ kind: 'auto', afterMs: 3000 });
    expect(plan(60000)).toEqual({ kind: 'none' });
    expect(plan(120000)).toEqual({ kind: 'none' });
    expect(plan()).toEqual({ kind: 'manual' });
  });
});

describe('docsAnswerFromError', () => {
  it('rethrows an abort and a defect; a TypeError is unreachable', () => {
    const abort = new DOMException('aborted', 'AbortError');
    expect(() => docsAnswerFromError(abort)).toThrow(abort);
    const defect = new RangeError('a bug');
    expect(() => docsAnswerFromError(defect)).toThrow(defect);
    expect(docsAnswerFromError(new TypeError('Failed to fetch'))).toEqual({ s: 'unreachable' });
  });
});

    );

    expect(document.querySelector('pre.docs-fail-detail')?.textContent).toBe('Traceback: x');

    expect(screen.getByRole('alert')).toHaveAttribute('data-failure', 'git-failed');

    expect(screen.getByRole('alert')).toHaveTextContent('(demo-root)');

});

describe('DocsFailureView: Retry follows the answer, and only a passed handler is offered', () => {
  const retryFor = (answer: DocsNotOk, withHandler = true): HTMLElement | null => {
    const { unmount } = render(<DocsFailureView answer={answer} onRetry={withHandler ? () => undefined : undefined} />);
    const button = screen.queryByRole('button', { name: 'Retry' });
    unmount();
    return button;
  };

  it('a manual word and an auto word offer Retry; a none word, a stale lock and a missing handler do not', () => {
    expect(retryFor(failed('repo-unreadable'))).not.toBeNull();
    expect(retryFor(failed('docs-busy', { retryAfterMs: 2000 }))).not.toBeNull();
    expect(retryFor(failed('bad-path'))).toBeNull();
    expect(retryFor(failed('ref-locked', { lockAgeMs: 120000 }))).toBeNull();
    expect(retryFor(failed('repo-unreadable'), false)).toBeNull();
  });

  it('a click calls the handler once', () => {
    const onRetry = vi.fn();
    render(<DocsFailureView answer={failed('fetch-failed')} onRetry={onRetry} />);
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Retry' }));
    expect(onRetry).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  it('the slots: unreachable and unexpected-response offer Retry; auth and no-docs-route never do', () => {
    expect(retryFor({ s: 'unreachable' })).not.toBeNull();
    expect(retryFor({ s: 'unexpected-response', status: 502, contentType: 'text/html' })).not.toBeNull();
    expect(retryFor({ s: 'auth' })).toBeNull();
    expect(retryFor({ s: 'no-docs-route' })).toBeNull();
  });

  it('each slot renders its sentence; an unexpected-response with no content type says so', () => {
    const textOf = (answer: DocsNotOk): string | null => {
      const { unmount } = render(<DocsFailureView answer={answer} />);
      const text = screen.getByRole('alert').textContent;
      unmount();
      return text;
    };
    expect(textOf({ s: 'auth' })).toBe('Sign in to read Docs.');
    expect(textOf({ s: 'unreachable' })).toBe('The server could not be reached; Docs needs a connection.');
    expect(textOf({ s: 'unexpected-response', status: 502, contentType: 'text/html' }))
      .toBe('The server answered 502 (text/html).');
    expect(textOf({ s: 'unexpected-response', status: 500, contentType: '' }))
      .toBe('The server answered 500 (no content type).');
  });
});

describe('a pre-Docs server (M4.F6 = M7.1)', () => {
  it('a 404 {error: not-found} with no failure, through createApi, renders "predates Docs" and no docs sentence', async () => {
    const api = createApi((async () => new Response(JSON.stringify({ ok: false, error: 'not-found' }),
      { status: 404, headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8' } })) as typeof fetch);
    const answer = await api.docs.tree('demo', null);
    expect(answer.s).toBe('no-docs-route');
    if (answer.s === 'ok') return;
    render(<DocsFailureView answer={answer} onRetry={() => undefined} />);
    const text = screen.getByRole('alert').textContent ?? '';
    expect(text).toBe('This server predates Docs; update the server box.');
    for (const sentence of Object.values(DOCS_FAILURE_SENTENCE)) expect(text).not.toContain(stem(sentence));
  });
});

```ts
// The Docs client's own words (spec 2026-10-01 4.3, 4.7 and 5.4): the slots a loader answers when the server did not
// answer a page, the answer unions every `api.docs.*` call resolves to, the loader seam `DocsScreen` takes, the one
// classifier from a rejected request to a slot, the two 200-answer readers, and the retry plan with the three waits
// the PWA keeps itself.
//
// A loader NEVER rejects for a docs word or a server answer: a word is `{s: 'failed', body}` (an unknown word from a
// newer server kept whole), and everything else that is not a page is one of the client slots below. It rejects in
// exactly two cases, both the caller's own: an abort (the caller's signal) and a defect (anything that is neither a
// server answer nor a network failure, rethrown as is rather than dressed up as a slot).
import {
  DOCS_FAILURE_RETRY, DOCS_FAILURES, DOCS_RASTER_EXT, DOCS_RASTER_TYPES, contentClass, sniffRaster,
  type DocPin, type DocsFailure, type DocsFailureBody, type DocsFileResponse, type DocsProjectsResponse,
  type DocsRefreshResponse, type DocsRefSpec, type DocsTreeResponse, type RasterMime, type RasterType,
} from '../../../shared/docs';
// A type-only import, erased at build time: lib/api.ts imports this module, so a value import back would be a cycle.
import type { ApiError } from '../lib/api';

/** What a loader answers when the server did not answer a page or a docs word (spec 4.3, 4.7):
 *  - `auth`: a 401; `request` has already raised the login overlay when the body named a verdict.
 *  - `unreachable`: `fetch` rejected (offline, DNS, a dropped connection), or the body could not be read.
 *  - `no-docs-route`: a pre-Docs server, a 404 whose body is `{error: 'not-found'}` with no `failure` (spec 7.1).
 *  - `unexpected-response`: any other answer that is not a docs envelope. `contentType` is the response's
 *    `content-type` header as sent, and `''` has ONE meaning: the response carried no such header. */
export type DocsClientSlot =
  | { s: 'auth' }
  | { s: 'unreachable' }
  | { s: 'no-docs-route' }
  | { s: 'unexpected-response'; status: number; contentType: string };

/** Every arm of a loader's answer that is not a page: a docs word, known or not, or a client slot. */
export type DocsNotOk = { s: 'failed'; body: DocsFailureBody } | DocsClientSlot;

/** A loader's answer: the server's envelope as is, or why there is none. */
export type DocsAnswer<T> = { s: 'ok'; value: T } | DocsNotOk;

export type DocsIndexAnswer = DocsAnswer<DocsProjectsResponse>;
export type DocsTreeAnswer = DocsAnswer<DocsTreeResponse>;
export type DocsFileAnswer = DocsAnswer<DocsFileResponse>;
/** A raster's bytes and its MIME type. `mime` comes from `DOCS_RASTER_TYPES` for the path's declared type, never
 *  from the response or a Blob (spec 5.4). `bytes` is backed by a plain `ArrayBuffer`, which is what a `Blob` part
 *  takes. */
export interface DocsRasterBytes { readonly bytes: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>; readonly mime: RasterMime }
export type DocsRasterAnswer = DocsAnswer<DocsRasterBytes>;
/** Spec 4.3's `DocsRefreshAnswer`, renamed: server/src/docs/policy.ts already exports that name (the route's own
 *  verdict), and single-definition.test.ts holds every server/src/docs export to one declaration in the four roots. */
export type DocsRefreshLoaderAnswer = DocsAnswer<DocsRefreshResponse>;

/** The loader seam (spec 4.3). `api.docs` is the default; tests inject their own.
 *  - `tree`'s `ref: null` is the default view (no `?ref=`).
 *  - `file`'s and `raster`'s `signal` absent means the request is never aborted.
 *  - `refresh`'s `body.ref: null` is the default branch.
 *  - `file` serves every class but `raster` and THROWS `wrong-representation` for a raster path; `raster` serves
 *    the raster class only and throws the same for any other path. Both are programming errors (spec 5.4). */
export interface DocsLoaders {
  projects(): Promise<DocsIndexAnswer>;
  tree(project: string, ref: DocsRefSpec | null): Promise<DocsTreeAnswer>;
  file(project: string, pin: DocPin, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<DocsFileAnswer>;
  raster(project: string, pin: DocPin, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<DocsRasterAnswer>;
  refresh(project: string, body: { ref: string | null; reason: 'auto' | 'manual' }): Promise<DocsRefreshLoaderAnswer>;
}

/** Whether `w` is a word this build knows. An unknown word is kept whole and rendered as unknown, never folded. */
export function isDocsFailureWord(w: string): w is DocsFailure {
  return Object.hasOwn(DOCS_FAILURES, w);
}

/** `ApiError` without importing its class (see the import above): it is the one error that names itself so. */
function isApiError(err: unknown): err is ApiError {
  return err instanceof Error && err.name === 'ApiError';
}

function hasFailureWord(body: unknown): body is DocsFailureBody {
  return typeof body === 'object' && body !== null && typeof (body as { failure?: unknown }).failure === 'string';
}

function errorCodeOf(body: unknown): unknown {
  return typeof body === 'object' && body !== null ? (body as { error?: unknown }).error : undefined;
}

/** A rejected docs request as a slot (refinement (k)), first match wins:
 *  1. an `ApiError` whose body has a string `failure` is that word, known or not, whatever the status;
 *  2. a 401 is `auth` (`request` raised the overlay before it threw, when the body named a verdict);
 *  3. a 404 whose body's `error` is `not-found` is `no-docs-route`: the status AND the code, never either alone;
 *  4. any other `ApiError` is `unexpected-response`;
 *  5. a `TypeError` (what `fetch` and a body read reject with when the network fails) is `unreachable`;
 *  6. anything else is RETHROWN: an abort (the caller's signal: a `DOMException` named `AbortError`, which is
 *     neither of the two above), for which there is no slot, and a defect. */
export function docsAnswerFromError(err: unknown): DocsNotOk {
  if (isApiError(err)) {
    if (hasFailureWord(err.body)) return { s: 'failed', body: err.body };
    if (err.status === 401) return { s: 'auth' };
    if (err.status === 404 && errorCodeOf(err.body) === 'not-found') return { s: 'no-docs-route' };
    return { s: 'unexpected-response', status: err.status, contentType: err.contentType ?? '' };
  }
  if (err instanceof TypeError) return { s: 'unreachable' };
  throw err;
}

function unexpected(res: Response): DocsClientSlot {
  return { s: 'unexpected-response', status: res.status, contentType: res.headers.get('content-type') ?? '' };
}

/** A 2xx JSON answer as the route's envelope: an object with `ok: true` and every one of `fields` present. Anything
 *  else (a proxy's page, a JSON that is not an object, `ok` not `true`, a field missing) is `unexpected-response`
 *  with the response's own status and content type. A body that cannot be read rejects (a `TypeError`), for the
 *  caller's `docsAnswerFromError`. */
export async function readDocsEnvelope<T>(res: Response, fields: readonly string[]): Promise<DocsAnswer<T>> {
  const text = await res.text();
  let value: unknown;
  try {
    value = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    return unexpected(res);
  }
  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null) return unexpected(res);
  const record = value as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (record['ok'] !== true || fields.some((f) => record[f] === undefined)) return unexpected(res);
  return { s: 'ok', value: value as T };
}

/** The raster type a path declares, or `null`, whose one meaning is "`contentClass(path)` is not `raster`". When
 *  `contentClass` says raster, the extension is one of `DOCS_RASTER_EXT`'s keys after ASCII-only lowering, so every
 *  character of it is ASCII and `toLowerCase` lowers it the same way. A raster class with no table entry would mean
 *  L0's two tables disagree: a defect, thrown. */
export function declaredRaster(path: string): RasterType | null {
  if (contentClass(path) !== 'raster') return null;
  const name = path.slice(path.lastIndexOf('/') + 1);
  const ext = name.slice(name.lastIndexOf('.') + 1).toLowerCase();
  if (!Object.hasOwn(DOCS_RASTER_EXT, ext)) throw new Error(`declaredRaster: no raster type for '${path}'`);
  return DOCS_RASTER_EXT[ext as keyof typeof DOCS_RASTER_EXT];
}

/** A 2xx raster answer, checked twice (spec 5.4, M5.18): its `content-type` must EQUAL the declared type's MIME, else
 *  `unexpected-response`; then `sniffRaster` must match, else a client-built `raster-mismatch {declared, size}`. */
export async function readDocsRaster(res: Response, declared: RasterType): Promise<DocsRasterAnswer> {
  const mime = DOCS_RASTER_TYPES[declared].mime;
  if (res.headers.get('content-type') !== mime) return unexpected(res);
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(await res.arrayBuffer());
  if (sniffRaster(declared, bytes) === 'mismatch') {
    return { s: 'failed', body: { ok: false, failure: 'raster-mismatch', declared, size: bytes.byteLength } };
  }
  return { s: 'ok', value: { bytes, mime } };
}

/** The PWA's own waits (spec 4.7, refinement (l)). The server's `Retry-After` never reaches the PWA (`ApiError`
 *  keeps no headers), and `caps-unknown` carries no wait in its body, so these three are the client's. */
export const DOCS_REF_LOCKED_RETRY_MS = 3000;
/** A `ref-locked` lock at least this old is stale: no automatic retry, "stale lock on {ref}". */
export const DOCS_LOCK_STALE_MS = 60000;
export const DOCS_CAPS_UNKNOWN_RETRY_MS = 5000;

/** What a page offers on a failure: one automatic retry after `afterMs`, a Retry button, or nothing. */
export type DocsRetryPlan = { kind: 'auto'; afterMs: number } | { kind: 'manual' } | { kind: 'none' };

/** The retry plan for one failure body, from L0's `DOCS_FAILURE_RETRY` (spec 4.7, refinement (l)):
 *  - an unknown word: `none` (its sentence says to reload; the same server would answer the same word);
 *  - `none` and `manual`: as the class says;
 *  - `auto`: wait the body's `retryAfterMs` when it is a finite number at least 0, else 5 000 ms for
 *    `caps-unknown`, else 0;
 *  - `ref-locked` (`auto-while-young`): `lockAgeMs` a number under 60 000, or `null` (the lock already went), waits
 *    3 000 ms; a number at or over 60 000 is `none` (a stale lock); ABSENT (ccd could not measure it) is `manual`,
 *    never folded into `null`. */
export function docsRetryPlan(body: DocsFailureBody): DocsRetryPlan {
  const word: string = body.failure;
  if (!isDocsFailureWord(word)) return { kind: 'none' };
  const cls = DOCS_FAILURE_RETRY[word];
  if (cls === 'none') return { kind: 'none' };
  if (cls === 'manual') return { kind: 'manual' };
  if (cls === 'auto-while-young') {
    const age = body.lockAgeMs;
    if (age === undefined) return { kind: 'manual' };
    if (age === null || age < DOCS_LOCK_STALE_MS) return { kind: 'auto', afterMs: DOCS_REF_LOCKED_RETRY_MS };
    return { kind: 'none' };
  }
  const after = body.retryAfterMs;
  if (typeof after === 'number' && Number.isFinite(after) && after >= 0) return { kind: 'auto', afterMs: after };
  return { kind: 'auto', afterMs: word === 'caps-unknown' ? DOCS_CAPS_UNKNOWN_RETRY_MS : 0 };
}
```

export const DOCS_SLOT_SENTENCE: Record<DocsClientSlot['s'], string> = {
  'auth': 'Sign in to read Docs.',
  'unreachable': 'The server could not be reached; Docs needs a connection.',
  'no-docs-route': 'This server predates Docs; update the server box.',
  'unexpected-response': 'The server answered {status} ({contentType}).',

type TriedResult = NonNullable<DocsFailureContext['tried']>[number]['result'];

export const TRIED_RESULT_TEXT: Record<TriedResult, string> = {
  'resolved': 'resolved',
  'absent': 'not found',
  'dangling': 'points at a missing branch',

/** `unresolved-ref {hint: 'tag'}` (spec 4.7). */

/** A word this build does not know, from a newer server (spec 4.7, verbatim): never folded into a known one. */
export function unknownWordSentence(word: string): string {
  return fillSentence("The server answered '{word}', which this app version does not know; reload to update.", { word });
}

/** Fill every `{name}` in `template` from `fields`, in one pass: a field that is absent renders `?`, and a value
 *  that itself holds braces is not filled again. */
export function fillSentence(template: string, fields: Readonly<Record<string, string | number>>): string {
  return template.replace(/\{([A-Za-z]+)\}/g, (_m: string, name: string) =>
    Object.hasOwn(fields, name) ? String(fields[name]) : '?');
}

/** A byte count in KiB, rounded up, so a non-empty file never reads as 0. */
export function kib(bytes: number): string {
  return `${Math.ceil(bytes / 1024)} KiB`;
}

/** A commit's short form: its first 8 hex characters, everywhere (refinement (s)). */
export function shortCommit(sha: string): string {
  return sha.slice(0, 8);
}

/** The sentence for one failure body: a known word's sentence filled from the body's own context (sizes in KiB), or
 *  the unknown-word sentence naming the word. */
export function failureSentence(body: DocsFailureBody): string {
  const word: string = body.failure;
  if (!isDocsFailureWord(word)) return unknownWordSentence(word);
  const fields: Record<string, string | number> = {};
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(body)) {
    if (typeof value === 'string' || (typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value))) fields[name] = value;
  }
  if (typeof body.size === 'number') fields['size'] = kib(body.size);
  if (typeof body.cap === 'number') fields['cap'] = kib(body.cap);
  return fillSentence(DOCS_FAILURE_SENTENCE[word], fields);
}

/** The sentence for a client slot; an `unexpected-response` with no content-type header says so in words. */
export function slotSentence(slot: DocsClientSlot): string {
  if (slot.s !== 'unexpected-response') return DOCS_SLOT_SENTENCE[slot.s];
  return fillSentence(DOCS_SLOT_SENTENCE['unexpected-response'],
    { status: slot.status, contentType: slot.contentType === '' ? 'no content type' : slot.contentType });
}

```tsx
// What a Docs page shows in place of a listing or a body when a loader answered no page (spec 2026-10-01 4.7): the
// sentence, the context its word names, and the actions its retry class allows. A pure renderer: the caller decides
// WHEN an action is offered by passing its handler (an absent handler means the action is not offered), and this
// view decides only WHETHER the answer allows it at all (a `none` word never shows Retry, whatever is passed).
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { docsRetryPlan, type DocsNotOk } from './failures';
import {
  NOT_A_FILE_KIND_TEXT, TRIED_RESULT_TEXT, UNRESOLVED_TAG_HINT, failureSentence, slotSentence,
} from './docsText';

export interface DocsFailureViewProps {
  readonly answer: DocsNotOk;
  /** Retry the read that failed. Absent: no Retry is offered. */
  readonly onRetry?: () => void;
  /** `unresolved-ref`'s manual fetch (`reason: 'manual'`). Absent: not offered. */
  readonly onFetchFromOrigin?: () => void;
  /** The page URL for `unresolved-ref`'s `suggest`. Absent: the suggestion is shown as text, not as a link. */
  readonly suggestHref?: (name: string) => string;
}

/** Whether the answer allows a Retry at all: a word by its retry plan, a slot by what it is. `auth` re-fetches on
 *  sign-in and `no-docs-route` cannot change by retrying, so neither offers one. */
function allowsRetry(answer: DocsNotOk): boolean {
  switch (answer.s) {
    case 'failed':
      return docsRetryPlan(answer.body).kind !== 'none';
    case 'unreachable':
    case 'unexpected-response':
      return true;
    case 'auth':
    case 'no-docs-route':
      return false;
  }
}

function FailureContext(p: { readonly answer: DocsNotOk; readonly suggestHref?: (name: string) => string }): ReactNode {
  if (p.answer.s !== 'failed') return null;
  const body = p.answer.body;
  const word: string = body.failure;
  const parts: ReactNode[] = [];
  if (word === 'unresolved-ref') {
    if (body.tried !== undefined && body.tried.length > 0) {
      parts.push(
        <ul key="tried" className="docs-fail-list">
          {body.tried.map((t, i) => (
            <li key={i}><code>{t.ref}</code> {TRIED_RESULT_TEXT[t.result] ?? t.result}</li>
          ))}
        </ul>,
      );
    }
    if (typeof body.suggest === 'string' && body.suggest !== '') {
      parts.push(
        <p key="suggest" className="docs-fail-suggest">
          Did you mean{' '}
          {p.suggestHref === undefined
            ? <code>{body.suggest}</code>
            : <a href={p.suggestHref(body.suggest)}>{body.suggest}</a>}
          ?
        </p>,
      );
    }
    if (body.hint === 'tag') parts.push(<p key="hint" className="docs-fail-hint">{UNRESOLVED_TAG_HINT}</p>);
  }
  if (word === 'ambiguous-worktree' && body.candidates !== undefined) {
    parts.push(
      <ul key="candidates" className="docs-fail-list">
        {body.candidates.map((c) => <li key={c}><code>{c}</code></li>)}
      </ul>,
    );
  }
  if (word === 'not-a-file' && body.kind !== undefined && Object.hasOwn(NOT_A_FILE_KIND_TEXT, body.kind)) {
    parts.push(<p key="kind" className="docs-fail-kind">{NOT_A_FILE_KIND_TEXT[body.kind]}</p>);
  }
  if (typeof body.stderrHead === 'string' && body.stderrHead !== '') {
    parts.push(<pre key="stderr" className="docs-fail-detail">{body.stderrHead}</pre>);
  }
  return parts;
}

export function DocsFailureView(p: DocsFailureViewProps): ReactNode {
  const { answer } = p;
  const sentence = answer.s === 'failed' ? failureSentence(answer.body) : slotSentence(answer);
  const retry = p.onRetry !== undefined && allowsRetry(answer) ? p.onRetry : undefined;
  const fetchFromOrigin =
    answer.s === 'failed' && answer.body.failure === 'unresolved-ref' ? p.onFetchFromOrigin : undefined;
  return (
    <section
      className="docs-fail"
      role="alert"
      data-state={answer.s}
      data-failure={answer.s === 'failed' ? answer.body.failure : undefined}
    >
      <p className="docs-fail-sentence">{sentence}</p>
      <FailureContext answer={answer} suggestHref={p.suggestHref} />
      {(retry !== undefined || fetchFromOrigin !== undefined) && (
        <div className="docs-fail-actions">
          {fetchFromOrigin !== undefined && (
            <button type="button" className="btn-ghost docs-fail-action" onClick={fetchFromOrigin}>
              Fetch from origin
            </button>
          )}
          {retry !== undefined && (
            <button type="button" className="btn-ghost docs-fail-action" onClick={retry}>Retry</button>
          )}
        </div>
      )}
    </section>
  );
}
```

Replace with:
```ts
      const res = await request(`${sid(id)}/upload`, { method: 'POST', body: form });
      return ((await res.json()) as { clip: StagedClip }).clip;
    },
    /**
     * The Docs reader's loaders (spec 2026-10-01 4.3, 5.4): `DocsScreen`'s default `DocsLoaders`. Every call goes
     * through `request`, so a 401 still raises the one login overlay, and carries the marker header through
     * `DOCS_REQUEST_HEADER`/`DOCS_REQUEST_HEADER_VALUE` to the URL L0's `docsApi` builds. Each resolves a union and
     * never rejects for a server answer (`docs/failures.ts`): it rejects only when the caller's signal aborts, or for
     * a defect. `file` and `raster` refuse each other's paths by throwing `wrong-representation` before any request.
     */
    docs: ((): DocsLoaders => {
      const marker = { [DOCS_REQUEST_HEADER]: DOCS_REQUEST_HEADER_VALUE };
      const read = async <T>(path: string, fields: readonly string[], init: RequestInit): Promise<DocsAnswer<T>> => {
        try {
          return await readDocsEnvelope<T>(await request(path, init), fields);
        } catch (err) {
          return docsAnswerFromError(err);
        }
      };
      return {
        projects: () => read<DocsProjectsResponse>(docsApi.projects(), ['index'], { headers: marker }),
        tree: (project, ref) =>
          read<DocsTreeResponse>(docsApi.tree(project, ref), ['tree', 'refreshDue'], { headers: marker }),
        file: (project, pin, signal) => {
          if (contentClass(pin.path) === 'raster') throw new Error('wrong-representation');
          return read<DocsFileResponse>(docsApi.file(project, pin), ['contentClass', 'show'], { headers: marker, signal });
        },
        raster: (project, pin, signal) => {
          const declared = declaredRaster(pin.path);
          if (declared === null) throw new Error('wrong-representation');
          return (async () => {
            try {
              return await readDocsRaster(await request(docsApi.file(project, pin), { headers: marker, signal }), declared);
            } catch (err) {
              return docsAnswerFromError(err);
            }
          })();
        },
        refresh: (project, body) => read<DocsRefreshResponse>(docsApi.refresh(project), ['fetch', 'tree'], {
          method: 'POST',
          headers: { ...marker, 'content-type': 'application/json' },
          body: JSON.stringify({ ref: body.ref, reason: body.reason }),
        }),
      };
    })(),
  };
}
```

### Task 3: Bound W4's r10, r11 and 2-2 in the shared Markdown pipeline, each value measured and stated: no highlighting past a 256-character word, no chord past 64 characters, and the parse's element count includes the chips inline code draws

**Model routing:** `sonnet`, effort `high`. Four small edits to the shared Markdown modules and their tests; no package, no CSS, no new import edge. The judgment is in WHERE each bound sits (the word scan before highlight.js, the length check before the trim and the split, the chip count inside the parse so `too-wide` fires before any render) and in the count being exactly what the component draws, which the measured corpus decides (decision 1).

**Spec rows:** W5 bound r10, W5 bound r11 and W5 bound 2-2 (the coordinator's ruling of 2026-10-13: each a case and a mutation row, by name); section 4.10's "Bounds on the shared components" (the values, chat and docs alike); section 4.12's chat clause (the component bounds reach chat: chat's worker path gains the 2-2 count, its synchronous path the r10 and r11 bounds); section 4.9's limits table (two new limits, declared once). Refinements applied: (d) the 2-2 bound is the parse's own element count, (e) `MD_HIGHLIGHT_MAX_WORD_CHARS = 256`, (f) `MD_KEYSTROKE_MAX_CHARS = 64`, (g) the count measured on real documents. Refinement (d) is one of the plan's five deviations; this task builds it and Task 12's last step defines it. Decision 1 below narrows (d)'s count from the architecture's upper bound to the exact count, which keeps (d)'s departure as it is (the bound stays in the parse's count, not in the components) and changes only how many elements a non-chord span adds.

**Files:**
- Create: `pwa/test/markdown-bounds.test.tsx` (212 lines, 17 cases) — the three bounds, each by name: r10 (seven cases), r11 (four), 2-2 (six).

- Modify: `pwa/src/lib/markdownGuard.ts` — two Find/Replace edits (line 1, the header's first line; line 17, its one import) and an end-of-file append: `keystrokeParts`, `NAMED_KEY` and `SINGLE` move here from `markdown.tsx` (decision 1), with r11's length check first. 227 lines become 246.

**Decisions this task makes** (1-3 adapt the architecture's entry for this task to measured facts; none departs from the spec's text beyond refinement (d), which Task 12 defines):
1. **The 2-2 count is EXACT, so `keystrokeParts` moves into the worker closure.** The architecture's rule (every inline `code` of at most 64 characters adds `2 x (its '+' count) + 1`) adds one element for EVERY short span, chord or not. Measured in Step 0 over the 317 `.md` files under `docs/superpowers`, it pushes four real plans and specs over `DOCS_MAX_RENDER_ELEMENTS` (the largest from 16 968 to 25 752), each of which would then render as plain text: refinement (g)'s stop condition. The exact count (what the component draws) moves no real document (largest 16 968 before and after; the golden corpus' largest 23 before, 26 after). An exact count needs the component's own predicate in the worker, so `keystrokeParts` with `NAMED_KEY` and `SINGLE` (byte-identical regular expressions) moves from `markdown.tsx` to `markdownGuard.ts`, which BOTH `markdownParse.ts` and `markdown.tsx` already import: no import edge and no file is added to either closure (`markdown-purity.test.ts`'s `ROOTS` and `ALLOWED_PACKAGES` unchanged, as Global Constraints require). `inlineCodeExtraElements` keeps the architecture's name and test seam. The component and the count call one function, so they cannot drift.
2. **The 2-2 red cases use 400 chords, not 20 000.** Twenty thousand spans are `too-wide` before this task too (20 000 `code` elements and a `p` make 20 001), so that case could not be red first. A 31-plus chord (32 single-character parts, 63 characters, within r11) draws 64 elements a span: 400 spans count 1 + 400 x 64 = 25 601 (`too-wide`; 401 before this task, a tree), and 300 spans count 19 201 (a tree), whose rendered DOM holds exactly 19 201 elements, so the count is what renders. The built-artefact case uses the same 400. W4's measured shape (50 chords of 2 048 parts) is kept as a case: each span is 4 095 characters, so r11 makes it plain code and it parses as a tree of 51 elements.
3. **W4's two chat cases that pinned 2 048-part chips are re-derived, not deleted.** r11 changes chat's rendering of a chord span over 64 characters: it was chips up to 2 048 parts, it is now plain inline code. "the longest chord a 4 KiB message can hold is still chips" and "keystrokeParts answers null past CHAT_SYNC_MAX_BYTES / 2 parts" go red under the new code (measured at Task 3's code with the old texts of `chat-hardening.test.tsx` and `markdown-limits.test.ts`: `3 failed | 134 passed (137)`, the third being the limits file's "eleven" title), so each is rewritten in place to the new bound (32 parts chips, 33 plain, the 2 048-part chord `null`). No golden case holds an accepted span over 16 characters (Step 0), so every golden file stays byte-identical, which `CI=1` proves.
4. **What the count reads.** `measure` keeps a parallel stack of parent tag names (an explicit stack, as before: no recursion), and an inline `code`'s text is its `text` children's values joined, which is what react-markdown hands the component (one text child for an inline code span). A fenced block's `code` (parent `pre`) adds nothing: `CodeBlock` renders it and draws no chips. A span holding a newline cannot arrive (CommonMark turns line endings in a code span into spaces); were one to, the count would add at most what `keystrokeParts` accepts while the component would draw a plain `code`, so the count stays an upper bound.
5. **r10's scan and label.** `longestWordRun` runs only for a block highlight.js would be asked to colour (registered, not `highlight={false}`, within the size cap), so it costs one linear pass over at most 65 536 characters. The class is the one Step 0 measured slow (`[A-Za-z0-9_$]`: a run of digits, of `_` or of hex is as slow as letters in `bash`); a run of non-ASCII letters measured under 1 ms at 16 384 characters in `typescript` and `bash`, so it is outside the class by measurement, not by assumption.
6. **Cheap reds.** Every case that asserts `hljs.highlight` is not called spies it with an empty answer, and r11's ordering case spies `String.prototype.split` with a fixed answer and reads its call count before restoring it, so a red run never pays the quadratic cost. The one deliberately costly case is r11's time-boxed control (under 1 s; measured 8.5-9.8 s unbounded at load 35), a second, non-row case beside the ordering case that carries r11's row.

Many grammars' worst shapes cost 100-370 ms at EVERY line length (for example `javascript` over `(`, about 250-300 ms), so no line bound brings them to ordinary code's cost; only two families grow with line length: `markdown` over `[` 79 / 120 / 245 / 380 / 451 / 1 772 ms at 512 / 1 024 / 2 048 / 3 072 / 4 096 / 16 384, `markdown` over `[[` 64 / 116 / 306 / 376 / 468 / 1 921 ms, and `yaml` over `W ` and `m ` 148-163 / 193-202 / 247-256 / 243-279 / 255-302 ms at 512-4 096. The basis is the coordinator's reading of the ruling (mail 4768): the line bound removes the cost that GROWS with line length, so it stops where that growth meets the length-independent plateau; at 2 048 the worst line-driven shape costs 245-263 ms, the plateau, where 4 096 would cost about twice it. **The corpus** (a snapshot, measured 2026-10-14 before this plan's own rows blocks grew): the longest line in a registered fence was 2 927 characters; the bound left 1 real fence plain at 2 048 (30 at 1 024, 163 at 512), beside the 3 blocks the size cap already leaves plain. A departure from §4.10's three bounds, defined in `## Deviations found`. interface HNode { type: string; tagName?: string; value?: string; properties?: { className?: unknown }; children?: HNode[] }

/** The text of every descendant text node, explicit stack. */
function textOf(n: HNode): string {
  let out = '';
  const stack: HNode[] = [n];
  while (stack.length > 0) {
    const x = stack.pop()!;
    if (x.type === 'text') out += x.value ?? '';
    if (x.children) for (let i = x.children.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) stack.push(x.children[i]!);
  }
  return out;
}

/** The longest run of [A-Za-z0-9_$]. */
function longestRun(s: string): number {
  let best = 0;
  let run = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i += 1) {
    const c = s.charCodeAt(i);
    const w = (c >= 48 && c <= 57) || (c >= 65 && c <= 90) || (c >= 97 && c <= 122) || c === 95 || c === 36;
    run = w ? run + 1 : 0;
    if (run > best) best = run;
  }
  return best;
}

interface Stat { file: string; value: number }
function corpusStats(docs: readonly { file: string; src: string; profile: MarkdownProfile }[]) {
  let word: Stat = { file: '', value: 0 };
  let span: Stat = { file: '', value: 0 };
  let before: Stat = { file: '', value: 0 };
  let after: Stat = { file: '', value: 0 };
  let afterLoose: Stat = { file: '', value: 0 };
  const longChips: string[] = [];
  const notTree: string[] = [];
  const crossings: string[] = [];
  const crossingsLoose: string[] = [];
  for (const d of docs) {
    const o = parseMarkdown(d.src, d.profile);
    if (o.kind !== 'tree') {
      notTree.push(`${d.file}: ${JSON.stringify(o)}`);
      continue;
    }
    let elements = 0;
    let extra = 0;
    let loose = 0;
    const stack: { n: HNode; parent: string }[] = [{ n: o.tree as unknown as HNode, parent: '' }];
    while (stack.length > 0) {
      const { n, parent } = stack.pop()!;
      if (n.type === 'element') {
        elements += 1;
        if (n.tagName === 'code') {
          const text = textOf(n);
          const cls = n.properties?.className;
          const lang = Array.isArray(cls) ? String(cls.find((c) => String(c).startsWith('language-')) ?? '').slice(9) : '';
          if (parent === 'pre') {
            if (lang && hljs.getLanguage(lang)) {
              const r = longestRun(text);
              if (r > word.value) word = { file: d.file, value: r };
            }
          } else {
            // The architecture's first rule, recorded for comparison: 2 x (its '+' count) + 1 for every span of at
            // most 64 characters, chord or not.
            if (text.length <= 64) loose += 2 * (text.split('+').length - 1) + 1;
            const keys = keystrokeParts(text);
            // The chips the component would draw for this span under r11 (at most 64 characters): 2 x parts - 1
            // more elements than the one `code` the walk already counted.
            if (keys !== null && text.length <= 64) extra += 2 * keys.length - 1;
            if (keys !== null) {
              if (text.length > span.value) span = { file: d.file, value: text.length };
              if (text.length > 64) longChips.push(`${d.file}: ${text.length}`);
            }
          }
        }
      }
      if (n.children) for (const c of n.children) stack.push({ n: c, parent: n.type === 'element' ? n.tagName ?? '' : '' });
    }
    if (elements <= 20000 && elements + extra > 20000) crossings.push(`${d.file}: ${elements} -> ${elements + extra}`);
    if (elements <= 20000 && elements + loose > 20000) crossingsLoose.push(`${d.file}: ${elements} -> ${elements + loose}`);
    if (elements > before.value) before = { file: d.file, value: elements };
    if (elements + loose > afterLoose.value) afterLoose = { file: d.file, value: elements + loose };
    if (elements + extra > after.value) after = { file: d.file, value: elements + extra };
  }
  return { docs: docs.length, word, span, before, after, crossings, afterLoose, crossingsLoose, longChips, notTree };
}

function mdFiles(dir: string): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  const dirs = [dir];
  while (dirs.length > 0) {
    const d = dirs.pop()!;
    for (const e of readdirSync(d, { withFileTypes: true })) {
      const p = path.join(d, e.name);
      if (e.isDirectory()) dirs.push(p);
      else if (e.isFile() && e.name.endsWith('.md')) out.push(p);
    }
  }
  return out.sort();
}

it('corpus', () => {
  const tags = [...new Set([...hljs.listLanguages(), ...CHAT_ALIAS_TAGS, ...CHAT_UNREGISTERED_TAGS])];
  const golden = [...CHAT_CORPUS, ...languageCases(tags), RECAP_CASE]
    .map((c) => ({ file: c.name, src: c.text, profile: 'chat' as const }));

    .map((f) => ({ file: path.relative(REPO, f), src: readFileSync(f, 'utf8'), profile: 'docs' as const }));
  print({ case: 'corpus', ...env(), golden: corpusStats(golden), docs: corpusStats(docs) });
}, 590_000);

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the bounds' test.** Create `pwa/test/markdown-bounds.test.tsx` with exactly this content (the middle dot in the expected labels is U+00B7, as `CodeBlock`'s existing label spells it; every fixture is generated, no host, user or path):

```tsx
// Docs W5 part 1, Task 3: the three bounds on the shared Markdown pipeline (spec 2026-10-01 section 4.10's "Bounds
// on the shared components" and section 4.12's chat clause; the plan's refinements (d), (e), (f) and (g); the
// coordinator's ruling of 2026-10-13: each bound carries a case here and a mutation row, by name).
//   r10: `CodeBlock` never asks highlight.js to colour a block holding a run of `[A-Za-z0-9_$]` longer than
//        `MD_HIGHLIGHT_MAX_WORD_CHARS` (one such run costs the square of its length in four grammars).
//   r11: `keystrokeParts` answers `null` for a span longer than `MD_KEYSTROKE_MAX_CHARS` before it trims or splits
//        (the split's pattern backtracks over a run of whitespace).
//   2-2: the parse's element count includes the chips `SHARED_COMPONENTS.code` draws for inline code, so `too-wide`
//        fires in the parse, before anything renders, for docs and for chat's worker path alike.
// Every parse here is `parseMarkdown`, the function the worker runs; chat's worker path gets it through an injected
// parser. `hljs.highlight` is spied where a case asserts it is not called, and answers nothing, so a red run never
// pays for a long word.
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { act, cleanup, render } from '@testing-library/react';
import hljs from 'highlight.js/lib/core';
import type { Root as HastRoot } from 'hast';
import { ChatMarkdown, CodeBlock, SHARED_COMPONENTS, longestWordRun } from '../src/lib/markdown';
import { keystrokeParts, utf8ByteLength } from '../src/lib/markdownGuard';
import {
  CHAT_SYNC_MAX_BYTES, DOCS_MAX_RENDER_ELEMENTS, MD_HIGHLIGHT_MAX_WORD_CHARS, MD_KEYSTROKE_MAX_CHARS,
} from '../src/lib/markdownLimits';
import { inlineCodeExtraElements, parseMarkdown, type MarkdownProfile } from '../src/lib/markdownParse';
import type { MarkdownParser } from '../src/lib/markdownRunner';
import { renderHast } from '../src/lib/renderHast';

afterEach(() => {
  cleanup();
  vi.restoreAllMocks();
});

/** Spies `hljs.highlight` and answers an empty highlight: a case that counts calls never pays for one. */
const spyHighlight = () =>
  vi.spyOn(hljs, 'highlight').mockReturnValue({ value: '' } as unknown as ReturnType<typeof hljs.highlight>);

/** One fenced block, as react-markdown hands it to the `pre` component. */
function block(lang: string, body: string): HTMLElement {
  return render(
    <CodeBlock>
      <code className={`language-${lang}`}>{`${body}\n`}</code>
    </CodeBlock>,
  ).container;
}

const label = (c: HTMLElement): string | null | undefined => c.querySelector('.code-block-lang')?.textContent;

/** The tree `parseMarkdown` gives `src`, or a thrown error naming the outcome that was not a tree. */
function treeOf(src: string, profile: MarkdownProfile): HastRoot {
  const o = parseMarkdown(src, profile);
  if (o.kind !== 'tree') throw new Error(`not a tree: ${JSON.stringify(o)}`);
  return o.tree;
}

/** Chat's Markdown for `text` through an injected parser that answers what the worker would, settled. */
async function chat(text: string) {
  const parser = vi.fn<MarkdownParser>((src, opts) => Promise.resolve(parseMarkdown(src, opts.profile)));
  const r = render(<div className="msg-assist"><ChatMarkdown text={text} parser={parser} /></div>);
  await act(async () => {
    await Promise.resolve();
  });
  return { ...r, parser };
}

/** A chord of `n` single-character parts: `a+a+...+a`, 2n - 1 characters. */
const chord = (n: number): string => `${'a+'.repeat(n - 1)}a`;
/** `n` inline code spans of `span`, one paragraph. */
const spans = (n: number, span: string): string => Array.from({ length: n }, () => `\`${span}\``).join(' ');

describe('W5 bound r10: no highlighting for a block holding a word longer than MD_HIGHLIGHT_MAX_WORD_CHARS', () => {
  it('a ts fence holding a 257-character identifier is not highlighted and says why; 256 is highlighted', () => {
    const highlight = spyHighlight();
    const over = `const ${'a'.repeat(257)} = 1;`;
    const c = block('ts', over);
    expect(highlight).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(label(c)).toBe('TypeScript · not highlighted (a 257-character word)');
    expect(c.querySelector('pre > code.hljs')?.textContent).toBe(over);
    cleanup();
    const at = block('ts', `const ${'a'.repeat(256)} = 1;`);
    expect(highlight).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(label(at)).toBe('TypeScript');
  });

  it('a 32 KiB one-identifier ts fence through SHARED_COMPONENTS never reaches highlight.js', () => {
    const highlight = spyHighlight();
    const { container } = render(renderHast(treeOf(`\`\`\`ts\n${'a'.repeat(32768)}\n\`\`\`\n`, 'docs'), { components: SHARED_COMPONENTS }));
    expect(highlight).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(label(container)).toBe('TypeScript · not highlighted (a 32768-character word)');
  });

  it("the same fence through chat's worker path (ChatMarkdown, injected parser) never reaches highlight.js", async () => {
    const highlight = spyHighlight();
    const text = `\`\`\`ts\n${'a'.repeat(32768)}\n\`\`\`\n`;
    expect(utf8ByteLength(text)).toBeGreaterThan(CHAT_SYNC_MAX_BYTES);
    const { container, parser } = await chat(text);
    expect(parser).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(container.querySelector('pre.msg-plain')).toBeNull();
    expect(highlight).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(label(container)).toBe('TypeScript · not highlighted (a 32768-character word)');
  });

  it('a block over MD_HIGHLIGHT_BLOCK_MAX_CHARS keeps its size label even when it holds a long word', () => {
    const highlight = spyHighlight();
    expect(label(block('ts', 'a'.repeat(70000)))).toBe('TypeScript · not highlighted (69 KiB)');
    expect(highlight).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('an unregistered fence keeps its plain label whatever its words', () => {
    const highlight = spyHighlight();
    expect(label(block('mermaid', 'a'.repeat(300)))).toBe('mermaid');
    expect(highlight).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('ordinary code still highlights', () => {
    const c = block('ts', 'const answer = 42; // the answer');
    expect(label(c)).toBe('TypeScript');
    expect(c.querySelectorAll('.hljs-keyword').length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  it('longestWordRun counts letters, digits, _ and $ only, in one pass', () => {
    expect(longestWordRun('')).toBe(0);
    expect(longestWordRun('ab cd')).toBe(2);
    expect(longestWordRun('a_b$c9')).toBe(6);
    expect(longestWordRun('a-b.c')).toBe(1);
    expect(longestWordRun('é'.repeat(300))).toBe(0);
    expect(longestWordRun(`${'x'.repeat(300)} ${'y'.repeat(5)}`)).toBe(300);
    expect(longestWordRun('Z'.repeat(MD_HIGHLIGHT_MAX_WORD_CHARS + 1))).toBe(257);
  });
});

describe('W5 bound r11: a code span longer than MD_KEYSTROKE_MAX_CHARS is never a chord', () => {
  it('keystrokeParts answers null for a whitespace flood before it trims or splits', () => {
    const raw = `a${' '.repeat(80000)}b`;
    const split = vi.spyOn(String.prototype, 'split').mockImplementation(() => ['a', 'b']);
    const trim = vi.spyOn(String.prototype, 'trim');
    const got = keystrokeParts(raw);
    const splits = split.mock.calls.length;
    const trims = trim.mock.calls.length;
    split.mockRestore();
    trim.mockRestore();
    expect(got).toBeNull();
    expect(splits).toBe(0);
    expect(trims).toBe(0);
  });

  it('control: the 80 000-space flood answers in under a second', () => {
    const t = performance.now();
    expect(keystrokeParts(`a${' '.repeat(80000)}b`)).toBeNull();
    expect(performance.now() - t).toBeLessThan(1000);
  }, 60_000);

  it('a 64-character chord still draws chips; a 65-character one is plain inline code', () => {
    const at = `Esc+${'a+'.repeat(29)}Fn`;
    const over = `Esc+${'a+'.repeat(29)}Tab`;
    expect([at.length, over.length]).toEqual([MD_KEYSTROKE_MAX_CHARS, MD_KEYSTROKE_MAX_CHARS + 1]);
    expect(keystrokeParts(at)).toHaveLength(31);
    expect(keystrokeParts(over)).toBeNull();
    const chips = render(renderHast(treeOf(`Press \`${at}\` now.`, 'docs'), { components: SHARED_COMPONENTS })).container;
    expect(chips.querySelectorAll('kbd')).toHaveLength(31);
    cleanup();
    const plain = render(renderHast(treeOf(`Press \`${over}\` now.`, 'docs'), { components: SHARED_COMPONENTS })).container;
    expect(plain.querySelectorAll('kbd')).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(plain.querySelector('code.md-code')?.textContent).toBe(over);
  });

  it("W4's measured shape, 50 chords of 2 048 parts, is plain code now and parses as a tree", () => {
    const long = chord(2048);
    expect(keystrokeParts(long)).toBeNull();
    expect(inlineCodeExtraElements(long)).toBe(0);
    expect(parseMarkdown(spans(50, long), 'docs').kind).toBe('tree');
  });
});

describe("W5 bound 2-2: the parse's element count includes the chips inline code draws", () => {
  // A 31-plus chord: 32 single-character parts, 63 characters, so within r11. One span draws `span.kbd-combo`,
  // 32 `kbd` and 31 `span.kbd-plus` (64 elements) where the walk counted one `code`.
  const CHORD = chord(32);
  const PER_SPAN = 2 * 32;

  it('inlineCodeExtraElements: a chord of N parts adds 2N - 1, a named key 1, anything else 0', () => {
    expect(inlineCodeExtraElements('Ctrl+Shift+P')).toBe(5);
    expect(inlineCodeExtraElements('Esc')).toBe(1);
    expect(inlineCodeExtraElements(CHORD)).toBe(PER_SPAN - 1);
    expect(inlineCodeExtraElements('npm test')).toBe(0);
    expect(inlineCodeExtraElements('')).toBe(0);
    expect(inlineCodeExtraElements(chord(33))).toBe(0);
  });

  it.each<MarkdownProfile>(['docs', 'chat'])('400 spans of a 31-plus chord are too-wide in the %s profile, before any render', (profile) => {
    expect(parseMarkdown(spans(400, CHORD), profile)).toEqual({ kind: 'too-wide', elements: 1 + 400 * PER_SPAN });
  });

  it('300 such spans are a tree, and the DOM it draws holds exactly the counted elements', () => {
    const tree = treeOf(spans(300, CHORD), 'docs');
    const { container } = render(renderHast(tree, { components: SHARED_COMPONENTS }));
    expect(container.querySelectorAll('kbd')).toHaveLength(300 * 32);
    expect(container.querySelectorAll('*')).toHaveLength(1 + 300 * PER_SPAN);
    expect(1 + 300 * PER_SPAN).toBeLessThanOrEqual(DOCS_MAX_RENDER_ELEMENTS);
  });

  it("code under pre is CodeBlock's and never chips: 400 fenced blocks holding the chord are a tree", () => {
    expect(parseMarkdown(`\`\`\`\n${CHORD}\n\`\`\`\n\n`.repeat(400), 'docs').kind).toBe('tree');
  });

  it("chat's worker path shows the flood as plain text with the too-wide note, drawing no chip", async () => {
    const text = spans(400, CHORD);
    expect(utf8ByteLength(text)).toBeGreaterThan(CHAT_SYNC_MAX_BYTES);
    const { container } = await chat(text);
    expect(container.querySelector('pre.msg-plain')?.textContent).toBe(text);
    expect(container.querySelector('p.msg-plain-note')?.textContent)
      .toBe(`Shown as plain text: this message would draw ${1 + 400 * PER_SPAN} elements (limit ${DOCS_MAX_RENDER_ELEMENTS}).`);
    expect(container.querySelectorAll('kbd')).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});

Append exactly this block to the end of the file (the file ends with `});` and a newline; the block starts with an empty line). It reuses the file's `out` (the build directory its `beforeAll` fills), its `LOADER` (with the job's profile swapped to `docs`, asserted to have changed) and its imports; the 26 399-character source fits one `argv` string.

```ts

// Docs W5 part 1, Task 3 (W5 bound 2-2, refinement (d)): the parse's element count includes the chips inline code
// draws. The count runs inside the worker closure, so only the built chunk proves the shipped worker carries it: a
// docs job of 400 spans of a 31-plus chord (64 elements a span, 25 601 in all) must answer too-wide, not a tree.
describe('the built markdownWorker chunk counts the chips inline code draws (W5 bound 2-2)', () => {
  it('answers a docs job of 400 spans of a 31-plus chord with too-wide and 25 601 elements', () => {
    const assets = path.join(out, 'assets');
    const chunk = readdirSync(assets).find((n) => /^markdownWorker-[\w-]+\.js$/.test(n));
    expect(chunk).toBeDefined();
    const docsLoader = LOADER.replace("profile: 'chat'", "profile: 'docs'");
    expect(docsLoader).not.toBe(LOADER);
    const src = Array.from({ length: 400 }, () => `\`${'a+'.repeat(31)}a\``).join(' ');
    const stdout = execFileSync(
      process.execPath,
      ['--input-type=module', '-e', docsLoader, path.join(assets, chunk!), src],
      { encoding: 'utf8', env: { PATH: process.env['PATH'] ?? '' }, timeout: 60_000 },
    );
    const result = JSON.parse(stdout.trim().split('\n').at(-1)!) as {
      load: string; replies?: { id: number; outcome: { kind: string; elements?: number } }[];
    };
    expect(result.load).toBe('ok');
    expect(result.replies).toEqual([{ id: 7, outcome: { kind: 'too-wide', elements: 1 + 400 * 64 } }]);
  }, 90_000);
});

```ts

/** Keystroke-shaped inline code: the named keys, and any one letter, digit or ASCII punctuation mark. */
const NAMED_KEY =
  /^(?:Ctrl|Control|Cmd|Command|⌘|Alt|Option|⌥|Opt|Shift|⇧|Win|Super|Meta|Fn|Esc|Escape|Enter|Return|↵|⏎|Tab|⇥|Space|Spacebar|Backspace|⌫|Delete|Del|Insert|Ins|Home|End|PageUp|PgUp|PageDown|PgDn|Up|Down|Left|Right|↑|↓|←|→|F(?:[1-9]|1[0-2]))$/;
const SINGLE = /^[\p{L}\p{N}`~!@#$%^&*()\-_=+[\]{};:'",.<>/?\\|]$/u;
/** The parts an inline code span draws as `<kbd>` chips (`Cmd+K`, `Esc`), or `null` when it is not a chord and stays
 *  plain inline code. ONE predicate for the component that draws the chips (`SHARED_COMPONENTS.code` in
 *  `markdown.tsx`) and the parse that counts them (`inlineCodeExtraElements` in `markdownParse.ts`), which is why it
 *  lives here, in the worker's closure (W5 Task 3, the plan's refinement (d)). A span longer than
 *  `MD_KEYSTROKE_MAX_CHARS` is `null` before it is trimmed or split (W5 bound r11): the split's pattern backtracks over
 *  a run of whitespace, so its cost grows with the square of the span's length, and the check comes first. */
export function keystrokeParts(raw: string): string[] | null {
  if (raw.length > MD_KEYSTROKE_MAX_CHARS) return null;
  const parts = raw.trim().split(/\s*\+\s*/);
  const ok = (p: string): boolean => NAMED_KEY.test(p) || SINGLE.test(p);
  if (parts.length > 1) return parts.every(ok) ? parts : null;
  return NAMED_KEY.test(parts[0]!) ? parts : null; // bare single chars stay chips
}
```

 *  part count above half of `CHAT_SYNC_MAX_BYTES` cannot come from a message chat renders on the main thread;
 *  past it the span stays plain code, as any code that is not a keystroke does. The parse's element cap counts hast
 *  elements, and one span of N parts draws 2N-1 more. */
const KEYSTROKE_MAX_PARTS = CHAT_SYNC_MAX_BYTES / 2;
export function keystrokeParts(raw: string): string[] | null {

  if (parts.length > KEYSTROKE_MAX_PARTS) return null;

  return NAMED_KEY.test(parts[0]!) ? parts : null; // bare single chars stay chips
