```tsx
/** The longest run of `[A-Za-z0-9_$]` in `s` (0 for none): one pass over its UTF-16 code units, no regular
 *  expression, so its cost is linear in the length of `s` whatever it holds. */
export function longestWordRun(s: string): number {
  let best = 0;
  let run = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i += 1) {
    const c = s.charCodeAt(i);
    if ((c >= 0x30 && c <= 0x39) || (c >= 0x41 && c <= 0x5a) || (c >= 0x61 && c <= 0x7a) || c === 0x5f || c === 0x24) {
      run += 1;
      if (run > best) best = run;
    } else {
      run = 0;
    }
  }
  return best;
}

/** Fenced code: language label + copy bar over a syntax-highlighted well.
 *  The bar is a SIBLING above the scrolling <pre>, never an overlay.
 *  Highlighted only when the language is registered, `highlight` is not `false`, the block is at most
 *  `MD_HIGHLIGHT_BLOCK_MAX_CHARS` characters (after the trailing-newline strip), and its longest run of
 *  `[A-Za-z0-9_$]` is at most `MD_HIGHLIGHT_MAX_WORD_CHARS` (W5 bound r10). A registered block over the size cap
 *  renders as plain text and says so in its label, its size in whole KiB of characters, rounded up; one within it
 *  that holds a longer word renders as plain text labelled with that word's length. The size check comes first, so
 *  a block over the cap is never scanned. */
```

```ts
/** Step 4: drops `position` from every node and measures the deepest node below the root (the root is 0) and
 *  the element count, in one walk with an explicit stack. */
function measure(tree: WalkNode): { depth: number; elements: number } {
  const nodes: WalkNode[] = [tree];
  const depths: number[] = [0];
  let depth = 0;
  let elements = 0;
  while (nodes.length > 0) {
    const node = nodes.pop()!;
    const d = depths.pop()!;
    delete node.position;
    if (node.type === 'element') elements += 1;
    if (d > depth) depth = d;
    const children = node.children;
    if (children) {
      for (let i = children.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {
        nodes.push(children[i]!);
        depths.push(d + 1);
      }
    }
  }
  return { depth, elements };
}
```

Replace with:
```ts
/** The elements `SHARED_COMPONENTS.code` draws for an inline code span of `text` beyond the one `code` element the
 *  walk already counts (W5 bound 2-2): a chord of N parts draws `span.kbd-combo`, N `kbd` and N - 1 `span.kbd-plus`,
 *  2N elements in place of one, so 2N - 1 more; any other span draws its one `code`, so 0. The component and this
 *  count call the same `keystrokeParts`, so a span over `MD_KEYSTROKE_MAX_CHARS` adds nothing to either. */
export function inlineCodeExtraElements(text: string): number {
  const keys = keystrokeParts(text);
  return keys === null ? 0 : 2 * keys.length - 1;
}

/** Step 4: drops `position` from every node and measures the deepest node below the root (the root is 0) and
 *  the element count, in one walk with an explicit stack. A `code` element whose parent is not a `pre` (inline
 *  code; a fenced block's `code` is `CodeBlock`'s, which draws no chips) adds `inlineCodeExtraElements` of its text
 *  children's text, the text its component receives. */
function measure(tree: WalkNode): { depth: number; elements: number } {
  const nodes: WalkNode[] = [tree];
  const depths: number[] = [0];
  const parents: (string | undefined)[] = [undefined];
  let depth = 0;
  let elements = 0;
  while (nodes.length > 0) {
    const node = nodes.pop()!;
    const d = depths.pop()!;
    const parent = parents.pop();
    delete node.position;
    if (node.type === 'element') elements += 1;
    if (node.type === 'element' && node.tagName === 'code' && parent !== 'pre') {
      let text = '';
      for (const child of node.children ?? []) if (child.type === 'text') text += child.value ?? '';
      elements += inlineCodeExtraElements(text);
    }
    if (d > depth) depth = d;
    const children = node.children;
    if (children) {
      const tag = node.type === 'element' ? node.tagName : undefined;
      for (let i = children.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {
        nodes.push(children[i]!);
        depths.push(d + 1);
        parents.push(tag);
      }
    }
  }
  return { depth, elements };
}
```

**Model routing:** `sonnet`, effort `high`. Small edits to two worker-closure modules and the parse hook, three test files, two comments and seven `red` strings in W4's plan; no package, no CSS, no new import edge. The judgment is in keeping the docs `<br>` exactly three spellings in exactly one profile (built in the raw step, never parsed), in amending W4's equality case so it still fails on any other difference, and in making the hook's one-frame window observable in a test (decision 5).

**Spec rows:** M9.1 and A16 (the 2026-10-12 rich-docs spec: `<br>`, `<br/>` and `<br />` with no attributes become a real `br` element in the docs profile, all other raw HTML stays text, chat unchanged; W4's profile-equality case amended to "equal, except on inputs that hold `<br>`, which differ only by `br` elements in the docs profile"); W4's carried N1 (the hook's commit-to-effect window), which review 412's R5 asks to carry with a measured example: this task closes it and its red case IS that example; review 412's residue R3 and R4 (re-record the measured `red` of W4-T11-M52 to M55, M58, M59 and W4-T6-M5), R6's worker half (`markdownWorker.ts`'s stale quoted `worker:` literal; the `vite.config.ts` half is Task 12's) and R7 (`markdownGuard.ts`'s comment word that makes Tailwind ship an unused rule). Neither is a deviation (both fill a silence or follow the rich-docs spec's A16).

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes, from `pwa/src/lib/markdownParse.ts`: `parseMarkdown(src: string, profile?: MarkdownProfile): ParseOutcome` (already routes its profile to the private `run`), `settleHast(tree: HastRoot): ParseOutcome`, the private `rawToText(tree: WalkNode): void` and `measure`, `answerMarkdownJob(data: unknown, post: (reply: MarkdownReply) => void): void` (already routes a job's `profile`), `MarkdownProfile = 'chat' | 'docs'`, `ParseOutcome`. From `pwa/src/lib/useParsedMarkdown.ts`: `useParsedMarkdown(text: string, parser: MarkdownParser, opts: { readonly profile: MarkdownProfile; readonly budgetMs: number; readonly attempt?: number }): ParsedMarkdown`. From `pwa/src/lib/markdown.tsx`: `SHARED_COMPONENTS` (no `br` component: a `br` element renders as React's own `<br>`). From `pwa/src/lib/renderHast.tsx`: `renderHast(tree: HastRoot, opts: RenderHastOptions): ReactElement`. From `pwa/src/lib/markdownRunner.ts`: `MarkdownParser`.
- Produces, `pwa/src/lib/markdownParse.ts`: `export function settleHast(tree: HastRoot, profile: MarkdownProfile = 'chat'): ParseOutcome;` — an absent `profile` means `'chat'`, so every one-argument caller keeps chat's raw step (the parameter has that one meaning; it is never `null`). In the `'docs'` profile, a `raw` node whose WHOLE value matches the module-private `DOCS_BR = /^<br(?: ?\/)?>$/` (lower case, no attribute, at most one space before the slash) becomes `{ type: 'element', tagName: 'br', properties: {}, children: [] }`, wherever it stands (inline in a paragraph, a table cell or a list item, or a block-level raw node that is only the tag); every other raw node becomes `{ type: 'text', value }` in both profiles. The `br` elements are counted by `measure` like any element, so they count toward `DOCS_MAX_RENDER_ELEMENTS` before anything renders. `WalkNode` gains `properties?: Record<string, unknown>` (absent = not an element step 3 built; nothing reads it). `parseMarkdown`, `ParseOutcome`, `MarkdownJob`, `MarkdownReply` and `answerMarkdownJob` keep their signatures; `parseWithoutPrescan` stays chat.
- Produces, `pwa/src/lib/useParsedMarkdown.ts`: `useParsedMarkdown` keeps its signature and `ParsedMarkdown` keeps `{ outcome: ParseOutcome | null; lastGood: HastRoot | null; pending: boolean }` with their meanings (`outcome` null = no outcome has settled for a request that was still the latest when it settled; `lastGood` null = no tree has settled; `pending` true = no outcome has settled for the current text, profile, budget and attempt). What changes: `jobs.latest` is written by a `useLayoutEffect` with NO dependency list (at every commit, from the committed render's props), so a reply for an earlier text that settles between a newer text's commit and that commit's passive effects lands in `lastGood` alone, as the `outcome` docstring already promised. Jobs still start in the passive effect, so `pending`, the queue, StrictMode's double mount and unmount's abort are unchanged.

**Decisions this task makes** (none departs from the spec's text):
1. **The `<br>` is built in the raw step, never parsed.** `rawToText` already visits every `raw` node with an explicit stack; it gains the profile and one test of the node's whole value. No HTML parser and no package enters the worker closure (`markdown-purity.test.ts` unedited and green; mutation M7 shows it reds on a `rehype-raw` import). A `raw` node is what remark-rehype emits for HTML in Markdown, so measured at planning (this task's Step 1 fixtures): `a<br>b` is `p > [text a, raw <br>, text b]`; a line that is only `<br>` is one block-level raw node `<br>` under the root, which also matches and becomes a root-level `br` (the rule is "whole value"); `<br>` followed by a newline and text is ONE block-level raw node `<br>\nhello`, which does not match and stays text; `<br class=x>`, `<br onclick=x>`, `<BR>`, `<br  />` and `</br>` are their own raw nodes and stay text.
2. **A16's amended equality case keeps failing on any other difference.** W4's case iterated the chat corpus, which holds no raw `<br>` (`grep -c '<br' pwa/test/markdownCorpus.ts` prints `0`) and cannot gain one (its golden files are byte-identical by rule). So the amended case iterates the corpus PLUS eight `BR_INPUTS` (the three spellings, a lone `<br>`, a mixed line, a table cell, a quote and a list item). For each input the one-argument outcome equals chat's; the docs outcome equals chat's after `brAsChatText` puts back, as text, every `br` element that stands where chat holds a text node of one of the three spellings (any other difference survives and fails the deep-equal; a hard line break's `br` is in both trees); and an input that holds none of the three spellings is strictly equal. Finally every `BR_INPUTS` entry must DIFFER between the profiles, so the case reds when the rule is missing (red first) and when it leaks into chat (mutation M1).
3. **M9.1's cases** (appended, seventeen): the three spellings each give exactly one `br` between two text nodes in docs and literal text in chat; a lone `<br>` line; seven refused spellings (an attribute, an event handler, upper case, two spaces before the slash, a closing tag, a block raw node holding more than the tag, a `<script>` element) stay literal text with the docs outcome equal to chat's; 20 000 `a<br>` give `too-wide` with 20 001 elements in docs (the `br`s count before any render) and a tree in chat; `renderHast` draws `<p>a<br>b</p>` for docs and `<p>a&lt;br&gt;b</p>` for chat; `settleHast` with one argument keeps chat.
4. **Chat is byte-identical.** The rule is behind `profile === 'docs'`; chat's synchronous path never reaches `settleHast` (react-markdown's own `<Markdown>` renders raw HTML as text there), and its worker path posts `profile: 'chat'`. `CI=1` golden, `render-hast` (M4.P10) and the unmodified `message-links` prove it.
5. **N1's window, made deterministic.** The window is the time between a commit and its passive effects; in a browser the worker's reply is a task that can run there. Under `act`, React flushes a commit's passive effects before any microtask, so a real promise resolved in the window cannot settle inside it. The N1 case therefore has its parser answer with a thenable whose fulfilment the test calls itself, from a `useLayoutEffect` of the component that renders the hook (declared after the hook, so it runs after the hook's own layout effects and before any passive effect of that commit). At the state Task 3 left, the reply for text A lands while `jobs.latest` is still A, so A's tree becomes the `outcome` while text B is pending (Step 4 shows the diff: `"outcome": { "kind": "tree", ... "value": "A" }` where `null` is expected): that is review 412 R5's measured example, recorded in the SDD ledger (Step 4) and carried by Task 14's results as closed here. With the layout effect, the reply is an earlier request's: `{ outcome: null, lastGood: <A's tree>, pending: true }`, then B's own reply gives `{ outcome: <B>, lastGood: <B>, pending: false }`. Mutation M8 moves the write back to a passive effect and reds the case. The layout effect has no dependency list on purpose: the committed render's props ARE the latest request, so no list can leave a field out. A list missing `attempt` would have left a Retry's reply forever an earlier request's (`pending` stuck true), which no W4 case covers (W4's attempt case never settles the retried job); the second appended case, a control green before and after, settles a Retry and holds the request whole (mutation M9 writes `attempt: 0` and reds it). N1's other minor (texts A, B, A, then C shows B's tree while C parses) is the hook's newest-first rule (W4's refinement (i)) and stays as it is; its docstring nits are W7's (ledger).
6. **R3 and R4 are re-measured at this task's base, not copied from review 412.** Review 412 measured at W4's tip; Task 3 added one `chat-hardening` case (113 to 114) and `main` has added one `ccrc-doctor` case since (912 to 913), so the counts move while every verdict and every red case title stays what the review found. Step 0 measures each row in a scratch copy with W4's own row JSON (the id's LAST occurrence, as W4's extractor reads it); Step 8 writes the measured lines. If Step 0 prints a different count, the worker writes the count it measured in place of the planned one; a different set of red titles, or a row that does not go red, is an ask.
7. **R7 is a built-artefact fact, so its check builds.** Tailwind scans source text, and `markdownGuard.ts`'s comment word `table-cell` makes the production CSS ship `.table-cell{display:table-cell}`, used by nothing. The fix is a comment word, which no test can hold without pinning prose, so Steps 0 and 10 build the app for production in a scratch copy (Global Constraints, built artefacts) and count the rule: `1` before, `0` after. Measured at planning: `index-*.css` 140 893 bytes before, 140 862 after (W4's size before the word arrived). `.table` (from other words) is unaffected.
8. **W4 rows whose anchors this task moves.** W4's rows are W4's history (Task 14 runs W5's table only), and five of them anchor on text this task rewrites: `W4-T3-M17`, `W4-T4-M3` and `W4-T4-M4` (the one-line raw-to-text assignment), `W4-T3-M21` (`rawToText`'s one-argument signature) and `W4-T4-M2` (`settleHast`'s `rawToText(node);` call). Each guard is still held, by this task's cases: the raw-HTML-as-text case and the seven refused spellings red when raw nodes survive or the walk stops, and the 100 000-deep `settleHast` case reds on recursion. They are not re-anchored here; a re-run of W4's table would report them as absent anchors, not as survivors. `W4-T6-M24`'s anchor (the passive effect's dependency list) stays unique because the layout effect has no list (decision 5). # Docs W5 part 1, Task 4 Step 0: re-measures seven of W4's mutation rows (review 412's R3 and R4) in a scratch copy,
```python
# one row at a time, restoring the file after each. usage: python3 -I w4rows.py <copy> <row id>...
# Prints one line per row: the id, the summary, and the titles of the cases that went red, sorted.
import json, os, re, subprocess, sys
copy = sys.argv[1]
plan_path = os.path.join(copy, 'docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-09-native-docs-reader-w4-pwa-foundation.md')
plan = open(plan_path, encoding='utf-8').read()
fence = '`' * 3  # spelled so this script can sit inside a Markdown fence
last = {}
for m in re.finditer(fence + r'json\n(.*?)\n' + fence, plan, re.S):
    try:
        rows = json.loads(m.group(1))
    except ValueError:
        continue
    if isinstance(rows, list):
        for r in rows:
            if isinstance(r, dict) and 'id' in r:
                last[r['id']] = r  # an id's LAST occurrence wins (a later task's re-anchor)
report = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(sys.argv[0])), 'w4rows-report.json')
for rid in sys.argv[2:]:
    row = last[rid]
    f = os.path.join(copy, row['file'])
    src = open(f, encoding='utf-8').read()
    if src.count(row['old']) != 1:
        print(rid, 'ANCHOR-COUNT', src.count(row['old']))
        continue
    open(f, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(src.replace(row['old'], row['new'], 1))
    try:
        subprocess.run(['./node_modules/.bin/vitest', 'run', *row['tests'], '--reporter=json', '--outputFile.json=' + report],
                       cwd=os.path.join(copy, row['pkg']), capture_output=True, timeout=590)
        r = json.load(open(report, encoding='utf-8'))
        failed = sorted(a['title'] for t in r['testResults'] for a in t['assertionResults'] if a['status'] == 'failed')
        skipped = f" | {r['numPendingTests']} skipped" if r['numPendingTests'] else ''
        print(rid, f"{r['numFailedTests']} failed | {r['numPassedTests']} passed{skipped} ({r['numTotalTests']})", json.dumps(failed))
    finally:
        open(f, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(src)
        if os.path.exists(report):
            os.remove(report)
```

Replace with:
```ts
const treeOf = (o: ParseOutcome): HastRoot => {
  if (o.kind !== 'tree') throw new Error(`expected a tree, got ${JSON.stringify(o)}`);
  return o.tree;
};

/** The three spellings the docs profile draws as a `br` element (the 2026-10-12 spec's A16), as a whole value. */
const BR_SPELLING = /^<br(?: ?\/)?>$/;

/** `docs` with every `br` element that stands where `chat` holds a text node spelling `<br>`, `<br/>` or `<br />`
 *  put back as that text node: the one difference A16 allows between the two profiles, undone. Every other node is
 *  copied as it is, so any other difference survives the copy and fails the deep-equal that follows. A hard line
 *  break's `br` is in both trees, so it is compared like any element. Explicit stack. */
function brAsChatText(docs: ParseOutcome, chat: ParseOutcome): ParseOutcome {
  if (docs.kind !== 'tree' || chat.kind !== 'tree') return docs;
  const tree = structuredClone(docs.tree);
  const stack: [AnyNode, AnyNode][] = [[tree as unknown as AnyNode, chat.tree as unknown as AnyNode]];
  while (stack.length > 0) {
    const [d, c] = stack.pop()!;
    const dk = d.children ?? [];
    const ck = c.children ?? [];
    for (let i = 0; i < dk.length; i += 1) {
      const dn = dk[i]!;
      const cn = ck[i];
      if (cn === undefined) continue;
      if (dn.type === 'element' && dn.tagName === 'br' && cn.type === 'text' && BR_SPELLING.test(cn.value ?? '')) {
        dk[i] = { type: 'text', value: cn.value };
      } else {
        stack.push([dn, cn]);
      }
    }
  }
  return { ...docs, tree };
}

/** Inputs holding a raw `<br>`, `<br/>` or `<br />` (A16): each differs between the two profiles, only by `br`. */
const BR_INPUTS: readonly string[] = [
  'a<br>b',
  'a<br/>b',
  'a<br />b',
  '<br>',
  'one<br>two<br/>three<br />four',
  '| a | b |\n|---|---|\n| x<br>y | z |',
  '> quoted<br>line',
  '- item<br>more',
];
```

```ts
describe("M9.1: the docs profile's real <br> (the 2026-10-12 spec's A16; the W5 plan's refinement (i))", () => {
  const BR = { type: 'element', tagName: 'br', properties: {}, children: [] };
  const P = (children: unknown[]) => ({ type: 'element', tagName: 'p', properties: {}, children });
  const brs = (o: ParseOutcome): AnyNode[] => nodes(treeOf(o)).filter((n) => n.type === 'element' && n.tagName === 'br');
  const textOf = (o: ParseOutcome): string =>
    nodes(treeOf(o)).filter((n) => n.type === 'text').map((n) => n.value).reverse().join('');

  it.each(['<br>', '<br/>', '<br />'])('a%sb is one br element between two text nodes in the docs profile', (tag) => {
    expect(parseMarkdown(`a${tag}b`, 'docs')).toEqual({
      kind: 'tree',
      depth: 2,
      tree: { type: 'root', children: [P([{ type: 'text', value: 'a' }, BR, { type: 'text', value: 'b' }])] },
    });
  });

  it.each(['<br>', '<br/>', '<br />'])('a%sb stays literal text in the chat profile', (tag) => {
    expect(parseMarkdown(`a${tag}b`, 'chat')).toEqual({
      kind: 'tree',
      depth: 2,
      tree: { type: 'root', children: [P([{ type: 'text', value: 'a' }, { type: 'text', value: tag }, { type: 'text', value: 'b' }])] },
    });
  });

  it('a line that is only <br> is one br element under the root in the docs profile, and text in chat', () => {
    expect(parseMarkdown('<br>', 'docs')).toEqual({ kind: 'tree', depth: 1, tree: { type: 'root', children: [BR] } });
    expect(parseMarkdown('<br>', 'chat')).toEqual({ kind: 'tree', depth: 1, tree: { type: 'root', children: [{ type: 'text', value: '<br>' }] } });
  });

  it.each([
    ['an attribute', 'a<br class=x>b'],
    ['an event handler', 'a<br onclick=x>b'],
    ['upper case', 'a<BR>b'],
    ['two spaces before the slash', 'a<br  />b'],
    ['a closing tag', 'a</br>b'],
    ['a block-level raw node holding more than the tag', '<br>\nhello'],
    ['a script element', '<script>x</script>'],
  ])('%s stays literal text in the docs profile', (_why, src) => {
    const o = parseMarkdown(src, 'docs');
    expect(brs(o)).toEqual([]);
    expect(nodes(treeOf(o)).filter((n) => n.type === 'raw')).toEqual([]);
    expect(textOf(o)).toBe(src);
    expect(o).toEqual(parseMarkdown(src, 'chat'));
  });

  it('the br elements count toward DOCS_MAX_RENDER_ELEMENTS before anything renders', () => {
    const src = 'a<br>'.repeat(20000);
    expect(parseMarkdown(src, 'docs')).toEqual({ kind: 'too-wide', elements: 20001 });
    expect(parseMarkdown(src, 'chat').kind).toBe('tree');
  }, 60000);

  it('the docs br renders through renderHast as a real <br>; chat renders the tag as text', () => {
    const docs = render(renderHast(treeOf(parseMarkdown('a<br>b', 'docs')), { components: SHARED_COMPONENTS }));
    expect(docs.container.innerHTML).toBe('<p>a<br>b</p>');
    cleanup();
    const chat = render(renderHast(treeOf(parseMarkdown('a<br>b', 'chat')), { components: SHARED_COMPONENTS }));
    expect(chat.container.innerHTML).toBe('<p>a&lt;br&gt;b</p>');
    cleanup();
  });

  it("settleHast with one argument keeps 'chat'; with 'docs' a hand-built raw <br/> becomes a br element", () => {
    const tree = (): HastRoot => ({ type: 'root', children: [{ type: 'raw', value: '<br/>' }] }) as unknown as HastRoot;
    expect(settleHast(tree())).toEqual({ kind: 'tree', depth: 1, tree: { type: 'root', children: [{ type: 'text', value: '<br/>' }] } });
    expect(settleHast(tree(), 'chat')).toEqual(settleHast(tree()));
    expect(settleHast(tree(), 'docs')).toEqual({ kind: 'tree', depth: 1, tree: { type: 'root', children: [BR] } });
  });
});
```

```tsx

describe("W5 N1: the hook's commit-to-effect window is closed (the latest request is recorded at commit)", () => {
  // W4's carried N1 (review 412's R5): the latest request was written in a passive effect, so a reply for the previous
  // text that settled after a newer text committed, but before that commit's passive effects ran, was taken as the
  // latest one's and became the `outcome` while the newer text was pending. In a browser that reply is the worker's
  // message, a task that can run between a commit and its passive effects. Here the window is made deterministic: the
  // parser answers with a thenable whose fulfilment the test calls itself, from a layout effect of the component that
  // renders the hook, which runs after the hook's own layout effects and before any passive effect of that commit.
  it('a reply for text A that lands after text B commits, before its passive effects, is never the outcome for B', () => {
    const srcs: string[] = [];
    const fulfil: ((o: ParseOutcome) => void)[] = [];
    const parser: MarkdownParser = (src) => {
      srcs.push(src);
      return {
        then(onFulfilled: (o: ParseOutcome) => void) {
          fulfil.push(onFulfilled);
        },
      } as unknown as Promise<ParseOutcome>;
    };
    const a = treeOf('A');
    const { result, rerender } = renderHook(
      (p: { readonly text: string }) => {
        const parsed = useParsedMarkdown(p.text, parser, { profile: 'chat', budgetMs: 2000 });
        useLayoutEffect(() => {
          if (p.text === 'B') fulfil[0]?.(tree(a));
        }, [p.text]);
        return parsed;
      },
      { initialProps: { text: 'A' } },
    );
    expect(srcs).toEqual(['A']);
    rerender({ text: 'B' });
    expect(srcs).toEqual(['A', 'B']);
    expect(result.current).toEqual({ outcome: null, lastGood: a, pending: true });
    const b = treeOf('B');
    act(() => {
      fulfil[1]?.(tree(b));
    });
    expect(result.current).toEqual({ outcome: tree(b), lastGood: b, pending: false });
  });

  it('Retry (a changed attempt alone) is the latest request: its reply becomes the outcome, and nothing is pending', async () => {
    const { parser, calls } = deferredParser();
    const { result, rerender } = mount(parser, { text: 'a' });
    await settle(calls[0], TIMEOUT);
    rerender({ text: 'a', attempt: 1 });
    expect(calls).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(result.current.pending).toBe(true);
    const a = treeOf('a');
    await settle(calls[1], tree(a));
    expect(result.current).toEqual({ outcome: tree(a), lastGood: a, pending: false });
  });
});
```

```ts
// Docs W5 part 1, Task 4 (M9.1, the 2026-10-12 spec's A16): the docs profile's real `<br>` is made in the parse's raw
// step, inside the worker closure, so only the built chunk proves the shipped worker carries it, for the docs profile
// alone: a docs job of `a<br>b` answers a tree holding one `br` element, and a chat job the tag as literal text.
describe('the built markdownWorker chunk draws a raw <br> as a br element in the docs profile alone (M9.1)', () => {
  it('answers a docs job of a<br>b with one br element, and a chat job with the tag as text', () => {
    const assets = path.join(out, 'assets');
    const chunk = readdirSync(assets).find((n) => /^markdownWorker-[\w-]+\.js$/.test(n));
    expect(chunk).toBeDefined();
    const docsLoader = LOADER.replace("profile: 'chat'", "profile: 'docs'");
    expect(docsLoader).not.toBe(LOADER);
    const answer = (loader: string) => {
      const stdout = execFileSync(
        process.execPath,
        ['--input-type=module', '-e', loader, path.join(assets, chunk!), 'a<br>b'],
        { encoding: 'utf8', env: { PATH: process.env['PATH'] ?? '' }, timeout: 60_000 },
      );
      return JSON.parse(stdout.trim().split('\n').at(-1)!) as { load: string; replies?: unknown[] };
    };
    const paragraph = (middle: unknown) => ({
      kind: 'tree',
      depth: 2,
      tree: {
        type: 'root',
        children: [{ type: 'element', tagName: 'p', properties: {}, children: [{ type: 'text', value: 'a' }, middle, { type: 'text', value: 'b' }] }],
      },
    });
    const docs = answer(docsLoader);
```

```ts
/** Step 3: every `raw` node becomes a `text` node with the same value, in place, with an explicit stack. */
function rawToText(tree: WalkNode): void {
  const stack: WalkNode[] = [tree];
  while (stack.length > 0) {
    const node = stack.pop()!;
    const children = node.children;
    if (!children) continue;
    for (let i = 0; i < children.length; i += 1) {
      const child = children[i]!;
      if (child.type === 'raw') children[i] = { type: 'text', value: child.value ?? '' };
      else if (child.children) stack.push(child);
    }
  }
}
```

Replace with:
```ts
/** The one raw spelling the docs profile draws (A16): a whole value of `<br>`, `<br/>` or `<br />`, lower case, with
 *  no attribute. `<BR>`, `<br class=x>` and a block-level raw node holding more than the tag do not match. */
const DOCS_BR = /^<br(?: ?\/)?>$/;

/** Step 3: every `raw` node becomes a `text` node with the same value, in place, with an explicit stack; in the
 *  docs profile a raw node `DOCS_BR` matches becomes an empty `br` element instead. No HTML is parsed: the element
 *  is built here, and every other raw value stays text in both profiles. */
function rawToText(tree: WalkNode, profile: MarkdownProfile): void {
  const stack: WalkNode[] = [tree];
  while (stack.length > 0) {
    const node = stack.pop()!;
    const children = node.children;
    if (!children) continue;
    for (let i = 0; i < children.length; i += 1) {
      const child = children[i]!;
      if (child.type === 'raw') {
        const value = child.value ?? '';
        children[i] = profile === 'docs' && DOCS_BR.test(value)
          ? { type: 'element', tagName: 'br', properties: {}, children: [] }
          : { type: 'text', value };
      } else if (child.children) {
        stack.push(child);
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```ts
export type TreeSlot =
  | { s: 'loading' }
  | { s: 'ok'; answer: DocsTreeResponse; receivedAt: number }
  | { s: 'failed'; body: DocsFailureBody }
  | DocsClientSlot;                                   // exactly spec 4.3's type
export type FileSlot =
  | { s: 'none' }
  | { s: 'loading'; pin: DocPin }
  | { s: 'ok'; pin: DocPin; answer: DocsFileResponse; receivedAt: number }
  | { s: 'failed'; pin: DocPin; body: DocsFailureBody }
  | { s: 'too-large'; pin: DocPin; size: number; cap: number }
  | { s: 'changing'; pin: DocPin; word: DocsFailure }
  | (DocsClientSlot & { pin: DocPin });
export type Freshness =
  | { s: 'idle' }
  | { s: 'fetching'; reason: 'auto' | 'manual' }
  | { s: 'answered'; fetch: DocsRefreshFetch; at: number }
  | { s: 'soon'; retryAt: number }
  | { s: 'stale-lock'; ref: string | null }
  | { s: 'refresh-failed'; answer: DocsNotOk }
  | { s: 'relist-failed'; answer: DocsNotOk };
export function treeKey(project: string, ref: DocsRefSpec | null): string;   // project + NUL + (ref === null ? '' : docsRefText(ref))
export function fileKey(pin: DocPin, tree: DocsTreeOk): string;             // committed: blob + section + path; draft: every pin field
export function pinFor(tree: DocsTreeOk, page: DocsPageLocation): DocPin | null;
export interface DocsVisit {
  readonly tree: TreeSlot | null;
  readonly file: FileSlot;
  readonly freshness: Freshness;
  readonly updatedTo: string | null;
  readonly pendingFragment: string | null;
  retryTree(): void;
  retryFile(): void;
  refreshManual(): void;
  fetchFromOrigin(): void;
  setFragment(fragment: string | null): void;
}
export function useDocsVisit(page: DocsPageLocation | null, loaders: DocsLoaders): DocsVisit;
// pwa/src/docs/docsText.ts
export const DOCS_RELIST_WORDS: ReadonlySet<DocsFailure>;                    // exactly the four words of spec 4.3 item 1
```

The one meaning of every null, absence and catch-all arm:
- `useDocsVisit`'s `page: null`: the URL failed to parse; no request is made.
- `DocsVisit.tree: null`: the page names no project (the index, or `page` null). The index's data is `loaders.projects()`, which Task 9 reads; the visit never calls it.
- `TreeSlot` `loading`: a GET for this key is in flight or about to start (a page's first render, before its effect).
- `FileSlot` `none`: no file request is due: the tree slot is not `ok`, the page is not a leaf of this tree, `pinFor` answered null, or the leaf is a raster (`DocImage` loads raster bytes through `loaders.raster`, Task 7). Each of these is told apart by the tree slot and `pinFor`, which the caller holds.
- `FileSlot` `too-large`: the entry's listed size (the draft's for a draft pin, the committed side's otherwise) is over `DOCS_CLASS_CAP[contentClass(path)]`; nothing was requested (spec 4.4). A listed size of `null` is unknown and is requested (the server enforces the cap).
- `FileSlot` `ok`'s `pin`: the OPENED pin. It differs from `pinFor`'s answer only while a re-list moved the pin and the new read is in flight; the old body stays on screen meanwhile (spec 4.3, "keeping scroll"). A committed body kept by blob after the branch moves reports the NEW pin (the bytes are the same blob).
- `pinFor` null: the page opens no file in this tree (not a `path` page, a directory page, no entry at that path, or `entryView` opens nothing: a committed symlink or submodule, a withheld new file, a new file under `view=committed`).
- `fileKey`'s committed fallback `commit + section + path` is used only for a committed pin whose entry is not committed in `tree` (`pinFor` never makes one).
- `Freshness` `stale-lock`'s `ref: null`: the `ref-locked` body named no ref.
- `updatedTo: null`: no re-list changed this leaf's pin in this visit (a leaf is the tree key, section, path and `view`, so opening the committed version of a draft is a new leaf, not an update). A string is the new pin's commit (committed) or the holder's HEAD (draft).
- `pendingFragment: null`: nothing to scroll to. The visit only holds it; Task 9 sets it (a direct load's hash, Task 6's cross-doc click) and clears it after scrolling.

**Decisions this task makes** (each pinned by a case below; the architecture's interface is widened where it could not hold its own rows, and these are refinements, not deviations: none contradicts the spec's text):

1. **`tree` is `TreeSlot | null`.** The architecture typed it `TreeSlot`, but the index and an unparsed URL have no project, and `loading` there would be a slot that never resolves (an overloaded state).
2. **`FileSlot` gains `too-large`.** Spec 4.4: "A leaf whose listed size exceeds `DOCS_CLASS_CAP` ... shows the `too-large` sentence **without** requesting it". The visit owns the request, so the visit is where it is withheld; folding it into `none` would overload `none`.
3. **`Freshness` carries `DocsNotOk`, and has `refresh-failed`.** A re-list by GET (on return to the tab, or Re-list) can fail with a client slot (`unreachable`), not only a word, so `relist-failed` carries `answer: DocsNotOk` (the architecture's `body` could not hold it); a POST that got no route answer at all is `refresh-failed`, which the architecture's union had no arm for. Task 10 renders `answer` with `DocsFailureView`'s own `failureSentence`/`slotSentence`. `stale-lock`'s `ref` is `string | null` (decision above).
4. **The committed key is the blob plus its place.** `fileKey` is `blob, section, path` joined by NUL, not the blob alone: two paths can hold one blob with different extensions, and the answer's `contentClass` comes from the path. The property spec 4.3 item 2 wants (a file unchanged across a moving branch is not downloaded again) holds unchanged.
5. **`DOCS_RELIST_WORDS` lives in `docsText.ts`.** The hook compares a file read's word against four words, one of which, quoted on a code line, is held by `single-definition.test.ts`'s archive-door census to the files it names; `docsText.ts` is the PWA file that census already excuses (Task 2's decision 2). Declaring the set there keeps `single-definition.test.ts` untouched by this task and spells the word in no new file.
6. **Auto-refresh fires when a slot BECOMES ok, by GET.** A re-list of a listing already held (on return to the tab, Re-list, a file word) is a GET and never a POST (M4.A3), even when its answer says `refreshDue` and the key was never auto-refreshed; a slot that becomes ok after `loading` or a failure (the first answer, a retry, a sign-in) may auto-refresh once. A refresh answer's own tree never triggers one.
7. **A refresh whose fetch failed ignores its tree.** Spec 4.3: "a `fetch` failure changes only the freshness chip", so the tree slot is the same object afterwards (Task 10's M4.F4 reads its listing node by identity). With `fetch` `ran` or `skipped`: an ok tree replaces the slot; a tree failure keeps a held listing (`relist-failed`) or becomes the slot when none is held.
8. **A failed re-list keeps the listing,** except `auth`, which becomes the slot so that sign-in re-fetches it (the overlay is up either way).
9. **Retries:** one automatic retry per (request kind, key, word) for the visit (`tree`, `file` and `refresh` keep separate entries in the one `autoRetried` set), only for a word whose `docsRetryPlan` is `auto`. A refresh's fetch failure that is `fetch-too-soon` shows `soon` until its retry; a stale `ref-locked` (plan `none`) shows `stale-lock` and never retries; an unmeasured lock age (plan `manual`) shows `answered` and waits for the chip's tap. The retry POST keeps the original reason.
10. **The four re-list words** from a file read (`DOCS_RELIST_WORDS`) re-list the tree once and read again; the second time the slot is `changing`, and `retryFile()` re-lists and reads again. Any other `auto` word from a file read is read again once after its wait.
11. **Unmount ends the visit:** every timer is cleared and every file read in flight is aborted (its `AbortError` is swallowed; any other rejection is rethrown, a defect). StrictMode's double effect starts nothing twice: the mount effect starts no request, and the per-render effect's starts are guarded by the slot maps.

```ts
// Docs W5 part 1 fixtures (Task 5): a tree answer built from placeholders only (project `demo`, branches `main` and
// `ws/a`, a checkout at `/repo/demo`), the page a URL parses to, and loaders whose every call is a spy. Later Docs
// tests build on these; nothing here reaches a server.
import { vi, type Mock } from 'vitest';
import {
  DOC_SECTION_SLUGS, DOC_SECTIONS, parseDocsPage,
  type DocsEntry, type DocsFailureBody, type DocsFileResponse, type DocsPageLocation, type DocsRefreshFetch,
  type DocsRefreshResponse, type DocsTreeOk, type DocsTreeResponse, type DraftsFacts,
} from '../../shared/docs';
import type {
  DocsFileAnswer, DocsIndexAnswer, DocsLoaders, DocsRasterAnswer, DocsRefreshLoaderAnswer, DocsTreeAnswer,
} from '../src/docs/failures';

export const COMMIT_A = 'a'.repeat(40);
export const COMMIT_B = 'b'.repeat(40);
export const BLOB_1 = '1'.repeat(40);
export const BLOB_2 = '2'.repeat(40);
export const FP_1 = 'f'.repeat(64);
export const SERVED = 'refs/remotes/origin/main';

/** A committed regular file of 100 bytes, no draft. */
export function entry(section: DocsEntry['section'], path: string, over: Partial<DocsEntry> = {}): DocsEntry {
  return { section, path, committed: { kind: 'file', blob: BLOB_1, size: 100 }, draft: null, ...over };
}

/** A draft overlaying `entry`: a regular file with a fingerprint (opens as a draft in a ref view). */
export function draftOf(state: NonNullable<DocsEntry['draft']>['state'],
  over: Partial<NonNullable<DocsEntry['draft']>> = {}): NonNullable<DocsEntry['draft']> {
  return { state, kind: 'file', size: 120, fp: FP_1, trust: 'status', ...over };
}

/** The main checkout holding `main` at `head`, its HEAD equal to the served commit unless `baseEqual` says not. */
export function holder(head = COMMIT_A, baseEqual = true): DraftsFacts {
  return {
    state: 'holder', branch: 'main', worktree: { path: '/repo/demo', head, class: 'main' }, baseEqual, base: null,
    caveats: [], opaque: [],
  };
}

export interface TreeOver {
  readonly commit?: string;
  readonly entries?: DocsEntry[];
  readonly drafts?: DraftsFacts;
}

export function treeOk(over: TreeOver = {}): DocsTreeOk {
  const commit = over.commit ?? COMMIT_A;
  return {
    v: 1, verb: 'docs-tree', ok: true, elapsedMs: 5, project: 'demo',
    repo: { key: '0'.repeat(32), objectFormat: 'sha1', shallow: false },
    github: { state: 'named', slug: 'example-org/example-repo' },
    ref: {
      requested: null, served: SERVED, name: 'main', side: 'origin', commit, via: 'default:origin-head', tried: [],
      relation: 'equal', counterpart: null,
    },
    mainCheckout: { path: '/repo/demo', branch: 'main', head: commit },
    sections: DOC_SECTION_SLUGS.map((slug) => ({ slug, path: DOC_SECTIONS[slug], state: 'present', count: 1 })),
    entries: over.entries ?? [entry('specs', 'a.md'), entry('specs', 'b.md', { committed: { kind: 'file', blob: BLOB_2, size: 100 } })],
    unlisted: { count: 0, byReason: {} },
    drafts: over.drafts ?? { state: 'none', branch: 'main', skipped: [] },
    freshness: { remote: 'origin', trackedRef: SERVED, stamp: null, fetchHead: null },
  };
}

export function treeResponse(tree: DocsTreeOk = treeOk(), refreshDue = false): DocsTreeResponse {
  return { ok: true, tree, refreshDue };
}

export const okTree = (tree: DocsTreeOk = treeOk(), refreshDue = false): DocsTreeAnswer =>
  ({ s: 'ok', value: treeResponse(tree, refreshDue) });

/** A failure body for `word` with any context (an unknown word is allowed: it is kept whole). */
export const bodyOf = (word: string, ctx: Record<string, unknown> = {}): DocsFailureBody =>
  ({ ok: false, failure: word, ...ctx }) as unknown as DocsFailureBody;

export const failedAnswer = (word: string, ctx: Record<string, unknown> = {}): { s: 'failed'; body: DocsFailureBody } =>
  ({ s: 'failed', body: bodyOf(word, ctx) });

export function fileResponse(text = '# A'): DocsFileResponse {
  return {
    ok: true, contentClass: 'markdown', from: 'ccd',
    show: {
      v: 1, verb: 'docs-show', ok: true, elapsedMs: 3, source: 'committed', section: 'specs', path: 'a.md',
      size: text.length, sha256: 'c'.repeat(64), encoding: 'utf8', text,
    },
  };
}

export const okFile = (text = '# A'): DocsFileAnswer => ({ s: 'ok', value: fileResponse(text) });

export const RAN: DocsRefreshFetch = {
  state: 'ran',
  answer: {
    v: 1, verb: 'docs-fetch', ok: true, elapsedMs: 40, branch: 'main', trackedRef: SERVED, before: COMMIT_A,
    after: COMMIT_A, moved: 'unchanged', stamp: 'written',
  },
};

export function okRefresh(fetch: DocsRefreshFetch = RAN,
  tree: DocsTreeResponse | DocsFailureBody = treeResponse()): DocsRefreshLoaderAnswer {
  const value: DocsRefreshResponse = { ok: true, fetch, tree };
  return { s: 'ok', value };
}

/** A fetch failure inside an ok refresh answer. */
export const fetchFailed = (word: string, ctx: Record<string, unknown> = {}): DocsRefreshFetch =>
  ({ state: 'failed', failure: bodyOf(word, ctx) });

export interface FakeLoaders {
  readonly loaders: DocsLoaders;
  readonly projects: Mock<() => Promise<DocsIndexAnswer>>;
  readonly tree: Mock<DocsLoaders['tree']>;
  readonly file: Mock<DocsLoaders['file']>;
  readonly raster: Mock<DocsLoaders['raster']>;
  readonly refresh: Mock<DocsLoaders['refresh']>;
}

/** Spies that answer `tree`, `file` and `refresh` by default; a test queues others with `mockResolvedValueOnce`. */
export function fakeLoaders(answers: {
  tree?: DocsTreeAnswer; file?: DocsFileAnswer; refresh?: DocsRefreshLoaderAnswer;
} = {}): FakeLoaders {
  const projects = vi.fn(async (): Promise<DocsIndexAnswer> => ({ s: 'unreachable' }));
  const tree = vi.fn(async (): Promise<DocsTreeAnswer> => answers.tree ?? okTree());
  const file = vi.fn(async (): Promise<DocsFileAnswer> => answers.file ?? okFile());
  const raster = vi.fn(async (): Promise<DocsRasterAnswer> => ({ s: 'unreachable' }));
  const refresh = vi.fn(async (): Promise<DocsRefreshLoaderAnswer> => answers.refresh ?? okRefresh());
  return { loaders: { projects, tree, file, raster, refresh }, projects, tree, file, raster, refresh };
}

/** The location a Docs URL parses to; throws on a URL that does not parse (a fixture defect). */
export function pageAt(url: string): DocsPageLocation {
  const q = url.indexOf('?');
  const parsed = parseDocsPage(q < 0 ? url : url.slice(0, q), q < 0 ? '' : url.slice(q));
  if (!parsed.ok) throw new Error(`fixture URL ${url} does not parse: ${parsed.why}`);
  return parsed.loc;
}
```

```tsx
// Docs W5 part 1, Task 5: one visit's slots (spec 2026-10-01 4.3). The tree slot is keyed by (project, ref) and
// reused across the visit's pages; the leaf's pin comes from `pinFor` (committed, draft or none); a committed body is
// keyed by its blob; a file read that says the listing moved re-lists once, then says "changing"; a word with an
// `auto` plan is retried once per (key, word), a `manual` one never; a 401 re-fetches on sign-in (M4.F5); and an
// unmount ends every timer and read. Loaders are spies; nothing reaches a server.
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { act, cleanup, renderHook } from '@testing-library/react';
import { DOCS_CLASS_CAP, type DocPin, type DocsPageLocation } from '../../shared/docs';
import { clearAuthLost, raiseAuthLost } from '../src/lib/auth';
import { DOCS_RELIST_WORDS } from '../src/docs/docsText';
import { fileKey, pinFor, treeKey, useDocsVisit } from '../src/docs/useDocsVisit';
import type { DocsLoaders } from '../src/docs/failures';
import {
  BLOB_1, BLOB_2, COMMIT_A, COMMIT_B, FP_1, SERVED, draftOf, entry, failedAnswer, fakeLoaders, holder, okFile, okTree,
  pageAt, treeOk,
} from './docsFixtures';

afterEach(() => {
  cleanup();
  clearAuthLost();
  vi.useRealTimers();
});

const NUL = String.fromCharCode(0);

/** Let every answer already resolved land, and the renders and effects it causes run. */
async function flush(): Promise<void> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 6; i += 1) await act(async () => {});
}

async function advance(ms: number): Promise<void> {
  await act(async () => {
    vi.advanceTimersByTime(ms);
  });
  await flush();
}

function visit(loaders: DocsLoaders, url: string | null, strict = false) {
  return renderHook(
    (p: { page: DocsPageLocation | null }) => useDocsVisit(p.page, loaders),
    { initialProps: { page: url === null ? null : pageAt(url) }, reactStrictMode: strict },
  );
}

const committedPin = (path: string, commit = COMMIT_A): DocPin =>
  ({ kind: 'committed', commit, servedRef: SERVED, section: 'specs', path });

describe('treeKey and the tree slot (spec 4.3)', () => {
  it('is exactly project + NUL + the ref as the page names it, empty for the default view', () => {
    expect(treeKey('demo', null)).toBe('demo' + NUL);
    expect(treeKey('demo', { kind: 'bare', name: 'ws/a' })).toBe('demo' + NUL + 'ws/a');
    expect(treeKey('demo', { kind: 'qualified', ref: 'refs/heads/main' })).toBe('demo' + NUL + 'refs/heads/main');
  });

  it('a page that failed to parse, and the index, make no request and have no tree slot', async () => {
    const f = fakeLoaders();
    const a = visit(f.loaders, null);
    const b = visit(f.loaders, '/docs');
    await flush();
    expect(f.tree).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(a.result.current.tree).toBeNull();
    expect(b.result.current.tree).toBeNull();
    expect(b.result.current.file).toEqual({ s: 'none' });
    expect(b.result.current.freshness).toEqual({ s: 'idle' });
  });

  it('shows loading, then the answer, with the time it was received', async () => {
    const f = fakeLoaders();
    const { result } = visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo');
    expect(result.current.tree).toEqual({ s: 'loading' });
    await flush();
    expect(f.tree).toHaveBeenCalledWith('demo', null);
    expect(result.current.tree?.s).toBe('ok');
  });

  it('two refs of one project are two slots, and going back to the first costs no GET', async () => {
    const f = fakeLoaders();
    f.tree.mockResolvedValueOnce(okTree(treeOk({ commit: COMMIT_A })));
    f.tree.mockResolvedValueOnce(okTree(treeOk({ commit: COMMIT_B })));
    const { result, rerender } = visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo?ref=a');
    await flush();
    rerender({ page: pageAt('/docs/demo?ref=b') });
    await flush();
    expect(f.tree).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(f.tree.mock.calls[1]).toEqual(['demo', { kind: 'bare', name: 'b' }]);
    const b = result.current.tree;
    expect(b?.s === 'ok' && b.answer.tree.ref.commit).toBe(COMMIT_B);
    rerender({ page: pageAt('/docs/demo?ref=a') });
    await flush();
    expect(f.tree).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    const a = result.current.tree;
    expect(a?.s === 'ok' && a.answer.tree.ref.commit).toBe(COMMIT_A);
  });

  it('one GET per key at a time: a Retry while the GET is in flight adds none', async () => {
    const f = fakeLoaders();
    f.tree.mockImplementationOnce(() => new Promise(() => {}));
    const { result } = visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo');
    await flush();
    act(() => result.current.retryTree());
    await flush();
    expect(f.tree).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  it('a tree failure is the slot; an unknown word is kept whole', async () => {
    const f = fakeLoaders({ tree: failedAnswer('a-word-from-a-newer-server') });
    const { result } = visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo');
    await flush();
    expect(result.current.tree).toEqual(failedAnswer('a-word-from-a-newer-server'));
  });
});

describe('pinFor: the leaf the tree implies (spec 4.3 item 5)', () => {
  const modified = entry('specs', 'a.md', { draft: draftOf('modified') });

  it('a default-view leaf opens the committed side at the served commit', () => {
    expect(pinFor(treeOk(), pageAt('/docs/demo/specs/a.md'))).toEqual(committedPin('a.md'));
  });

  it('the default view never opens a draft, even one a holder at the served commit admits', () => {
    const tree = treeOk({ entries: [modified], drafts: holder() });
    expect(pinFor(tree, pageAt('/docs/demo/specs/a.md'))).toEqual(committedPin('a.md'));
  });

  it("a ref view opens an admitted modified draft at the holder's branch, HEAD and fingerprint", () => {
    const tree = treeOk({ entries: [modified], drafts: holder(COMMIT_A) });
    expect(pinFor(tree, pageAt('/docs/demo/specs/a.md?ref=refs/heads/main'))).toEqual(
      { kind: 'draft', branch: 'main', head: COMMIT_A, section: 'specs', path: 'a.md', fp: FP_1 });
  });

  it('view=committed on that draft opens the committed side', () => {
    const tree = treeOk({ entries: [modified], drafts: holder() });
    expect(pinFor(tree, pageAt('/docs/demo/specs/a.md?ref=refs/heads/main&view=committed'))).toEqual(committedPin('a.md'));
  });

  it('a holder whose HEAD is not the served commit overlays nothing', () => {
    const tree = treeOk({ entries: [modified], drafts: holder(COMMIT_B, false) });
    expect(pinFor(tree, pageAt('/docs/demo/specs/a.md?ref=refs/heads/main'))).toEqual(committedPin('a.md'));
  });

  it.each(['deleted', 'typechange'] as const)('a %s draft opens the committed side', (state) => {
    const tree = treeOk({ entries: [entry('specs', 'a.md', { draft: draftOf(state) })], drafts: holder() });
    expect(pinFor(tree, pageAt('/docs/demo/specs/a.md?ref=refs/heads/main'))).toEqual(committedPin('a.md'));
  });

  it('a withheld new file opens nothing', () => {
    const tree = treeOk({
      entries: [entry('specs', 'n.md', { committed: null, draft: draftOf('untracked', { fp: null }) })], drafts: holder(),
    });
    expect(pinFor(tree, pageAt('/docs/demo/specs/n.md?ref=refs/heads/main'))).toBeNull();
  });

  it('a new file under view=committed opens nothing (there is no committed side)', () => {
    const tree = treeOk({ entries: [entry('specs', 'n.md', { committed: null, draft: draftOf('added') })], drafts: holder() });
    expect(pinFor(tree, pageAt('/docs/demo/specs/n.md?ref=refs/heads/main&view=committed'))).toBeNull();
  });

  it('a committed symlink opens nothing', () => {
    const tree = treeOk({ entries: [entry('specs', 'l.md', { committed: { kind: 'symlink', blob: BLOB_1, size: 4 } })] });
    expect(pinFor(tree, pageAt('/docs/demo/specs/l.md'))).toBeNull();
  });

  it('a directory page, a path with no entry, a section and a project open nothing', () => {
    const tree = treeOk({ entries: [entry('specs', 'd/a.md')] });
    expect(pinFor(tree, pageAt('/docs/demo/specs/d/'))).toBeNull();
    expect(pinFor(tree, pageAt('/docs/demo/specs/d'))).toBeNull();
    expect(pinFor(tree, pageAt('/docs/demo/specs'))).toBeNull();
    expect(pinFor(tree, pageAt('/docs/demo'))).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe('fileKey: a committed body by its blob, a draft by its whole pin (spec 4.3 item 2)', () => {
  it('a committed key names the blob and its place, never the commit', () => {

});

describe('the file slot', () => {
  it('a leaf reads its committed pin once and shows the answer with that pin', async () => {
    const f = fakeLoaders();
    const { result } = visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo/specs/a.md');
    await flush();
    expect(f.file).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(f.file.mock.calls[0]?.[0]).toBe('demo');
    expect(f.file.mock.calls[0]?.[1]).toEqual(committedPin('a.md'));
    expect(f.file.mock.calls[0]?.[2]).toBeInstanceOf(AbortSignal);
    expect(result.current.file.s).toBe('ok');
    expect(result.current.file.s === 'ok' && result.current.file.pin).toEqual(committedPin('a.md'));
  });

  it('a draft leaf in a ref view reads the draft pin', async () => {
    const f = fakeLoaders({ tree: okTree(treeOk({ entries: [entry('specs', 'a.md', { draft: draftOf('modified') })], drafts: holder() })) });
    visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo/specs/a.md?ref=refs/heads/main');
    await flush();
    expect(f.file.mock.calls[0]?.[1]).toEqual(
      { kind: 'draft', branch: 'main', head: COMMIT_A, section: 'specs', path: 'a.md', fp: FP_1 });
  });

  it('a directory, a section and a raster leaf read no file', async () => {
    const f = fakeLoaders({ tree: okTree(treeOk({ entries: [entry('specs', 'd/a.md'), entry('specs', 'p.png')] })) });
    const { result, rerender } = visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo/specs/d/');

    await flush();

    await flush();
    expect(f.file).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(result.current.file).toEqual({ s: 'none' });
  });

  it('a leaf listed over its class cap is too-large and is never requested (spec 4.4)', async () => {
    const cap = DOCS_CLASS_CAP.markdown;
    const big = entry('specs', 'big.md', { committed: { kind: 'file', blob: BLOB_1, size: cap + 1 } });
    const f = fakeLoaders({ tree: okTree(treeOk({ entries: [big] })) });

    await flush();
    expect(f.file).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(result.current.file).toEqual({ s: 'too-large', pin: committedPin('big.md'), size: cap + 1, cap });
  });

  it('a leaf listed at exactly its cap is read', async () => {
    const cap = DOCS_CLASS_CAP.markdown;
    const edge = entry('specs', 'edge.md', { committed: { kind: 'file', blob: BLOB_1, size: cap } });
    const f = fakeLoaders({ tree: okTree(treeOk({ entries: [edge] })) });
    visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo/specs/edge.md');
    await flush();
    expect(f.file).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  it('a committed leaf whose blob is unchanged after the branch moves is not read again, and reports the new pin', async () => {
    const f = fakeLoaders();
    f.tree.mockResolvedValueOnce(okTree(treeOk({ commit: COMMIT_A })));
    f.tree.mockResolvedValueOnce(okTree(treeOk({ commit: COMMIT_B })));
    const { result } = visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo/specs/a.md');
    await flush();
    act(() => result.current.retryTree());
    await flush();
    expect(f.tree).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(f.file).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(result.current.file.s === 'ok' && result.current.file.pin).toEqual(committedPin('a.md', COMMIT_B));
    expect(result.current.updatedTo).toBeNull();
  });

  it('a changed blob is read at the new pin, the old body stays until it answers, then updatedTo names the commit', async () => {
    const f = fakeLoaders();
    const moved = treeOk({ commit: COMMIT_B, entries: [entry('specs', 'a.md', { committed: { kind: 'file', blob: BLOB_2, size: 100 } })] });
    f.tree.mockResolvedValueOnce(okTree(treeOk()));
    f.tree.mockResolvedValueOnce(okTree(moved));
    let release: (v: Awaited<ReturnType<DocsLoaders['file']>>) => void = () => {};
    const { result } = visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo/specs/a.md');
    await flush();
    f.file.mockImplementationOnce(() => new Promise((r) => { release = r; }));
    act(() => result.current.retryTree());
    await flush();
    expect(f.file).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(f.file.mock.calls[1]?.[1]).toEqual(committedPin('a.md', COMMIT_B));
    expect(result.current.file.s === 'ok' && result.current.file.pin).toEqual(committedPin('a.md'));
    expect(result.current.updatedTo).toBeNull();
    await act(async () => release(okFile('# B')));
    await flush();
    expect(result.current.file.s === 'ok' && result.current.file.pin).toEqual(committedPin('a.md', COMMIT_B));
    expect(result.current.updatedTo).toBe(COMMIT_B);
  });

  it('opening the committed version of a draft is a new leaf, not an update', async () => {
    const tree = treeOk({ entries: [entry('specs', 'a.md', { draft: draftOf('modified') })], drafts: holder() });
    const f = fakeLoaders({ tree: okTree(tree) });
    const { result, rerender } = visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo/specs/a.md?ref=refs/heads/main');
    await flush();
    rerender({ page: pageAt('/docs/demo/specs/a.md?ref=refs/heads/main&view=committed') });
    await flush();
    expect(f.file).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(result.current.updatedTo).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe('a file read that says the listing moved (spec 4.3 item 1)', () => {
  const WORDS = ['unknown-commit', 'draft-changed', 'worktree-moved', 'worktree-gone'];

  it('the re-list words are exactly the four the spec names', () => {
    expect([...DOCS_RELIST_WORDS].sort()).toEqual([...WORDS].sort());
  });

  it.each(WORDS)('%s re-lists the tree once and reads again, then shows changing with Retry', async (word) => {
    const f = fakeLoaders();
    f.file.mockResolvedValueOnce(failedAnswer(word));
    f.file.mockResolvedValueOnce(failedAnswer(word));

    await flush();
    expect(f.tree).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(f.file).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(result.current.file).toEqual({ s: 'changing', pin: committedPin('a.md'), word });
    await flush();
    expect(f.tree).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    act(() => result.current.retryFile());
    await flush();
    expect(f.tree).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
    expect(f.file).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
    expect(result.current.file.s).toBe('ok');
  });

  it('a word outside the four is the slot, with no re-list', async () => {
    const f = fakeLoaders({ file: failedAnswer('absent-path') });

    await flush();
    expect(f.tree).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(result.current.file).toEqual({ s: 'failed', pin: committedPin('a.md'), body: failedAnswer('absent-path').body });
  });
});

describe('retries: one automatic retry per key and word, a manual word never (spec 4.3 item 4, 4.7)', () => {
  it('docs-busy {retryAfterMs: 2000} re-GETs the tree once at 2000, then offers only Retry', async () => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    const f = fakeLoaders({ tree: failedAnswer('docs-busy', { retryAfterMs: 2000 }) });
    const { result } = visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo');
    await flush();
    expect(f.tree).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    await advance(1999);
    expect(f.tree).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    await advance(1);
    expect(f.tree).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    await advance(600_000);
    expect(f.tree).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(result.current.tree?.s).toBe('failed');
    act(() => result.current.retryTree());
    await flush();
    expect(f.tree).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
  });

  it('a manual word never retries by itself', async () => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    const f = fakeLoaders({ tree: failedAnswer('git-failed') });
    visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo');
    await flush();
    await advance(600_000);
    expect(f.tree).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  it('caps-unknown waits 5 s', async () => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    const f = fakeLoaders({ tree: failedAnswer('caps-unknown') });
    visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo');
    await flush();
    await advance(4999);
    expect(f.tree).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    await advance(1);
    expect(f.tree).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
  });

  it('the bookkeeping is per word: a second word gets its own one retry, a repeated one none', async () => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    const f = fakeLoaders();
    f.tree.mockResolvedValueOnce(failedAnswer('docs-busy', { retryAfterMs: 1000 }));
    f.tree.mockResolvedValueOnce(failedAnswer('link-failed', { retryAfterMs: 1000 }));
    f.tree.mockResolvedValueOnce(failedAnswer('docs-busy', { retryAfterMs: 1000 }));
    visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo');
    await flush();
    await advance(1000);
    await advance(1000);
    expect(f.tree).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
    await advance(60_000);
    expect(f.tree).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
  });

  it('a file read answering an auto word is read once more after its wait, then offers Retry', async () => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    const f = fakeLoaders({ file: failedAnswer('docs-busy', { retryAfterMs: 2000 }) });
    const { result } = visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo/specs/a.md');
    await flush();
    expect(f.file).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    await advance(2000);
    expect(f.file).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    await advance(600_000);
    expect(f.file).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(result.current.file.s).toBe('failed');
    act(() => result.current.retryFile());
    await flush();
    expect(f.file).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
  });

  it('a file read answering a manual word is not read again until Retry', async () => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    const f = fakeLoaders({ file: failedAnswer('git-failed') });
    const { result } = visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo/specs/a.md');
    await flush();
    await advance(600_000);
    expect(f.file).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    act(() => result.current.retryFile());
    await flush();
    expect(f.file).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
  });
});

describe('sign-in and unmount', () => {
  it('M4.F5: a 401 gives the auth slot, and clearAuthLost() calls loaders.tree again', async () => {
    const f = fakeLoaders();
    f.tree.mockResolvedValueOnce({ s: 'auth' });
    const { result } = visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo');
    await flush();
    expect(result.current.tree).toEqual({ s: 'auth' });
    raiseAuthLost('expired');
    act(() => clearAuthLost());
```

```tsx
  it('an ok tree replaces the slot and the freshness is answered', async () => {

  /** A visit whose auto POST waits for the test, so the slot before the answer can be held. */
  async function heldThenAnswered(answer: DocsRefreshLoaderAnswer) {
    let settle: (a: DocsRefreshLoaderAnswer) => void = () => {};
    const f = fakeLoaders({ tree: due() });
    f.refresh.mockImplementationOnce(() => new Promise((r) => { settle = r; }));

  });

    let settle: (a: DocsRefreshLoaderAnswer) => void = () => {};

    const { result } = visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo/specs/a.md');
    await flush();
    expect(f.file).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    let release: (a: Awaited<ReturnType<DocsLoaders['file']>>) => void = () => {};
    f.file.mockImplementationOnce(() => new Promise((r) => { release = r; }));
    await act(async () => settle(okRefresh(RAN, treeResponse(moved))));
    await flush();
    expect(f.file).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(f.file.mock.calls[1]?.[1]).toMatchObject({ kind: 'committed', commit: COMMIT_B });
    expect(result.current.file).toMatchObject({ s: 'ok', pin: { commit: COMMIT_A } });
    expect(result.current.updatedTo).toBeNull();
    await act(async () => release(okFile('# B')));
    await flush();
    expect(result.current.file).toMatchObject({ s: 'ok', pin: { commit: COMMIT_B } });
    expect(result.current.updatedTo).toBe(COMMIT_B);
  });

  it('a POST the route did not answer is refresh-failed', async () => {
    const f = fakeLoaders({ tree: due(), refresh: { s: 'unreachable' } });
    const { result } = visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo');

    expect(result.current.freshness).toEqual({ s: 'refresh-failed', answer: { s: 'unreachable' } });

    visit(f.loaders, '/docs/demo');

    await advance(2000);
    expect(f.refresh).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    await advance(600_000);
    expect(f.refresh).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
  });
});
```
