- [ ] **Step 6: Write the hook.** Create `pwa/src/docs/useDocsVisit.ts` with exactly:

```ts
// One Docs visit's state (spec 2026-10-01 4.3): the tree slots, the file slots, the leaf's expected pin, auto-refresh
// once per open, the retry plan's timers and the three lock ages (refinement (l)), and the re-list triggers (a
// refresh answer, a file read that says the listing is stale, a return to the tab after DOCS_STALE_MS, a sign-in).
// A visit is one mount of the hook: everything it remembers, including which keys it auto-refreshed and which
// failures it auto-retried, dies with the mount, so reopening the screen is a new visit.
//
// Every request is started from an effect or an answer handler, never from render; render only reads. The visit's
// memory lives in refs (so an answer handler always reads the newest state, and StrictMode's second effect pass sees
// the first pass's in-flight request), and a version counter re-renders when an answer lands.
import { useEffect, useReducer, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import {
  DOCS_CLASS_CAP, DOCS_STALE_MS, contentClass, docsRefText, entryView,
  type DocPin, type DocsEntry, type DocsFailure, type DocsFailureBody, type DocsFileResponse, type DocsPageLocation,
  type DocsRefreshFetch, type DocsRefSpec, type DocsTreeOk, type DocsTreeResponse,
} from '../../../shared/docs';
import { onAuthRegained } from '../lib/auth';
import {
  docsRetryPlan, type DocsClientSlot, type DocsFileAnswer, type DocsLoaders, type DocsNotOk,
  type DocsRefreshLoaderAnswer, type DocsTreeAnswer,
} from './failures';
import { DOCS_RELIST_WORDS } from './docsText';

/** A tree slot, exactly spec 4.3's type. `loading` is also what a page shows before its first GET has started. */
export type TreeSlot =
  | { s: 'loading' }
  | { s: 'ok'; answer: DocsTreeResponse; receivedAt: number }
  | { s: 'failed'; body: DocsFailureBody }
  | DocsClientSlot;

/** The current leaf's body. Every arm but `none` carries the pin it is about.
 *  - `none`: no file request is due here: the tree slot is not `ok`, the page is not a leaf of this tree, `pinFor`
 *    answered null, or the leaf is a raster (`DocImage` loads its bytes through `loaders.raster`).
 *  - `too-large`: the listed size is over `DOCS_CLASS_CAP` for the path's class; nothing was requested (spec 4.4).
 *  - `changing`: a read answered a word that means the listing moved (`DOCS_RELIST_WORDS`) after the one automatic
 *    re-list was spent; the page offers Retry.
 *  - `ok`: `pin` is the OPENED pin. After a re-list it can be older than `pinFor`'s answer only while the new pin's
 *    read is in flight (the old body stays on screen). */
export type FileSlot =
  | { s: 'none' }
  | { s: 'loading'; pin: DocPin }
  | { s: 'ok'; pin: DocPin; answer: DocsFileResponse; receivedAt: number }
  | { s: 'failed'; pin: DocPin; body: DocsFailureBody }
  | { s: 'too-large'; pin: DocPin; size: number; cap: number }
  | { s: 'changing'; pin: DocPin; word: DocsFailure }
  | (DocsClientSlot & { pin: DocPin });

/** The refresh state of the current tree key (spec 4.5's freshness chip reads it beside the tree's own facts).
 *  - `idle`: no refresh this visit for this key.
 *  - `fetching`: a POST is in flight.
 *  - `answered`: the route answered `fetch`; `at` is when (Date.now()).
 *  - `soon`: `fetch-too-soon`; one automatic POST is due at `retryAt` (Date.now() clock).
 *  - `stale-lock`: `ref-locked` with a lock at least `DOCS_LOCK_STALE_MS` old; no automatic retry. `ref` null: the
 *    answer named no ref.
 *  - `refresh-failed`: the POST itself got no route answer (a word from the route, or a client slot).
 *  - `relist-failed`: a re-list (a refresh's tree, or a GET) failed while a listing was held; the listing stays. */
export type Freshness =
  | { s: 'idle' }
  | { s: 'fetching'; reason: 'auto' | 'manual' }
  | { s: 'answered'; fetch: DocsRefreshFetch; at: number }
  | { s: 'soon'; retryAt: number }
  | { s: 'stale-lock'; ref: string | null }
  | { s: 'refresh-failed'; answer: DocsNotOk }
  | { s: 'relist-failed'; answer: DocsNotOk };

const NUL = '\u0000';

/** A tree slot's key: the project and the ref as the page names it, never the path (spec 4.3), so every page of
 *  one (project, ref) shares one listing and two refs of one project are two slots. */
export function treeKey(project: string, ref: DocsRefSpec | null): string {
  return project + NUL + (ref === null ? '' : docsRefText(ref));
}

function findEntry(tree: DocsTreeOk, section: DocPin['section'], path: string): DocsEntry | undefined {
  return tree.entries.find((e) => e.section === section && e.path === path);
}

/** A file body's key (spec 4.3 item 2). A committed body is keyed by its blob (and its place, since the class comes
 *  from the path), so a file unchanged across a moving branch is not downloaded again; a committed pin whose entry
 *  is not committed in `tree` falls back to the exact commit. A draft is keyed by every field of its pin. */
export function fileKey(pin: DocPin, tree: DocsTreeOk): string {
  if (pin.kind === 'draft') return ['draft', pin.branch, pin.head, pin.section, pin.path, pin.fp].join(NUL);
  const blob = findEntry(tree, pin.section, pin.path)?.committed?.blob;
  return blob === undefined
    ? ['commit', pin.commit, pin.section, pin.path].join(NUL)
    : ['blob', blob, pin.section, pin.path].join(NUL);
}

/** The pin the tree implies for the page's leaf (spec 4.3 item 5; pure). Null has one meaning: the page opens no
 *  file in this tree (not a leaf page, no such entry, or `entryView` opens nothing for it). The default view
 *  (`page.ref === null`) never opens a draft; `view=committed` opens the committed side of a draft row, or nothing
 *  when there is none. */
export function pinFor(tree: DocsTreeOk, page: DocsPageLocation): DocPin | null {
  if (page.kind !== 'path' || page.dirSlash) return null;
  const entry = findEntry(tree, page.section, page.path);
  if (entry === undefined) return null;
  const view = entryView(entry, tree.drafts, page.ref === null ? 'default' : 'ref');
  if (view.opens === 'none') return null;
  const committed: DocPin = {
    kind: 'committed', commit: tree.ref.commit, servedRef: tree.ref.served, section: page.section, path: page.path,
  };
  if (view.opens === 'committed') return committed;
  if (page.view === 'committed') return view.offersCommitted ? committed : null;
  const drafts = tree.drafts;
  const fp = entry.draft?.fp;
  // entryView opens a draft only for an admitted holder's regular file with a fingerprint.
  if (drafts.state !== 'holder' || fp === undefined || fp === null) {
    throw new Error('pinFor: a draft opened with no holder or fingerprint');
  }
  return { kind: 'draft', branch: drafts.branch, head: drafts.worktree.head, section: page.section, path: page.path, fp };
}

/** One visit, as the Docs views read it. */
export interface DocsVisit {
  /** The current page's tree slot; null = the page names no project (the index, or a URL that did not parse). */
  readonly tree: TreeSlot | null;
  readonly file: FileSlot;
  readonly freshness: Freshness;
  /** The commit the current leaf now reads at (a committed pin's commit, a draft pin's holder HEAD) after a re-list
   *  changed its pin and the new read answered; null = no such change for this leaf in this visit. */
  readonly updatedTo: string | null;
  /** A fragment to scroll to once the body renders; null = nothing to scroll to. */
  readonly pendingFragment: string | null;
  /** GET the current tree again now: Retry on a failed slot, Re-list on an ok one. A no-op while one is in flight. */
  retryTree(): void;
  /** Read the current leaf again: after `changing`, re-list first; after any other failure, read again. */
  retryFile(): void;
  /** The freshness chip's tap: one manual POST, only while the tree slot is ok and no POST is in flight. */
  refreshManual(): void;
  /** `unresolved-ref`'s Fetch from origin: one manual POST, only while the slot holds that word. */
  fetchFromOrigin(): void;
  setFragment(fragment: string | null): void;
}

type Target = { readonly project: string; readonly ref: DocsRefSpec | null };
type FileEntry = { slot: Exclude<FileSlot, { s: 'none' } | { s: 'too-large' }>; treeKey: string; awaitingRelist: boolean };
type Wanted =
  | { kind: 'none' }
  | { kind: 'too-large'; slot: FileSlot }
  | { kind: 'read'; target: Target; tKey: string; fKey: string; leaf: string; pin: DocPin };

interface Store {
  alive: boolean;
  readonly targets: Map<string, Target>;
  readonly trees: Map<string, TreeSlot>;
  readonly treeInflight: Set<string>;
  readonly refreshInflight: Set<string>;
  readonly freshness: Map<string, Freshness>;
  readonly files: Map<string, FileEntry>;
  /** Per leaf (tree key, section, path, view): the file key last shown `ok`. */
  readonly shown: Map<string, string>;
  readonly updatedTo: Map<string, string>;
  readonly timers: Set<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>;
  readonly aborts: Set<AbortController>;
}

function newStore(): Store {
  return {
    alive: false, targets: new Map(), trees: new Map(), treeInflight: new Set(), refreshInflight: new Set(),
    freshness: new Map(), files: new Map(), shown: new Map(), updatedTo: new Map(),
    timers: new Set(), aborts: new Set(),
  };
}

function targetOf(page: DocsPageLocation | null): Target | null {
  if (page === null || page.kind === 'index') return null;
  return { project: page.project, ref: page.ref };
}

/** Spec 2 row 60's PWA half (refinement (m)): a `refs/heads/` view never auto-POSTs, whatever `refreshDue` says. */
function isLocalHeadsRef(ref: DocsRefSpec | null): boolean {
  return ref !== null && ref.kind === 'qualified' && ref.ref.startsWith('refs/heads/');
}

function samePin(a: DocPin, b: DocPin): boolean {
  if (a.kind === 'committed' && b.kind === 'committed') {
    return a.commit === b.commit && a.servedRef === b.servedRef && a.section === b.section && a.path === b.path;
  }
  if (a.kind === 'draft' && b.kind === 'draft') {
    return a.branch === b.branch && a.head === b.head && a.section === b.section && a.path === b.path && a.fp === b.fp;
  }
  return false;
}

function wantedFile(slot: TreeSlot | null, page: DocsPageLocation | null, target: Target | null): Wanted {
  if (slot?.s !== 'ok' || page?.kind !== 'path' || target === null) return { kind: 'none' };
  const tree = slot.answer.tree;
  const pin = pinFor(tree, page);
  if (pin === null || contentClass(page.path) === 'raster') return { kind: 'none' };
  const entry = findEntry(tree, page.section, page.path);
  const size = pin.kind === 'draft' ? entry?.draft?.size : entry?.committed?.size;
  const cap = DOCS_CLASS_CAP[contentClass(page.path)];
  if (typeof size === 'number' && size > cap) return { kind: 'too-large', slot: { s: 'too-large', pin, size, cap } };
  const tKey = treeKey(target.project, target.ref);
  const leaf = [tKey, page.section, page.path, page.view].join(NUL);
  return { kind: 'read', target, tKey, fKey: fileKey(pin, tree), leaf, pin };
}

function pinCommit(pin: DocPin): string {
  return pin.kind === 'committed' ? pin.commit : pin.head;
}

/** The visit for `page` (null = a URL that failed to parse: no request). `loaders` may change identity between
 *  renders; the newest is used for every later request. */
export function useDocsVisit(page: DocsPageLocation | null, loaders: DocsLoaders): DocsVisit {
  const [, bump] = useReducer((n: number) => n + 1, 0);
  const [pendingFragment, setFragment] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const loadersRef = useRef(loaders);
  loadersRef.current = loaders;
  const pageRef = useRef(page);
  pageRef.current = page;
  // Spec 4.3 items 3 and 4: one Set each, per mount. A key is added BEFORE its POST, synchronously.
  const autoRefreshed = useRef(new Set<string>());
  const autoRetried = useRef(new Set<string>());
  const storeRef = useRef<Store | null>(null);
  storeRef.current ??= newStore();
  const st = storeRef.current;

  const changed = (): void => {
    if (st.alive) bump();
  };
  const later = (ms: number, fn: () => void): void => {
    const t = setTimeout(() => {
      st.timers.delete(t);
      fn();
    }, ms);
    st.timers.add(t);
  };
  /** One automatic retry per (request kind, key, word) for the whole visit; true when this call takes it. */
  const takeAutoRetry = (scope: string, key: string, word: string): boolean => {
    const id = [scope, key, word].join(NUL);
    if (autoRetried.current.has(id)) return false;
    autoRetried.current.add(id);
    return true;
  };

  /** Drop every file entry that waited for `tKey`'s re-list, so the next render reads its leaf again. */
  const releaseRelistWaiters = (tKey: string): void => {
    for (const [fKey, e] of st.files) if (e.awaitingRelist && e.treeKey === tKey) st.files.delete(fKey);
  };

  const setTreeOk = (key: string, answer: DocsTreeResponse): void => {
    st.trees.set(key, { s: 'ok', answer, receivedAt: Date.now() });
    if (st.freshness.get(key)?.s === 'relist-failed') st.freshness.set(key, { s: 'idle' });
  };

  const refresh = (target: Target, reason: 'auto' | 'manual'): void => {
    const key = treeKey(target.project, target.ref);
    if (st.refreshInflight.has(key)) return;
    st.refreshInflight.add(key);
    st.freshness.set(key, { s: 'fetching', reason });
    const body = { ref: target.ref === null ? null : docsRefText(target.ref), reason };
    void loadersRef.current.refresh(target.project, body).then((a) => {
      st.refreshInflight.delete(key);
      if (!st.alive) return;
      applyRefresh(target, key, reason, a);
      changed();
    });
  };

  const applyRefresh = (target: Target, key: string, reason: 'auto' | 'manual', a: DocsRefreshLoaderAnswer): void => {
    const now = Date.now();
    if (a.s !== 'ok') {
      st.freshness.set(key, { s: 'refresh-failed', answer: a });
      if (a.s === 'failed') {
        const plan = docsRetryPlan(a.body);
        if (plan.kind === 'auto' && takeAutoRetry('refresh', key, a.body.failure)) {
          later(plan.afterMs, () => refresh(target, reason));
        }
      }
      return;
    }
    const { fetch, tree } = a.value;
    if (fetch.state === 'failed') {
      // A fetch failure changes only the chip (spec 4.3): the listing it came with is the one already held.
      const body = fetch.failure;
      const plan = docsRetryPlan(body);
      let fresh: Freshness = { s: 'answered', fetch, at: now };
      if (plan.kind === 'auto' && takeAutoRetry('refresh', key, body.failure)) {
        later(plan.afterMs, () => refresh(target, reason));
        if (body.failure === 'fetch-too-soon') fresh = { s: 'soon', retryAt: now + plan.afterMs };
      } else if (body.failure === 'ref-locked' && plan.kind === 'none') {
        fresh = { s: 'stale-lock', ref: typeof body.ref === 'string' ? body.ref : null };
      }
      st.freshness.set(key, fresh);
      return;
    }
    if (tree.ok) {
      setTreeOk(key, tree);
      releaseRelistWaiters(key);
      st.freshness.set(key, { s: 'answered', fetch, at: now });
    } else if (st.trees.get(key)?.s === 'ok') {
      st.freshness.set(key, { s: 'relist-failed', answer: { s: 'failed', body: tree } });
    } else {
      st.trees.set(key, { s: 'failed', body: tree });
      st.freshness.set(key, { s: 'answered', fetch, at: now });
    }
  };

  const listTree = (target: Target): void => {
    const key = treeKey(target.project, target.ref);
    if (st.treeInflight.has(key)) return;
    st.treeInflight.add(key);
    st.targets.set(key, target);
    // A held listing stays on screen through its re-list; anything else shows loading.
    if (st.trees.get(key)?.s !== 'ok') st.trees.set(key, { s: 'loading' });
    void loadersRef.current.tree(target.project, target.ref).then((a) => {
      st.treeInflight.delete(key);
      if (!st.alive) return;
      applyTreeGet(target, key, a);
      changed();
    });
  };

  const applyTreeGet = (target: Target, key: string, a: DocsTreeAnswer): void => {
    releaseRelistWaiters(key);
    const relisted = st.trees.get(key)?.s === 'ok';
    if (a.s === 'ok') {
      setTreeOk(key, a.value);
      // Auto-refresh (spec 4.3): when the slot BECOMES ok (a re-list of a held listing is a GET only, M4.A3), once
      // per key per visit, and never on a refs/heads/ view (refinement (m)).
      if (!relisted && a.value.refreshDue && !isLocalHeadsRef(target.ref) && !autoRefreshed.current.has(key)) {
        autoRefreshed.current.add(key);
        refresh(target, 'auto');
      }
      return;
    }
    if (relisted && a.s !== 'auth') {
      st.freshness.set(key, { s: 'relist-failed', answer: a });
      return;
    }
    st.trees.set(key, a);
    if (a.s === 'failed') {
      const plan = docsRetryPlan(a.body);
      if (plan.kind === 'auto' && takeAutoRetry('tree', key, a.body.failure)) {
        later(plan.afterMs, () => listTree(target));
      }
    }
  };

  const readFile = (w: Extract<Wanted, { kind: 'read' }>): void => {
    const { fKey, tKey, pin } = w;
    // The entry is the single-flight mark: the effect starts a read only for a key with no entry.
    st.files.set(fKey, { slot: { s: 'loading', pin }, treeKey: tKey, awaitingRelist: false });
    const ctl = new AbortController();
    st.aborts.add(ctl);
    void loadersRef.current.file(w.target.project, pin, ctl.signal).then((a) => {
      st.aborts.delete(ctl);
      if (!st.alive) return;
      applyFile(w, a);
      changed();
    }, (err: unknown) => {
      st.aborts.delete(ctl);
      if (ctl.signal.aborted) return;
      throw err;
    });
  };

  const applyFile = (w: Extract<Wanted, { kind: 'read' }>, a: DocsFileAnswer): void => {
    const { fKey, tKey, pin } = w;
    const put = (slot: FileEntry['slot'], awaitingRelist = false): void => {
      st.files.set(fKey, { slot, treeKey: tKey, awaitingRelist });
    };
    if (a.s === 'ok') {
      put({ s: 'ok', pin, answer: a.value, receivedAt: Date.now() });
      return;
    }
    if (a.s !== 'failed') {
      put({ ...a, pin });
      return;
    }
    const word = a.body.failure;
    if (DOCS_RELIST_WORDS.has(word)) {
      // Spec 4.3 item 1: the listing moved under the read. Re-list once automatically, then "changing, Retry".
      if (takeAutoRetry('file', fKey, word)) {
        put({ s: 'loading', pin }, true);
        listTree(w.target);
      } else {
        put({ s: 'changing', pin, word });
      }
      return;
    }
    put({ s: 'failed', pin, body: a.body });
    const plan = docsRetryPlan(a.body);
    if (plan.kind === 'auto' && takeAutoRetry('file', fKey, word)) {
      later(plan.afterMs, () => {
        st.files.delete(fKey);
        changed();
      });
    }
  };

  // The mount: sign-in re-fetches, a return to the tab re-lists a stale listing, and unmount ends every timer and
  // read. StrictMode runs this twice; nothing here starts a request, so the second pass changes nothing.
  useEffect(() => {
    st.alive = true;
    const unsubscribe = onAuthRegained(() => {
      for (const [key, slot] of st.trees) {
        const target = st.targets.get(key);
        if (slot.s === 'auth' && target !== undefined) listTree(target);
      }
      for (const [fKey, e] of st.files) if (e.slot.s === 'auth') st.files.delete(fKey);
      changed();
    });
    const onVisibility = (): void => {
      if (document.visibilityState !== 'visible') return;
      const target = targetOf(pageRef.current);
      if (target === null) return;
      const slot = st.trees.get(treeKey(target.project, target.ref));
      // A GET, never a POST (spec 4.3, M4.A3).
      if (slot?.s === 'ok' && Date.now() - slot.receivedAt > DOCS_STALE_MS) listTree(target);
    };
    document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', onVisibility);
    return () => {
      st.alive = false;
      unsubscribe();
      document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', onVisibility);
      for (const t of st.timers) clearTimeout(t);
      st.timers.clear();
      for (const c of st.aborts) c.abort();
      st.aborts.clear();
    };
    // `st` is this mount's store: one object for the hook's life, so this runs once per mount (twice under
    // StrictMode, whose second pass finds nothing to start).
  }, [st]);

  const target = targetOf(page);
  const tKey = target === null ? null : treeKey(target.project, target.ref);
  const tree: TreeSlot | null = tKey === null ? null : (st.trees.get(tKey) ?? { s: 'loading' });
  const wanted = wantedFile(tree, page, target);

  // Start what this page needs and settle what it shows. Runs after every commit; every start is guarded.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (target !== null && tKey !== null && !st.trees.has(tKey)) listTree(target);
    if (wanted.kind !== 'read') return;
    const e = st.files.get(wanted.fKey);
    if (e === undefined) {
      readFile(wanted);
      return;
    }
    if (e.slot.s !== 'ok') return;
    let dirty = false;
    if (!samePin(e.slot.pin, wanted.pin)) {
      // The same blob at a newer commit: the bytes held are the bytes at the new pin.
      st.files.set(wanted.fKey, { ...e, slot: { ...e.slot, pin: wanted.pin } });
      dirty = true;
    }
    const prev = st.shown.get(wanted.leaf);
    if (prev !== wanted.fKey) {
      st.shown.set(wanted.leaf, wanted.fKey);
      if (prev !== undefined) {
        st.updatedTo.set(wanted.leaf, pinCommit(wanted.pin));
        dirty = true;
      }
    }
    if (dirty) changed();
  });

  let file: FileSlot = { s: 'none' };
  let updatedTo: string | null = null;
  if (wanted.kind === 'too-large') file = wanted.slot;
  if (wanted.kind === 'read') {
    updatedTo = st.updatedTo.get(wanted.leaf) ?? null;
    const e = st.files.get(wanted.fKey);
    if (e !== undefined && e.slot.s !== 'loading') {
      file = e.slot;
    } else {
      // While the new pin's read is in flight, the leaf keeps the body it showed (spec 4.3: "keeping scroll").
      const prev = st.shown.get(wanted.leaf);
      const held = prev === undefined || prev === wanted.fKey ? undefined : st.files.get(prev);
      file = held?.slot.s === 'ok' ? held.slot : { s: 'loading', pin: wanted.pin };
    }
  }
  const freshness: Freshness = tKey === null ? { s: 'idle' } : (st.freshness.get(tKey) ?? { s: 'idle' });

  return {
    tree,
    file,
    freshness,
    updatedTo,
    pendingFragment,
    retryTree: () => {
      const t = targetOf(pageRef.current);
      if (t === null) return;
      listTree(t);
      changed();
    },
    retryFile: () => {
      const t = targetOf(pageRef.current);
      const slot = t === null ? undefined : st.trees.get(treeKey(t.project, t.ref));
      const w = wantedFile(slot ?? null, pageRef.current, t);
      if (w.kind !== 'read') return;
      const e = st.files.get(w.fKey);
      if (e === undefined || e.slot.s === 'ok' || e.slot.s === 'loading') return;
      if (e.slot.s === 'changing') {
        st.files.set(w.fKey, { slot: { s: 'loading', pin: w.pin }, treeKey: w.tKey, awaitingRelist: true });
        listTree(w.target);
      } else {
        st.files.delete(w.fKey);
      }
      changed();
    },
    refreshManual: () => {
      const t = targetOf(pageRef.current);
      if (t === null || st.trees.get(treeKey(t.project, t.ref))?.s !== 'ok') return;
      refresh(t, 'manual');
      changed();
    },
    fetchFromOrigin: () => {
      const t = targetOf(pageRef.current);
      const slot = t === null ? undefined : st.trees.get(treeKey(t.project, t.ref));
      if (t === null || slot?.s !== 'failed' || slot.body.failure !== 'unresolved-ref') return;
      refresh(t, 'manual');
      changed();
    },
    setFragment,
  };
}
```

```bash
git add pwa/src/docs/useDocsVisit.ts pwa/src/docs/docsText.ts pwa/test/docsFixtures.ts pwa/test/docs-visit.test.tsx pwa/test/docs-refresh.test.tsx
git status --porcelain | grep -vE '^(A |M ) ' ; git diff --cached --name-only | wc -l
git commit -m "pwa: useDocsVisit holds the visit's tree and file slots, pinFor, auto-refresh once per open, the retries and the re-lists (docs W5.1)" \
  -m "One visit is one mount (spec 4.3). Tree slots are keyed by project and ref, never by path, so a project, section, leaf and sibling share one GET; pinFor answers the leaf's committed pin, the admitted draft's pin in a ref view, or null; a committed body is keyed by its blob and place, so an unchanged file survives a moving branch without a second download; a file read answering one of the four re-list words re-lists once, then reads 'changing' with Retry; a re-list keeps the old body until the new pin answers and then names it in updatedTo." \
  -m "Auto-refresh: when a tree slot becomes ok by GET with refreshDue, once per key per mount (a Set in a useRef, added before the POST), never on a refs/heads/ view (refinement (m)); unresolved-ref offers a manual Fetch from origin. A refresh answer's ok tree replaces the slot, its fetch failure changes only the freshness, and its tree failure keeps the listing. One automatic retry per kind, key and word for an auto plan: fetch-too-soon at its retryAfterMs, a young or gone ref lock at 3 s, never a stale lock (stale-lock) or an unmeasured one (manual). A return to the tab after DOCS_STALE_MS re-lists by GET only; sign-in re-fetches auth slots; unmount clears every timer and aborts every read. DOCS_RELIST_WORDS sits in docsText.ts, the PWA file single-definition's archive-door census already excuses (refinement (l); M4.A1-A3, M4.F5, rows 60 and 61)." \
  -m "Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
```

### Task 6: The docs link policy: detachUrls (a copy, URLs moved to a WeakMap, images numbered, the page highlight budget), DocLink and DocLinkContext, docsLocation, fragments, and PreHighlightContext in the shared pre

```ts
// pwa/src/docs/docsLinks.ts
export interface DetachedUrls {
  readonly attrs: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;   // every URL property moved off the element; {} when none
  readonly imageIndex: number | null;                 // null = not an img
  readonly highlight: boolean | null;                 // null = not a pre
}
export interface Detached {
  readonly tree: HastRoot;                            // the copy
  readonly urls: WeakMap<HastElement, DetachedUrls>;  // keyed by the COPY's elements (the `node` a component gets)
  readonly images: number;
}
export function detachUrls(tree: HastRoot): Detached;  // pure; returns a copy; never writes its input
export type DocsPageTarget =
  | { kind: 'index' }
  | { kind: 'project' }
  | { kind: 'default-view'; project: string }
  | { kind: 'section'; section: DocSectionSlug }
  | { kind: 'path'; section: DocSectionSlug; path: string; dirSlash: boolean; view?: 'effective' | 'committed' };
export function docsLocation(page: DocsPageLocation, to: DocsPageTarget): DocsPageLocation;  // the ONE builder
export type DocLinkTarget =
  | { kind: 'in-app'; href: string; fragment: string | null }
  | { kind: 'fragment'; fragment: string }
  | { kind: 'external'; href: string }
  | { kind: 'github'; href: string }
  | { kind: 'inert'; title: string };
export function docLinkTarget(ctx: DocLinkContextValue, raw: string): DocLinkTarget;  // pure decision for DocLink
// pwa/src/docs/DocLink.tsx
export interface DocLinkContextValue {
  readonly project: string;
  readonly pageRef: DocsRefSpec | null;
  readonly view: 'effective' | 'committed';
  readonly section: DocSectionSlug;
  readonly path: string;
  readonly tree: DocsTreeOk;
  readonly pageSource: 'committed' | 'draft';
  readonly urls: WeakMap<HastElement, DetachedUrls>;
  readonly onFragment: (fragment: string) => void;
}
export const DocLinkContext: React.Context<DocLinkContextValue | null>;
export function DocLink(p: React.ComponentProps<'a'> & { node?: HastElement }): ReactNode;
// pwa/src/lib/markdown.tsx
export const PreHighlightContext: React.Context<((pre: HastElement) => boolean) | null>;
// pwa/src/docs/docsText.ts
export type DocLinkInertReason =
  | Extract<DocRefResolution, { kind: 'refused' }>['why']
  | Extract<DocRefResolution, { kind: 'self-contained' }>['scheme']
  | Extract<GithubLink, { ok: false }>['why'];
export const DOC_LINK_INERT_SENTENCE: Record<DocLinkInertReason, string>;
export const DOC_LINK_OUTSIDE_PAGE: string;
```

The one meaning of every null, absence and catch-all arm:
- `DetachedUrls.imageIndex: null`: the element is not an `img`. `highlight: null`: it is not a `pre`. An element with no URL property, not an `img` and not a `pre` has NO entry in `urls` (`urls.get` answers `undefined`, which `DocLink` reads as a link with no `href`: raw `''`, refused `empty`).
- `DocLinkTarget` `in-app`'s `fragment: null`: the link names no fragment. `href` never carries one; `DocLink` appends `#fragment` for the DOM only.
- `DocsPageTarget` `path`'s `view` absent: `effective`.
- `DocLinkContextValue.pageRef: null`: the default view (the page names no ref).
- `DocLinkContext`'s `null` (the default): `DocLink` is rendered outside a Docs page and renders every link inert, titled `DOC_LINK_OUTSIDE_PAGE`.
- `PreHighlightContext`'s `null` (the default): no page budget (chat), so the block rule alone decides; with a budget, a `pre` rendered with no `node` is not highlighted (fail closed; neither react-markdown nor `renderHast` omits it).
- `docsLocation` from the index (`page.kind === 'index'`) with a `project`, `section` or `path` target throws: the index names no project (a programming error, never a page).

**Decisions this task makes** (each pinned by a case below; refinements, not deviations: none contradicts the spec's text):

1. **`DocsPageTarget` gains `default-view`.** The architecture's union keeps the page's project, so the index's rows (Task 9) and the linked-worktree redirect (Task 9, refinement (c)) had no way to name another project's default view without a `DocsPageLocation` literal, which refinement (q) forbids in a view. `{kind: 'default-view', project}` answers `{kind: 'project', project, ref: null}` from any page.
2. **`docsLocation` keeps exactly `project` and `ref`.** It builds each arm field by field rather than spreading the page, so a section location never carries a leaf's `path` or `view`; `frame` is always `inline` (W6 owns `full`).
3. **`detachUrls` moves URL keys off EVERY element, whatever its tag** (fail closed: `html-url-attributes`' tag lists say where a browser reads the key as a URL, and nothing depends on them being right). A value becomes text as hast-util-to-jsx-runtime would write it: a string as is, a number in decimal, a list space-joined; a boolean, `null` or `undefined` is deleted and not recorded (it holds no URL).
4. **The budget counts every block's `pre > code` text in document order, highlighted or not**, and once the running sum passes `DOCS_HIGHLIGHT_PAGE_MAX_CHARS`, that block and every later one is `false` (spec 4.10: "marks every block past ... as `highlight:false`"). The sum is in UTF-16 code units, the unit `CodeBlock` measures.
5. **A fragment is matched by comparing ids as strings** (the raw fragment, or it percent-decoded once) over `article.querySelectorAll('[id]')`, so no selector is built from document text. Spec 4.11 names `CSS.escape` for the same purpose; jsdom has no `CSS` global (measured: `typeof window.CSS === 'undefined'` under jsdom 28), and the comparison needs no escaping. An empty fragment names nothing.
6. **A fragment link handles every click the same way** (prevented, scrolled, never a history entry): a new tab would only open this same page. A doc link leaves modifier and middle clicks to the browser, as spec 4.11 says.
7. **`DocLink` passes every non-URL prop the tree gave the `a` through** (`id`, `title`, the footnote's `data-*` and `aria-*`), so a GFM footnote's back-reference finds its `id`; it drops `href`, `ping`, `target`, `rel` and `onClick` and writes its own. An inert span carries only `className` and `title`.
8. **The `github` arm carries no note.** The architecture's `{kind: 'github'; href}` drops `githubBlobUrl`'s `may-differ`; the trailing mark is the text " ↗ GitHub" in `span.doc-link-gh`, a class Task 11 registers beside `.doc-link-inert` (spec 4.14's list names `.doc-link-inert` and not this one).
9. **The inert sentences live in `docsText.ts`** (`DOC_LINK_INERT_SENTENCE`, keyed by every refusal, both self-contained schemes and every `githubBlobUrl` refusal, so a new word is a compile error), and the title is `<sentence>: <raw>`, `raw` being the `href` exactly as `detachUrls` moved it (the parse's percent-encoded form).
10. **Measured while writing this task:** the parse percent-encodes a backslash, so `[g](\\evil.example/x)` arrives as `%5Cevil.example/x` and resolves to a file named `\evil.example` under `specs`: an in-app Docs page (`/docs/demo/specs/%5Cevil.example/x?ref=ws/a`), never a host. The hostile-corpus case pins that answer.

````tsx
// Docs W5 part 1, Task 6: the docs link policy (spec 2026-10-01 4.11; refinements (n), (o), (q)). `detachUrls` returns
// a copy of a parsed tree with every `html-url-attributes` property moved into a WeakMap (it never writes its input),
// numbers the images and records each `pre`'s highlight decision; `DocLink` is the only thing that puts an `href` in
// the DOM, from `docLinkTarget`'s one decision: a doc link in-app at the page's ref with `view` dropped (M4.U3), an
// external link opened on tap only (M4.U4), a fragment scrolled inside the article with no history entry (M4.U7), an
// in-repo file outside the sections through `githubBlobUrl`, and an inert span for everything else. `docsLocation` is
// the one page-location builder. Every page is a placeholder (`demo`, `ws/a`, `example-org/example-repo`).
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { cleanup, fireEvent, render } from '@testing-library/react';
import type { Element as HastElement, ElementContent, Root as HastRoot, RootContent } from 'hast';
import { urlAttributes } from 'html-url-attributes';
import { docsPageUrl, githubBlobUrl, type DocsTreeOk } from '../../shared/docs';
import { SHARED_COMPONENTS } from '../src/lib/markdown';
import { parseMarkdown } from '../src/lib/markdownParse';
import { renderHast } from '../src/lib/renderHast';
import { DocLink, DocLinkContext, type DocLinkContextValue } from '../src/docs/DocLink';
import { detachUrls, docLinkTarget, docsLocation, type Detached } from '../src/docs/docsLinks';
import { DOC_LINK_INERT_SENTENCE, DOC_LINK_OUTSIDE_PAGE, type DocLinkInertReason } from '../src/docs/docsText';
import { pageAt, treeOk } from './docsFixtures';

afterEach(() => {
  cleanup();
  vi.restoreAllMocks();
  history.replaceState(null, '', '/');
});

const treeOf = (src: string): HastRoot => {
  const o = parseMarkdown(src, 'docs');
  if (o.kind !== 'tree') throw new Error(`expected a tree, got ${o.kind}`);
  return o.tree;
};

/** The page every case renders on: `specs/a.md` of `demo`, at the ref `ws/a`, in the committed view. */
function ctxFor(d: Detached, over: Partial<DocLinkContextValue> = {}): DocLinkContextValue {
  return {
    project: 'demo', pageRef: { kind: 'bare', name: 'ws/a' }, view: 'committed', section: 'specs', path: 'a.md',
    tree: treeOk(), pageSource: 'committed', urls: d.urls, onFragment: vi.fn(), ...over,
  };
}

/** `src` parsed in the docs profile, detached, and rendered with `DocLink` inside an `<article>`, as a Docs page. */
function renderDoc(src: string, over: Partial<DocLinkContextValue> = {}) {
  const detached = detachUrls(treeOf(src));
  const ctx = ctxFor(detached, over);
  const r = render(
    <article>
      <DocLinkContext value={ctx}>
        {renderHast(detached.tree, { components: { ...SHARED_COMPONENTS, a: DocLink } })}
      </DocLinkContext>
    </article>,
  );
  return { ...r, ctx, detached };
}

const firstLink = (c: HTMLElement): HTMLAnchorElement => {
  const a = c.querySelector('a');
  if (a === null) throw new Error('no link rendered');
  return a;
};

/** Every element of `root`, in document pre-order (an element before its children, siblings first to last). */
function elements(root: HastRoot): HastElement[] {
  const out: HastElement[] = [];
  const stack: RootContent[] = [...root.children].reverse();
  while (stack.length > 0) {
    const n = stack.pop()!;
    if (n.type !== 'element') continue;
    out.push(n);
    for (let i = n.children.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) stack.push(n.children[i]!);
  }
  return out;
}

function deepFreeze<T>(v: T): T {
  const stack: unknown[] = [v];
  while (stack.length > 0) {
    const o = stack.pop();
    if (o !== null && typeof o === 'object' && !Object.isFrozen(o)) {
      Object.freeze(o);
      for (const k of Object.keys(o)) stack.push((o as Record<string, unknown>)[k]);
    }
  }
  return v;
}

const el = (tagName: string, properties: HastElement['properties'], children: ElementContent[] = []): HastElement =>
  ({ type: 'element', tagName, properties, children });

describe('detachUrls: a copy with every URL moved into the map (spec 4.11; refinement (n))', () => {
  it('returns a copy and never writes its input: a deep-frozen tree detaches, and its JSON is unchanged', () => {
    const tree = deepFreeze(treeOf('[x](../plans/p.md) ![i](i.png)\n\n```ts\nconst a = 1;\n```\n'));
    const before = JSON.stringify(tree);
    const d = detachUrls(tree);
    expect(JSON.stringify(tree)).toBe(before);
    expect(d.tree).not.toBe(tree);
    const [p] = tree.children;
    const [copy] = d.tree.children;
    expect(copy).not.toBe(p);
    expect(copy?.type === 'element' && p?.type === 'element' && copy.children[0]).not.toBe(
      p?.type === 'element' && p.children[0]);
    // Text nodes are shared: the copy is of the root and every element only.
    const text = (r: HastRoot) => elements(r).find((e) => e.tagName === 'code')?.children[0];
    expect(text(d.tree)).toBe(text(tree));
  });

  it('moves every html-url-attributes key out of the copy, on any tag, into the map, and keeps every other property', () => {
    const keys = Object.keys(urlAttributes);
    const tagOf = (k: string): string => urlAttributes[k]?.[0] ?? 'div';
    const children = keys.map((k) => el(tagOf(k), { [k]: `u-${k}`, id: `i-${k}`, className: ['c'] }));
    children.push(el('div', { href: 'off-tag', title: 't' }));
    // Values hast's types do not expect on these keys, as a hand-built or future tree could carry them.
    children.push(el('a', { ping: ['p1', 'p2'], href: 7, cite: null, src: false } as unknown as HastElement['properties']));
    const tree: HastRoot = { type: 'root', children };
    const d = detachUrls(tree);
    const copies = d.tree.children as HastElement[];
    keys.forEach((k, i) => {
      const c = copies[i]!;
      expect(Object.hasOwn(c.properties, k)).toBe(false);
      expect(c.properties).toEqual({ id: `i-${k}`, className: ['c'] });
      expect(d.urls.get(c)?.attrs).toEqual({ [k]: `u-${k}` });
    });
    const offTag = copies[keys.length]!;
    expect(offTag.properties).toEqual({ title: 't' });
    expect(d.urls.get(offTag)?.attrs).toEqual({ href: 'off-tag' });
    const odd = copies[keys.length + 1]!;
    expect(odd.properties).toEqual({});
    expect(d.urls.get(odd)?.attrs).toEqual({ ping: 'p1 p2', href: '7' });
  });

  it('numbers img elements 0..n-1 in document order, counts them, and records nothing for an element with nothing', () => {
    const d = detachUrls(treeOf('![a](a.png)\n\n- ![b](b.png)\n\n[![c](c.png)](d.md) text'));
    expect(d.images).toBe(3);
    const imgs = elements(d.tree).filter((e) => e.tagName === 'img');
    expect(imgs.map((e) => [e.properties['alt'], d.urls.get(e)?.imageIndex, d.urls.get(e)?.attrs['src']]))
      .toEqual([['a', 0, 'a.png'], ['b', 1, 'b.png'], ['c', 2, 'c.png']]);
    expect(imgs.every((e) => !Object.hasOwn(e.properties, 'src') && d.urls.get(e)?.highlight === null)).toBe(true);
    const a = elements(d.tree).find((e) => e.tagName === 'a')!;
    expect(d.urls.get(a)).toEqual({ attrs: { href: 'd.md' }, imageIndex: null, highlight: null });
    expect(elements(d.tree).filter((e) => e.tagName === 'p' || e.tagName === 'li').some((e) => d.urls.has(e))).toBe(false);
  });

  it('a second detach of the copy finds no URL (part 2 reuses the first copy and its map)', () => {
    const d = detachUrls(treeOf('[x](https://a.example/x)'));
    const again = detachUrls(d.tree);
    const a = elements(again.tree).find((e) => e.tagName === 'a')!;
    expect(again.urls.has(a)).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe('docsLocation: the one page-location builder (refinement (q))', () => {
  const page = pageAt('/docs/demo/specs/a.md?ref=ws/a&view=committed');

  it('keeps the page project and ref and applies the target; view is effective unless the target names it', () => {
    expect(docsLocation(page, { kind: 'index' })).toEqual({ kind: 'index' });
    expect(docsLocation(page, { kind: 'project' })).toEqual({ kind: 'project', project: 'demo', ref: { kind: 'bare', name: 'ws/a' } });
    expect(docsLocation(page, { kind: 'section', section: 'plans' }))
      .toEqual({ kind: 'section', project: 'demo', section: 'plans', ref: { kind: 'bare', name: 'ws/a' } });
    expect(docsLocation(page, { kind: 'path', section: 'plans', path: 'd', dirSlash: true })).toEqual({
      kind: 'path', project: 'demo', section: 'plans', path: 'd', dirSlash: true, ref: { kind: 'bare', name: 'ws/a' },
      view: 'effective', frame: 'inline',
    });
    expect(docsPageUrl(docsLocation(page, { kind: 'path', section: 'specs', path: 'a.md', dirSlash: false, view: 'committed' })))
      .toBe('/docs/demo/specs/a.md?ref=ws/a&view=committed');
  });

  it("default-view opens another project's default view from any page, the index included", () => {
    expect(docsLocation(pageAt('/docs'), { kind: 'default-view', project: 'b' })).toEqual({ kind: 'project', project: 'b', ref: null });
    expect(docsLocation(page, { kind: 'default-view', project: 'b' })).toEqual({ kind: 'project', project: 'b', ref: null });
  });

  it('the index names no project: any target that keeps one is a programming error', () => {
    expect(() => docsLocation(pageAt('/docs'), { kind: 'section', section: 'specs' })).toThrow(/index names no project/);
  });
});

describe('DocLink: doc links in-app (M4.U3; refinement (o))', () => {
  const want = docsPageUrl(docsLocation(pageAt('/docs/demo/specs/a.md?ref=ws/a&view=committed'),
    { kind: 'path', section: 'plans', path: 'p.md', dirSlash: false }));

  it('[x](../plans/p.md) from specs/a.md at ref ws/a links in-app with the ref kept and view dropped', () => {
    expect(want).toBe('/docs/demo/plans/p.md?ref=ws/a');
    const { container } = renderDoc('[x](../plans/p.md)');
    const a = firstLink(container);
    expect(a.getAttribute('href')).toBe(want);
    expect(a.hasAttribute('target')).toBe(false);
  });

  it('a plain click is prevented and pushes the page URL, and never opens a window', () => {
    const push = vi.spyOn(history, 'pushState');
    const open = vi.spyOn(window, 'open').mockReturnValue(null);
    const { container } = renderDoc('[x](../plans/p.md)');
    expect(fireEvent.click(firstLink(container))).toBe(false);
    expect(push).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(push.mock.calls[0]?.[2]).toBe(want);
    expect(location.pathname + location.search).toBe(want);
    expect(open).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it.each([['meta', { metaKey: true }], ['ctrl', { ctrlKey: true }], ['shift', { shiftKey: true }],
    ['alt', { altKey: true }], ['middle', { button: 1 }]] as const)('a %s click is left to the browser', (_name, init) => {
    const push = vi.spyOn(history, 'pushState');
    const { container } = renderDoc('[x](../plans/p.md)');
    let prevented: boolean | null = null;
    // Runs after React's root listener: it reads DocLink's decision, then stops jsdom's own navigation.
    window.addEventListener('click', (e) => { prevented = e.defaultPrevented; e.preventDefault(); }, { once: true });
    fireEvent.click(firstLink(container), init);
    expect(prevented).toBe(false);
    expect(push).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('a cross-doc fragment: the href carries #part-2, a plain click navigates without it and hands it to onFragment', () => {
    const push = vi.spyOn(history, 'pushState');
    const { container, ctx } = renderDoc('[x](../plans/p.md#part-2)');
    const a = firstLink(container);
    expect(a.getAttribute('href')).toBe(`${want}#part-2`);
    fireEvent.click(a);
    expect(push.mock.calls[0]?.[2]).toBe(want);
    expect(ctx.onFragment).toHaveBeenCalledWith('part-2');
    expect(location.hash).toBe('');
  });

  it('a doc link with no fragment hands none over', () => {
    const { container, ctx } = renderDoc('[x](../plans/p.md)');
    fireEvent.click(firstLink(container));
    expect(ctx.onFragment).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });
});

describe('DocLink: external links on tap only (M4.U4)', () => {
  it('an https link has target _blank and rel noopener noreferrer, and opens a window only when tapped', () => {
    const open = vi.spyOn(window, 'open').mockReturnValue(null);
    const push = vi.spyOn(history, 'pushState');
    const { container } = renderDoc('[x](https://a.example/p)');
    const a = firstLink(container);
    expect(a.getAttribute('href')).toBe('https://a.example/p');
    expect(a.getAttribute('target')).toBe('_blank');
    expect(a.getAttribute('rel')?.split(' ').sort()).toEqual(['noopener', 'noreferrer']);
    expect(open).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(fireEvent.click(a)).toBe(false);
    expect(open).toHaveBeenCalledWith('https://a.example/p', '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer');
    expect(push).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  const INERT: readonly (readonly [string, DocLinkInertReason])[] = [
    ['javascript:alert(1)', 'scheme'],
    ['/api/example/x', 'root-relative'],
    ['//evil.example/x', 'protocol-relative'],
    ['data:text/html,x', 'data'],
    ['blob:https://a.example/x', 'blob'],
    ['../../../../x.md', 'above-root'],
    ['', 'empty'],
  ];

  it.each(INERT)('[x](%s) renders span.doc-link-inert with no href, titled with its sentence and the raw target', (raw, why) => {
    const { container } = renderDoc(`[x](${raw})`);
    expect(container.querySelector('a')).toBeNull();
    expect(container.querySelectorAll('[href]')).toHaveLength(0);
    const span = container.querySelector('span.doc-link-inert');
    expect(span?.textContent).toBe('x');
    expect(span?.getAttribute('title')).toBe(`${DOC_LINK_INERT_SENTENCE[why]}: ${raw}`);
  });

  it('docLinkTarget answers the same words without rendering', () => {
    const d = detachUrls(treeOf('x'));
    expect(docLinkTarget(ctxFor(d), 'javascript:alert(1)'))
      .toEqual({ kind: 'inert', title: `${DOC_LINK_INERT_SENTENCE.scheme}: javascript:alert(1)` });
    expect(docLinkTarget(ctxFor(d), '#a')).toEqual({ kind: 'fragment', fragment: 'a' });
    expect(docLinkTarget(ctxFor(d), 'mailto:you@example.com')).toEqual({ kind: 'external', href: 'mailto:you@example.com' });
  });
});

describe('DocLink: an in-repo file outside the sections links to GitHub (spec 4.11 repo arm, 3.11)', () => {
  it('[r](../../../README.md) is a GitHub link built by githubBlobUrl, with the trailing mark, opened on tap', () => {
    const open = vi.spyOn(window, 'open').mockReturnValue(null);
    const t = treeOk();
    const link = githubBlobUrl(t.github, t.ref, { kind: 'repo', repoPath: 'README.md' });
    expect(link).toEqual({ ok: true, url: 'https://github.com/example-org/example-repo/blob/main/README.md', note: null });
    const { container } = renderDoc('[r](../../../README.md)');
    const a = firstLink(container);
    expect(a.getAttribute('href')).toBe(link.ok ? link.url : null);
    expect(a.getAttribute('target')).toBe('_blank');
    expect(a.getAttribute('rel')?.split(' ').sort()).toEqual(['noopener', 'noreferrer']);
    expect(a.textContent).toBe('r ↗ GitHub');
    fireEvent.click(a);
    expect(open).toHaveBeenCalledWith(link.ok ? link.url : null, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer');
  });

  it('with no GitHub origin it is inert and says why', () => {
    const tree: DocsTreeOk = { ...treeOk(), github: { state: 'none' } };
    const { container } = renderDoc('[r](../../../README.md)', { tree });
    expect(container.querySelectorAll('[href]')).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(container.querySelector('span.doc-link-inert')?.getAttribute('title'))
      .toBe(`${DOC_LINK_INERT_SENTENCE['no-github-origin']}: ../../../README.md`);
  });
});

describe('DocLink: fragments scroll inside the article (M4.U7)', () => {
  const FOOTNOTE = 'See [1](#user-content-fn-1).\n\nA claim.[^1]\n\n[^1]: The note.\n';

  it('[1](#user-content-fn-1) scrolls the matching element inside the article and makes no history entry', () => {
    const scroll = vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'scrollIntoView');
    const push = vi.spyOn(history, 'pushState');
    const before = history.length;
    const { container } = renderDoc(FOOTNOTE);
    const a = firstLink(container);
    expect(a.getAttribute('href')).toBe('#user-content-fn-1');
    expect(fireEvent.click(a)).toBe(false);
    expect(scroll).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(scroll.mock.contexts[0]).toBe(container.querySelector('li#user-content-fn-1'));
    expect(history.length).toBe(before);
    expect(push).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(location.hash).toBe('');
  });

  it('a modifier click on an anchor is handled the same way: scrolled in the article, no history entry', () => {
    const scroll = vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'scrollIntoView');
    const before = history.length;
    const { container } = renderDoc(FOOTNOTE);
    expect(fireEvent.click(firstLink(container), { metaKey: true })).toBe(false);
    expect(scroll.mock.contexts[0]).toBe(container.querySelector('li#user-content-fn-1'));
    expect(history.length).toBe(before);
  });

  it('the footnote reference keeps its id, so the back-reference finds it', () => {
    const scroll = vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'scrollIntoView');
    const { container } = renderDoc(FOOTNOTE);
    const back = container.querySelector('a[href="#user-content-fnref-1"]');
    expect(back).not.toBeNull();
    fireEvent.click(back!);
    expect(scroll.mock.contexts[0]).toBe(container.querySelector('a#user-content-fnref-1'));
  });

  it('an element with that id outside the article is never scrolled', () => {
    const scroll = vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'scrollIntoView');
    const outside = document.createElement('div');
    outside.id = 'elsewhere';
    document.body.append(outside);
    try {
      const { container } = renderDoc('[x](#elsewhere)');
      expect(fireEvent.click(firstLink(container))).toBe(false);
      expect(scroll).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    } finally {
      outside.remove();
    }
  });
});

describe('no URL reaches the DOM except through DocLink (spec 4.11)', () => {
  const HOSTILE = [
    '[a](javascript:alert(1)) [b](/api/example/x) [c](//evil.example/x) [d](data:text/html,x)',
    '[e](blob:https://a.example/x) [f](../../../../x.md) [g](\\\\evil.example/x) [h](%01javascript:x)',
    'www.a.example <https://a.example/auto> [i](../plans/p.md) [j](#k) [r](../../../README.md)',
    '![m](/api/example/x.png) ![n](https://evil.example/x.png) ![o](../../README.png)',
  ].join('\n\n');

  it('control: without detachUrls the same tree draws an img whose src is an /api/ path', () => {
    const { container } = render(renderHast(treeOf(HOSTILE), { components: SHARED_COMPONENTS }));
    expect(container.querySelector('img[src="/api/example/x.png"]')).not.toBeNull();
  });

  it('detached and rendered with DocLink: no src anywhere, and every href is an a DocLink built', () => {
    const { container } = renderDoc(HOSTILE);
    expect(container.querySelectorAll('[src],[srcset],[action],[formaction],[poster],[cite],[ping],[data]')).toHaveLength(0);
    const hrefs = [...container.querySelectorAll('[href]')].map((e) => [e.tagName, e.getAttribute('href')]);
    // The backslash form arrives percent-encoded (`%5C`), so it names a file under specs: an in-app page, never a host.
    expect(hrefs).toEqual([
      ['A', '/docs/demo/specs/%5Cevil.example/x?ref=ws/a'],
      ['A', 'http://www.a.example/'],
      ['A', 'https://a.example/auto'],
      ['A', '/docs/demo/plans/p.md?ref=ws/a'],
      ['A', '#k'],
      ['A', 'https://github.com/example-org/example-repo/blob/main/README.md'],
    ]);
    expect(container.querySelectorAll('span.doc-link-inert')).toHaveLength(7);
  });
});

describe('DocLink outside a Docs page', () => {
  it('renders inert, with no href, when no DocLinkContext is provided', () => {
    const d = detachUrls(treeOf('[x](https://a.example/x)'));
    const { container } = render(renderHast(d.tree, { components: { ...SHARED_COMPONENTS, a: DocLink } }));
    expect(container.querySelectorAll('[href]')).toHaveLength(0);

````

The hostile corpus spells its backslash form as `\\\\` inside a JavaScript string, which is `\\` in the Markdown, one escaped backslash; inspect it with `grep -n 'evil.example/x) \[h\]' pwa/test/docs-links.test.tsx` if a copy step decoded it. No raw control byte is written: `%01` is percent-encoded text.

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the highlight budget's failing test.** Create `pwa/test/docs-highlight-budget.test.tsx` with exactly:
```tsx
// Docs W5 part 1, Task 6: the page highlight budget (spec 2026-10-01 4.10 "Highlighting"; M4.H2; refinement (h)).
// `detachUrls` sums `pre > code` text in document order and records `highlight: false` for every block from the one
// that takes the sum past `DOCS_HIGHLIGHT_PAGE_MAX_CHARS`; `SHARED_COMPONENTS.pre` reads `PreHighlightContext` with
// the `node` it is given, so a Docs page that provides the decision gives `CodeBlock` `highlight={false}` for those
// blocks, and chat, which provides nothing, is decided by the block rule alone, as before. The trees are built by
// hand, exactly as the parse emits a fenced block, so no case parses half a megabyte.
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { cleanup, render } from '@testing-library/react';
import type { Element as HastElement, Root as HastRoot } from 'hast';
import { PreHighlightContext, SHARED_COMPONENTS } from '../src/lib/markdown';
import { DOCS_HIGHLIGHT_PAGE_MAX_CHARS, MD_HIGHLIGHT_BLOCK_MAX_CHARS } from '../src/lib/markdownLimits';
import { renderHast } from '../src/lib/renderHast';
import { DocLink } from '../src/docs/DocLink';
import { detachUrls } from '../src/docs/docsLinks';

afterEach(cleanup);

/** A fenced `ts` block as the parse emits it: `pre > code.language-ts`, holding `text`. */
const fence = (text: string): HastElement => ({
  type: 'element', tagName: 'pre', properties: {},
  children: [{ type: 'element', tagName: 'code', properties: { className: ['language-ts'] }, children: [{ type: 'text', value: text }] }],
});

/** `chars` characters of TypeScript holding exactly one keyword, then spaces, then the newline the parse keeps: cheap
 *  for highlight.js, so the case measures the decision, not the grammar. */
const body = (chars: number): string => 'const a = 1;' + ' '.repeat(chars - 13) + '\n';

const page = (sizes: readonly number[]): HastRoot => ({ type: 'root', children: sizes.map((n) => fence(body(n))) });

const pres = (root: HastRoot): HastElement[] =>
  root.children.filter((c): c is HastElement => c.type === 'element' && c.tagName === 'pre');

const BLOCK = 60000;

describe('detachUrls records each pre\'s decision in document order (spec 4.10; refinement (n))', () => {
  it('true while the running sum is within the budget, false from the block that passes it, for every later block', () => {
    const d = detachUrls(page([DOCS_HIGHLIGHT_PAGE_MAX_CHARS - 20, 20, 13, 13]));
    expect(pres(d.tree).map((p) => d.urls.get(p)?.highlight)).toEqual([true, true, false, false]);
    expect(pres(d.tree).map((p) => d.urls.get(p)?.imageIndex)).toEqual([null, null, null, null]);
  });

  it('counts only the text under the pre\'s code children', () => {
    const lead: HastElement = { type: 'element', tagName: 'pre', properties: {},
      children: [{ type: 'text', value: 'x'.repeat(DOCS_HIGHLIGHT_PAGE_MAX_CHARS + 1) }] };
    const d = detachUrls({ type: 'root', children: [lead, fence(body(13))] });
    expect(pres(d.tree).map((p) => d.urls.get(p)?.highlight)).toEqual([true, true]);
  });
});

describe('M4.H2: the page budget reaches CodeBlock through PreHighlightContext (refinement (h))', () => {
  it('the fixture: eight 60 000-character blocks fit the page budget, nine do not, and each is within the block cap', () => {
    expect(body(BLOCK)).toHaveLength(BLOCK);
    expect(8 * BLOCK).toBeLessThanOrEqual(DOCS_HIGHLIGHT_PAGE_MAX_CHARS);
    expect(9 * BLOCK).toBeGreaterThan(DOCS_HIGHLIGHT_PAGE_MAX_CHARS);
    expect(BLOCK).toBeLessThanOrEqual(MD_HIGHLIGHT_BLOCK_MAX_CHARS);
  });

  const keywordsPerBlock = (c: HTMLElement): number[] =>
    [...c.querySelectorAll('.code-block')].map((b) => b.querySelectorAll('.hljs-keyword').length);

  it('nine 60 000-character ts blocks: the first eight are highlighted and the ninth is not', () => {
    const d = detachUrls(page(Array.from({ length: 9 }, () => BLOCK)));
    const { container } = render(
      <PreHighlightContext value={(pre) => d.urls.get(pre)?.highlight !== false}>
        {renderHast(d.tree, { components: { ...SHARED_COMPONENTS, a: DocLink } })}
      </PreHighlightContext>,
    );
    expect(keywordsPerBlock(container)).toEqual([1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0]);
    expect(container.querySelectorAll('pre > code')[8]?.textContent).toBe(body(BLOCK).slice(0, -1));
  });

  it('with no provider (chat) all nine are highlighted: the block rule alone decides', () => {
    const d = detachUrls(page(Array.from({ length: 9 }, () => BLOCK)));
    const { container } = render(renderHast(d.tree, { components: SHARED_COMPONENTS }));
    expect(keywordsPerBlock(container)).toEqual([1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1]);
  });

  it('pre passes the decision the node it renders: the provider is asked about that element and no other', () => {
    const d = detachUrls(page([13, 13, 13]));
    const second = pres(d.tree)[1];
    const asked: HastElement[] = [];
    const { container } = render(
      <PreHighlightContext value={(pre) => { asked.push(pre); return pre !== second; }}>
        {renderHast(d.tree, { components: SHARED_COMPONENTS })}
      </PreHighlightContext>,
    );
    expect(keywordsPerBlock(container)).toEqual([1, 0, 1]);
    expect(new Set(asked)).toEqual(new Set(pres(d.tree)));
  });
});
```

```ts
export const DOCS_RELIST_WORDS: ReadonlySet<DocsFailure> =
  new Set<DocsFailure>(['unknown-commit', 'draft-changed', 'worktree-moved', 'worktree-gone']);

/** Why a Markdown link on a Docs page is inert (spec 4.11, the `DocLink` arm "everything else"): a `resolveDocRef`
 *  refusal, a self-contained scheme (`data`, `blob`), or the reason `githubBlobUrl` gives no link for an in-repo
 *  file outside the four sections. */
export type DocLinkInertReason =
  | Extract<DocRefResolution, { kind: 'refused' }>['why']
  | Extract<DocRefResolution, { kind: 'self-contained' }>['scheme']
  | Extract<GithubLink, { ok: false }>['why'];

/** The first half of an inert link's title, `<sentence>: <raw>` (spec 4.11). */
export const DOC_LINK_INERT_SENTENCE: Record<DocLinkInertReason, string> = {
  'empty': 'This link has no target',
  'malformed': 'This link holds a space, a control character or a backslash',
  'scheme': 'This link uses a scheme Docs does not open',
  'protocol-relative': 'This link names another host without a scheme',
  'root-relative': 'This link points at a server path, not at a document',
  'above-root': 'This link climbs above the repository',
  'bad-path': 'This link names a path Docs cannot address',
  'data': 'This link carries its own content, which Docs does not open',
  'blob': 'This link points at an object made inside a browser, which Docs does not open',
  'no-github-origin': 'This file is outside the Docs sections, and the repository has no GitHub origin',
  'not-on-origin': 'This file is outside the Docs sections, and this branch is not on GitHub',
  'uncommitted': 'This file is outside the Docs sections, and it is not committed',
  'bad-slug': "This file is outside the Docs sections, and the repository's GitHub name cannot be linked",
  'bad-target': 'This file is outside the Docs sections, and its branch or path cannot be linked',
};

/** The whole title of a link `DocLink` renders with no Docs page around it (no `DocLinkContext`). */
export const DOC_LINK_OUTSIDE_PAGE = 'Links open only inside a Docs page';
```

The keys are quoted on code lines; none is a word any census holds to another file (`single-definition`'s archive-door census holds only the fourth re-list word, already here).

```ts
// The Docs link policy (spec 2026-10-01 4.10 "Highlighting" and 4.11; W5 part 1 Task 6). `detachUrls` takes every
// URL out of a parsed tree before it renders, so no URL-bearing attribute reaches the DOM except through `DocLink` (and,
// from Task 7, `DocImage`), and records the page highlight budget's decision for each `pre`; `docLinkTarget` is the one
// decision `DocLink` renders; `docsLocation` is the one builder of a page location a Docs view links to (refinement
// (q)). Pure: no React, no DOM, no module state, and no input is ever written.
import type { Element as HastElement, Root as HastRoot, RootContent } from 'hast';
import { urlAttributes } from 'html-url-attributes';
import {
  docsPageUrl, githubBlobUrl, resolveDocRef, type DocSectionSlug, type DocsPageLocation,
} from '../../../shared/docs';
import { DOCS_HIGHLIGHT_PAGE_MAX_CHARS } from '../lib/markdownLimits';
import { DOC_LINK_INERT_SENTENCE, type DocLinkInertReason } from './docsText';
import type { DocLinkContextValue } from './DocLink';

/** What `detachUrls` recorded for one element of the copy. `attrs` holds every URL property moved off it (empty when it
 *  carried none), keyed by its hast property name, its value as text. `imageIndex: null` means the element is not an
 *  `img`; `highlight: null` means it is not a `pre`. */
export interface DetachedUrls {
  readonly attrs: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
  readonly imageIndex: number | null;
  readonly highlight: boolean | null;
}

/** A detached copy: the tree to render, the map its elements' URLs and decisions live in (keyed by the COPY's
 *  elements, which are the `node` a component receives), and how many `img` elements it numbered. */
export interface Detached {
  readonly tree: HastRoot;
  readonly urls: WeakMap<HastElement, DetachedUrls>;
  readonly images: number;
}

/** Every property name `html-url-attributes` lists. Moved off EVERY element whatever its tag: the package's tag lists
 *  say where a browser reads the key as a URL, and a key on another tag is moved too, so nothing depends on that
 *  list being right (fail closed). */
const URL_KEYS: readonly string[] = Object.keys(urlAttributes);

/** A hast property value as URL text: a string as is, a number in decimal, a list space-joined (as hast-util-to-jsx-
 *  runtime writes a space-separated attribute); `null` for a boolean, `null` or `undefined`, which hold no URL. */
function urlText(value: unknown): string | null {
  if (typeof value === 'string') return value;
  if (typeof value === 'number') return String(value);
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map((v) => String(v)).join(' ');
  return null;
}

/** The characters of text under `pre`'s `code` children (spec 4.10: `pre > code`), in UTF-16 code units as `CodeBlock`
 *  measures a block. Iterative. */
function preCodeChars(pre: HastElement): number {
  let chars = 0;
  const stack: RootContent[] = pre.children.filter((c) => c.type === 'element' && c.tagName === 'code');
  while (stack.length > 0) {
    const node = stack.pop()!;
    if (node.type === 'text') chars += node.value.length;
    else if (node.type === 'element') for (const c of node.children) stack.push(c);
  }
  return chars;
}

/** A copy of `tree` with every URL moved out (spec 4.11; refinement (n)). Iteratively, in document pre-order: the root
 *  and every element are copied (text, comment and doctype nodes are shared, untouched); every `URL_KEYS` property of
 *  an element is deleted from its copy and recorded in `urls` under the copy; `img` elements are numbered 0..n-1;
 *  and each `pre` records the page highlight budget's decision: the `pre > code` text of every block so far, this one
 *  included, is summed, and the block is `highlight: true` while the sum is at most `DOCS_HIGHLIGHT_PAGE_MAX_CHARS`,
 *  `false` from the block that passes it on, for every later block too. An element with nothing to record has no
 *  entry. Never writes `tree`, so a kept outcome can be detached again, and part 2's Export reuses the copy and its
 *  map (a second detach of the copy finds no URL). */
export function detachUrls(tree: HastRoot): Detached {
  const urls = new WeakMap<HastElement, DetachedUrls>();
  const root: HastRoot = { ...tree, children: [] };
  // Children are pushed last to first, so they pop first to last; each entry names the array its copy joins.
  const stack: { node: RootContent; to: RootContent[] }[] = [];
  const schedule = (from: readonly RootContent[], to: RootContent[]): void => {
    for (let i = from.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) stack.push({ node: from[i]!, to });
  };
  let images = 0;
  let codeChars = 0;
  schedule(tree.children, root.children);
  while (stack.length > 0) {
    const { node, to } = stack.pop()!;
    if (node.type !== 'element') {
      to.push(node);
      continue;
    }
    const properties = { ...node.properties };
    const attrs: Record<string, string> = {};
    for (const key of URL_KEYS) {
      if (!Object.hasOwn(properties, key)) continue;
      const text = urlText(properties[key]);
      delete properties[key];
      if (text !== null) attrs[key] = text;
    }
    const copy: HastElement = { ...node, properties, children: [] };
    let imageIndex: number | null = null;
    if (node.tagName === 'img') {
      imageIndex = images;
      images += 1;
    }
    let highlight: boolean | null = null;
    if (node.tagName === 'pre') {
      codeChars += preCodeChars(node);
      highlight = codeChars <= DOCS_HIGHLIGHT_PAGE_MAX_CHARS;
    }
    if (Object.keys(attrs).length > 0 || imageIndex !== null || highlight !== null) {
      urls.set(copy, { attrs, imageIndex, highlight });
    }
    to.push(copy);
    schedule(node.children, copy.children);
  }
  return { tree: root, urls, images };
}

/** Where a page links (refinement (q)). `index`: the Docs index. `project`, `section` and `path`: a page of the same
 *  project at the same ref. `default-view`: another (or the same) project's default view, `ref: null`, from any page,
 *  the index included. A `path` target's `view` absent means `effective`. */
export type DocsPageTarget =
  | { kind: 'index' }
  | { kind: 'project' }
  | { kind: 'default-view'; project: string }
  | { kind: 'section'; section: DocSectionSlug }
  | { kind: 'path'; section: DocSectionSlug; path: string; dirSlash: boolean; view?: 'effective' | 'committed' };

/** THE one builder of a page location a Docs view links to (refinement (q)): it keeps `page`'s project and ref and
 *  applies `to`; `frame` is always `inline` (W6 owns `full`). Every page URL a view writes is
 *  `docsPageUrl(docsLocation(page, to))`; no view builds a `DocsPageLocation` literal. The index names no project, so
 *  a `project`, `section` or `path` target from it is a programming error and throws. */
export function docsLocation(page: DocsPageLocation, to: DocsPageTarget): DocsPageLocation {
  if (to.kind === 'index') return { kind: 'index' };
  if (to.kind === 'default-view') return { kind: 'project', project: to.project, ref: null };
  if (page.kind === 'index') throw new Error(`docsLocation: the index names no project for a ${to.kind} target`);
  const { project, ref } = page;
  switch (to.kind) {
    case 'project':
      return { kind: 'project', project, ref };
    case 'section':
      return { kind: 'section', project, section: to.section, ref };
    case 'path':
      return {
        kind: 'path', project, section: to.section, path: to.path, dirSlash: to.dirSlash, ref,
        view: to.view ?? 'effective', frame: 'inline',
      };
  }
}

/** What `DocLink` renders for one link (spec 4.11). `in-app`: a Docs page of the same project at the page's ref
 *  (`href` is that page's URL, never with a fragment; `fragment: null` means the link names none). `fragment`: an
 *  anchor in this page. `external`: an http, https or mailto URL, opened on tap only. `github`: an in-repo file outside
 *  the four sections, on GitHub through `githubBlobUrl`. `inert`: everything else, with the span's whole title. */
export type DocLinkTarget =
  | { kind: 'in-app'; href: string; fragment: string | null }
  | { kind: 'fragment'; fragment: string }
  | { kind: 'external'; href: string }
  | { kind: 'github'; href: string }
  | { kind: 'inert'; title: string };

/** The one decision for a Markdown link on a Docs page: `raw`, the link's `href` as `detachUrls` moved it (`''` for a
 *  link with none), resolved from the page's own section and path by L0 `resolveDocRef`. A doc link keeps the page's
 *  project and ref and drops `view` (`docsLocation`'s `path` target with no `view`); an inert link's title is
 *  `<sentence>: <raw>`. */
export function docLinkTarget(ctx: DocLinkContextValue, raw: string): DocLinkTarget {
  const inert = (why: DocLinkInertReason): DocLinkTarget => ({ kind: 'inert', title: `${DOC_LINK_INERT_SENTENCE[why]}: ${raw}` });
  const r = resolveDocRef({ section: ctx.section, path: ctx.path }, raw);
  switch (r.kind) {
    case 'doc': {
      const here: DocsPageLocation = { kind: 'project', project: ctx.project, ref: ctx.pageRef };
      const href = docsPageUrl(docsLocation(here, { kind: 'path', section: r.section, path: r.path, dirSlash: false }));
      return { kind: 'in-app', href, fragment: r.fragment };
    }
    case 'fragment':
      return { kind: 'fragment', fragment: r.fragment };
    case 'external':
      return { kind: 'external', href: r.url };
    case 'repo': {
      const link = githubBlobUrl(ctx.tree.github, ctx.tree.ref, { kind: 'repo', repoPath: r.repoPath });
      return link.ok ? { kind: 'github', href: link.url } : inert(link.why);
    }
    case 'self-contained':
      return inert(r.scheme);
    case 'refused':
      return inert(r.why);
  }
}
```

Then create `pwa/src/docs/DocLink.tsx` with exactly:

```tsx
// The Markdown `a` of a Docs page (spec 2026-10-01 4.11; W5 part 1 Task 6) and the context it reads. `DocLink` is,
// with Task 7's `DocImage`, the only way a URL reaches the DOM from a document: `detachUrls` took every URL out of the
// tree, and `DocLink` reads the link's own from the map through its `node`, asks `docLinkTarget` what it is, and
// renders that: an in-app link, an anchor that scrolls inside the article, an external or GitHub link opened on tap,
// or an inert span with no `href`.
import { createContext, useContext, type ComponentProps, type MouseEvent, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import type { Element as HastElement } from 'hast';
import type { DocSectionSlug, DocsRefSpec, DocsTreeOk } from '../../../shared/docs';
import { openExternal } from '../lib/markdown';
import { navigate } from '../lib/router';
import { DOC_LINK_OUTSIDE_PAGE } from './docsText';
import { docLinkTarget, type DetachedUrls } from './docsLinks';

/** The page a link is resolved from (spec 4.11's `{project, pageRef, view, section, path, tree, pageSource}`; refinement
 *  (p)), plus the detached tree's map and the fragment hand-off. `pageRef: null` is the default view (the page names
 *  no ref). `pageSource` is the source of the body on screen. `onFragment` receives a cross-doc link's fragment when
 *  its plain click navigates in-app, so the visit scrolls to it once the new body renders (refinement (o)). */
export interface DocLinkContextValue {
  readonly project: string;
  readonly pageRef: DocsRefSpec | null;
  readonly view: 'effective' | 'committed';
  readonly section: DocSectionSlug;
  readonly path: string;
  readonly tree: DocsTreeOk;
  readonly pageSource: 'committed' | 'draft';
  readonly urls: WeakMap<HastElement, DetachedUrls>;
  readonly onFragment: (fragment: string) => void;
}

/** The Docs page around a document body. `null`, the default, has ONE meaning: `DocLink` is rendered outside a Docs
 *  page, and renders every link inert. */
export const DocLinkContext = createContext<DocLinkContextValue | null>(null);

/** A primary-button click with no modifier: the one click `DocLink` handles in-app. A modifier or middle click is the
 *  browser's (a new tab onto `/docs/...`). */
function isPlainClick(e: MouseEvent): boolean {
  return e.button === 0 && !e.metaKey && !e.ctrlKey && !e.shiftKey && !e.altKey;
}

/** The element inside `article` whose id is `fragment`, or `fragment` percent-decoded once. The ids are compared as
 *  strings, so no selector is ever built from document text (spec 4.11 names `CSS.escape`; this needs no escaping, and
 *  jsdom has no `CSS`). An empty fragment names nothing. */
function fragmentTarget(article: Element, fragment: string): Element | null {
  if (fragment === '') return null;
  let decoded: string | null;
  try {
    decoded = decodeURIComponent(fragment);
  } catch {
    decoded = null;
  }
  for (const el of article.querySelectorAll('[id]')) {
    if (el.id === fragment || el.id === decoded) return el;
  }
  return null;
}

/** A fragment link's click, whatever the button or modifier: prevented, so there is never a history entry (a new tab
 *  would open this same page), and the element the fragment names inside this link's `<article>` is scrolled into
 *  view; nothing outside the article is. */
function scrollToFragment(e: MouseEvent<HTMLAnchorElement>, fragment: string): void {
  e.preventDefault(); // no history entry, whatever the click
  const article = e.currentTarget.closest('article');
  if (article !== null) fragmentTarget(article, fragment)?.scrollIntoView();
}

/** The Markdown `a` of a Docs page (spec 4.11). Its URL comes only from the detached map, through `node`; every other
 *  prop the tree gave it (an `id`, a `title`, a footnote's `data-*` and `aria-*`) is passed on, and no URL prop is.
 *  - `in-app`: `href` is the page URL plus `#fragment` when the link names one (a new tab keeps it); a plain left
 *    click is prevented, hands the fragment to `onFragment`, and navigates to the URL without it.
 *  - `fragment`: `scrollToFragment`, on any click.
 *  - `external` and `github`: `target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"`, opened with `openExternal` on tap only;
 *    a GitHub link carries the trailing "↗ GitHub" mark.
 *  - `inert`, and any link outside a Docs page: `<span className="doc-link-inert" title>` with no `href`. */
export function DocLink(p: ComponentProps<'a'> & { node?: HastElement }): ReactNode {
  const { node, children, href: _href, ping: _ping, target: _target, rel: _rel, onClick: _onClick, ...rest } = p;
  const ctx = useContext(DocLinkContext);
  if (ctx === null) return <span className="doc-link-inert" title={DOC_LINK_OUTSIDE_PAGE}>{children}</span>;
  const raw = (node === undefined ? undefined : ctx.urls.get(node)?.attrs['href']) ?? '';
  const t = docLinkTarget(ctx, raw);
  switch (t.kind) {
    case 'in-app':
      return (
        <a {...rest} href={t.fragment === null ? t.href : `${t.href}#${t.fragment}`} onClick={(e) => {
          if (!isPlainClick(e)) return;
          e.preventDefault();
          if (t.fragment !== null) ctx.onFragment(t.fragment);
          navigate(t.href);
        }}>{children}</a>
      );
    case 'fragment':
      return <a {...rest} href={`#${t.fragment}`} onClick={(e) => scrollToFragment(e, t.fragment)}>{children}</a>;
    case 'external':
    case 'github':
      return (
        <a {...rest} href={t.href} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" onClick={(e) => openExternal(e, t.href)}>
          {children}
          {t.kind === 'github' && <>{' '}<span className="doc-link-gh">↗ GitHub</span></>}
        </a>
      );
    case 'inert':
      return <span className="doc-link-inert" title={t.title}>{children}</span>;
  }
}
```

`docsLinks.ts` imports `DocLinkContextValue` from `DocLink.tsx` as a TYPE only (erased under `verbatimModuleSyntax`), while `DocLink.tsx` imports `docLinkTarget` as a value: no runtime cycle. The unused names in `DocLink`'s destructuring (`_href`, `_ping`, `_target`, `_rel`, `_onClick`) sit beside a rest element, which `noUnusedLocals` does not report (measured: `tsc` is clean).

```tsx
function SharedPre({ children, node }: { children?: ReactNode; node?: HastElement }): ReactNode {
  const budget = useContext(PreHighlightContext);
  const refused = budget !== null && (node === undefined || !budget(node));
  return <CodeBlock highlight={refused ? false : undefined}>{children}</CodeBlock>;
}
```

```bash
  -m "SHARED_COMPONENTS.pre reads PreHighlightContext with its node, so a Docs page's budget gives CodeBlock highlight={false} past the budget, while chat provides none and renders byte-identical (golden, M4.P10, message-links unedited; M4.H2). docsLocation is the one page-location builder, with a default-view target for another project's default view (refinements (h), (n), (o), (p), (q))." \
  -m "Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
```

```ts
// pwa/src/docs/docsLinks.ts
export type ImagePin =
  | { ok: true; pin: DocPin; draft: boolean; uncommittedNotShown: boolean }
  | { ok: false; why: 'absent' | 'deleted-in-worktree' | 'draft-withheld' };
export function imagePinFor(
  e: DocsEntry | undefined, tree: DocsTreeOk, page: DocsPageLocation & { kind: 'path' },
): ImagePin;   // THE pin rule: DocImage now, Export in part 2, the W6 mockup planner
// pwa/src/docs/fetchQueue.ts
export const DOCS_PWA_FETCH_CONCURRENCY = 2;
export interface FetchQueue {
  run<T>(job: (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<T>;
  dispose(): void;
}
export function createFetchQueue(concurrency?: number): FetchQueue;   // RangeError unless a positive integer
// pwa/src/docs/objectUrls.ts
export const DOCS_SAVE_REVOKE_MS = 30000;

export function saveBytes(name: string, bytes: Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>): void;
export function showBytes(show: DocsShowOk): Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer> | null;
export function downloadDocFile(project: string, pin: DocPin, basename: string,
  loaders?: Pick<DocsLoaders, 'file' | 'raster'>): Promise<DocsAnswer<void>>;
// pwa/src/docs/DocImage.tsx
export interface DocsAssetContextValue {
  readonly loaders: Pick<DocsLoaders, 'file' | 'raster'>;
  readonly queue: FetchQueue;
  readonly onDraftAsset: (count: number) => void;
}
export const DocsAssetContext: React.Context<DocsAssetContextValue | null>;
export function DocImage(p: React.ComponentProps<'img'> & { node?: HastElement }): ReactNode;
// pwa/src/docs/docsText.ts
export type DocImageRefusal =
  | 'outside-page'
  | Extract<ImagePin, { ok: false }>['why']
  | 'not-image' | 'external' | 'too-large' | 'fragment' | 'repo'
  | Extract<DocRefResolution, { kind: 'self-contained' }>['scheme']
  | Extract<DocRefResolution, { kind: 'refused' }>['why'];
export const DOC_IMAGE_REFUSED_SENTENCE: Record<DocImageRefusal, string>;
export const DOC_IMAGE_TEXT: { readonly refused: 'Image not loaded: {reason}'; readonly load: 'Load image';
  readonly openExternal: 'Open image externally'; readonly openViewer: 'Open in viewer'; readonly draft: 'draft';
  readonly uncommittedNotShown: 'uncommitted change not shown'; readonly loading: 'Loading image…';
  readonly loaderFailed: 'Image not loaded: the request failed ({error}).' };
export const DOCS_SHOW_NO_BYTES: string;   // a client-built malformed-answer's `why`: the answer held no bytes
```
