```tsx
describe('a tree renders through detachUrls and DOC_COMPONENTS (spec 4.10 step 4)', () => {
  const SRC = '# T\n\n[p](../plans/p.md) and ![i](https://evil.example/x.png)\n';

  it('renderHast gets the detached copy, DOC_COMPONENTS and no urlTransform; links go through DocLink', async () => {
    const outcome = parseMarkdown(SRC, 'docs');
    if (outcome.kind !== 'tree') throw new Error('fixture does not parse');
    const { container } = render(<DocMarkdown text={SRC} pinKey="p" parser={answering(outcome)} link={LINK} />);
    await waitFor(() => expect(container.querySelector('article.doc-body.msg-assist')).not.toBeNull());
    expect(renderSpy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    const [tree, opts] = renderSpy.mock.calls[0]!;
    expect(opts).toEqual({ components: DOC_COMPONENTS });
    expect(Object.hasOwn(opts, 'urlTransform')).toBe(false);
    expect(tree).not.toBe(outcome.tree);
    const para = (root: HastRoot): HastElement =>
      root.children.find((c): c is HastElement => c.type === 'element' && c.tagName === 'p')!;
    const linkOf = (root: HastRoot): HastElement =>
      para(root).children.find((c): c is HastElement => c.type === 'element' && c.tagName === 'a')!;
    expect(linkOf(tree).properties).not.toHaveProperty('href');
    expect(linkOf(outcome.tree).properties['href']).toBe('../plans/p.md');
    expect(container.querySelector('article a')?.getAttribute('href')).toBe(docsPageUrl({
      kind: 'path', project: 'demo', section: 'plans', path: 'p.md', dirSlash: false, ref: null, view: 'effective', frame: 'inline',
    }));
    expect(container.querySelector('img')).toBeNull();
    expect(container.querySelector('.doc-img-refused')).not.toBeNull();
  });

  it('the copy is memoised per outcome: a re-render with a new link object renders the same copy', async () => {
    const outcome = parseMarkdown(SRC, 'docs');
    const parser = answering(outcome);
    const { container, rerender } = render(<DocMarkdown text={SRC} pinKey="p" parser={parser} link={LINK} />);
    await waitFor(() => expect(container.querySelector('article')).not.toBeNull());
    rerender(<DocMarkdown text={SRC} pinKey="p" parser={parser} link={{ ...LINK }} />);
    expect(renderSpy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(renderSpy.mock.calls[1]![0]).toBe(renderSpy.mock.calls[0]![0]);
    expect(parser).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  it('the page highlight budget reaches the blocks: of nine 60 000-character ts blocks the ninth is not highlighted', async () => {
    const body = 'const a = 1;' + ' '.repeat(60000 - 13) + '\n';
    const fence = (): HastElement => ({
      type: 'element', tagName: 'pre', properties: {},
      children: [{ type: 'element', tagName: 'code', properties: { className: ['language-ts'] }, children: [{ type: 'text', value: body }] }],
    });
    const tree: HastRoot = { type: 'root', children: Array.from({ length: 9 }, fence) };
    const { container } = render(<DocMarkdown text="nine blocks" pinKey="p" parser={answering({ kind: 'tree', tree, depth: 3 })} link={LINK} />);
    await waitFor(() => expect(container.querySelectorAll('.code-block')).toHaveLength(9), { timeout: 60000 });
    expect([...container.querySelectorAll('.code-block')].map((b) => b.querySelectorAll('.hljs-keyword').length))
      .toEqual([1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0]);
  }, 90000);
});

describe('the note actions (spec 4.10 step 5)', () => {
  it('a timeout under the normal budget offers Format anyway, which parses again at the large budget; a large timeout offers nothing', async () => {
    const parser = vi.fn<MarkdownParser>(async (_src, o) => ({ kind: 'timeout', budgetMs: o.budgetMs }));
    const text = doc(KIB);
    const { container, getByRole, queryByRole } = render(<DocMarkdown text={text} pinKey="p" parser={parser} link={LINK} />);
    await waitFor(() => expect(container.querySelector('.doc-plain-note')?.textContent)
      .toBe(docsPlainNote({ kind: 'timeout', budgetMs: DOCS_PARSE_BUDGET_MS(KIB) })));
    fireEvent.click(getByRole('button', { name: DOC_MARKDOWN_ACTION.formatAnyway }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(parser).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2));
    expect(parser.mock.calls.map((c) => c[1].budgetMs)).toEqual([DOCS_PARSE_BUDGET_MS(KIB), DOCS_PARSE_BUDGET_LARGE_MS]);
    await waitFor(() => expect(container.querySelector('.doc-plain-note')?.textContent)
      .toBe(docsPlainNote({ kind: 'timeout', budgetMs: DOCS_PARSE_BUDGET_LARGE_MS })));
    expect(queryByRole('button', { name: DOC_MARKDOWN_ACTION.formatAnyway })).toBeNull();
  });

  it('worker-failed offers Retry, which parses the same text again and renders what it answers', async () => {
    const parser = vi.fn<MarkdownParser>()
      .mockResolvedValueOnce({ kind: 'worker-failed', error: 'error' })
      .mockImplementation(async (src, o) => parseMarkdown(src, o.profile));
    const { container, getByRole } = render(<DocMarkdown text="# Again" pinKey="p" parser={parser} link={LINK} />);
    await waitFor(() => expect(container.querySelector('.doc-plain-note')?.textContent)
      .toBe(docsPlainNote({ kind: 'worker-failed', error: 'error' })));
    fireEvent.click(getByRole('button', { name: DOC_MARKDOWN_ACTION.retry }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(container.querySelector('article h1')?.textContent).toBe('Again'));
    expect(parser.mock.calls.map((c) => c[0])).toEqual(['# Again', '# Again']);
  });

  it.each([
    { kind: 'refused', why: 'delimiter-run', line: 1, value: 100 },
    { kind: 'too-deep', depth: 100 },
    { kind: 'too-wide', elements: 20001 },
    { kind: 'threw', error: 'RangeError' },
    { kind: 'worker-unavailable' },
    { kind: 'timeout', budgetMs: DOCS_PARSE_BUDGET_LARGE_MS },
  ] as const)('%j offers no action', async (o) => {
    const { container } = render(<DocMarkdown text={doc(5 * KIB)} pinKey="p" parser={answering(o)} link={LINK} />);
    await waitFor(() => expect(container.querySelector('.doc-plain-note')).not.toBeNull());
    expect(container.querySelector('button')).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe('M4.B2: the doc-body boundary, keyed by the pin (spec 4.12)', () => {
  it('a throwing renderer gives DocPlain with the fallback note while the header beside it stays; a new pin resets it', async () => {
    const warn = vi.spyOn(console, 'warn').mockImplementation(() => {});
    vi.spyOn(console, 'error').mockImplementation(() => {});
    hast.throwing = true;
    const parser = realParser();
    const page = (pinKey: string) => (
      <>
        <header className="docs-truth">origin/main · aaaaaaaa</header>
        <DocMarkdown text="# Body" pinKey={pinKey} parser={parser} link={LINK} />
      </>
    );
    const { container, rerender } = render(page('pin-1'));
    await waitFor(() => expect(container.querySelector('.doc-plain-note')?.textContent).toBe(DOC_BODY_FALLBACK_NOTE));
    expect(container.querySelector('pre.doc-plain')?.textContent).toBe('# Body');
    expect(container.querySelector('header.docs-truth')?.textContent).toBe('origin/main · aaaaaaaa');
    expect(container.querySelector('article')).toBeNull();

    hast.throwing = false;

    rerender(page('pin-2'));
    await waitFor(() => expect(container.querySelector('article.doc-body h1')?.textContent).toBe('Body'));
    expect(container.querySelector('.doc-plain')).toBeNull();
    expect(container.querySelector('header.docs-truth')).not.toBeNull();
  });
});

describe('docMarkdownSource: a markdown leaf\'s bytes (spec 4.10 step 6)', () => {
  const b64 = (bytes: readonly number[]): string => btoa(String.fromCharCode(...bytes));

  it('utf8 text is Markdown as sent', () => {
    expect(docMarkdownSource(show({ encoding: 'utf8', text: '# A' }))).toEqual({ kind: 'markdown', text: '# A' });
  });

  it('base64 bytes that are strict UTF-8 are Markdown, decoded', () => {
    const bytes = [...new TextEncoder().encode('# Café "q"')];
    expect(docMarkdownSource(show({ encoding: 'base64', b64: b64(bytes) }))).toEqual({ kind: 'markdown', text: '# Café "q"' });
  });

  it('base64 bytes that are not UTF-8 are decoded non-fatally and shown as plain text: "Not valid UTF-8."', () => {
    const src = docMarkdownSource(show({ encoding: 'base64', b64: b64([0x23, 0x20, 0xff, 0x41, 0xc3]) }));
    expect(src).toEqual({ kind: 'not-utf8', text: '# �A�' });
    if (src.kind !== 'not-utf8') throw new Error('unreachable');
    const { container } = render(<DocPlain text={src.text} note={DOC_NOT_UTF8_NOTE} />);
    expect(container.querySelector('.doc-plain-note')?.textContent).toBe('Not valid UTF-8.');
    expect(container.querySelector('pre.doc-plain')?.textContent).toBe('# �A�');
  });

  it('an answer whose encoding names a missing field, or base64 that does not decode, holds no bytes', () => {
    expect(docMarkdownSource(show({ encoding: 'utf8' }))).toEqual({ kind: 'no-bytes' });
    expect(docMarkdownSource(show({ encoding: 'base64' }))).toEqual({ kind: 'no-bytes' });
    expect(docMarkdownSource(show({ encoding: 'base64', b64: '!!!' }))).toEqual({ kind: 'no-bytes' });
    expect(docMarkdownSource(show({ encoding: 'base64', text: '# A' }))).toEqual({ kind: 'no-bytes' });
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: The component.** Create `pwa/src/docs/DocMarkdown.tsx` with exactly:

```tsx
// A Docs page's Markdown body (spec 2026-10-01 4.10 "DocMarkdown", steps 1-6, and 4.12's doc-body mount; W5 part 1
// Task 8). In order:
//   1. the gate: a document over `DOCS_RENDER_GATE_BYTES` UTF-8 bytes asks first, and nothing is parsed until the
//      reader chooses **Format anyway** (a `DOCS_PARSE_BUDGET_LARGE_MS` job) or **Show as text**;
//   2. the parse, through `useParsedMarkdown` on the page's parser (`docsRunner.parse` from `DocsScreen`), profile
//      `docs`, budget `DOCS_PARSE_BUDGET_MS(bytes)`; the body says "Formatting…" until the outcome for this text lands;
//   3. `worker-unavailable` on a text of at most `CHAT_SYNC_MAX_BYTES` parses here, on the main thread; a longer one
//      is plain text with its own note;
//   4. a tree is detached once per outcome (`detachUrls`: a copy, every URL moved into its map) and rendered with
//      `renderHast(copy, {components: DOC_COMPONENTS})` and no url transform, in `<article className="doc-body
//      msg-assist">`, inside the doc-body `RenderBoundary` keyed by the pin; every other outcome is `DocPlain`;
//   5. each outcome but a tree has one note (`docsPlainNote`); a `timeout` under the normal budget offers **Format
//      anyway**, a `worker-failed` offers **Retry**;
//   6. a `.md` whose bytes arrived as base64 is decoded by `docMarkdownSource`: strict UTF-8 renders as Markdown, and
//      anything else is decoded with a non-fatal `TextDecoder('utf-8')` and shown as plain text, "Not valid UTF-8.".
// The element cap is the parse's (`too-wide`, counted before anything renders): nothing here counts after a render.
// New class names (registered by Task 11): `doc-gate`, `doc-gate-copy`, `doc-gate-btn`, `doc-formatting`,
// `doc-plain`, `doc-plain-note`, `doc-plain-action`.
import { useMemo, useState, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import type { Components } from 'react-markdown';
import type { Element as HastElement, Root as HastRoot } from 'hast';
import type { DocsShowOk } from '../../../shared/docs';
import { RenderBoundary } from '../components/RenderBoundary';
import { PreHighlightContext, SHARED_COMPONENTS } from '../lib/markdown';
import { utf8ByteLength } from '../lib/markdownGuard';
import {
  CHAT_SYNC_MAX_BYTES, DOCS_MAX_RENDER_ELEMENTS, DOCS_PARSE_BUDGET_LARGE_MS, DOCS_PARSE_BUDGET_MS,
  DOCS_RENDER_GATE_BYTES, MD_MAX_CONTAINER_DEPTH, MD_MAX_DELIMITER_RUN, MD_MAX_TREE_DEPTH,
} from '../lib/markdownLimits';
import { parseMarkdown, type ParseOutcome } from '../lib/markdownParse';
import type { MarkdownParser } from '../lib/markdownRunner';
import { renderHast } from '../lib/renderHast';
import { useParsedMarkdown } from '../lib/useParsedMarkdown';
import { DocImage } from './DocImage';
import { DocLink, DocLinkContext, type DocLinkContextValue } from './DocLink';
import { detachUrls } from './docsLinks';
import { showBytes } from './objectUrls';

/** The components a Docs body renders with (spec 4.10): the shared code, pre and table, and the Docs `a` and `img`,
 *  which are the only way a URL from the document reaches the DOM. */
export const DOC_COMPONENTS: Components = { ...SHARED_COMPONENTS, a: DocLink, img: DocImage };

/** The doc-body boundary's note (spec 4.12's table). */
export const DOC_BODY_FALLBACK_NOTE = 'This document could not be displayed; shown as plain text.';
/** The note of a `.md` whose bytes are not UTF-8 (spec 4.10 step 6). */
export const DOC_NOT_UTF8_NOTE = 'Not valid UTF-8.';
/** The body's line while the parse runs (spec 4.10 step 2). */
export const DOC_FORMATTING = 'Formatting…';
/** The two gate buttons and the two note actions (spec 4.10 steps 1 and 5). */
export const DOC_MARKDOWN_ACTION = {
  formatAnyway: 'Format anyway',
  showAsText: 'Show as text',
  retry: 'Retry',
} as const;

/** `n` in decimal, its digits grouped by three with a space, as the spec writes its limits ("limit 20 000"). */
function grouped(n: number): string {
  return String(n).replace(/\B(?=(\d{3})+(?!\d))/g, ' ');
}

/** `bytes` in MiB to one decimal place, with its unit: 614 400 bytes is "0.6 MiB". */
export function mib(bytes: number): string {
  return `${(bytes / 1048576).toFixed(1)} MiB`;
}

/** The gate's sentence (spec 4.10 step 1). */
export function docGateSentence(bytes: number): string {
  return `This document is ${mib(bytes)}. Formatting it may take a while.`;
}

/** The note of a document shown as text because the reader chose **Show as text** at the gate. */
export function docShownAsTextNote(bytes: number): string {
  return `This document is ${mib(bytes)}; shown as plain text, as asked.`;
}

/** The one-line note above a document Docs shows as plain text: why it was not formatted (spec 4.10 step 5). Exhaustive
 *  over every outcome but `tree` (a new kind is a compile error here); the limits are interpolated from
 *  `markdownLimits.ts`, never restated. */
export function docsPlainNote(o: Exclude<ParseOutcome, { kind: 'tree' }>): string {
  switch (o.kind) {
    case 'refused':
      return o.why === 'container-depth'
        ? `Line ${grouped(o.line)} nests ${grouped(o.value)} levels deep (limit ${grouped(MD_MAX_CONTAINER_DEPTH)}); shown as plain text.`
        : `Line ${grouped(o.line)} has a run of ${grouped(o.value)} emphasis marks (limit ${grouped(MD_MAX_DELIMITER_RUN)}); shown as plain text.`;
    case 'too-deep':
      return `This document nests ${grouped(o.depth)} levels deep (limit ${grouped(MD_MAX_TREE_DEPTH)}); shown as plain text.`;
    case 'too-wide':
      return `This document would draw ${grouped(o.elements)} elements (limit ${grouped(DOCS_MAX_RENDER_ELEMENTS)}); shown as plain text.`;
    case 'threw':
      return `This document could not be formatted (${o.error}); shown as plain text.`;
    case 'timeout':
      return `Formatting took longer than ${o.budgetMs / 1000} s; shown as plain text.`;
    case 'worker-unavailable':
      return 'This browser cannot format long documents in the background; shown as plain text.';
    case 'worker-failed':
      return `The formatter stopped (${o.error}); shown as plain text.`;
  }
}

/** A document shown as plain text: the note line, then `action` when given (absent = no action), then the text
 *  verbatim in `<pre className="doc-plain">`. */
export function DocPlain(p: { readonly text: string; readonly note: string; readonly action?: ReactNode }): ReactNode {
  return (
    <>
      <p className="doc-plain-note">{p.note}</p>
      {p.action}
      <pre className="doc-plain">{p.text}</pre>
    </>
  );
}

/** What a markdown leaf's show answer holds (spec 4.10 step 6). `markdown`: text to format, `utf8` as sent or `base64`
 *  bytes that decode as strict UTF-8 (ccd sends valid UTF-8 as base64 when that frames shorter, spec 3's encoding
 *  rule). `not-utf8`: base64 bytes that are not UTF-8, decoded non-fatally (each bad sequence a U+FFFD) for
 *  `DocPlain` with `DOC_NOT_UTF8_NOTE`. `no-bytes`: the field the answer's encoding names is missing, or its base64
 *  does not decode (the caller shows a malformed answer). */
export type DocMarkdownSource =
  | { readonly kind: 'markdown'; readonly text: string }
  | { readonly kind: 'not-utf8'; readonly text: string }
  | { readonly kind: 'no-bytes' };

export function docMarkdownSource(show: DocsShowOk): DocMarkdownSource {
  if (show.encoding === 'utf8') return typeof show.text === 'string' ? { kind: 'markdown', text: show.text } : { kind: 'no-bytes' };
  const bytes = showBytes(show);
  if (bytes === null) return { kind: 'no-bytes' };
  try {
    return { kind: 'markdown', text: new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true }).decode(bytes) };
  } catch {
    return { kind: 'not-utf8', text: new TextDecoder('utf-8').decode(bytes) };
  }
}

/** The props of `DocMarkdown`. `text`: the document, as it is to be formatted. `pinKey`: the pin the text was read
 *  at, as a string (the doc-body boundary's reset key; the caller also keys `DocMarkdown` by it, so a new pin starts
 *  over and its stale job is aborted). `parser`: the page's parser. `link`: the page the body's links and images
 *  resolve from; `DocMarkdown` adds the detached `urls`. */
export interface DocMarkdownProps {
  readonly text: string;
  readonly pinKey: string;
  readonly parser: MarkdownParser;
  readonly link: Omit<DocLinkContextValue, 'urls'>;
}

/** A parsed tree on the page: detached ONCE per tree (the memo is keyed by the tree object), then rendered with
 *  `DOC_COMPONENTS` and no url transform, under the page's link context and highlight budget. Lives inside the
 *  doc-body boundary, so a throw from `renderHast` or from any component it draws is the boundary's. */
function DocTree(p: { readonly tree: HastRoot; readonly link: Omit<DocLinkContextValue, 'urls'> }): ReactNode {
  const detached = useMemo(() => detachUrls(p.tree), [p.tree]);
  const ctx = useMemo<DocLinkContextValue>(() => ({ ...p.link, urls: detached.urls }), [p.link, detached]);
  const budget = useMemo(() => (pre: HastElement): boolean => detached.urls.get(pre)?.highlight !== false, [detached]);
  return (
    <DocLinkContext value={ctx}>
      <PreHighlightContext value={budget}>
        <article className="doc-body msg-assist">{renderHast(detached.tree, { components: DOC_COMPONENTS })}</article>
      </PreHighlightContext>
    </DocLinkContext>
  );
}

/** Steps 2-5 for one budget and attempt. `large`: the reader chose **Format anyway**. */
function DocParse(p: DocMarkdownProps & {
  readonly bytes: number; readonly budgetMs: number; readonly attempt: number;
  readonly onFormatAnyway: () => void; readonly onRetry: () => void;
}): ReactNode {
  const { outcome, pending } = useParsedMarkdown(p.text, p.parser, { profile: 'docs', budgetMs: p.budgetMs, attempt: p.attempt });
  // Step 3: no worker here, and the text is small enough to parse on the main thread. Memoised per outcome.
  const inThread = useMemo(
    () => (outcome?.kind === 'worker-unavailable' && p.bytes <= CHAT_SYNC_MAX_BYTES ? parseMarkdown(p.text, 'docs') : null),
    [outcome, p.text, p.bytes],
  );
  if (pending || outcome === null) return <p className="doc-formatting">{DOC_FORMATTING}</p>;
  const shown = inThread ?? outcome;
  if (shown.kind === 'tree') {
    return (
      <RenderBoundary where="doc body" resetKey={p.pinKey} fallback={() => <DocPlain text={p.text} note={DOC_BODY_FALLBACK_NOTE} />}>
        <DocTree tree={shown.tree} link={p.link} />
      </RenderBoundary>
    );
  }
  let action: ReactNode = null;
  if (shown.kind === 'timeout' && shown.budgetMs < DOCS_PARSE_BUDGET_LARGE_MS) {
    action = <button type="button" className="doc-plain-action" onClick={p.onFormatAnyway}>{DOC_MARKDOWN_ACTION.formatAnyway}</button>;
  } else if (shown.kind === 'worker-failed') {
    action = <button type="button" className="doc-plain-action" onClick={p.onRetry}>{DOC_MARKDOWN_ACTION.retry}</button>;
  }
  return <DocPlain text={p.text} note={docsPlainNote(shown)} action={action} />;
}

/** What the reader has chosen. `ask`: the gate is up and nothing is parsed. `format`: the normal budget. `large`:
 *  **Format anyway**, the large budget. `text`: **Show as text**. */
type Choice = 'ask' | 'format' | 'large' | 'text';

/** A Docs page's Markdown body (spec 4.10). The caller keys it by `pinKey`. */
export function DocMarkdown(p: DocMarkdownProps): ReactNode {
  const bytes = useMemo(() => utf8ByteLength(p.text), [p.text]);
  const [choice, setChoice] = useState<Choice>(() => (bytes > DOCS_RENDER_GATE_BYTES ? 'ask' : 'format'));
  const [attempt, setAttempt] = useState(0);
  if (choice === 'ask') {
    return (
      <div className="doc-gate">
        <p className="doc-gate-copy">{docGateSentence(bytes)}</p>
        <button type="button" className="doc-gate-btn" onClick={() => setChoice('large')}>{DOC_MARKDOWN_ACTION.formatAnyway}</button>
        <button type="button" className="doc-gate-btn" onClick={() => setChoice('text')}>{DOC_MARKDOWN_ACTION.showAsText}</button>
      </div>
    );
  }
  if (choice === 'text') return <DocPlain text={p.text} note={docShownAsTextNote(bytes)} />;
  const budgetMs = choice === 'large' ? DOCS_PARSE_BUDGET_LARGE_MS : DOCS_PARSE_BUDGET_MS(bytes);
  return (
    <DocParse
      {...p} bytes={bytes} budgetMs={budgetMs} attempt={attempt}
      onFormatAnyway={() => setChoice('large')} onRetry={() => setAttempt((n) => n + 1)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Task 9: DocsScreen, the app's docs arm and data-view, the index, project, section, directory and leaf views, leaf routing by content class (the html stand-in), and the linked-worktree redirect
**Model routing:** implementer `sonnet`, effort `high`; per-task reviewer `opus` (lens 3 of "How this wave runs": the visit's state machine, here one mount per visit, the index read once, the redirects by replace; lens 4: what each page says, here the views' words, refinement (c)'s sentence and the `html` stand-in; lens 2 for the leaf's `svg`, raster and `html` routes; lens 5 for mutation-table discipline). No subagent inherits a model.
**Spec rows:** M4.R2; M4.R4; the W5 halves of M4.R1 (the injected `loaders.tree` called with ref `b`) and M4.B1 (a throwing `DocsScreen` at `/docs`); M5.3's leaf-routing half; M5.20; spec 3.1's canonicalisation (the slash-less forms, and a directory's slash decided by the tree answer); 4.2's app arm; 4.3's module-scope defaults; 4.4's views, rows, layout of the leaf by class and the too-large rule; 4.7's redirect; 5.5's SVG leaf; 6.1's "too-large from the listed size without a request". Refinements (b) (the `html` stand-in until W6; a deviation Task 12 defines), (c) (`branch: null` is not called detached; a deviation Task 12 defines), (o) (a pending fragment scrolls once after the new body renders; a direct load's `location.hash` too), (q) (every page URL is `docsPageUrl(docsLocation(page, to))`), (r) (the index's `unwalked`, `duplicates` and withheld counts). This task writes no deviation number anywhere. The header (crumbs, back, truth line, freshness chip, actions, banners, "Updated to") is Task 10's: this task leaves the views headless and gives Task 10 the drafted-asset count it needs.

Every `null` here has one meaning, stated beside it. Inside `DocsScreen`, `IndexSlot | null` is `null` exactly when no index request has been made in this visit; the redirect note's `null` means the redirect owes no sentence. `DocsTreeView` renders nothing for the index and for a leaf (the screen never hands it either). `DocsLeaf` renders nothing when `page` names no entry of `tree` (the screen hands it only a leaf `docsPathKind` found).

**Decisions this task makes** (each pinned by a case below; refinements, not deviations, except (b) and (c), which the architecture already names and Task 12 defines):

1. **A path page's kind is the tree answer's, through `docsPathKind`, and only LISTED entries count.** An entry with exactly this section and path that `entryView` lists in the page's mode is a leaf; else a listed entry under `path + '/'` makes a directory; else it is "Not in this listing at <short>". So a draft-only file is "not in this listing" in the default view (where its hint applies) and a leaf in a ref view. `listDir` uses the same `listed` rule, so a folder's count is the number of listed entries under it.
2. **A directory reached without its slash replace-navigates to the slash form; a leaf reached WITH a slash replace-navigates to the slash-less form** (spec 3.1 decides the first; the second is its mirror, since `pinFor` opens nothing for a slashed page). Both, the canonical-URL fix and the owner redirect are one `useEffect` in `DocsScreen` that always calls `navigate(href, {replace: true})` (M4.R4: `history.length` unchanged).
3. **`same-page` joins `docsLocation`'s targets** (Task 6's union): "this very page (section, path, view, frame) in `project` at `ref`". The owner redirect and the missing page's **Open the draft view** both need a page URL that changes the project or the ref and keeps the rest; spelling `{...page, project, ref}` in a view would break refinement (q), so the spread lives once, in `docsLocation`. Task 10's banner links ("Open the draft view", "Open the local view", "Back to the draft") reuse it.
4. **The owner redirect (spec 4.7, refinement (c)).** `linked-worktree` or `shared-repo` with a string `owner`: the same page in the owner's project, by replace. `branch` a string that `parseDocsRef` admits: that ref (`{kind: 'bare', name}` for `ws/a`). `branch: null`: the owner's default view (`ref: null`) and refinement (c)'s sentence, "That checkout is not on a named branch, or its branch could not be read; showing <owner>'s default branch." (never "detached"). A `branch` string Docs cannot address (`a..b`): the default view, saying "That checkout's branch <b> is not one Docs can address; showing <owner>'s default branch." `branch` ABSENT (a `shared-repo` answer may name only its owner, spec 2's table): the page's own ref, since it is the same repository. `owner` not a string (`null`, or absent): no redirect; the page renders the word's sentence through `DocsFailureView`. While the redirect is owed the page says "Opening <owner>…". The sentence survives the navigation because `DocsScreen` is one mount: it is held with the URL it was written for and shown only there.
5. **An `other` leaf is never read for display.** Spec 4.4 gives `other` "No preview (N KiB)" and Download; reading up to 2 MiB to show neither would be waste. `useDocsVisit`'s `wantedFile` answers `none` for `other` AFTER its too-large rule, so an `other` leaf over its cap still shows the `too-large` sentence; Download reads the bytes itself (`downloadDocFile`). N is the listed size of the side the pin opens, in KiB rounded up (`kib`).
6. **A raster leaf is ONE `DocImage`** (spec 4.4): a one-image page whose only `img` element is synthetic, with the leaf's own file name (percent-encoded, `./<name>`) as its detached `src` and image index 0, under the leaf's own `DocLinkContext`. So the pin rule (`imagePinFor`), the class cap (a refused "Image not loaded: it is <size>; Docs shows images up to <cap>", no request), the queue, the raster checks and the object URL are all `DocImage`'s; no second raster path exists. (A tap on that image navigates to its own leaf, which is the page already shown: a no-op apart from a history entry, left as `DocImage` does it.)
7. **An SVG leaf draws the bytes the visit already read** (spec 5.5), through `svgDataUrl`, which `DocImage.tsx` now exports beside its private `base64Of` (additive: `fetchImage`'s own line is unchanged, so Task 7's row on it stands). Never `blob:`, never `/api/`, and `URL.createObjectURL` is not called. An answer whose `contentClass` is not `svg` is a client-built `malformed-answer` with `DOCS_SHOW_NOT_SVG`; no bytes in the named field is `DOCS_SHOW_NO_BYTES`.
8. **A `text` leaf is the shared `CodeBlock` when a registered grammar knows its extension, else `<pre className="doc-plain">`.** The architecture's outline says "pre.doc-plain highlighted through CodeBlock", but `CodeBlock` draws its own bar and `<pre>` (and carries the 64 Ki-character and r10 bounds); wrapping it in a second `pre` would nest two. So `x.ts` gives `.code-block` labelled `TypeScript` with `hljs` spans, and `x.txt` gives `pre.doc-plain`. The grammar test is `hljs.getLanguage(ext)` on the one instance `lib/markdown.tsx` registers (the extension is ASCII once `contentClass` said `text`, so `toLowerCase` lowers it exactly). Bytes that are not UTF-8 are `DocPlain` with "Not valid UTF-8." through Task 8's `docMarkdownSource` (whose strict-then-non-fatal rule is refinement (x), a deviation).
9. **The `html` stand-in (refinement (b)):** "HTML mockups open in a later release; Source shows the file and Download saves it.", "Size: <KiB>", **Source** (the text renderer: `pre.doc-plain` of the file) and **Download**. No `iframe`, `frame`, `object`, `embed` or `srcdoc` attribute, and the HTML reaches only a text node; `?frame=full` renders the same. W6 replaces this arm with `MockupView`.
10. **A pending fragment scrolls once after the new body renders** (refinement (o)): `DocsLeaf` watches its own subtree with a `MutationObserver` until `fragmentTarget` (now exported from `DocLink.tsx`, so one id rule serves both) finds the id inside the leaf's `<article>`, scrolls it into view and clears the fragment. A direct load's `location.hash` is handed to the visit once, on mount.
11. **The index (spec 4.4, refinement (r)).** Rows with docs come first: `ready` rows by name, then every other state by name; "Projects with no docs (N)" folds `ready` rows whose four counts are all 0 and plain folders with no section on disk (`null` counts as maybe, so it is never folded). Names sort by code unit, never by locale. A ready row: name, `<default> · <short commit>`, `sectionCountsText`, "fetched <formatAge>" or "never fetched" (no `fetch` field: nothing), and "same repository as <others>" for a `duplicates` group. Other states in words: "part of <owner>" as a link to the owner's default view (a `null` owner: "part of a repository outside the projects folder"), "partial clone", "not a git repository", "no default branch", "unreadable". Footers "<n> folder(s) not listed (names Docs cannot address)." and "<n> project(s) not checked (Docs ran out of time listing them)."; `cacheAgeMs` is not shown. One GET per visit: returning to `/docs` reuses the answer; a failure offers Retry; a sign-in re-reads an `auth` answer.
12. **The project page:** four rows in `DOC_SECTION_SLUGS` order from `tree.sections`: label, repo path, count; a ref view adds "<n> draft(s)" (entries whose `entryView` badge is set and not `withheld`) and " · <m> withheld" when `m > 0`; `absent` and `not-a-directory` rows are not buttons and say "not in this repository at <short>" / "is not a directory at <short>". Notes: "<n> file(s) not listed (names Docs cannot address)." and "Drafts inside nested repositories are not shown: <dirs>."
13. **Section and directory pages:** a filter (by name, case-insensitive) and `listDir`'s rows, each a `<button className="docs-row">` that navigates with a history entry through `docsLocation` (so the page's `ref` is kept): glyph, name, the `ENTRY_BADGE_TEXT` badge, a `symlink`/`submodule` mark, and the size of the side the row opens in KiB. A missing path says "Not in this listing at <short>.", and in the default view of a holder whose worktree has a non-deleted draft at or under the path, "It may be an uncommitted draft on <branch>." with **Open the draft view** linking `?ref=refs/heads/<branch>` (qualified, as rows 67 and M4.T2 require of every draft-view link).
14. **Every view word is `DOCS_VIEW_TEXT`'s** (appended to `docsText.ts`, filled by `fillSentence`, with `pluralS` for `{s}`), except the index's four state words, which sit in `DocsIndexView.tsx` as a `Record` over the row's state type. The cases spell the spec's phrases verbatim.
15. **The defaults' identities are module-scope (spec 4.3)** and that is what makes images load once: `DocsAssetContext`'s value is memoised on `loaders`, so a new `loaders` object per render would reload every image (Task 7's contract). The case renders with the DEFAULT loaders over a stubbed `fetch` (tree, file, image: 3 requests) and re-renders: still 3. `docsRunner.prewarm()` runs on mount only when the parser is the default one (an injected parser has no worker to warm).
16. **The asset context is one per mount**: the queue is `useState(createFetchQueue)` and is never disposed (each `DocImage` aborts its own job when it unmounts, so nothing outlives the screen; disposing in an effect cleanup would kill it under StrictMode's double mount). The drafted-asset count sums `onDraftAsset`'s deltas into state and is rendered as `data-draft-assets` on `.docs-screen`; Task 10's banner ("This draft page embeds {k} uncommitted asset{s}") reads the same state.
17. **Class names for Task 11 to register** (nothing here styles them): `docs-screen`, `docs-loading`, `docs-note`, `docs-invalid`, `docs-redirect-note`, `docs-hint-link`, `docs-index`, `docs-index-head`, `docs-filter`, `docs-rows`, `docs-row` (a `<button>`, and on a `div` with `docs-row-off`), `docs-row-name`, `docs-row-ref`, `docs-row-count`, `docs-row-age`, `docs-row-note`, `docs-row-state`, `docs-row-path`, `docs-row-drafts`, `docs-row-glyph`, `docs-row-mark`, `docs-row-size`, `docs-badge`, `docs-nodocs`, `docs-owner-link`, `docs-project`, `docs-listing`, `docs-missing`, `docs-leaf`, `docs-leaf-actions`, `docs-leaf-action`, `docs-svg`, `docs-svg-img`, `docs-standin`, `docs-raster`, `docs-changing`. Tap targets: `.docs-row`, `.docs-filter`, `.docs-leaf-action`, `.docs-owner-link`, `.docs-hint-link`, `.docs-nodocs > summary`.

```tsx
// Docs W5 part 1, Task 9: the Docs screen (spec 2026-10-01 3.1, 4.2-4.4, 4.7, 5.5, 6.1; M4.R4, M5.3's leaf-routing
// half, M5.20; refinements (b), (c), (o), (q), (r)). One mount is one visit: the URL is parsed and canonicalised by
// replace, a directory's slash is the tree answer's call, a linked worktree is followed to its owner by replace (and
// `branch: null` says what it means), and each view renders the slots and the tree answer it is given. Every test
// injects its loaders and a parser that parses in this thread, except the one that proves the defaults' identities,
// which stubs `fetch`. Placeholders only: projects `demo`, `a`, `b`; branches `main`, `ws/a`; `/repo/demo`.
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { act, cleanup, fireEvent, render, screen, waitFor, within } from '@testing-library/react';
import {
  DOCS_CLASS_CAP, DOCS_RASTER_TYPES,
  type DocPin, type DocsEntry, type DocsFileResponse, type DocsIndexOk, type DocsIndexRow, type DocsProjectsResponse,
  type DocsTreeOk, type DraftsFacts,
} from '../../shared/docs';
import { DocsScreen } from '../src/screens/DocsScreen';
import { DOCS_FAILURE_SENTENCE, DOCS_PAGE_INVALID_SENTENCE } from '../src/docs/docsText';
import type { DocsFileAnswer, DocsLoaders, DocsRasterAnswer } from '../src/docs/failures';
import { parseMarkdown } from '../src/lib/markdownParse';
import { docsRunner, type MarkdownParser } from '../src/lib/markdownRunner';
import { navigate, useLocation } from '../src/lib/router';
import {
  COMMIT_A, COMMIT_B, FP_1, draftOf, entry, failedAnswer, fakeLoaders, fileResponse, holder, okTree, treeOk,
  treeResponse, type FakeLoaders,
} from './docsFixtures';

/** Parses in this thread, as the worker would. */
const parser: MarkdownParser = async (src) => parseMarkdown(src, 'docs');

/** The screen under the live location, as the app's `docs` arm mounts it (one mount across navigations). */
function Routed(p: { readonly loaders: DocsLoaders }): ReactNode {
  const { path, search } = useLocation();
  return <DocsScreen path={path} search={search} loaders={p.loaders} parser={parser} />;
}

function open(url: string, f: FakeLoaders): ReturnType<typeof render> {
  navigate(url);
  return render(<Routed loaders={f.loaders} />);
}

const here = (): string => location.pathname + location.search;

/** A file answer of `contentClass` for `path`, its text sent as utf8. */
function fileAs(path: string, text: string, contentClass: DocsFileResponse['contentClass']): DocsFileAnswer {
  const r = fileResponse(text);
  return { s: 'ok', value: { ...r, contentClass, show: { ...r.show, path, size: text.length } } };
}

/** A PNG's own magic from L0's table (never spelled here) and two bytes of body. */
const pngBytes = (): Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer> => new Uint8Array([...DOCS_RASTER_TYPES.png.magic[0][0].bytes, 0, 255]);
const okPng = (): DocsRasterAnswer => ({ s: 'ok', value: { bytes: pngBytes(), mime: 'image/png' } });

/** Loaders whose `file` answers by path (an unknown path answers `absent-path`). */
function byPath(tree: DocsTreeOk, files: Readonly<Record<string, DocsFileAnswer>>): FakeLoaders {
  const f = fakeLoaders({ tree: okTree(tree) });
  f.file.mockImplementation(async (_project: string, pin: DocPin) => files[pin.path] ?? failedAnswer('absent-path'));
  f.raster.mockImplementation(async () => okPng());
  return f;
}

const SVG_DATA = 'data:image/svg+xml;base64,' + btoa(SVG_TEXT);

/** The index fixture (refinement (r)): every state, a duplicate pair, a no-docs pair, both footers. */
function indexAnswer(): DocsProjectsResponse {

    duplicates: [{ repoKey: 'k1', projects: ['a', 'b'] }],
    projects: [
      { project: 'wt', state: 'linked-worktree', github: { state: 'none' }, owner: 'a', branch: 'ws/a' },
      ready('b', {
        repoKey: 'k1', sections: { specs: 12, plans: 40, 'product-design': 3, conventions: 0 },
        fetch: { okAgeMs: 300000, lastOutcome: 'ok' },
      }),
      { project: 'pc', state: 'partial-clone', github: { state: 'none' } },
      ready('a', { repoKey: 'k1', sections: { specs: null, plans: 1, 'product-design': 0, conventions: 0 }, fetch: { okAgeMs: null, lastOutcome: 'fetch-transport' } }),
      { project: 'orphan', state: 'linked-worktree', github: { state: 'none' }, owner: null, branch: null },
      { project: 'plain', state: 'not-a-git-repo', github: { state: 'none' }, sectionsOnDisk: ['specs'] },
      { project: 'nd', state: 'no-default-branch', github: { state: 'none' } },
      { project: 'ru', state: 'repo-unreadable', github: { state: 'none' } },
      ready('empty', { sections: { specs: 0, plans: 0, 'product-design': 0, conventions: 0 } }),
      { project: 'junk', state: 'not-a-git-repo', github: { state: 'none' }, sectionsOnDisk: [] },
    ],
  };
  return { ok: true, index, cacheAgeMs: 1234 };
}

function openIndex(): FakeLoaders {
  const f = fakeLoaders();
  f.projects.mockResolvedValue({ s: 'ok', value: indexAnswer() });
  open('/docs', f);
  return f;
}

const mainRowNames = (): string[] =>
  [...document.querySelectorAll('.docs-index > .docs-rows .docs-row-name')].map((n) => n.textContent ?? '');

});

    rerender(<DocsScreen path="/docs/demo" search="" loaders={f.loaders} />);
    expect(prewarm).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    cleanup();
    render(<DocsScreen path="/docs/demo" search="" loaders={f.loaders} parser={parser} />);
    expect(prewarm).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  it('with the default loaders, a re-render makes no second request: the tree, the file and the image once each', async () => {
    vi.spyOn(docsRunner, 'prewarm').mockImplementation(() => {});
    const tree = treeOk({ entries: [entry('specs', 'a.md'), entry('specs', 'd.png')] });
    const json = (body: unknown): Response =>
      new Response(JSON.stringify(body), { status: 200, headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8' } });
    const fetchSpy = vi.fn(async (url: RequestInfo | URL): Promise<Response> => {
      const u = String(url);
      if (u.startsWith('/api/docs/demo/tree')) return json(treeResponse(tree));
      if (u.includes('path=a.md')) return json(fileResponse('# A\n\n![d](d.png)\n'));
      if (u.includes('path=d.png')) return new Response(pngBytes(), { status: 200, headers: { 'content-type': 'image/png' } });
      return new Response('{}', { status: 404 });
    });
    vi.stubGlobal('fetch', fetchSpy);
    navigate('/docs/demo/specs/a.md');
    const { rerender, container } = render(<DocsScreen path="/docs/demo/specs/a.md" search="" parser={parser} />);
    await waitFor(() => expect(container.querySelector('article img')?.getAttribute('src')).toMatch(/^blob:/));
    expect(fetchSpy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
    rerender(<DocsScreen path="/docs/demo/specs/a.md" search="" parser={parser} />);
    await act(async () => { await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 20)); });
    expect(fetchSpy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
    expect(container.querySelector('article img')?.getAttribute('src')).toMatch(/^blob:/);
  });

  it('the drafted-asset count is the sum of the images\' deltas, and drops to 0 when the page goes', async () => {
    const drafted = (path: string): DocsEntry => entry('specs', path, { draft: draftOf('modified') });
    const f = byPath(treeOk({ entries: [drafted('a.md'), drafted('p.png'), drafted('q.png')], drafts: holder() }), {
      'a.md': fileAs('a.md', '# A\n\n![p](p.png) ![q](q.png)\n', 'markdown'),
    });
    const { container } = open('/docs/demo/specs/a.md?ref=main', f);
    const screenEl = (): Element => container.querySelector('.docs-screen') as Element;
    await waitFor(() => expect(screenEl()).toHaveAttribute('data-draft-assets', '2'));
    expect(f.file.mock.calls[0]![1]).toMatchObject({ kind: 'draft', fp: FP_1 });
    act(() => { navigate('/docs/demo/specs?ref=main'); });
    await waitFor(() => expect(screenEl()).toHaveAttribute('data-draft-assets', '0'));
  });
});
```

```tsx
// mocked `DocsScreen` that throws while rendering at `/docs` shows "This screen could not be shown." inside

// draws the ladder again. W4 proved the boundary on a stand-in (`app-detail-boundary.test.tsx`, a throwing
// `RunsScreen`); this is the row's own fixture. Its own file because the module mock is per file.
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import type { MockInstance } from 'vitest';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { act, cleanup, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
import { navigate } from '../src/lib/router';
import { useFleetStore } from '../src/stores/fleet';

/** `vi.hoisted`: the mock factory runs while app.tsx is being evaluated, before this file's body. */
const boom = vi.hoisted(() => ({ on: true }));

vi.mock('../src/screens/DocsScreen', () => ({
  DocsScreen: (p: { path: string; search: string }): ReactNode => {
    if (boom.on) throw new Error('docs screen broke');
    return <h1>docs (stand-in) {p.path + p.search}</h1>;
  },
}));

const { App } = await import('../src/app');

let warn: MockInstance<typeof console.warn>;
let error: MockInstance<typeof console.error>;

beforeEach(() => {
  boom.on = true;
  warn = vi.spyOn(console, 'warn').mockImplementation(() => {});
  // React reports every error a boundary caught through console.error; silenced here, in this file only.
  error = vi.spyOn(console, 'error').mockImplementation(() => {});
});

afterEach(() => {
  cleanup();
  navigate('/');
  act(() => useFleetStore.setState({ sessions: [], conn: 'connecting', notices: [], blocked: false, pools: null }));
  warn.mockRestore();
  error.mockRestore();
});

const FALLBACK = 'This screen could not be shown.';
const detail = (): HTMLElement => document.querySelector('.shell-detail') as HTMLElement;

describe('a throwing DocsScreen keeps the shell (M4.B1, W5 half)', () => {
  it('draws the fallback inside .shell-detail at /docs while .shell-nav stays mounted', () => {
    navigate('/docs');
    render(<App />);
    expect(document.querySelector('.shell-nav')).not.toBeNull();
    expect(detail()).toContainElement(screen.getByText(FALLBACK));
    expect(warn).toHaveBeenCalledWith('ccrc: render error in detail', expect.objectContaining({ message: 'docs screen broke' }));
  });

  it('navigating to another Docs page resets the boundary, and the screen draws once it can', () => {
    navigate('/docs');
    render(<App />);
    expect(screen.getByText(FALLBACK)).toBeInTheDocument();
    boom.on = false;
    act(() => { navigate('/docs/demo'); });
    expect(screen.queryByText(FALLBACK)).toBeNull();
    expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { name: 'docs (stand-in) /docs/demo' })).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('navigating away from Docs resets it too', () => {
    navigate('/docs/demo?ref=ws/a');
    render(<App />);
    expect(screen.getByText(FALLBACK)).toBeInTheDocument();
    act(() => { navigate('/settings'); });
    expect(screen.queryByText(FALLBACK)).toBeNull();
    expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { name: /^settings$/i })).toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 4: The listing rules.** Create `pwa/src/docs/docsTree.ts` with exactly:

```ts
// The Docs listing's pure rules (spec 2026-10-01 4.4; W5 part 1 Task 9): what a section or directory page lists and
// in what order, what a path page IS (a leaf, a directory, or not in this listing), the section labels and the
// counts string. Every list of sections is derived from L0's `DOC_SECTION_SLUGS`, and the label and order tables are
// `Record`s over its type, so a fifth section is a compile error here until it has both. No React, no DOM, no state.
import {
  DOC_SECTION_SLUGS, entryView,
  type DocContentClass, type DocSectionSlug, type DocsEntry, type DocsTreeOk, type DraftsFacts, type EntryMode,
  type EntryView,
} from '../../../shared/docs';

/** A section's label, also the noun of its count (`12 specs · 40 plans · 3 design · 0 conventions`). */
export const SECTION_LABEL: Readonly<Record<DocSectionSlug, string>> = {
  specs: 'specs',
  plans: 'plans',
  'product-design': 'design',
  conventions: 'conventions',
};

/** How a section lists (spec 4.4): `specs` and `plans` newest first (name descending; their names are
 *  date-prefixed), the other two alphabetical. Folders and files each follow it. */
export const SECTION_ORDER: Readonly<Record<DocSectionSlug, 'newest-first' | 'alphabetical'>> = {
  specs: 'newest-first',
  plans: 'newest-first',
  'product-design': 'alphabetical',
  conventions: 'alphabetical',
};

/** A row's glyph by the path's content class (decorative; the row's name carries the meaning). */
export const CLASS_GLYPH: Readonly<Record<DocContentClass, string>> = {
  markdown: '¶',
  raster: '▣',
  svg: '◇',
  html: '⧉',
  text: '≡',
  other: '·',
};

/** A folder row's glyph. */
export const FOLDER_GLYPH = '▸';

/** One section or directory page's rows (spec 4.4): folders first, each with the number of LISTED entries anywhere
 *  under it, then files, each with its `entryView`. */
export interface DirListing {
  readonly folders: readonly { name: string; count: number }[];
  readonly files: readonly { entry: DocsEntry; view: EntryView }[];
}

/** Code-unit order, never the locale's: the same listing sorts the same way on every phone. */
function byName(a: string, b: string): number {
  return a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0;
}

/** The rows of `section` under `dir` (`''`: the section root; otherwise a directory path relative to the section,
 *  with no trailing slash). Only entries `entryView` lists in `mode` count, so a default-view page never lists a
 *  draft-only file and a ref view lists a new draft. Order is `SECTION_ORDER[section]` for folders and files alike. */
export function listDir(
  entries: readonly DocsEntry[], section: DocSectionSlug, dir: string, mode: EntryMode, drafts: DraftsFacts,
): DirListing {
  const prefix = dir === '' ? '' : dir + '/';
  const folders = new Map<string, number>();
  const files: { entry: DocsEntry; view: EntryView }[] = [];
  for (const entry of entries) {
    if (entry.section !== section || !entry.path.startsWith(prefix)) continue;
    const view = entryView(entry, drafts, mode);
    if (!view.listed) continue;
    const rest = entry.path.slice(prefix.length);
    const slash = rest.indexOf('/');
    if (slash < 0) files.push({ entry, view });
    else folders.set(rest.slice(0, slash), (folders.get(rest.slice(0, slash)) ?? 0) + 1);
  }
  const sign = SECTION_ORDER[section] === 'newest-first' ? -1 : 1;
  return {
    folders: [...folders].map(([name, count]) => ({ name, count })).sort((a, b) => sign * byName(a.name, b.name)),
    files: files.sort((a, b) => sign * byName(a.entry.path, b.entry.path)),
  };
}

/** The four section counts in `DOC_SECTION_SLUGS` order, joined by ` · ` (spec 4.4). A `null` count renders `?`:
 *  the count is not known, never zero. */
export function sectionCountsText(counts: Readonly<Record<DocSectionSlug, number | null>>): string {
  return DOC_SECTION_SLUGS.map((slug) => `${counts[slug] ?? '?'} ${SECTION_LABEL[slug]}`).join(' · ');
}

/** What a `path` page is, from the tree answer, never from the URL's shape (spec 3.1, 4.4): `leaf` when an entry has
 *  exactly this section and path and `entryView` lists it in `mode`; else `dir` when a listed entry lies under
 *  `path + '/'`; else `missing` ("Not in this listing"). */
export type DocsPathKind =
  | { readonly kind: 'leaf'; readonly entry: DocsEntry; readonly view: EntryView }
  | { readonly kind: 'dir' }
  | { readonly kind: 'missing' };

export function docsPathKind(tree: DocsTreeOk, section: DocSectionSlug, path: string, mode: EntryMode): DocsPathKind {
  const exact = tree.entries.find((e) => e.section === section && e.path === path);
  if (exact !== undefined) {
    const view = entryView(exact, tree.drafts, mode);
    if (view.listed) return { kind: 'leaf', entry: exact, view };
  }
  const under = path + '/';
  const dir = tree.entries.some((e) =>
    e.section === section && e.path.startsWith(under) && entryView(e, tree.drafts, mode).listed);
  return dir ? { kind: 'dir' } : { kind: 'missing' };
}

/** The last segment of a section-relative path: a leaf's file name, and the name Download saves it under. */
export function leafName(path: string): string {
  return path.slice(path.lastIndexOf('/') + 1);
}
```

- [ ] **Step 5: The project, section and directory pages, and the index.** Create `pwa/src/docs/DocsTreeView.tsx` with exactly:

```tsx
// The project, section and directory pages of the Docs screen (spec 2026-10-01 4.4; W5 part 1 Task 9), and a path
// page the tree answer does not list. Pure renderers of one tree answer: every row and link is built by
// `docsLocation` (refinement (q)), so it keeps the page's project and ref; rows come from `listDir` in
// `SECTION_ORDER`; every word is `DOCS_VIEW_TEXT`'s. The header (crumbs, truth line, actions, banners) is Task 10's.
import { useState, type MouseEvent, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import {
  DOC_SECTION_SLUGS, contentClass, docsPageUrl, entryView, parseDocsRef,
  type DocSectionSlug, type DocsPageLocation, type DocsTreeOk, type EntryMode,
} from '../../../shared/docs';
import { navigate } from '../lib/router';
import { docsLocation } from './docsLinks';
import { DOCS_VIEW_TEXT, ENTRY_BADGE_TEXT, fillSentence, kib, pluralS, shortCommit } from './docsText';
import { CLASS_GLYPH, FOLDER_GLYPH, SECTION_LABEL, docsPathKind, leafName, listDir } from './docsTree';

/** An in-app link to a Docs page: a real `href` (a modifier or middle click opens a new tab), and a plain left click
 *  navigates in place with a history entry. */
export function DocsPageLink(p: { readonly href: string; readonly className?: string; readonly children: ReactNode }): ReactNode {
  const onClick = (e: MouseEvent<HTMLAnchorElement>): void => {
    if (e.button !== 0 || e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey || e.shiftKey || e.altKey) return;
    e.preventDefault();
    navigate(p.href);
  };
  return <a href={p.href} className={p.className} onClick={onClick}>{p.children}</a>;
}

/** One `.docs-row` button (spec 4.4: one `<button>` per row); a tap navigates with a history entry. */
function RowButton(p: { readonly href: string; readonly children: ReactNode }): ReactNode {
  return <button type="button" className="docs-row" onClick={() => navigate(p.href)}>{p.children}</button>;
}

function modeOf(page: DocsPageLocation): EntryMode {
  return page.kind !== 'index' && page.ref !== null ? 'ref' : 'default';
}

/** A project's four section rows, in `DOC_SECTIONS` order, and its notes (spec 4.4's project row). */
function ProjectPage(p: { readonly tree: DocsTreeOk; readonly page: DocsPageLocation }): ReactNode {
  const { tree, page } = p;
  const mode = modeOf(page);
  const short = shortCommit(tree.ref.commit);
  const drafts = tree.drafts;
  return (
    <div className="docs-project">
      <ul className="docs-rows">
        {DOC_SECTION_SLUGS.map((slug) => {
          const s = tree.sections.find((x) => x.slug === slug);
          if (s === undefined) return null;
          const label = <span className="docs-row-name">{SECTION_LABEL[slug]}</span>;
          const path = <span className="docs-row-path">{s.path}</span>;
          if (s.state !== 'present') {
            const why = s.state === 'absent' ? DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.sectionAbsent : DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.sectionNotDir;
            return (
              <li key={slug}>
                <div className="docs-row docs-row-off" data-section={slug}>
                  {label} {path} <span className="docs-row-note">{fillSentence(why, { short })}</span>
                </div>
              </li>
            );
          }
          let drafted = 0;
          let withheld = 0;
          if (mode === 'ref') {
            for (const e of tree.entries) {
              if (e.section !== slug) continue;
              const badge = entryView(e, drafts, 'ref').badge;
              if (badge === 'withheld') withheld += 1;
              else if (badge !== null) drafted += 1;
            }
          }
          const href = docsPageUrl(docsLocation(page, { kind: 'section', section: slug }));
          return (
            <li key={slug}>
              <RowButton href={href}>
                {label} {path} <span className="docs-row-count">{s.count}</span>
                {drafted + withheld > 0 && (
                  <span className="docs-row-drafts">
                    {fillSentence(DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.sectionDrafts, { n: drafted, s: pluralS(drafted) })}
                    {withheld > 0 && ` · ${fillSentence(DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.sectionWithheld, { n: withheld })}`}
                  </span>
                )}
              </RowButton>
            </li>
          );
        })}
      </ul>
      {tree.unlisted.count > 0 && (
        <p className="docs-note">
          {fillSentence(DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.treeUnlisted, { n: tree.unlisted.count, s: pluralS(tree.unlisted.count) })}
        </p>
      )}
      {drafts.state === 'holder' && drafts.opaque.length > 0 && (
        <p className="docs-note">{fillSentence(DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.opaque, { dirs: drafts.opaque.join(', ') })}</p>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

/** A section root (`dir === ''`) or a directory: a filter and `listDir`'s rows (spec 4.4). */
function ListingPage(p: {
  readonly tree: DocsTreeOk; readonly page: DocsPageLocation; readonly section: DocSectionSlug; readonly dir: string;
}): ReactNode {
  const { tree, page, section, dir } = p;
  const [filter, setFilter] = useState('');
  const listing = listDir(tree.entries, section, dir, modeOf(page), tree.drafts);
  const needle = filter.toLowerCase();
  const shown = (name: string): boolean => needle === '' || name.toLowerCase().includes(needle);
  const prefix = dir === '' ? '' : dir + '/';
  const folders = listing.folders.filter((f) => shown(f.name));
  const files = listing.files.filter((f) => shown(leafName(f.entry.path)));
  return (
    <div className="docs-listing">
      <input
        type="search" className="docs-filter" aria-label={DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.filterEntries} value={filter}
        onChange={(e) => setFilter(e.target.value)}
      />
      {listing.folders.length + listing.files.length === 0 && <p className="docs-note">{DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.emptyListing}</p>}
      <ul className="docs-rows">
        {folders.map((f) => (
          <li key={'d:' + f.name}>
            <RowButton href={docsPageUrl(docsLocation(page, { kind: 'path', section, path: prefix + f.name, dirSlash: true }))}>
              <span className="docs-row-glyph" aria-hidden="true">{FOLDER_GLYPH}</span>
              <span className="docs-row-name">{f.name}/</span> <span className="docs-row-count">{f.count}</span>
            </RowButton>
          </li>
        ))}
        {files.map(({ entry, view }) => {
          const href = docsPageUrl(docsLocation(page, { kind: 'path', section, path: entry.path, dirSlash: false }));
          const size = view.opens === 'draft' ? entry.draft?.size : entry.committed?.size;
          const mark = view.committedKind === 'symlink' || view.committedKind === 'submodule' ? view.committedKind : null;
          return (
            <li key={'f:' + entry.path}>
              <RowButton href={href}>
                <span className="docs-row-glyph" aria-hidden="true">{CLASS_GLYPH[contentClass(entry.path)]}</span>
                <span className="docs-row-name">{leafName(entry.path)}</span>
                {view.badge !== null && <> <span className="docs-badge">{ENTRY_BADGE_TEXT[view.badge]}</span></>}
                {mark !== null && <> <span className="docs-row-mark">{mark}</span></>}
                {typeof size === 'number' && <> <span className="docs-row-size">{kib(size)}</span></>}
              </RowButton>
            </li>
          );
        })}
      </ul>
    </div>
  );
}

/** A path the tree answer does not list (spec 4.4): "Not in this listing at <short commit>", and, in the default view
 *  of a holder whose worktree has a draft at or under the path, the hint with **Open the draft view** linking this
 *  page at `refs/heads/<drafts.branch>`. */
function MissingPage(p: { readonly tree: DocsTreeOk; readonly page: DocsPageLocation & { kind: 'path' } }): ReactNode {
  const { tree, page } = p;
  const drafts = tree.drafts;
  const under = page.path + '/';
  const drafted = page.ref === null && drafts.state === 'holder' && tree.entries.some((e) =>
    e.section === page.section && (e.path === page.path || e.path.startsWith(under))
    && e.draft !== null && e.draft.state !== 'deleted');
  const draftRef = drafts.state === 'holder' ? parseDocsRef('refs/heads/' + drafts.branch) : null;
  return (
    <div className="docs-missing">
      <p className="docs-note">{fillSentence(DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.missing, { short: shortCommit(tree.ref.commit) })}</p>
      {drafted && drafts.state === 'holder' && draftRef !== null && (
        <p className="docs-note">
          {fillSentence(DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.missingDraftHint, { branch: drafts.branch })}{' '}
          <DocsPageLink
            className="docs-hint-link"
            href={docsPageUrl(docsLocation(page, { kind: 'same-page', project: page.project, ref: draftRef }))}
          >
            {DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.openDraftView}
          </DocsPageLink>
        </p>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

/** The project, section and directory pages, and a path page that is not a leaf (spec 4.4). A leaf is `DocsLeaf`'s;
 *  given one here (or the index), this renders nothing. */
export function DocsTreeView(p: { readonly tree: DocsTreeOk; readonly page: DocsPageLocation }): ReactNode {
  const { tree, page } = p;
  switch (page.kind) {
    case 'index':
      return null;
    case 'project':
      return <ProjectPage tree={tree} page={page} />;
    case 'section':
      return <ListingPage key={page.section} tree={tree} page={page} section={page.section} dir="" />;
    case 'path': {
      const kind = docsPathKind(tree, page.section, page.path, modeOf(page)).kind;
      if (kind === 'dir') {
        return <ListingPage key={page.section + '/' + page.path} tree={tree} page={page} section={page.section} dir={page.path} />;
      }
      return kind === 'missing' ? <MissingPage tree={tree} page={page} /> : null;
    }
  }
}
```

Create `pwa/src/docs/DocsIndexView.tsx` with exactly:

```tsx
// The Docs index (spec 2026-10-01 4.4's index row; refinement (r); W5 part 1 Task 9): every project folder the fleet
// box listed, `ready` rows with docs first by name, then the rest in words, and the projects with no docs folded
// under one disclosure. A pure renderer of one `projects()` answer; every link is `docsLocation`'s.
import { useState, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import { docsPageUrl, type DocsIndexRow, type DocsProjectsResponse } from '../../../shared/docs';
import { formatAge } from '../fleet/formatReset';
import { navigate } from '../lib/router';
import { docsLocation } from './docsLinks';
import { DOCS_VIEW_TEXT, fillSentence, pluralS, shortCommit } from './docsText';
import { sectionCountsText } from './docsTree';
import { DocsPageLink } from './DocsTreeView';

/** A non-ready state in words (spec 4.4). `linked-worktree` and `shared-repo` are "part of <owner>" instead. */
const INDEX_STATE_TEXT: Readonly<Record<Exclude<DocsIndexRow['state'], 'ready' | 'linked-worktree' | 'shared-repo'>, string>> = {
  'not-a-git-repo': 'not a git repository',
  'partial-clone': 'partial clone',
  'no-default-branch': 'no default branch',
  'repo-unreadable': 'unreadable',
};

/** The page the index's links start from. It names no project and no ref, so nothing refinement (q) guards (the page's
 *  project and ref, W5b's `at`) can be dropped by spelling it; every target from it is `default-view`. */
const INDEX: { kind: 'index' } = { kind: 'index' };

function byName(a: DocsIndexRow, b: DocsIndexRow): number {
  return a.project < b.project ? -1 : a.project > b.project ? 1 : 0;
}

/** Whether a row has docs to show: a ready repository with any section count other than 0 (`null`, unknown, counts
 *  as maybe), or a plain folder with a section on disk. Every other state is shown in words, docs or not. */
function hasDocs(row: DocsIndexRow): boolean {
  if (row.state === 'ready') return row.sections === undefined || Object.values(row.sections).some((n) => n !== 0);
  if (row.state === 'not-a-git-repo') return (row.sectionsOnDisk?.length ?? 0) > 0;
  return true;
}

function defaultViewHref(project: string): string {
  return docsPageUrl(docsLocation(INDEX, { kind: 'default-view', project }));
}

function IndexRow(p: { readonly row: DocsIndexRow; readonly sameAs: readonly string[] }): ReactNode {
  const { row, sameAs } = p;
  const dup = sameAs.length > 0
    ? <span className="docs-row-note">{fillSentence(DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.duplicate, { other: sameAs.join(', ') })}</span>
    : null;
  if (row.state === 'ready') {
    const fetch = row.fetch;
    return (
      <button type="button" className="docs-row" onClick={() => navigate(defaultViewHref(row.project))}>
        <span className="docs-row-name">{row.project}</span>
        {row.default !== undefined && (
          <> <span className="docs-row-ref">{row.default.name} · <code>{shortCommit(row.default.commit)}</code></span></>
        )}
        {row.sections !== undefined && <> <span className="docs-row-count">{sectionCountsText(row.sections)}</span></>}
        {fetch !== undefined && (
          <> <span className="docs-row-age">
            {fetch.okAgeMs === null
              ? DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.neverFetched
              : fillSentence(DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.fetched, { age: formatAge(fetch.okAgeMs / 1000) })}
          </span></>
        )}
        {dup !== null && <> {dup}</>}
      </button>
    );
  }
  let state: ReactNode;
  if (row.state === 'linked-worktree' || row.state === 'shared-repo') {
    const owner = row.owner;
    state = typeof owner === 'string'
      ? <DocsPageLink className="docs-owner-link" href={defaultViewHref(owner)}>{fillSentence(DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.partOf, { owner })}</DocsPageLink>
      : DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.partOfUnknown;
  } else {
    state = INDEX_STATE_TEXT[row.state];
  }
  return (
    <div className="docs-row docs-row-off" data-state={row.state}>
      <span className="docs-row-name">{row.project}</span> <span className="docs-row-state">{state}</span>
      {dup !== null && <> {dup}</>}
    </div>
  );
}

/** The index page (spec 4.4): the header sentence, a filter, the rows, the no-docs disclosure and the footers
 *  (refinement (r): `unwalked` has its own footer, `duplicates` say "same repository as", `cacheAgeMs` is not shown). */
export function DocsIndexView(p: { readonly answer: DocsProjectsResponse }): ReactNode {
  const index = p.answer.index;
  const [filter, setFilter] = useState('');
  const needle = filter.toLowerCase();
  const rows = index.projects.filter((r) => needle === '' || r.project.toLowerCase().includes(needle));
  const sameAs = (row: DocsIndexRow): string[] => {
    const group = index.duplicates.find((d) => row.repoKey !== undefined && d.repoKey === row.repoKey);
    return group === undefined ? [] : group.projects.filter((x) => x !== row.project);
  };
  const ready = rows.filter((r) => r.state === 'ready' && hasDocs(r)).sort(byName);
  const rest = rows.filter((r) => r.state !== 'ready' && hasDocs(r)).sort(byName);
  const none = rows.filter((r) => !hasDocs(r)).sort(byName);
  const unwalked = index.unwalked ?? 0;
  const item = (row: DocsIndexRow): ReactNode => <li key={row.project}><IndexRow row={row} sameAs={sameAs(row)} /></li>;
  return (
    <div className="docs-index">
      <p className="docs-index-head">{DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.indexHead}</p>
      <input
        type="search" className="docs-filter" aria-label={DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.filterProjects} value={filter}
        onChange={(e) => setFilter(e.target.value)}
      />
      <ul className="docs-rows">{ready.map(item)}{rest.map(item)}</ul>
      {none.length > 0 && (
        <details className="docs-nodocs">
          <summary>{fillSentence(DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.noDocs, { n: none.length })}</summary>
          <ul className="docs-rows">{none.map(item)}</ul>
        </details>
      )}
      {index.unlisted > 0 && (
        <p className="docs-note">{fillSentence(DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.indexUnlisted, { n: index.unlisted, s: pluralS(index.unlisted) })}</p>
      )}
      {unwalked > 0 && (
        <p className="docs-note">{fillSentence(DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.indexUnwalked, { n: unwalked, s: pluralS(unwalked) })}</p>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```
