```tsx
// The Docs header (spec 2026-10-01 4.4's layout, 4.5; W5 part 1 Task 10): back (up one level, never
// `history.back()`: a deep link has no history), the crumbs (on a phone the last two behind a leading `…`), the truth
// line (the served ref, the short commit with copy commit, how the ref was chosen, a leaf's source, badge and size,
// and the freshness chip), the actions (View on GitHub, Open committed version) and "Updated to <short>". A pure
// renderer of the page, the visit and the tree answer: it starts no request, and the chip's tap is the visit's
// `refreshManual`. Every draft word is `entryView`'s through `ENTRY_BADGE_TEXT`, the one badge function the rows use
// too (M4.T7). Share and Export are W5 part 2's.
import { useState, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import {
  docsPageUrl, entryView, githubBlobUrl,
  type DocPin, type DocsPageLocation, type DocsTreeOk, type EntryBadge, type EntryMode, type GithubTarget,
} from '../../../shared/docs';
import { formatAge } from '../fleet/formatReset';
import { openExternal } from '../lib/markdown';
import { navigate } from '../lib/router';
import { useMediaQuery } from '../lib/useMediaQuery';
import { useNow } from '../lib/useNow';
import { docsLocation } from './docsLinks';
import {
  DOCS_HEAD_TEXT, ENTRY_BADGE_TEXT, GITHUB_REFUSAL_TEXT, RELATION_SENTENCE, VIA_SENTENCE,
  failureSentence, fillSentence, kib, servedRefText, shortCommit, slotSentence, worktreeLabel,
} from './docsText';
import { SECTION_LABEL, docsPathKind } from './docsTree';
import { DocsPageLink } from './DocsTreeView';
import type { DocsNotOk } from './failures';
import { copyText } from './share';
import { pinFor, type DocsVisit, type Freshness } from './useDocsVisit';

type Leaf = DocsPageLocation & { kind: 'path' };
type TreePage = Exclude<DocsPageLocation, { kind: 'index' }>;

const SEP = ' · ';
/** `sourceDraft` after its `{badge}`, so a draft source can draw its badge as the `.docs-badge` the rows draw. */
const SOURCE_DRAFT_TAIL = DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.sourceDraft.slice(DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.sourceDraft.indexOf('{badge}') + '{badge}'.length);

function modeOf(page: DocsPageLocation): EntryMode {
  return page.kind !== 'index' && page.ref !== null ? 'ref' : 'default';
}

function notOkSentence(answer: DocsNotOk): string {
  return answer.s === 'failed' ? failureSentence(answer.body) : slotSentence(answer);
}

/** Where back goes (spec 4.4: "up one level"): a leaf or a directory to its parent directory or its section, a
 *  section to its project, a project to the index, the index to the fleet (`/`). The page's ref is kept; `view` is
 *  dropped. */
export function docsUpHref(page: DocsPageLocation): string {
  switch (page.kind) {
    case 'index':
      return '/';
    case 'project':
      return docsPageUrl(docsLocation(page, { kind: 'index' }));
    case 'section':
      return docsPageUrl(docsLocation(page, { kind: 'project' }));
    case 'path': {
      const cut = page.path.lastIndexOf('/');
      return docsPageUrl(docsLocation(page, cut < 0
        ? { kind: 'section', section: page.section }
        : { kind: 'path', section: page.section, path: page.path.slice(0, cut), dirSlash: true }));
    }
  }
}

/** One crumb: its label and the page it links. The last crumb is the page itself (rendered, not linked). */
export interface DocsCrumb { readonly label: string; readonly href: string }

/** The crumbs from the index down to `page`, each keeping the page's ref (refinement (q)). */
export function docsCrumbs(page: DocsPageLocation): DocsCrumb[] {
  const crumbs: DocsCrumb[] = [{ label: DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.index, href: docsPageUrl(docsLocation(page, { kind: 'index' })) }];
  if (page.kind === 'index') return crumbs;
  crumbs.push({ label: page.project, href: docsPageUrl(docsLocation(page, { kind: 'project' })) });
  if (page.kind === 'project') return crumbs;
  crumbs.push({ label: SECTION_LABEL[page.section], href: docsPageUrl(docsLocation(page, { kind: 'section', section: page.section })) });
  if (page.kind === 'section') return crumbs;
  const parts = page.path.split('/');
  parts.forEach((label, i) => {
    const last = i === parts.length - 1;
    const to = { kind: 'path', section: page.section, path: parts.slice(0, i + 1).join('/'), dirSlash: last ? page.dirSlash : true } as const;
    crumbs.push({ label, href: docsPageUrl(docsLocation(page, to)) });
  });
  return crumbs;
}

/** What View on GitHub points at (spec 3.11, 4.4): the repository root on a project page, the section, the
 *  directory, or the leaf (`uncommitted` when its entry has no committed side). Null has one meaning: the page has no
 *  GitHub counterpart (the index, or a path this listing does not hold). */
export function githubTargetFor(page: DocsPageLocation, tree: DocsTreeOk): GithubTarget | null {
  switch (page.kind) {
    case 'index':
      return null;
    case 'project':
      return { kind: 'root' };
    case 'section':
      return { kind: 'section', section: page.section };
    case 'path': {
      const k = docsPathKind(tree, page.section, page.path, modeOf(page));
      if (k.kind === 'leaf') return { kind: 'leaf', section: page.section, path: page.path, uncommitted: k.entry.committed === null };
      return k.kind === 'dir' ? { kind: 'dir', section: page.section, path: page.path } : null;
    }
  }
}

/** A leaf's source (spec 4.5). `badge` null on a draft: the opened draft pin's entry no longer opens a draft in
 *  this tree (the pin outlived a re-list); `worktreePath` null: the drafts are no longer held by one worktree. */
type LeafSource =
  | { readonly kind: 'none' }
  | { readonly kind: 'committed'; readonly viewCommitted: boolean }
  | { readonly kind: 'draft'; readonly badge: EntryBadge | null; readonly label: string; readonly worktreePath: string | null };

function leafSource(tree: DocsTreeOk, page: Leaf, opened: DocPin | null): LeafSource {
  if (opened === null) return { kind: 'none' };
  if (opened.kind === 'committed') return { kind: 'committed', viewCommitted: page.view === 'committed' };
  const d = tree.drafts;
  const e = tree.entries.find((x) => x.section === page.section && x.path === page.path);
  const badge = e === undefined ? null : entryView(e, d, modeOf(page)).badge;
  return d.state === 'holder'
    ? { kind: 'draft', badge, label: worktreeLabel(d.worktree), worktreePath: d.worktree.path }
    : { kind: 'draft', badge, label: opened.branch, worktreePath: null };
}

function badgeText(badge: EntryBadge | null): string {
  return badge === null ? DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.sourceDraftUnbadged : ENTRY_BADGE_TEXT[badge];
}

/** The truth line's source for a leaf (spec 4.5): `committed`, `committed (view=committed)`, or
 *  `draft · <state> in <worktree label>`. `opened` is the pin the leaf opened; null = nothing opened yet (or nothing
 *  to open), which reads "nothing opened". */
export function truthSource(tree: DocsTreeOk, page: Leaf, opened: DocPin | null): string {
  const s = leafSource(tree, page, opened);
  switch (s.kind) {
    case 'none':
      return DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.sourceNone;
    case 'committed':
      return s.viewCommitted ? DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.sourceViewCommitted : DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.sourceCommitted;
    case 'draft':
      return fillSentence(DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.sourceDraft, { badge: badgeText(s.badge), label: s.label });
  }
}

/** The freshness chip's `data-state` (spec 4.5's table). */
export type FreshChipState = 'none' | 'never' | 'ok' | 'local' | 'failed' | 'fetching' | 'soon';

/** The freshness chip (spec 4.5), from the tree's own facts and the visit's refresh state. Ages are
 *  `attemptAgeMs + (now - receivedAt)` (and `okAgeMs` likewise), in `formatAge`'s words; an answer this visit got is
 *  aged from when it landed. */
export function freshnessChip(
  tree: DocsTreeOk, receivedAt: number, freshness: Freshness, now: number,
): { readonly state: FreshChipState; readonly text: string } {
  const f = tree.freshness;
  const aged = (ms: number): string => formatAge(Math.floor((ms + Math.max(0, now - receivedAt)) / 1000));
  const okAge = f.stamp === null || f.stamp.okAgeMs === null ? DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.freshNeverGood : aged(f.stamp.okAgeMs);
  if (f.remote === null) return { state: 'none', text: DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.freshNone };
  switch (freshness.s) {
    case 'fetching':
      return { state: 'fetching', text: DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.freshFetching };
    case 'soon':
      return {
        state: 'soon',
        text: fillSentence(DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.freshSoon, { n: Math.max(0, Math.ceil((freshness.retryAt - now) / 1000)) }),
      };
    case 'stale-lock':
      return {
        state: 'failed',
        text: freshness.ref === null ? DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.freshStaleLockUnnamed : fillSentence(DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.freshStaleLock, { ref: freshness.ref }),
      };
    case 'relist-failed':
      return { state: 'failed', text: fillSentence(DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.freshRelistFailed, { sentence: notOkSentence(freshness.answer) }) };
    case 'refresh-failed':
      return { state: 'failed', text: fillSentence(DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.freshRefreshFailed, { sentence: notOkSentence(freshness.answer) }) };
    case 'answered':
      if (freshness.fetch.state === 'skipped') return { state: 'local', text: DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.freshLocalRef };
      if (freshness.fetch.state === 'failed') {
        const age = formatAge(Math.floor(Math.max(0, now - freshness.at) / 1000));
        return {
          state: 'failed',
          text: fillSentence(DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.freshFailed, { age, sentence: failureSentence(freshness.fetch.failure), okAge }),
        };
      }
      break;
    case 'idle':
      break;
  }
  const stamp = f.stamp;
  if (stamp === null) return { state: 'never', text: DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.freshNever };
  if (stamp.lastOutcome === 'ok') return { state: 'ok', text: fillSentence(DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.freshOk, { age: aged(stamp.attemptAgeMs) }) };
  if (stamp.lastOutcome === 'remote-branch-absent') return { state: 'local', text: DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.freshLocalOnly };
  const sentence = failureSentence({ ok: false, failure: stamp.lastOutcome });
  return { state: 'failed', text: fillSentence(DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.freshFailed, { age: aged(stamp.attemptAgeMs), sentence, okAge }) };
}

/** The crumbs (spec 4.4's layout): every crumb on a desktop; on a phone (under 900 px) the last two behind a leading
 *  `…` button, which shows them all. The last crumb is the page itself. */
function Crumbs(p: { readonly crumbs: readonly DocsCrumb[] }): ReactNode {
  const desktop = useMediaQuery('(min-width: 900px)');
  const [whole, setWhole] = useState(false);
  const folded = !desktop && !whole && p.crumbs.length > 2;
  const shown = folded ? p.crumbs.slice(-2) : p.crumbs;
  return (
    <nav className="docs-crumbs" aria-label={DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.crumbs}>
      <ol>
        {folded && (
          <li>
            <button type="button" className="docs-crumbs-more" aria-label={DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.crumbsMore} onClick={() => setWhole(true)}>
              …
            </button>
          </li>
        )}
        {shown.map((c, i) => (
          <li key={c.href}>
            {i === shown.length - 1
              ? <span className="docs-crumb-here" aria-current="page">{c.label}</span>
              : <DocsPageLink className="docs-crumb" href={c.href}>{c.label}</DocsPageLink>}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ol>
    </nav>
  );
}

/** "copy commit" (spec 4.5): the FULL commit, through `copyText`, the one clipboard writer under `pwa/src/docs`. */
function CopyCommit(p: { readonly commit: string }): ReactNode {
  const [said, setSaid] = useState<'copied' | 'failed' | null>(null);
  const onClick = (): void => {
    setSaid(null);
    void copyText(p.commit).then(() => setSaid('copied'), () => setSaid('failed'));
  };
  return (
    <>
      <button type="button" className="docs-copy" onClick={onClick}>{DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.copyCommit}</button>
      {said !== null && (
        <span className="docs-copy-said" role="status">{said === 'copied' ? DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.copied : DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.copyFailed}</span>
      )}
    </>
  );
}

/** The freshness chip: a `<button>` whose tap is one manual refresh, disabled while one runs; static text when the
 *  repository has no origin. */
function FreshChip(p: { readonly chip: ReturnType<typeof freshnessChip>; readonly onRefresh: () => void }): ReactNode {
  const { chip } = p;
  if (chip.state === 'none') return <span className="docs-fresh" data-state="none">{chip.text}</span>;
  return (
    <button type="button" className="docs-fresh" data-state={chip.state} disabled={chip.state === 'fetching'} onClick={p.onRefresh}>
      {chip.text}
    </button>
  );
}

/** The truth line (spec 4.5), facts inline joined by ` · `. */
function TruthLine(p: {
  readonly page: TreePage; readonly visit: DocsVisit; readonly tree: DocsTreeOk; readonly receivedAt: number;
  readonly now: number;
}): ReactNode {
  const { page, visit, tree } = p;
  const ref = tree.ref;
  const withRelation = ref.via === 'local' || ref.via === 'origin' || ref.via === 'qualified';
  const c = ref.counterpart;
  const counts: Record<string, number> = {};
  if (c !== null && c.ahead !== null) counts['ahead'] = c.ahead;
  if (c !== null && c.behind !== null) counts['behind'] = c.behind;
  let leaf: ReactNode = null;
  if (page.kind === 'path') {
    const k = docsPathKind(tree, page.section, page.path, modeOf(page));
    if (k.kind === 'leaf') {
      const file = visit.file;
      const opened = file.s === 'none' ? pinFor(tree, page) : file.pin;
      const s = leafSource(tree, page, opened);
      const source = s.kind === 'draft'
        ? (
          <span className="docs-truth-source" title={s.worktreePath ?? undefined}>
            {s.badge === null ? DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.sourceDraftUnbadged : <span className="docs-badge">{ENTRY_BADGE_TEXT[s.badge]}</span>}
            {fillSentence(SOURCE_DRAFT_TAIL, { label: s.label })}
          </span>
        )
        : <span className="docs-truth-source">{truthSource(tree, page, opened)}</span>;
      leaf = (
        <>
          {SEP}{source}
          {k.view.badge !== null && s.kind !== 'draft' && <>{SEP}<span className="docs-badge">{ENTRY_BADGE_TEXT[k.view.badge]}</span></>}
          {file.s === 'ok' && <>{SEP}<span className="docs-truth-size">{kib(file.answer.show.size)}</span></>}
        </>
      );
    }
  }
  return (
    <p className="docs-truth">
      <span className="docs-truth-ref" title={ref.served}>{servedRefText(ref)}</span>{SEP}
      <code className="docs-truth-commit" title={ref.commit}>{shortCommit(ref.commit)}</code>{' '}
      <CopyCommit commit={ref.commit} />{SEP}
      <span className="docs-truth-via">{fillSentence(VIA_SENTENCE[ref.via], ref.requested === null ? {} : { requested: ref.requested })}</span>
      {withRelation && (
        <>
          {SEP}
          <span className="docs-truth-relation" data-tone={ref.relation === 'diverged' ? 'warn' : 'info'}>
            {fillSentence(RELATION_SENTENCE[ref.relation], counts)}
          </span>
        </>
      )}
      {ref.tried[0]?.result === 'dangling' && <>{SEP}<span className="docs-truth-dangling">{DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.danglingHead}</span></>}
      {leaf}
      {SEP}
      <FreshChip chip={freshnessChip(tree, p.receivedAt, visit.freshness, p.now)} onRefresh={visit.refreshManual} />
    </p>
  );
}

/** View on GitHub (spec 3.11, opened with `openExternal` on tap), with its may-differ note, or its refusal in words. */
function GithubAction(p: { readonly tree: DocsTreeOk; readonly target: GithubTarget }): ReactNode {
  const link = githubBlobUrl(p.tree.github, p.tree.ref, p.target);
  if (!link.ok) {
    return <span className="docs-action-off">{fillSentence(DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.githubOff, { reason: GITHUB_REFUSAL_TEXT[link.why] })}</span>;
  }
  return (
    <>
      <a className="docs-action" href={link.url} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" onClick={(e) => openExternal(e, link.url)}>
        {DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.github}
      </a>
      {link.note === 'may-differ' && <span className="docs-action-note">{DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.githubMayDiffer}</span>}
    </>
  );
}

/** The actions (spec 4.5): View on GitHub, and Open committed version, offered iff `entryView(...).offersCommitted`
 *  on a leaf not already at `view=committed`. It navigates with a history entry (URL state, so Back returns to the
 *  draft); the commit never enters the URL, it is resolved from this visit's tree. */
function Actions(p: { readonly page: TreePage; readonly tree: DocsTreeOk }): ReactNode {
  const { page, tree } = p;
  const target = githubTargetFor(page, tree);
  let committedHref: string | null = null;
  if (page.kind === 'path' && page.view !== 'committed') {
    const k = docsPathKind(tree, page.section, page.path, modeOf(page));
    if (k.kind === 'leaf' && k.view.offersCommitted) {
      const to = { kind: 'path', section: page.section, path: page.path, dirSlash: false, view: 'committed' } as const;
      committedHref = docsPageUrl(docsLocation(page, to));
    }
  }
  if (target === null && committedHref === null) return null;
  return (
    <div className="docs-actions">
      {target !== null && <GithubAction tree={tree} target={target} />}
      {committedHref !== null && <DocsPageLink className="docs-action" href={committedHref}>{DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.openCommitted}</DocsPageLink>}
    </div>
  );
}

/** The Docs header. `tree` null has one meaning: the visit's tree slot is not `ok` (loading, failed, or the page names
 *  no project), so the header is back and the crumbs only (spec 4.7: a tree failure keeps the crumbs). */
export function DocsHead(p: { readonly page: DocsPageLocation; readonly visit: DocsVisit; readonly tree: DocsTreeOk | null }): ReactNode {
  const { page, visit, tree } = p;
  const now = useNow(30_000, tree !== null);
  const crumbs = docsCrumbs(page);
  const slot = visit.tree;
  const receivedAt = slot?.s === 'ok' ? slot.receivedAt : now;
  return (
    <header className="docs-head">
      <div className="docs-head-bar">
        <button type="button" className="docs-back" aria-label={DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.back} onClick={() => navigate(docsUpHref(page))}>
          ‹
        </button>
        <Crumbs key={crumbs.at(-1)?.href} crumbs={crumbs} />
      </div>
      {tree !== null && page.kind !== 'index' && (
        <>
          <TruthLine page={page} visit={visit} tree={tree} receivedAt={receivedAt} now={now} />
          <Actions page={page} tree={tree} />
        </>
      )}
      {visit.updatedTo !== null && (
        <p className="docs-updated" role="status">{fillSentence(DOCS_HEAD_TEXT.updatedTo, { short: shortCommit(visit.updatedTo) })}</p>
      )}
    </header>
  );
}
```

- [ ] **Step 6: The banners.** Create `pwa/src/docs/DocsBanners.tsx` with exactly:

```tsx
// The Docs banners (spec 2026-10-01 4.5's table; W5 part 1 Task 10): under the header, on every page with a listing,
// what the page does NOT show and why. The default view never overlays a draft, so its hint links the same page at
// the QUALIFIED `refs/heads/<branch>` (a bare name could serve origin and overlay nothing); a ref view overlays only
// when the holder's HEAD is the served commit, and otherwise says what the drafts are based on; each drafts state that
// shows none says why; a leaf's withheld, deleted, type-changed and conflicted drafts come from `entryView` (never a
// read of the draft's own state, M4.T7); a commit the branch no longer contains offers Re-list; drafted images are
// counted; `view=committed` offers the way back. A pure renderer: it starts no request (Retry and Re-list call
// `onRelist`), and every link is `docsPageUrl(docsLocation(page, to))` (refinement (q)).
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { docsPageUrl, parseDocsRef, type DocsPageLocation, type DocsTreeOk } from '../../../shared/docs';
import { docsLocation } from './docsLinks';
import {
  DOCS_BANNER_TEXT, DOCS_VIEW_TEXT, WITHHELD_SENTENCE, fillSentence, pluralS, servedRefText, shortCommit, worktreeLabel,
} from './docsText';
import { docsPathKind } from './docsTree';
import { DocsPageLink } from './DocsTreeView';
import type { FileSlot } from './useDocsVisit';

type Tone = 'info' | 'warn';

function Banner(p: { readonly id: string; readonly tone: Tone; readonly text: string; readonly children?: ReactNode }): ReactNode {
  return (
    <div className="docs-banner" data-banner={p.id} data-tone={p.tone} role="status">
      <span className="docs-banner-text">{p.text}</span>
      {p.children}
    </div>
  );
}

function RelistButton(p: { readonly label: string; readonly onRelist: () => void }): ReactNode {
  return <>{' '}<button type="button" className="btn-ghost docs-banner-action" onClick={p.onRelist}>{p.label}</button></>;
}

function HintLink(p: { readonly href: string | null; readonly label: string }): ReactNode {
  return p.href === null ? null : <>{' '}<DocsPageLink className="docs-hint-link" href={p.href}>{p.label}</DocsPageLink></>;
}

/** The banners for `page` over `tree`. `file` is the visit's file slot (only a leaf's `ok` answer is read, for
 *  `onRef`); `draftAssets` counts the drafted images on the page; `onRelist` is the visit's `retryTree`. The index
 *  has none. */
export function DocsBanners(p: {
  readonly page: DocsPageLocation; readonly tree: DocsTreeOk; readonly file: FileSlot; readonly draftAssets: number;
  readonly onRelist: () => void;
}): ReactNode {
  const { page, tree, file, draftAssets, onRelist } = p;
  if (page.kind === 'index') return null;
  const mode = page.ref === null ? 'default' : 'ref';
  const d = tree.drafts;
  const out: ReactNode[] = [];
  // `n` counts entries with a draft at all (spec 4.5), whatever the overlay would make of each.
  const n = tree.entries.filter((e) => e.draft !== null).length;

  switch (d.state) {
    case 'holder': {
      const label = worktreeLabel(d.worktree);
      const localRef = parseDocsRef('refs/heads/' + d.branch);
      const localHref = localRef === null ? null
        : docsPageUrl(docsLocation(page, { kind: 'same-page', project: page.project, ref: localRef }));
      if (mode === 'default' && n > 0) {
        out.push(
          <Banner key="default-hint" id="default-hint" tone="info"
            text={fillSentence(DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.defaultHint, { n, s: pluralS(n), label, branch: d.branch })}>
            <HintLink href={localHref} label={DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.openDraftView} />
          </Banner>,
        );
      }
      if (mode === 'ref' && !d.baseEqual && n > 0) {
        const text = fillSentence(DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.baseHint, {
          n, s: pluralS(n), label, branch: d.branch, short: shortCommit(d.worktree.head), served: servedRefText(tree.ref),
        });
        out.push(
          <Banner key="base-hint" id="base-hint" tone="info" text={text}>
            <HintLink href={localHref} label={DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.openLocalView} />
          </Banner>,
        );
      }
      if (d.caveats.includes('assume-unchanged') || d.caveats.includes('skip-worktree')) {
        out.push(<Banner key="caveat-hash" id="caveat-hash" tone="info" text={DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.caveatHash} />);
      }
      if (d.caveats.includes('filters-bypassed')) {
        out.push(<Banner key="caveat-filters" id="caveat-filters" tone="info" text={DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.caveatFilters} />);
      }
      break;
    }
    case 'ambiguous':
      out.push(
        <Banner key="ambiguous" id="ambiguous" tone="warn" text={fillSentence(DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.ambiguous, { branch: d.branch })}>
          <ul className="docs-banner-list">{d.candidates.map((c) => <li key={c}>{c}</li>)}</ul>
        </Banner>,
      );
      break;
    case 'untrusted':
      out.push(
        <Banner key="untrusted" id="untrusted" tone="warn"
          text={fillSentence(DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.untrusted, { branch: d.branch, why: d.why })} />,
      );
      break;
    case 'unreadable':
      out.push(<Banner key="unreadable" id="unreadable" tone="warn" text={fillSentence(DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.unreadable, { step: d.step })} />);
      break;
    case 'unsettled':
      out.push(
        <Banner key="unsettled" id="unsettled" tone="info" text={DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.unsettled}>
          <RelistButton label={DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.retry} onRelist={onRelist} />
        </Banner>,
      );
      break;
    case 'too-many':
      out.push(<Banner key="too-many" id="too-many" tone="info" text={fillSentence(DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.tooMany, { count: d.count })} />);
      break;
    case 'none':
      if (d.skipped.length > 0) {
        const why = [...new Set(d.skipped.map((x) => x.why))].join(', ');
        out.push(
          <Banner key="skipped" id="skipped" tone="info"
            text={fillSentence(DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.skipped, { k: d.skipped.length, branch: d.branch, why })} />,
        );
      }
      break;
  }

  if (page.kind === 'path') {
    const k = docsPathKind(tree, page.section, page.path, mode);
    if (k.kind === 'leaf') {
      const v = k.view;
      const label = d.state === 'holder' ? worktreeLabel(d.worktree) : d.branch;
      // "Showing the committed version." only when the page does show one (a withheld NEW file has none).
      const showing = (s: string): string => (v.opens === 'committed' ? s + ' ' + DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.showingCommitted : s);
      if (v.badge === 'withheld' && v.withheld !== null) {
        out.push(<Banner key="withheld" id="withheld" tone="info" text={showing(WITHHELD_SENTENCE[v.withheld])} />);
      }
      if (v.badge === 'deleted') {
        out.push(<Banner key="deleted" id="deleted" tone="info" text={showing(fillSentence(DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.deleted, { label }))} />);
      }
      if (v.badge === 'typechange') {
        out.push(<Banner key="typechange" id="typechange" tone="info" text={showing(fillSentence(DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.typechange, { label }))} />);
      }
      if (v.badge === 'conflicted') out.push(<Banner key="conflicted" id="conflicted" tone="warn" text={DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.conflicted} />);
      if (file.s === 'ok' && file.answer.show.onRef === 'not-contained') {
        const short = shortCommit(file.answer.show.commit ?? tree.ref.commit);
        out.push(
          <Banner key="not-contained" id="not-contained" tone="warn"
            text={fillSentence(DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.notContained, { short, served: servedRefText(tree.ref) })}>
            <RelistButton label={DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.relist} onRelist={onRelist} />
          </Banner>,
        );
      }
      if (draftAssets > 0) {
        out.push(
          <Banner key="draft-assets" id="draft-assets" tone="info"
            text={fillSentence(DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.draftAssets, { k: draftAssets, s: pluralS(draftAssets) })} />,
        );
      }
      if (page.view === 'committed') {
        const to = { kind: 'path', section: page.section, path: page.path, dirSlash: false, view: 'effective' } as const;
        out.push(
          <Banner key="view-committed" id="view-committed" tone="info"
            text={fillSentence(DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.viewCommitted, { short: shortCommit(tree.ref.commit) })}>
            <HintLink href={docsPageUrl(docsLocation(page, to))} label={DOCS_BANNER_TEXT.backToDraft} />
          </Banner>,
        );
      }
    }
  }
  return out.length === 0 ? null : <div className="docs-banners">{out}</div>;
}
```

```tsx
/** A path the tree answer does not list (spec 4.4): "Not in this listing at <short commit>", and, in the default view
 *  of a holder whose worktree has a draft at or under the path, the hint with **Open the draft view** linking this
 *  page at `refs/heads/<drafts.branch>`. */
function MissingPage(p: { readonly tree: DocsTreeOk; readonly page: DocsPageLocation & { kind: 'path' } }): ReactNode {
  const { tree, page } = p;
  const drafts = tree.drafts;
  const under = page.path + '/';
  const drafted = page.ref === null && drafts.state === 'holder' && tree.entries.some((e) =>
    e.section === page.section && (e.path === page.path || e.path.startsWith(under))
    && e.draft !== null && e.draft.state !== 'deleted');
  const draftRef = drafts.state === 'holder' ? parseDocsRef('refs/heads/' + drafts.branch) : null;
  return (
    <div className="docs-missing">
      <p className="docs-note">{fillSentence(DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.missing, { short: shortCommit(tree.ref.commit) })}</p>
      {drafted && drafts.state === 'holder' && draftRef !== null && (
        <p className="docs-note">
          {fillSentence(DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.missingDraftHint, { branch: drafts.branch })}{' '}
          <DocsPageLink
            className="docs-hint-link"
            href={docsPageUrl(docsLocation(page, { kind: 'same-page', project: page.project, ref: draftRef }))}
          >
            {DOCS_VIEW_TEXT.openDraftView}
          </DocsPageLink>
        </p>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

```

```tsx
}
```

Class names on the two surfaces this task adds: `docs-door`, `docs-door-glyph` (FleetScreen), `docs-session-row` (with `btn-ghost`, the actions sheet), `docs-menu-item` (with `menu-item`, the session menu). Every `null` above has the one meaning stated beside it.

**Decisions this task makes** (each pinned by a case below; refinements, not deviations: each fills a silence or resolves a conflict between two spec sentences without contradicting either's text):

1. **The registry is `INHERITED_GROUNDS`, with a `why` per entry.** Spec 4.14 says "registered in `design/audit.mjs` `GROUNDS` with a `why`, following `.settings-*`"; the `.settings-*` entries it cites are `INHERITED_GROUNDS` entries (`GROUNDS` holds a rule whose own background is translucent; `INHERITED_GROUNDS` a rule that paints none, which is every unpainted docs rule). Twenty entries, all on `--bg-page`: `.docs-screen`, `.shell-detail` and every view inside paint nothing, so body's `--bg-page` is behind them (the `.settings-back` reasoning). The door's second ground is measured in `contrast.test.ts` off the rule's own ink, as `.settings-door`'s is.
2. **What paints its own ground is measured with no entry.** `.docs-banner` (and its `warn` variant), `.docs-fail`, `.docs-fail .docs-fail-detail`, `.docs-badge`, `.docs-filter`, `.doc-img-chip` and `.docs-row:active` set a colour and an opaque ground, so the audit measures each on it; the failure view's coloured parts name `.docs-fail` and are measured through it (the named-ancestor route). Links (`.docs-action`, `.docs-hint-link`, `.docs-owner-link`, `.docs-fail-suggest a`) take `color: inherit`, which is not a colour of their own: they read in their container's measured ink. A class the spec lists that no colour rule styles (`.doc-plain`, `.docs-crumb-here`) inherits the body's measured ink and needs no entry; `.msg-plain` is W4's and already registered. Measured at planning: the gate goes from `ALL 640 PASS` to `ALL 698 PASS`, the docs sheet adds no `uncovered` key and no `problems`, every docs pair clears its floor (lowest: `--status-attention-text` on `--status-attention-tint`, 4.94 light, the badge).
3. **The menu item rides `.menu-item`'s own floor.** Spec 4.8 makes it a `menu-item` and 4.14 asks for a scrape of `min-height: var(--tap-min)`; `.menu-item` (in `session/chat.css`, which part 1 may not edit) floors at `52px`, above the 44 px token. A docs rule restating `var(--tap-min)` on it would LOWER the item below its siblings. So its scrape half asserts `.menu-item`'s floor is the token or at least the token's value, and that `docs.css` has no rule for `.docs-menu-item` (nothing here can lower it). The actions sheet's row rides `.btn-ghost`'s own `min-height: var(--tap-min)` (`components/primitives.css`) the same way; `docs.css` has no rule for `.docs-session-row`.
4. **Every Docs control gets both halves, not only the spec's list:** the door, back, crumb and `…`, row (section and index), filter, the no-docs fold's summary, the index's owner link, chip, copy commit, View on GitHub, both banner actions (Retry, the hint link), the failure view's Retry and Fetch from origin, a leaf's Source and Download, the gate's two buttons, the plain text's Retry, Load image, Open image externally, an image, the sheet row and the menu item. Each floor is in its own rule in `docs.css` (grouped selector lists count: `ruleIn` finds a selector inside one), and the token loop's list gains one rule per group.
5. **The door copies `.settings-door`'s box** (the `--tap-min` floor, `background: none`, `--ink-secondary`, the mono `--text-2xs` font, the `:active` scale to `--ink-primary`) with `gap: var(--sp-1)` for `.settings-door`'s literal `5px`, so the door's rule spells no length that is not a token or a hairline. (docs.css elsewhere spells a few literal lengths, as chat.css does: `2px` and `3px` rules and a `12em` measure; spec §4.14's "tokens only" is about colours.) It renders unconditionally (the index lists every project), and the head still wraps (`settings-screen.test.tsx`'s pins, unedited).
6. **The session row sits right after Restart's notes, before Swap account** (the notes are Restart's own sentences, so a row between them would split them), and the menu item after History. The row closes the sheet first, then navigates (spec 4.8: "`onClose()` then `navigate`"); the item goes through `menuAct`, which closes the menu first.
7. **`sessionDocsHref` builds through `docsLocation`** (refinement (q)): the default view is `docsLocation({kind: 'index'}, {kind: 'default-view', project})` and the branch view applies Task 9's `same-page` target with `{kind: 'bare', name: branch}`, so no `DocsPageLocation` literal is written here either. A branch outside the bare grammar (`HEAD`, `refs/heads/main`, `a..b`, `x y`, `main.lock`) links the default view rather than a page that would only fail to parse. The answer type is named (`SessionDocsLink`), with the architecture's exact shape.
8. **The text-scan guards say what they do not see** (lesson 8): the one-builder scan over the two callers, the literal-colour scan over `docs.css`, the two-import scan behind the built stylesheet and the `.shell-detail` reader each carry "NOT EXHAUSTIVE" and their evasions in their own comment; each has a behaviour case or a planted control beside it.
9. **The built stylesheet is checked by a step, as the architecture names it** (vitest runs `css: false`, so no in-process test can see `docs.css` at all). It builds Task 11's staged tree for production in a scratch copy and counts the door, its pressed state, the chip's states and the `.doc-body`-scoped rules in the one emitted `index-*.css`; Task 14's gate repeats it. Measured at planning: Task 10's tree, and this task's tree without DocsScreen's `import '../docs/docs.css';`, both emit 140 862 bytes with none of them; this task's tree emits 149 849 bytes with all of them. In-process, `tap-targets.test.tsx` pins the two imports the bundle rests on (DocsScreen imports `docs.css`; `app.tsx` imports DocsScreen statically).

```tsx
/** The actions sheet's Docs row for `session`, clicked; answers where it navigated and what `onClose` saw. */
function viaSheet(session: FleetSession): { href: string; closedAt: string | null } {
  let closedAt: string | null = null;
  render(<SessionActionsSheet session={session} open onClose={() => { closedAt = here(); }} onReap={() => {}} />);
  const row = document.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('.docs-session-row');
  expect(row, 'the sheet has a Docs row').not.toBeNull();
  fireEvent.click(row!);
  const href = here();
  cleanup();
  history.replaceState(null, '', '/');
  return { href, closedAt };
}

  fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Docs' }));
  const href = here();

  history.replaceState(null, '', '/');
```

```tsx
// ── native Docs reader W5 part 1, Task 11: the Docs door (design 2026-10-01 section 4.8, M4.L1) ───────────────
//
// The `/settings` door's twin above, with its placement pinned too: immediately before `.accounts-door` in the
// header's control cluster, with the word beside an aria-hidden glyph, rendered whether or not the fleet has a
// session. Its two tap-target halves live in tap-targets.test.tsx. The file-level afterEach does not reset the route.
describe('the Docs door (docs design 4.8, M4.L1)', () => {
  afterEach(() => navigate('/'));

  it('sits in the fleet header immediately before the accounts door, says Docs, and routes to /docs', () => {
    render(<FleetScreen store={makeStore()} />);
    const door = screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Docs: specs, plans and design notes' });
    expect(door).toHaveClass('docs-door');
    expect(door.parentElement).toHaveClass('fleet-head-right');
    expect(door.nextElementSibling).toHaveClass('accounts-door');
    const words = [...door.childNodes].filter((n) => n.nodeType === Node.TEXT_NODE).map((n) => n.textContent?.trim()).join('');
    expect(words).toBe('Docs');
    expect(door.querySelector('.docs-door-glyph')?.getAttribute('aria-hidden')).toBe('true');
    fireEvent.click(door);
    expect(location.pathname).toBe('/docs');
  });

  it('renders with no sessions at all', () => {
    const store = makeStore();
    render(<FleetScreen store={store} />);
    act(() => { store.setState({ conn: 'open', sessions: [] }); });
    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Docs: specs, plans and design notes' })).toHaveClass('docs-door');
  });
});
```

```ts
// ── native Docs reader W5 part 1, Task 11: the Docs door and the Docs screen's chrome (M4.S1, its docs-chrome form) ──
// Every rule in docs/docs.css that sets a colour is measured in both themes, on the ground it paints itself, through
// a painted ancestor its selector names, or on a ground registered in INHERITED_GROUNDS with its reason; none joins
// the frozen census and none is grandfathered. The door has two grounds, as `.settings-door` does: registered on the
// page, and measured here on `.shell-nav`'s --bg-surface off the rule's own ink, so a retint re-measures both.
describe('the Docs chrome is measured, not left in the blind spot (M4.S1)', () => {
  const docsRules = rulesOf(ROOT, 'src/docs/docs.css');
  const NOT_A_COLOUR = /^(inherit|currentColor|unset|initial|revert)$/i;
  const colourRules = docsRules.filter((r) => {
    const ink = declOf(r.body, 'color');
    return ink !== null && !NOT_A_COLOUR.test(ink);
  });
  /** The measured rows of one rule: the rule as a pair of its own (painted, or registered), or as a descendant
   *  measured through the painter its selector names. */
  const rowsOf = (key: string): typeof report.measured => report.measured.filter((m) => {
    const label = m.label.replace(/^(DARK|LIGHT)\s+/, '');
    return label === key || label.startsWith(`${key} [in `);
  });
  const inkOf = (key: string): string => {
    const rule = docsRules.find((r) => ruleKey(r) === key);
    expect(rule, key).toBeDefined();
    const ink = declOf((rule as { body: string }).body, 'color');
    expect(ink, key).not.toBeNull();
    return ink as string;
  };

  it('finds the sheet and its colour rules (not a vacuous pass)', () => {
    expect(report.sheets).toContain('src/docs/docs.css');
    expect(colourRules.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(28);
  });

  it('measures every docs rule that sets a colour in both themes, at or above its floor', () => {
    for (const r of colourRules) {
      const key = ruleKey(r);
      expect(report.uncovered, key).not.toContain(key);
      const rows = rowsOf(key);
      expect(rows.map((m) => m.label.split(/\s+/)[0]).sort(), key).toEqual(['DARK', 'LIGHT']);
      for (const row of rows) expect(row.ratio, row.label).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(row.floor);
    }
  });

  it('grandfathers nothing from docs.css, and every docs registration is on the page with a reason', () => {
    expect([...GRANDFATHERED_UNCOVERED].filter((k) => k.startsWith('docs.css '))).toEqual([]);
    const registered = Object.entries(INHERITED_GROUNDS).filter(([k]) => k.startsWith('docs.css '));
    expect(registered.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(20);
    for (const [key, entry] of registered) {
      expect(entry.under, key).toEqual(['var(--bg-page)']);
      expect(entry.why.length, key).toBeGreaterThan(40);
      expect(docsRules.some((r) => ruleKey(r) === key), key).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  it.each([
    ['docs.css .docs-door'],
    ['docs.css .docs-door:active'],
  ])('%s is registered on the page and also clears AA on the desktop sidebar it sits on', (key) => {
    expect(INHERITED_GROUNDS[key]?.under).toEqual(['var(--bg-page)']);
    for (const row of rowsOf(key)) expect(row.detail, row.label).toContain(`${inkOf(key)} on var(--bg-page)`);
    for (const theme of [DARK, LIGHT]) {
      expect(ratio(inkOf(key), ['var(--bg-surface)'], theme), key).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(4.5);
    }
  });

  // A text scan, NOT EXHAUSTIVE: it finds a hex colour, a colour function (`rgb(`, `rgba(`, `hsl(`, `hsla(`, `hwb(`,
  // `lab(`, `lch(`, `oklab(`, `oklch(`, `color(`) and the named colours listed below, outside comments. It does not
  // find a named colour missing from that list, a system colour (`Canvas`, `CanvasText`), or a colour that arrives
  // through an image or an `@property` initial value; `currentColor` and `transparent` are allowed on purpose.
  it('spells no literal colour (tokens only, section 4.14)', () => {
    const text = docsRules.map((r) => r.body).join(';');
    const NAMED = /:\s*[^;]*\b(black|white|red|green|blue|yellow|orange|purple|gray|grey|silver|maroon|navy|teal|olive|lime|aqua|fuchsia|pink|brown)\b/i;
    expect(text).not.toMatch(/#[0-9a-f]{3,8}\b/i);
    expect(text).not.toMatch(/(?<![\w-])(rgba?|hsla?|hwb|lab|lch|oklab|oklch|color)\(/i);
    expect(text).not.toMatch(NAMED);
  });
});
```

```tsx
// — native Docs reader W5 part 1, Task 11: the Docs door, the session links and the Docs screen's controls (spec
// 2026-10-01 4.8 and 4.14) —
//
// Both halves for each: the rule in docs/docs.css (or, for a control that rides a shared class, that class's own
// rule) holds `min-height: var(--tap-min)`, and a rendered element carries the class. The Docs screen renders with
// injected loaders and a parser that parses in this thread; nothing reaches a server. Placeholders only: project
// `demo`, branch `main`, `example-org/example-repo`, `https://a.example`.

const docsParser: MarkdownParser = async (src) => parseMarkdown(src, 'docs');

/** The Docs screen at `url`, as the app's docs arm mounts it. */
function openDocs(url: string, f: FakeLoaders, parser: MarkdownParser = docsParser): void {
  navigate(url);
  render(<DocsScreen path={location.pathname} search={location.search} loaders={f.loaders} parser={parser} />);
}

/** A markdown leaf `specs/a.md` whose text is `text`. */
function markdownLeaf(text: string, entries = [entry('specs', 'a.md')]): FakeLoaders {
  const r = fileResponse(text);
  return fakeLoaders({
    tree: okTree(treeOk({ entries })),
    file: { s: 'ok', value: { ...r, show: { ...r.show, size: text.length } } },
  });
}

const DOCS_INDEX: DocsProjectsResponse = {
  ok: true, cacheAgeMs: 0,
  index: {
    v: 1, verb: 'docs-index', ok: true, elapsedMs: 5, unlisted: 0, duplicates: [],
    projects: [
      { project: 'demo', state: 'ready', github: { state: 'none' },
        default: { name: 'main', via: 'default:origin-head', commit: 'a'.repeat(40) },
        sections: { specs: 1, plans: 1, 'product-design': 0, conventions: 0 } },
      { project: 'a', state: 'linked-worktree', github: { state: 'none' }, owner: 'demo', branch: 'main' },
      { project: 'b', state: 'ready', github: { state: 'none' },
        default: { name: 'main', via: 'default:origin-head', commit: 'b'.repeat(40) },
        sections: { specs: 0, plans: 0, 'product-design': 0, conventions: 0 } },
    ],
  },
};
```

```ts

// ── native Docs reader W5 part 1, Task 11: docs/docs.css leaves the pane alone (spec 2026-10-01 section 4.14) ──
// The Docs screen renders into the same detail pane, and the scroll contract above is shell.css's to keep: the Docs
// sheet declares NO overflow on `.shell-detail` in any spelling the reader sees (the shorthand, either longhand, any
// rule whose subject targets the pane, a compound or a descendant chain ending in it). It inherits every gap
// `declaredValues` lists in cssRule.ts, so it is NOT EXHAUSTIVE: a broader subject (`*`, `section`,
// `:where(.shell-detail)`) is not seen. A planted control proves the reader would see the regression in this sheet.
describe('docs/docs.css sets no overflow on .shell-detail (spec 4.14)', () => {
  const docsCss = readFileSync(path.join(import.meta.dirname, '..', 'src', 'docs', 'docs.css'), 'utf8');
  /** Every overflow value `css` declares on the pane; `[]` when no rule targets it at all (the expected state). */
  const paneOverflow = (css: string): string[] => {
    let found: string[] = [];
    try {
      found = ['overflow', 'overflow-x', 'overflow-y'].flatMap((prop) => declaredValues(css, '.shell-detail', prop));
    } catch (e) {
      if (!String(e).includes('no rule targeting .shell-detail')) throw e;
    }
    return found;
  };

  it('declares none', () => {
    expect(docsCss).toContain('.docs-screen');          // the real sheet, not an empty read
    expect(paneOverflow(docsCss)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it.each([
    '.shell-detail { overflow: hidden; }',
    '.app-shell .shell-detail { overflow-y: clip; }',
    'section.shell-detail { overflow-x: auto; }',
  ])('would see %s planted in it', (planted) => {
    expect(paneOverflow(`${docsCss}\n${planted}\n`)).not.toEqual([]);
  });
});
```

```ts
import type { Element as HastElement, Root as HastRoot, RootContent } from 'hast';
import { urlAttributes } from 'html-url-attributes';
```


Then append to the end of the file (after `imagePinFor`'s closing `}`, its last line):

```ts

/** A session's link into Docs (spec 4.8). `href`: the session's project at the branch its worktree holds NOW, written
 *  verbatim as `?ref=<branch>`, never the workspace slug (workspaces are renamed). `label`: the words both surfaces
 *  show. `branch`: the branch linked; null means the default view is linked, because the session reports no branch or
 *  one outside the bare grammar (and the string `null` never reaches a URL). */
export interface SessionDocsLink {
  readonly href: string;
  readonly label: string;
  readonly branch: string | null;
}

/** THE one builder of a session's link into Docs: `SessionActionsSheet`'s row and `SessionHeader`'s menu item both
 *  call it, and neither builds a Docs URL of its own. It reads `s.project`, never `boardHome(s)`: a session's docs
 *  are its own repository's, whatever card it renders on. The URL goes through `docsLocation` and `docsPageUrl`
 *  (refinement (q)). Null has one meaning: `s.project` fails the project grammar, so there is no row to render. */
export function sessionDocsHref(s: FleetSession): SessionDocsLink | null {
  const project = s.project;
  if (!isDocsProject(project)) return null;
  const home = docsLocation({ kind: 'index' }, { kind: 'default-view', project });
  const branch = s.branch !== null && isDocsBareRef(s.branch) ? s.branch : null;
  if (branch === null) return { href: docsPageUrl(home), label: 'Docs, default branch', branch: null };
  const at = docsLocation(home, { kind: 'same-page', project, ref: { kind: 'bare', name: branch } });
  return { href: docsPageUrl(at), label: 'Docs on ' + branch, branch };
}
```

- [ ] **Step 5: The stylesheet.** Create `pwa/src/docs/docs.css` with exactly:

```css
/* Docs (native Docs reader, design 2026-10-01 sections 4.8 and 4.14): the Docs door in the fleet header and the chrome
   of the Docs screen. Imported by screens/DocsScreen.tsx, which app.tsx imports statically, so this sheet is part of
   the one main stylesheet the door needs on the fleet screen (the build check in the W5 plan's Task 11 reads the
   BUILT index css for it; vitest runs with `css: false` and evaluates no stylesheet).

   TOKENS ONLY. No literal colour anywhere in this sheet (contrast.test.ts's docs describe scans for one), no
   `repeat(<n>, 1fr)` (fleet-css.test.ts walks every sheet), and no `overflow` on `.shell-detail` (shell-css.test.ts):
   the detail pane's scrolling is shell.css's, and the Docs screen scrolls inside it as /settings does.

   GROUNDS. `.docs-screen` paints no background, and neither do `.shell-detail` or the fleet header, so every rule
   here that sets a colour and no ground of its own sits on body's --bg-page and is registered on that ground in
   design/audit.mjs's INHERITED_GROUNDS, each with its reason (the `.settings-*` precedent: the uncovered census is
   frozen and admits no new identity). The door has a second ground, `.shell-nav`'s --bg-surface in the desktop
   sidebar, which contrast.test.ts measures off its own ink. The banners, the failure view, the badge, the filter,
   the image chip and a pressed row paint their own ground, so the audit measures them on it with no entry; the
   failure view's coloured parts name `.docs-fail` and are measured through it. Links take `color: inherit`, so
   they read in whatever measured ink their container has and set no colour of their own.

   TAP FLOOR. Every control here has `min-height: var(--tap-min)` in its own rule, and tap-targets.test.tsx holds
   both halves for each: the rule, and a rendered element with the class. The two `btn-ghost` controls take the floor
   from `.btn-ghost` (components/primitives.css) and restate it here beside the width they give back. */

/* — the Docs door, in the fleet header before `.accounts-door` (section 4.8): `.settings-door`'s box — */
.docs-door {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--sp-1); min-height: var(--tap-min);
  padding: 0 var(--sp-1);
  border: 0; border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  background: none; color: var(--ink-secondary);
  font: var(--weight-medium) var(--text-2xs) / 1 var(--font-mono);
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: transform var(--dur-press) var(--ease-swift), color var(--dur-fast) var(--ease-swift);
}
.docs-door:active { transform: scale(0.88); color: var(--ink-primary); }
/* The glyph is decoration beside the word, aria-hidden in the markup, sized in the UI font as `.settings-door-glyph`. */
.docs-door-glyph { font-family: var(--font-ui); font-size: var(--text-xs); line-height: 1; }

/* — the screen — */
.docs-screen { display: grid; gap: var(--sp-3); padding: var(--sp-2); min-width: 0; }
.docs-screen > * { min-width: 0; }
.docs-index, .docs-project, .docs-listing, .docs-leaf, .docs-missing, .docs-invalid,
.docs-svg, .docs-raster, .docs-standin, .docs-changing {
  display: grid; gap: var(--sp-2); min-width: 0;
}

/* — the header: back, the crumbs, the truth line, the actions — */
.docs-head { display: grid; gap: var(--sp-2); min-width: 0; }
.docs-head-bar { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--sp-1); min-width: 0; }
.docs-back {
  flex: none;
  min-width: var(--tap-min); min-height: var(--tap-min);
  border: none; border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  background: none; color: var(--ink-secondary);
  font: var(--weight-regular) var(--text-xl) / 1 var(--font-ui);
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: transform var(--dur-press) var(--ease-swift), color var(--dur-fast) var(--ease-swift);
}
.docs-back:active { transform: scale(0.88); color: var(--ink-primary); }
.docs-crumbs { min-width: 0; }
.docs-crumbs ol {
  display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0 var(--sp-1);
  margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; min-width: 0;
}
.docs-crumbs li { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--sp-1); min-width: 0; }
.docs-crumbs li + li::before { content: '/'; }
.docs-crumb, .docs-crumbs-more {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center;
  min-height: var(--tap-min); padding: 0 var(--sp-1);
  border: 0; border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  background: none; color: var(--ink-secondary);
  font: var(--weight-regular) var(--text-sm) / var(--leading-tight) var(--font-mono);
  text-decoration: none; overflow-wrap: anywhere; cursor: pointer;
}
.docs-crumb-here { font: var(--weight-medium) var(--text-sm) / var(--leading-tight) var(--font-mono); overflow-wrap: anywhere; }

.docs-truth {
  margin: 0; min-width: 0;
  font: var(--weight-regular) var(--text-xs) / var(--leading-normal) var(--font-mono);
  color: var(--ink-secondary); overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
.docs-truth-relation[data-tone='warn'] { color: var(--status-attention-text); }
.docs-truth-commit { font: inherit; }

/* The freshness chip: a button (a tap is one manual refresh), static text when the repository has no origin. */
.docs-fresh {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; vertical-align: middle;
  min-height: var(--tap-min); padding: 0 var(--sp-2);
  border: 1px solid var(--edge-strong); border-radius: var(--r-full);
  background: none; color: var(--ink-secondary);
  font: var(--weight-medium) var(--text-2xs) / var(--leading-tight) var(--font-mono);
  text-align: left; cursor: pointer;
}
.docs-fresh[data-state='failed'] { color: var(--status-dead-text); }
.docs-fresh[data-state='none'], .docs-fresh[data-state='fetching'] { color: var(--ink-tertiary); cursor: default; }

/* The bordered controls: copy commit, the leaf's Source and Download, Load image, the image's own action, the plain
   text's Format anyway or Retry, and the gate's two choices. */
.docs-copy, .docs-leaf-action, .doc-img-load, .doc-img-action, .doc-plain-action, .doc-gate-btn {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; vertical-align: middle;
  min-height: var(--tap-min); padding: 0 var(--sp-3);
  border: 1px solid var(--edge-strong); border-radius: var(--r-md);
  background: none; color: var(--ink-secondary);
  font: var(--weight-medium) var(--text-xs) / var(--leading-tight) var(--font-mono);
  cursor: pointer;
}

/* The link controls: View on GitHub, Open committed version, a banner's hint, the index's owner. Their ink is their
   container's (`inherit` is not a colour of their own, so the audit reads none here). */
.docs-action, .docs-hint-link, .docs-owner-link {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center;
  min-height: var(--tap-min); padding: 0 var(--sp-1);
  color: inherit; text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 2px;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
.docs-actions { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: var(--sp-1) var(--sp-2); min-width: 0; }
.docs-leaf-actions { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: var(--sp-2); }

/* The quiet lines: the notes, loading words, the index head, "Formatting…". */
.docs-note, .docs-loading, .docs-index-head, .doc-formatting {
  margin: 0;
  font-size: var(--text-sm); line-height: var(--leading-normal);
  color: var(--ink-secondary); overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
/* The meta words: an action's note or refusal, "copied", "Updated to", the GitHub mark on an in-repo link. */
.docs-action-note, .docs-action-off, .docs-copy-said, .docs-updated, .doc-link-gh {
  margin: 0;
  font: var(--weight-regular) var(--text-xs) / var(--leading-normal) var(--font-mono);
  color: var(--ink-tertiary); overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}

/* — the rows: index, project, section and directory listings — */
.docs-filter {
  width: 100%; min-height: var(--tap-min); padding: 0 var(--sp-3);
  border: 1px solid var(--edge-strong); border-radius: var(--r-md);
  background: var(--bg-surface); color: var(--ink-primary);
  font: var(--weight-regular) var(--text-input) / 1 var(--font-ui);
}
.docs-rows { display: grid; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; min-width: 0; }
.docs-row {
  display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: baseline; gap: var(--sp-1) var(--sp-2);
  width: 100%; min-width: 0; min-height: var(--tap-min); padding: var(--sp-2) var(--sp-1);
  border: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--edge-subtle); border-radius: 0;
  background: none; color: var(--ink-primary);
  font: var(--weight-regular) var(--text-sm) / var(--leading-tight) var(--font-ui);
  text-align: left; cursor: pointer;
}
.docs-row:active { background: var(--bg-surface); color: var(--ink-primary); }
.docs-row-off { color: var(--ink-secondary); cursor: default; }
.docs-row-name { min-width: 0; font-weight: var(--weight-medium); overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.docs-row-glyph { flex: none; font-family: var(--font-ui); }
.docs-row-path, .docs-row-count, .docs-row-note, .docs-row-age, .docs-row-size, .docs-row-ref, .docs-row-state,
.docs-row-mark, .docs-row-drafts {
  font: var(--weight-regular) var(--text-xs) / var(--leading-tight) var(--font-mono);
  color: var(--ink-tertiary); overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
.docs-badge {
  display: inline-block; padding: 0 var(--sp-1); border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  background: var(--status-attention-tint); color: var(--status-attention-text);
  font: var(--weight-medium) var(--text-2xs) / var(--leading-normal) var(--font-mono);
}
.docs-nodocs > summary { display: flex; align-items: center; min-height: var(--tap-min); cursor: pointer; }

/* — the banners and the failure view: each paints its own ground — */
.docs-banners { display: grid; gap: var(--sp-2); min-width: 0; }
.docs-banner {
  display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: var(--sp-1) var(--sp-2);
  padding: var(--sp-2) var(--sp-3);
  border-left: 3px solid var(--edge-strong); border-radius: var(--r-md);
  background: var(--bg-surface); color: var(--ink-primary);
  font-size: var(--text-sm); line-height: var(--leading-normal); min-width: 0;
}
.docs-banner[data-tone='warn'] { border-left-color: var(--status-attention); background: var(--status-attention-tint); }
.docs-banner-text { min-width: 0; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.docs-banner-list { flex-basis: 100%; margin: 0; padding-left: var(--sp-4); overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.btn-ghost.docs-banner-action, .btn-ghost.docs-fail-action { width: auto; min-height: var(--tap-min); padding: 0 var(--sp-3); }

.docs-fail {
  display: grid; gap: var(--sp-2); min-width: 0;
  padding: var(--sp-3);
  border-left: 3px solid var(--status-dead); border-radius: var(--r-md);
  background: var(--bg-surface); color: var(--ink-primary);
}
.docs-fail-sentence { margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-sm); line-height: var(--leading-normal); overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.docs-fail .docs-fail-suggest, .docs-fail .docs-fail-hint, .docs-fail .docs-fail-kind, .docs-fail .docs-fail-list {
  margin: 0;
  font-size: var(--text-xs); line-height: var(--leading-normal);
  color: var(--ink-secondary); overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
.docs-fail-suggest a { color: inherit; }
.docs-fail .docs-fail-detail {
  margin: 0; max-height: 12em; overflow: auto; padding: var(--sp-2);
  border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  background: var(--bg-well); color: var(--ink-on-well);
  font: var(--weight-regular) var(--text-xs) / var(--leading-mono) var(--font-mono);
  white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
.docs-fail-actions { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: var(--sp-2); }

/* — the document: `.doc-body.msg-assist` keeps chat's measured Markdown rules (chat.css); these add the page's own — */
.doc-body { min-width: 0; max-width: var(--measure-prose); }
.doc-body :target { scroll-margin-top: var(--sp-4); }
.doc-body .doc-img-link .msg-img { display: block; }
.doc-link-inert { color: var(--ink-secondary); text-decoration: underline dotted; cursor: help; }

.doc-img-link {
  display: inline-flex; max-width: 100%;
  min-width: var(--tap-min); min-height: var(--tap-min); padding: 0;
  border: 0; background: none; cursor: pointer;
}
.doc-img-refused, .doc-img-loading {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 0 var(--sp-2);
  border: 1px dashed var(--edge-strong); border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  font: var(--weight-regular) var(--text-xs) / var(--leading-normal) var(--font-mono);
  color: var(--ink-secondary); overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
.doc-img-failed {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 0 var(--sp-2);
  border: 1px dashed var(--status-dead); border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  font: var(--weight-regular) var(--text-xs) / var(--leading-normal) var(--font-mono);
  color: var(--status-dead-text); overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
.doc-img-chip {
  display: inline-block; padding: 0 var(--sp-1); border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  background: var(--bg-raised); color: var(--ink-secondary);
  font: var(--weight-medium) var(--text-2xs) / var(--leading-normal) var(--font-mono);
}
.docs-svg-img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }

.doc-gate {
  display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: var(--sp-2);
  padding: var(--sp-3); border: 1px solid var(--edge-subtle); border-radius: var(--r-md);
}
.doc-gate-copy { flex-basis: 100%; margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-sm); line-height: var(--leading-normal); }
.doc-plain-note { margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-xs); line-height: var(--leading-normal); color: var(--ink-secondary); }
.doc-plain {
  margin: 0; white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere;
  font: var(--weight-regular) var(--text-sm) / var(--leading-mono) var(--font-mono);
}
```

```ts
// pwa/browser/harness.ts
export const DEFAULT_CHROME = '/usr/bin/google-chrome';
export function resolveChrome(
  env?: Readonly<Record<string, string | undefined>>, // default process.env; CCRC_CHROME '' counts as unset
  fallback?: string,                                   // default DEFAULT_CHROME
): string;
//   THROWS (never returns a sentinel) when neither CCRC_CHROME nor fallback is an executable regular file
export type OriginName = 'a' | 'b' | 'c';
export interface OriginHit {
  readonly origin: OriginName; readonly method: string;
  readonly path: string;           // pathname + query
  readonly cookie: string | null;  // null = the request carried no Cookie header
}
export interface OriginAnswer {
  readonly status?: number;        // absent = 200
  readonly headers: Readonly<Record<string, string>>; // sent exactly, nothing added
  readonly body: string | Uint8Array;
}
export type OriginRoute = (hit: OriginHit) => OriginAnswer;
export interface Origins {
  readonly a: string; readonly b: string; // http://127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>: one site, two origins
  readonly c: string;                     // http://localhost:<ephemeral>: another site
  readonly hits: readonly OriginHit[];    // every request, in arrival order, unknown paths (404) included
  close(): Promise<void>;
}
export function startOrigins(routes: Readonly<Record<string, OriginRoute>>): Promise<Origins>; // keyed by pathname; plain node:http
export function waitForHit(o: Origins, from: number, pred: (h: OriginHit) => boolean, ms: number): Promise<OriginHit | null>;
//   null has one meaning: no hit at index >= from satisfied pred within ms
export function onePixelPng(): Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>; // a 1x1 RGBA PNG; its magic read from DOCS_RASTER_TYPES, never typed
```

The browser config: `pwa/vitest.browser.config.ts` (`include: ['browser/**/*.browser.test.{ts,tsx}']`, `environment: 'jsdom'`, `testTimeout: 60000`, `hookTimeout: 60000`); the script `"test:browser": "vitest run --config vitest.browser.config.ts"`; the CI job `browser-pwa`, named `browser (pwa)`, `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`, `timeout-minutes: 15`, the `CCRC_LEG` step-skip on every step, steps checkout, setup-node `'22'` (npm cache on `pwa/package-lock.json`), `npm ci` in `pwa/`, `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.browser.config.ts`, in `full-suite.needs` and `RESULTS`. Every `null` above has the one meaning stated beside it.

**Decisions this task makes** (each fills a silence or adapts the architecture's entry to a measured fact; none departs from the spec's text):

1. **`resolveChrome` takes its fallback as a second, optional parameter.** The architecture's signature is `resolveChrome(env?)`; the hermetic case "CCRC_CHROME at a missing path and no `/usr/bin/google-chrome`" cannot be written against the real path on a CI runner that HAS that file, so the fallback is a parameter defaulting to `DEFAULT_CHROME`, and one case pins the default by behaviour on whichever box runs it. A `CCRC_CHROME` that names something that is not an executable regular file falls through to the fallback (spec 5.7: "`CCRC_CHROME`, else `/usr/bin/google-chrome`"); the thrown message names both, so the red says what to fix.
2. **The harness records every request.** `Origins` gains `hits`, and the harness gains `waitForHit`, `onePixelPng` and the four `Origin*` types (the architecture names `OriginRoute` without its shape). "No request leaves the page" and "the request still arrives" (spec 5.3's CORP and `nosniff` rows) are both read from `hits`: a property asserts the exact list of requests after the page's `load` plus `SETTLE_MS` (1 500 ms), and each control waits up to 20 s for the request it proves can happen.
3. **Every property has a control in the same Chrome, and nosniff is measured on its own.** CORP `same-origin` alone refuses B's no-cors `<script src>` of A's JSON, so "without nosniff the script runs" is the response with BOTH CORP and `nosniff` removed, and the property is measured twice: with every header, and with `nosniff` alone (`DOCS_RESPONSE_HEADERS` less CORP). The JSON body is an array, `["ccrc-docs","demo"]`: valid JSON that is also a valid script, so the control can show a run (an object body such as `{"ok":true}` is a syntax error as a script and could never show one). The outcome is the script element's own event, written into `document.title`: `load` (fetched and executed) or `error` (refused). Measured at planning: `error`, `error`, `load`.
4. **M5.B5 draws the SVG exactly as Docs draws it.** The page's `<img>` source is `svgDataUrl(bytes)` from `docs/DocImage.tsx`; the SVG carries a `<script>`, an `onload` and an external `<image href>` to B, each of whose runs would be a console line and a request. The property also asserts the SVG was drawn (`naturalWidth` 1), so "nothing ran" cannot come from an image that failed to decode; the control opens the same SVG as a top-level `blob:image/svg+xml` document from a page on A and sees its script's request arrive with A's cookie (`ccrc_demo=a`, set for A in every context). The SVG-labelled-`image/png` clause of M5.B6 has no control in the spec; its control here is the same body as `image/svg+xml` with no docs headers, whose script runs (so the detector is not blind).
5. **The PNG fixture is built, not typed.** `onePixelPng()` writes the table's own magic (`DOCS_RASTER_TYPES.png.magic[0][0].bytes`), then IHDR, one deflated row and IEND with `node:zlib`'s `crc32`; the first case checks `sniffRaster('png', ...)` and that A draws it for itself (width 1), so a width of 0 on B and C means CORP refused it.
6. **The package edits are written by hand, then installed with `npm ci`.** Measured at planning with npm 11.11.0: `npm install --save-dev --save-exact playwright-core@1.63.0` also rewrites `package.json`'s one-line `engines` over three lines and adds the root's `license` and `engines` to the lock, which the file-shape invariants forbid. So Step 4 edits both files exactly and `npm ci` installs from the lock (it fails if the two disagree, and never writes the lock). 1.63.0 is the newest `playwright-core` at least two weeks old at planning (1.64.0 was published 2026-10-07); its `browsers.json` names Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12, revision 1243. It downloads no browser.
7. **`browser-pwa` joins the shape rules, not the required names.** `ci-pipeline.test.ts`'s no-job-`if:`/no-`needs:` loop and its step-skip loop gain `browser-pwa` (a job skipped by `if:` reads as red in `full-suite`), and `full-suite`'s needs list gains it; the "four required names" case does NOT (the operator's ruling). A describe of its own pins its one name, runner, deadline, exact steps, and that it reads no secret and asks for no permission. `ci-merge-queue.test.ts` is not edited: its required roots (`server`, `test`, `build-pwa`) do not reach the browser leg.
8. **One comment line beyond the three counted `ci.yml` edits.** `full-suite`'s own comment lists the legs it is green over; it gains "the browser leg", or it would be false. Nothing else outside the new job, the `needs:` list and the `RESULTS` string changes.
9. **R1 calls the plugin's own `apply`.** Half 1 runs it with `VITEST` deleted from `process.env` (restored in a `finally`), as `npm run dev` and `npm run build` see the environment: `serve` true, `build` false. Half 2 runs it as it is now, under vitest: `serve` false. Each half has its own case and row (M4, M5).
10. **The file lists are vitest's own.** Besides the config objects, two cases run `vitest list --filesOnly --json` in a child with only `PATH` and `HOME` (no `VITEST` variable of this run leaks in) and read which files each config collects: none under `browser/` for the hermetic config (and this file, so the list is not empty), and only `browser/*.browser.test.*` for the browser config. const PWA = path.join(import.meta.dirname, '..');
```ts
const BROWSER_INCLUDE = 'browser/**/*.browser.test.{ts,tsx}';

/** The test files vitest itself collects under `configFile` (null = the default, `vite.config.ts`), relative to the
 *  package root, sorted. Run in a child with only PATH and HOME, so no VITEST variable of this run leaks into it. */
function listed(configFile: string | null): string[] {
  const env: Record<string, string> = { PATH: process.env['PATH'] ?? '' };
  if (process.env['HOME'] !== undefined) env['HOME'] = process.env['HOME'];
  const args = ['list', '--filesOnly', '--json', ...(configFile === null ? [] : ['--config', configFile])];
  const stdout = execFileSync(path.join(PWA, 'node_modules', '.bin', 'vitest'), args,
    { cwd: PWA, env, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 120_000, stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'] });
  const files = JSON.parse(stdout.slice(stdout.indexOf('['))) as { file: string }[];
  return files.map((f) => path.relative(PWA, f.file).split(path.sep).join('/')).sort();
}

    expect(files.filter((f) => f.startsWith('browser/'))).toEqual([]);

describe('resolveChrome: no Chrome is a red leg, never a skipped one (spec 5.7)', () => {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), 'ccrc-chrome-'));
  afterAll(() => rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }));
  const exe = path.join(dir, 'chrome');
  writeFileSync(exe, '#!/bin/sh\n');
  chmodSync(exe, 0o755);
  const plain = path.join(dir, 'not-executable');
  writeFileSync(plain, '#!/bin/sh\n');
  chmodSync(plain, 0o644);
  const folder = path.join(dir, 'a-directory');
  mkdirSync(folder);
  const missing = path.join(dir, 'missing');

  it('CCRC_CHROME naming an executable file wins', () => {
    expect(resolveChrome({ CCRC_CHROME: exe }, missing)).toBe(exe);
  });

  it('with CCRC_CHROME unset, empty or missing, the fallback is taken when it is an executable file', () => {
    expect(resolveChrome({}, exe)).toBe(exe);
    expect(resolveChrome({ CCRC_CHROME: '' }, exe)).toBe(exe);
    expect(resolveChrome({ CCRC_CHROME: missing }, exe)).toBe(exe);
  });

  it('CCRC_CHROME at a missing path and no fallback: it THROWS, naming both', () => {
    expect(() => resolveChrome({ CCRC_CHROME: missing }, missing)).toThrow(/no Chrome for the browser leg/);
    expect(() => resolveChrome({ CCRC_CHROME: missing }, missing)).toThrow(JSON.stringify(missing));
    expect(() => resolveChrome({}, missing)).toThrow(`CCRC_CHROME is unset, and ${missing} is not an executable file`);
  });

  it('a file that is not executable, or a directory, is not a Chrome', () => {
    expect(() => resolveChrome({ CCRC_CHROME: plain }, missing)).toThrow(/no Chrome/);
    expect(() => resolveChrome({ CCRC_CHROME: folder }, missing)).toThrow(/no Chrome/);
    expect(() => resolveChrome({}, folder)).toThrow(/no Chrome/);
  });

  it('the default fallback is /usr/bin/google-chrome (where ubuntu-latest has Chrome)', () => {
    expect(DEFAULT_CHROME).toBe('/usr/bin/google-chrome');
    if (existsSync(DEFAULT_CHROME)) expect(resolveChrome({ CCRC_CHROME: missing })).toBe(DEFAULT_CHROME);
    else expect(() => resolveChrome({ CCRC_CHROME: missing })).toThrow(`${DEFAULT_CHROME} is not an executable file`);
  });
});

/** Every plugin object in a config's (possibly nested, possibly async-free) plugin list. */
function flatPlugins(list: PluginOption[] | undefined): Plugin[] {
  const out: Plugin[] = [];
  const walk = (p: PluginOption): void => {
    if (Array.isArray(p)) p.forEach(walk);
    else if (p !== null && typeof p === 'object' && 'name' in p) out.push(p);
  };
  (list ?? []).forEach(walk);
  return out;
}

describe("the dev alias's scope: serve only, never under vitest (W4 review 412, residue R1)", () => {
  const alias = flatPlugins(hermetic.plugins).filter((p) => p.name === 'ccrc-dev-worker-safe-entries');
  const apply = (command: ConfigEnv['command']): boolean => {
    const a = alias[0]?.apply;
    expect(typeof a, 'the dev alias has no apply function').toBe('function');
    return (a as (config: UserConfig, env: ConfigEnv) => boolean)({}, { command, mode: 'development' });
  };
  /** Run `f` with VITEST unset, as `npm run dev` and `npm run build` see the environment, then restore it. */
  const outsideVitest = <T>(f: () => T): T => {
    const saved = process.env['VITEST'];
    delete process.env['VITEST'];
    try { return f(); } finally { if (saved !== undefined) process.env['VITEST'] = saved; }
  };

  it('is registered once, in the main plugin list', () => {
    expect(alias).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it('half 1: outside vitest it applies when serving and never when building', () => {
    expect(outsideVitest(() => apply('serve'))).toBe(true);
    expect(outsideVitest(() => apply('build'))).toBe(false);
  });

  it('half 2: under vitest (VITEST set, as now) it does not apply, even when serving', () => {
    expect(process.env['VITEST'], 'this case must run under vitest').toBeDefined();
    expect(apply('serve')).toBe(false);
    expect(apply('build')).toBe(false);
  });
});
```
