## Deviations found

- **D-4917 (2026-10-14)** — W5 is two sequential runs on one plan family, not one run (spec §7.7's wave preamble, "one run row, with one worker and one reviewer run", and its W5 row; operator ruling 2026-10-13). W5's row ships about twenty right-sized tasks, which do not fit one context with a held-out review and a close. Part 1 (this plan, run 413) ships the L0 widening, the Docs screen, `DocMarkdown` with the r10, r11 and 2-2 bounds, the docs `<br>`, the doors, `docs.css` and the browser leg with M5.B5 and M5.B6, and the seams part 2 consumes (`pinFor`, `imagePinFor`, `detachUrls`' copy, `copyText`, `saveBytes`, `docs-scans.test.ts`, the browser harness); part 2 (its own plan, run, pull request and review, dispatched after part 1 merges, from a `main` that holds it) ships Share, Markdown, text and image Export, `ExportAssets`, the settled-outcome context, the Markdown CSS move and M5.B9. The three rows the spec amended in place split on the same line: M4.T7's base form (row and leaf badge equal, the scan over `pwa/src/docs`) is part 1's and its amended clause (share, provenance, export) part 2's; M4.S1's docs-chrome registrations are part 1's and its re-keying and Share and Export chrome part 2's; M5.17's `rasterObjectUrl`, `downloadDocFile` and `saveBytes` clauses are part 1's and its `downloadExport` clause part 2's. The merge gate splits by what each part ships: R1 and R2 gate part 1's merge (part 1 issues all of W5's docs traffic); §4.17's measurements, M5.B9 and the Export-time finding gate part 2's. Part 2's plan cites this entry. Refinement (a); every task of this plan.
- **D-4918 (2026-10-14)** — the `html` leaf renders a stand-in until W6, not `MockupView` (spec §4.4's leaf row: class `html` "gives §5's `MockupView`", which is W6's). Part 1 renders the leaf's header and truth line, the sentence "HTML mockups open in a later release; Source shows the file and Download saves it.", the size, **Source** (the text renderer over `docs.file`) and **Download** (`downloadDocFile`): no `iframe`, no `srcDoc`, no frame of any kind, and `?frame=full` renders the same stand-in. W6 replaces the stand-in with `MockupView` in `DocsLeaf.tsx`'s `html` arm; part 2's Share notes an `html` leaf as source, and Export is not offered for `html` in W5. Refinement (b); Task 9, row W5P1-T9-M19.
- **D-4919 (2026-10-14)** — a linked worktree whose `branch` is `null` is not called detached (spec §4.7's redirect sentence, "that checkout is detached; showing <owner>'s default branch"). `branch: null` covers both a detached HEAD and an unmeasured read (the W2 adapter's carried constraint), so the page says "That checkout is not on a named branch, or its branch could not be read; showing <owner>'s default branch." and redirects to the owner's default view (`ref: null`), by replace, as §4.7 says. Goal 4 ("a page says exactly what it served") outranks the quoted sentence. Refinement (c); Task 9, rows W5P1-T9-M5 and W5P1-T9-M6.
- **D-4920 (2026-10-14)** — the 2-2 bound lives in the parse's own element count, not in the shared Markdown components (spec §4.10's bounds on the shared components and the coordinator's ruling of 2026-10-13, which put all three bounds "in the shared Markdown components"). 2-2 is a count problem: `measure` counted an inline `code` as one element while `SHARED_COMPONENTS.code` draws a chord as chips, so `DOCS_MAX_RENDER_ELEMENTS` did not bound the DOM; a budget kept inside the components would be render-time mutable state (StrictMode's double render and React's render order would make it nondeterministic) and would cut a document mid-render. `markdownParse.ts`'s `measure` instead adds, for every inline `code` element (not under `pre`), `inlineCodeExtraElements` of its text, exactly what the component draws (2N-1 for a chord of N parts) beyond the one `code` the walk already counts: one `span.kbd-combo`, N `kbd` and N - 1 `span.kbd-plus` in its place, and 0 for a span that is not a chord. `keystrokeParts` moved into `markdownGuard.ts`, which both the parse and the components already import, so the count and the component answer through one predicate and no import or file joins the worker closure. So `too-wide` fires before anything renders, in the worker, for docs, chat's worker path and part 2's Export alike; chat's synchronous path (at most 4 096 bytes) is bounded by its size. The components keep r10's word bound and r11's length bound (`MD_KEYSTROKE_MAX_CHARS` = 64, which caps one span at 32 parts). Task 3 Step 0 measured the exact count moving no real document under `docs/superpowers` across `DOCS_MAX_RENDER_ELEMENTS`, where the upper bound first planned (`2 x (its '+' count) + 1` for every short span) moved four (recorded in the SDD ledger). Refinement (d); Task 3, rows W5P1-T3-M8 to W5P1-T3-M11.
- **D-4921 (2026-10-14)** — a Markdown leaf whose bytes arrived as base64 is formatted when they are strict UTF-8; only bytes that are not valid UTF-8 get the non-fatal decode, plain text and "Not valid UTF-8." (spec §4.10 step 6: a `.md` that arrived as base64 "decodes through a non-fatal `TextDecoder('utf-8')` and shows as plain text: 'Not valid UTF-8.'"). ccd's encoding rule (spec §2 (f)'s "Encoding", as §6.1 restates it) also sends VALID UTF-8 as base64, when the text holds a NUL or when base64 frames shorter (a quote-heavy file), so the literal reading would label a valid file "Not valid UTF-8." and decline to format it; goal 4 ("a page says exactly what it served") decides. `docMarkdownSource` decodes with `{fatal: true}` first: strict UTF-8 is Markdown; anything else is decoded non-fatally (each bad sequence a U+FFFD) and shown as `DocPlain` with `DOC_NOT_UTF8_NOTE`, which is the spec's behaviour for invalid bytes (coordinator ruling during planning, 2026-10-13). Refinement (x); Task 8's decision 6, rows W5P1-T8-M14, W5P1-T8-M15 and W5P1-T8-M20 (M20 reverts to the spec's literal reading).
- **D-4922 (2026-10-14)** — a fourth bound on highlighting: `CodeBlock` does not highlight a registered block that holds a line longer than `MD_HIGHLIGHT_MAX_LINE_CHARS` = 2 048 characters (spec §4.10 names three bounds on the shared Markdown components, r10, r11 and 2-2, and §4.9's page cap; this is a fourth). The task review measured grammars that are quadratic on shapes that are not one long identifier, with a cost that grows with line length: a `markdown` fence holding one 64 KiB line of `[` about 9.6 s, `[a` or `![` over a 32 KiB line 1.2-1.5 s, a `yaml` fence holding one 64 KiB line of `a a a ...` 2.8-3.6 s, where §4.9 and §4.10 promise a bounded main thread for an arbitrary repository document. Order: the size cap first (a block over it keeps its KiB label and is never scanned), then r10's word scan, then the line scan, both linear with no regular expression; the label is `{label} · not highlighted (a {n}-character line)`. Chat and part 2's Export get the bound through the same components. The value is measured: the line bound removes the cost that grows with line length and stops where that growth meets the length-independent plateau of the slowest grammars (Task 3's decision 9 records the sweep, the two growing families at 512-16 384 characters, the plateau and the corpus: 1 real fence of 17 384 left plain). The operator's ruling on ask 30 (2026-10-14) chose a line bound, on an option that proposed 4 096; the coordinator's ruling by mail 4761 set the terms (the value measured, not taken from the option) and mail 4768 accepted the measured 2 048 and its basis. It joins r10, r11 and 2-2 in the merge gate. Task 3's fix commit `9a1d9b076`, rows W5P1-T3-M16 to W5P1-T3-M21. Its sweep put one unit on each line, so it never tried whitespace that spans lines, the shape review 439 F1 found quadratic in `typescript` and `javascript`; D-4925's fifth bound covers that shape, and the plateau the results carry was re-measured with the five bounds in place.
- **D-4923 (2026-10-14)** — r10's word class counts every UTF-16 code unit from 0x7f up as part of a word, not only `[A-Za-z0-9_$]` (the plan's Task 3 decision 5 and refinement (e), which put non-ASCII outside the class on a `typescript` and `bash` measurement; the spec's r10 bound itself, "one long word", is unchanged). highlight.js's PHP grammar takes `\x7f-\xff` as identifier characters, so a 64 KiB `php` fence of `_é` repeated, whose ASCII runs are each one character long, cost 38 s while the narrower class scored it 1. Failing closed costs nothing real: the longest run in a registered-language fence under `docs/superpowers` is 107 under the widened class (64 under the old). The coordinator's ruling by mail 4768 (2026-10-14). Task 3's fix commit `9a1d9b076`, row W5P1-T3-M15 and Task 3's decision 8.
- **D-4924 (2026-10-14)** — a link to the page being read that carries a fragment (`a.md#sec` or `../specs/a.md#sec` on `specs/a.md`) takes `DocLink`'s `fragment` arm, not its in-app `doc` arm (spec §4.11's `DocLink` arm table routes every `doc` resolution, this page included, through in-app navigation). The `doc` arm pushed a second history entry for the same URL, dropped `view`, and scrolled only if the visit happened to render the unchanged body again; the `fragment` arm is M4.U7's in-page anchor: it scrolls inside the article and writes no history entry. Only `DocLink`'s choice of arm changes: L0's `resolveDocRef`, which §5's viewer shares, is untouched and still answers `doc`. A same-page link with no fragment still takes the `doc` arm, and another page with the same file name is unaffected. On a `view=committed` page such a link now scrolls inside the committed view being read, where the `doc` arm kept the page's `ref` but dropped `view`, leaving the committed view; on a ref-view page the `doc` arm kept the ref too, so there only the history entry and the scroll differ. An anchor stays on the view you are reading. The coordinator's ruling by mail 4784 (2026-10-14). Task 6's fix commits `08f385a6f` and `c8d141da9`, rows W5P1-T6-M27 to W5P1-T6-M30.
- **D-4925 (2026-10-14)** — a fifth bound on highlighting: `CodeBlock` does not highlight a registered block whose longest run of blank code units (ECMAScript whitespace: U+0009 to U+000D, U+0020, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000 to U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000 and U+FEFF; a run that crosses line breaks) is longer than `MD_HIGHLIGHT_MAX_BLANK_CHARS` = 2 048 (spec §4.10 names three bounds on the shared Markdown components, r10, r11 and 2-2, and D-4922 added the line bound; this is a fifth). Review 439 F1 measured highlight.js's `typescript` and `javascript` grammars going quadratic on a fence made only of whitespace that spans lines: its word run and its longest line are 0, so none of the four bounds stopped it, and 64 KiB of `\n` cost 5.1-5.6 s, about 40 s for a page of eight under `DOCS_HIGHLIGHT_PAGE_MAX_CHARS`, where §4.9 and §4.10 promise a bounded main thread for an arbitrary repository document; chat's worker path has no page budget. Order, as `CodeBlock` runs it: the size cap first (a block over it is never scanned); then r10's word scan and the line scan, each run whenever the size cap passes; then this scan, run only when none of the size, word and line checks refused; each linear with no regular expression; a block that trips more than one is labelled by the first of word, line and blank run (review 450 F5 corrected this sentence, which said every scan ran only when the ones before it did not refuse); the label is `{label} · not highlighted (a {n}-character run of whitespace)`. Chat's synchronous and worker paths and part 2's Export get it through the same `CodeBlock`. The value is measured by D-4922's basis: a sweep of all 15 registered grammars over 28 cross-line shapes (pure blank runs of 11 kinds, and 17 short units each followed by a line break) found, among those shapes, only `typescript` and `javascript` growing, and only on a run that holds a line terminator (review 450 then found multi-character shapes outside those families that grow, bounded by D-4928); the bound stops where that growth meets the length-independent plateau (at 2 048 the costliest shape that reaches it, U+2028 or U+2029 alternated with `\n`, costs 225-336 ms (re-measured 2026-10-14 at load about 31, three repetitions: review 450 F6 found this entry and the basis table giving two figures for it) against a plateau of 230-290 ms; 4 096 would cost about twice it). The longest blank run in a real registered-language fence is 104, so no real fence goes plain. The coordinator's ruling in fix round 1 (mail 4807, review 439 F1). It joins r10, r11, 2-2 and the line bound in the merge gate. Commits `b54180624` and `5ca3efb77`, rows W5P1-T13-M34 to W5P1-T13-M38.
- **D-4926 (2026-10-14)** — the truth line's `diverged` sentence names the side that is served: with origin served (a qualified `refs/remotes/origin/<b>`) it reads "local and origin have diverged ({ahead} vs {behind}), showing origin's", in the words `VIA_SENTENCE.origin` uses; with local served it is spec §4.5's sentence unchanged ("…, showing local"). Spec §4.5's `RELATION_SENTENCE.diverged` (spec:1780) was written for a diverged ref that always serves local, and spec §3 has a qualified ref change only which side is served, never how relation is computed, so the verbatim sentence said "showing local" over a page showing origin; goal 4 ("a page says exactly what it served") decides. The count swap (ccd's served-side counts turned into local's lead and origin's lead) is unchanged, and `local-ahead` and `local-behind` were already true on both sides. Review 439 F6; the coordinator's ruling in fix round 1 (mail 4807), which records the spec correction in the ledger. Commit `899f56c3d`, rows W5P1-T13-M41 and W5P1-T13-M42 (W5P1-T10-M5 and W5P1-T13-M23 re-measured).
- **D-4927 (2026-10-14)** — the not-contained banner describes the leaf's pin: `DocsBanners` shows "Commit … is no longer on … Re-list" only when the answer's `show.commit` equals the pin's commit. Spec §4.3 contradicts itself on a Re-list that moves the tree to a new commit while the leaf's blob is unchanged: item 2 keys committed bodies by blob and does not re-download them, while "the new tree changes the leaf's pin → the leaf re-reads", with M4.EX12's three-way commit equality, says they are. The plan chose item 2 (Task 5 decision 4) and Task 13's 3-3 kept the formatted body, so the body read at commit A stays across the move to B, with its answer's `show.onRef` measured for A; the banner then outlived the Re-list it offers, and every later Re-list did nothing. Item 2 wins for the body (no re-read and no "Updated to" for a same-blob move); the banner and the truth line describe the pin, and after a move to B the pin comes from the fresh tree, so B is on the ref by construction. **The cost, for part 2:** M4.EX12's equality (provenance commit = pin commit = answer commit) does not hold for a body kept across a same-blob move; part 2's Share must take the pin's commit as provenance for such a body (same blob), or re-read before it enables (listed under the part-2 seams in the results). Review 439 F3; the coordinator's ruling in fix round 1 (mail 4807). Commit `95032db0a`, rows W5P1-T13-M39 (W5P1-T10-M46, W5P1-T10-M60 and W5P1-T10-M61 re-anchored or re-measured).
- **D-4928 (2026-10-14)** — highlighting is bounded by grammar as well as by shape: `CodeBlock` highlights a `typescript` or `javascript` block (every alias highlight.js 11.11.1 resolves to them) only up to `MD_HIGHLIGHT_JS_BLOCK_MAX_CHARS` = 8 192 characters and a `rust` block only up to `MD_HIGHLIGHT_RUST_BLOCK_MAX_CHARS` = 4 096, labelled in the size form; a Docs page highlights at most `DOCS_HIGHLIGHT_SCAN_PAGE_MAX_CHARS` = 393 216 characters of those grammars' code together and at most `DOCS_HIGHLIGHT_MARKDOWN_PAGE_MAX_CHARS` = 131 072 of `markdown`, each summed in `detachUrls`' page walk beside `DOCS_HIGHLIGHT_PAGE_MAX_CHARS`, a block of another grammar never refused by either; and `xml` (html, svg and every alias it declares) is registered through one wrapper that removes the `subLanguage` of its `<script>` and `<style>` modes, so their contents render as plain text. The bounded set is derived once (`deriveBoundedCaps`, `HIGHLIGHT_BOUNDED_CAPS`) as the closure of the base grammars under highlight.js `subLanguage` (an empty array reaching every registered grammar), and a test walks every registered grammar independently and pins it, with no script or style mode of xml carrying a `subLanguage`. Spec §4.10 names three bounds on the shared Markdown components, D-4922 added the line bound and D-4925 the whitespace bound; this is a sixth. Review 450 F1 found a shape that passes all five, `'<a>'` repeated (highlight.js's JSX `hasClosingTag` scans forward from every tag): about 2.8 s per 64 KiB block in `typescript` and `javascript`, about 23-26 s for a page of eight; a sweep of all 15 grammars over one fixed list of 77 units of one to four characters and up to ten keywords per grammar, at 16 and 64 KiB, then found `rust` quadratic on an unclosed raw string (`r#"`: 3.8 s per 64 KiB, 14 s at 128 KiB), a security review of the first commit found `xml` embedding javascript through `<script>`, and measurement found xml's `<script>`/`<style>` regions quadratic whatever they embed (`<script>` one per line: 8 KiB 7.9 s, 16 KiB of `<script><a>` 33 s), and `markdown`, which hands every HTML tag to xml, linear at about twice the plateau (`<a>` lines 652 ms per 64 KiB against 242-356). The values are the operator's and the coordinator's answers to asks 38 (the 8 KiB cap and the 384 KiB page budget: `<a>` lines cost 5.5-6.7 ms a KiB at 6-10 KiB, 10 at 16 KiB, 22 at 32 KiB, 43 at 64 KiB, a rate that rises with the block's size from the smallest size measured, so no size is cheapest per KiB (review 460 F8 found the reason first given here, the values that keep a crafted page near the plateau, unsupported: what such a page costs is stated below); rust joins at 4 KiB), 39 (the set is closed under `subLanguage`, mail 4975), 40 (xml without its script and style sub-languages, mail 4987) and 41 (markdown's own 128 KiB page budget, mail 4990). Real fences, measured through the Docs pipeline (each page parsed as Docs parses it, then `detachUrls`, `highlightBlockCap` and the three scans), so excluding the one page Docs refuses as too wide: 736 of `docs/superpowers` are plain under the final set, on 78 pages, of 8 508 `typescript`, `javascript` and `rust` fences the 64 KiB cap and the general page budget highlighted (532 over the block cap, 204 refused by the scan page budget alone; review 460 measured 743 while xml and markdown were in the set; no `rust` fence exists; the most markdown code on a page Docs formats is 24 056 characters, so the markdown budget costs none; review 460 F7 found that the 755 on 79 pages, the 762 and the 33 KiB recorded before were counted by fence pattern and included the too-wide page, and that the 8 582 beside them counted `typescript` and `javascript` fences only; one 375-character html fence loses its script/style colouring). The wrapper also reaches past script and style contents in two grammars that hand tags to `xml` with a kept continuation: in a `markdown` block, chat's included, every inline tag after an unclosed `<script>` or `<style>` renders with no tag, name or attribute colour until a closing tag, and in `typescript`'s JSX the rest of a block after an unclosed `<script>` is plain, where stock highlight.js coloured both (review 460 F9, measured; no markdown fence of `docs/superpowers` holds the shape, and chat's golden files are unchanged). The caps and the xml wrapper also reach `text` leaves, which `TextBody` renders through the same `CodeBlock` (review 460 F11): the spec's Docs screen table (§4.4) highlights a text leaf "through `CodeBlock` under the 64 Ki-char rule", and its chat paragraph lists "the 64 Ki-char highlight cap" among what reaches chat; under this entry a `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.mjs` or `.cjs` leaf over 8 KiB renders unhighlighted, labelled in the size form, and an `.xml`, `.xsl` or `.xhtml` leaf shows its script and style contents plain (`.rs` is not a text extension, so no rust leaf is highlighted at all, before or after). Leaves counted on 2026-10-15: the four Docs sections of this repository hold 292 files (290 `.md`, one `.json`, one `.html`) and none of those extensions, so no real leaf here changes. Asks 40 and 41 asked for "the end-to-end page under the target" as a case; a wall-clock assertion is load-sensitive on a shared box, so the case is deterministic instead: one end-to-end case through `detachUrls` and `CodeBlock` asserts which blocks of a mixed crafted page each budget admits (`docs-highlight-budget.test.tsx`), and the timings are recorded in the results (review 460 F10, the coordinator's ruling; a test-shape choice, not a departure). What the bounds leave, measured end to end through `detachUrls` and `CodeBlock` on pages that fill each budget exactly with every block highlighted (2026-10-15; review 460 F4 and F5 found the earlier pages one block short, because the budgets count the newline the parse keeps), beside a plateau page of eight 65 535-character blocks timed in the same run (1.7-2.2 s, load 17-157): 48 blocks of 8 191 characters of `<a>` lines 2.3-3.1 s in `typescript` or `javascript`; the markdown budget's two blocks of `<a>` lines 0.78-0.94 s (the reviewer measured 1.0-1.5 s); the accepted crafted page, which holds both the scan budget and the markdown budget because the budgets are summed apart, 3.2-3.5 s here and 3.75-4.37 s in the reviewer's three runs, 1.6-1.9 times the plateau page beside it (the 3.4 s and 1.4 times this entry carried before were measured one block short); chat has no page budget, so a message bounds each block, never their sum. The sweeps' coverage as run and what they did not try (the empty pairs and the link opener among them, which review 460 F6 found inside the size class this entry once called covered) are stated in `markdownLimits.ts` and under `### Carried, not fixed`. Review 460 (F1 to F3, the reviewer's figures) found shapes that pass every bound: `markdown` on link openers (`'[]('` or `'[[]('` in lines of 2 048 characters) about 4.5-5.5 s per 64 KiB block, about 9-11 s for a page through the markdown budget; `yaml` flow collections (`[]` or `{}` repeated) quadratic in the block's size, about 1.1-1.4 s per 64 KiB block and 7.5 s for a page of eight; the worst combined page found 10.6 s; in chat, with no page budget, about 4.5 s for one crafted markdown block and 1.1-1.4 s for one yaml block. Real documents are unaffected (the most markdown code on a page Docs formats is 24 056 characters, its largest markdown block 17 042). Four reviews in a row each found a new shape, so more crafted shapes probably exist. ### The six bounds

- **r10**: `MD_HIGHLIGHT_MAX_WORD_CHARS` = 256; no highlighting for a block holding a word (a run of `[A-Za-z0-9_$]` or of any UTF-16 code unit from 0x7f up: the wider class is a departure from refinement (e)'s first reading, recorded in `## Deviations found`, because highlight.js's PHP grammar takes `\x7f-\xff` as identifier characters and a 64 KiB `php` fence of `_é` repeated cost 38 s while the narrow class scored it 1) longer than this, labelled with the word's length (refinement (e)). Basis: at 256 a block's worst case costs what ordinary code of the same size does, so `DOCS_HIGHLIGHT_PAGE_MAX_CHARS` keeps bounding the page (planning: one `typescript` identifier run cost 21, 11, 146 and 2 291 ms at 256, 1 024, 4 096 and 16 384 characters; 64 KiB of 256-character runs 131 ms against 139 ms of ordinary code). Rows: W5P1-T3-M1 red, W5P1-T3-M2 red, W5P1-T3-M3 red, W5P1-T3-M4 red, W5P1-T3-M13 red, W5P1-T3-M15 red.
- **r11**: `MD_KEYSTROKE_MAX_CHARS` = 64; a code span longer than this is never a chord: `keystrokeParts` answers null before it trims or splits (refinement (f)), which also caps one span at 32 parts. Basis: the longest chord named keys make is about 40 characters, and at 64 the split costs under 0.1 ms (planning: 0.09, 0.84, 16, 396 and 3 854 ms for a span of `a`, L spaces and `b` at L = 64, 1 024, 4 096, 16 384 and 40 000). Rows: W5P1-T3-M5 red, W5P1-T3-M6 red, W5P1-T3-M7 red, W5P1-T3-M12 red, W5P1-T3-M14 red.
- **2-2**: `DOCS_MAX_RENDER_ELEMENTS` = 20000; the parse's own element count adds, for every inline `code` not under `pre`, exactly what the chip component draws (2N-1 for a chord of N parts), so `too-wide` fires before anything renders, in the worker, for every profile (refinements (d) and (g)). Basis: Task 3 Step 0 measured the exact count moving no real document under `docs/superpowers` across the limit. Rows: W5P1-T3-M8 red, W5P1-T3-M9 red, W5P1-T3-M10 red, W5P1-T3-M11 red.
- **line**: `MD_HIGHLIGHT_MAX_LINE_CHARS` = 2048; no highlighting for a registered block that holds a line longer than this (a line ends at a line feed or a carriage return), labelled "{label} · not highlighted (a {n}-character line)": the size cap is checked first, then r10's word scan and this linear line scan with no regular expression, each run whenever the size cap passes (Task 3's decision 9: a fourth bound beside spec 4.10's three, recorded in `## Deviations found`). Basis: some grammars are quadratic on shapes that are not one long identifier, and that cost grows with line length (a `markdown` fence of one 64 KiB line of `[` about 9.6 s, a `yaml` fence of one 64 KiB line of `a a a ...` 2.8-3.6 s); the bound stops where that growth meets the length-independent plateau of the slowest grammars, and at 2 048 the worst line-driven shape costs 245-263 ms, where 4 096 would cost about twice it. Its sweep put one unit on each line; whitespace that spans lines is the fifth bound's shape. The plateau itself is carried below. Rows: W5P1-T3-M16 red, W5P1-T3-M17 red, W5P1-T3-M18 red, W5P1-T3-M19 red, W5P1-T3-M20 red, W5P1-T3-M21 red.
- **blank**: `MD_HIGHLIGHT_MAX_BLANK_CHARS` = 2048; no highlighting for a registered block whose longest run of blank code units (ECMAScript whitespace, a run that crosses line breaks) is longer than this, labelled "{label} · not highlighted (a {n}-character run of whitespace)": checked after the size, word and line bounds, by one linear scan with no regular expression (review 439 F1, a fifth bound, recorded in `## Deviations found`). Basis: `typescript` and `javascript` cost highlight.js the square of a blank run that holds a line terminator (64 KiB of `\n` about 5-6 s; about 40 s for a page of eight), which none of the four bounds above caught; a sweep of all 15 grammars over 28 cross-line shapes (pure blank runs, and short units each followed by a line break) found, among those shapes, no other grammar that grows (review 450 then found multi-character shapes that do: the sixth bound). The bound stops where that growth meets the plateau: at 2 048 the worst run that reaches it (U+2028 or U+2029 alternated with `\n`; a longer run of U+2028 alone is r10's) costs 225-336 ms, re-measured at load about 31, against a plateau of 230-290 ms, where 4 096 would cost about twice it; the longest blank run in a real fence is 104. Rows: W5P1-T13-M34 red, W5P1-T13-M35 red, W5P1-T13-M36 red, W5P1-T13-M37 red, W5P1-T13-M38 red.
- **grammar**: `MD_HIGHLIGHT_JS_BLOCK_MAX_CHARS` = 8192, `MD_HIGHLIGHT_RUST_BLOCK_MAX_CHARS` = 4096, `DOCS_HIGHLIGHT_SCAN_PAGE_MAX_CHARS` = 393216, `DOCS_HIGHLIGHT_MARKDOWN_PAGE_MAX_CHARS` = 131072; a `typescript` or `javascript` block (every alias they carry) over the first, or a `rust` block over the second, is not highlighted, labelled in the size form; a Docs page highlights at most the third of those grammars' code together and at most the fourth of `markdown`, each summed in `detachUrls` beside the page budget, a block of another grammar never refused by either; `xml` is registered without the `subLanguage` of its `<script>` and `<style>` modes; and the set of bounded grammars is the closure of the base set under highlight.js `subLanguage`, derived once and pinned by a test (review 450 F1, a sixth bound, recorded in `## Deviations found` with asks 38-41). Basis: `'<a>'` repeated makes `typescript` and `javascript` quadratic (JSX `hasClosingTag`: 2.8 s per 64 KiB block, 5.5-6.7 ms a KiB at 6-10 KiB, 43 at 64 KiB), an unclosed `r#"` makes `rust` quadratic (3.8 s per 64 KiB), xml's `<script>`/`<style>` regions are quadratic whatever they embed (8 KiB of `<script>` one per line 7.9 s), and `markdown`, which hands every tag to xml, is linear at about twice the plateau (64 KiB of `<a>` lines 652 ms against 242-356). Cost: 755 real fences of `docs/superpowers` (79 pages) are plain, one 375-character html fence loses its script/style colouring, and the markdown budget costs none (the most markdown code on a real page is 33 KiB). What the six bounds leave is carried below. Rows: W5P1-T13-M63 red, W5P1-T13-M64 red, W5P1-T13-M65 red, W5P1-T13-M66 red, W5P1-T13-M67 red, W5P1-T13-M68 red, W5P1-T13-M69 red, W5P1-T13-M70 red, W5P1-T13-M71 red, W5P1-T13-M76 red, W5P1-T13-M77 red, W5P1-T13-M78 red, W5P1-T13-M79 red, W5P1-T13-M80 red, W5P1-T13-M81 red, W5P1-T13-M82 red, W5P1-T13-M83 red, W5P1-T13-M84 red, W5P1-T13-M85 red, W5P1-T13-M86 red, W5P1-T13-M87 red.
- Re-measured here (node v24.14.1, highlight.js 11.11.1, one run each, on this box's load): a 256-character `typescript` identifier highlights in 1.57 ms and a 4 096-character one in 113.15 ms; a span of `a`, 64 spaces and `b` splits in 0.11 ms, and with 16 384 spaces in 261.7 ms. The built worker's 2-2 answer is the gate's `built-worker` line above.

NOT tried: units of more than four characters, mixtures of different units, nesting, and valid code shaped to defeat a grammar; a shape outside those families may still grow, in any grammar. Until review 450 this entry said that no grammar's cost grew past the five bounds; F1 falsified it. CARRIED to the operator by the coordinator. Cost: a crafted page can hold the main thread for about 3.4 s while it highlights (this box, load about 47), and a shape outside the swept families possibly longer.

Cost: a crafted chat message of many blocks holds the main thread for their sum while it highlights.

### After the merge, not this wave

1. The coordinator fills `### Merge gate` (R1 and R2, after the operator's W3 dark rollout) in a docs-only commit on this branch; only then does part 1 merge. An R1 failure fires `docs-chunked-reads`.

3. Part 2 (Share and Export) is planned after this review and dispatched from a `main` that holds this merge; W5b follows part 2, rolled `--server-first`; the standalone docs server retires after W7.
